This pathology report describes a surgical procedure in which the right kidney was removed laparoscopically due to a tumor. The tumor is diagnosed as renal cell carcinoma, clear cell type. Tissue samples were submitted for further investigations, and no digital pictures were taken. Various blocks were created for microscopic examination.

The report is signed by a resident physician and an attending pathologist who confirm the diagnosis.

Overall, the report indicates the presence of a relatively large and moderately aggressive renal cell carcinoma in the right kidney, with lymph node metastasis in two out of nine nodes examined.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a nephrectomy for a renal tumor. The final diagnosis is renal cell carcinoma with both papillary and clear cell features. The surrounding non-neoplastic kidney tissue is essentially normal, but there is peritumoral renal parenchymal changes. The molecular fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) analysis demonstrated trisomy of chromosomes 7 and 17 in both the papillary and clear cell areas of the carcinoma, as well as foci with tetrasomy of chromosome 17 in the papillary areas. This molecular phenotype is most consistent with a papillary renal cell carcinoma. The exact characterization of the lesion will be performed after further molecular testing. The TNM stage is Ta, Nx, Mx.

The report also indicates the presence of parathyroid glands within normal limits and notes the presence of multiple papillary microcarcinomas in both lobes of the thyroid. The report's findings suggest the presence of metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma and related tissue abnormalities.

The pathology report describes a patient who underwent a total thyroidectomy due to a thyroid nodule. The specimen received contained a 1.1 x 1.1 x 1.0 cm centrally placed encapsulated cystic nodule with focal calcifications and granular appearance. The report indicates that papillary thyroid carcinoma was found and there was metastatic involvement in two out of three lymph nodes in the central neck, with focal extranodal extension. The report also notes that there was no capsular or vascular invasion and no extrathyroidal extension.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid carcinoma. The total thyroidectomy specimen shows two foci of papillary thyroid carcinoma, measuring 0.1 cm and 2.5 cm, in the right lobe. The largest focus is an encapsulated follicular variant with focal capsular and angiolymphatic invasion. Both foci are confined to the thyroid. The pathological stage is pT2N1a. There is also nodular thyroid hyperplasia present. In the selective neck dissection, metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma is found in four out of seven lymph nodes examined, with no extranodal extension. The margins are uninvolved by carcinoma.

This pathology report includes the following findings:

1. PRESTRAP MUSCLE TISSUE, EXCISION:
No tumor is present in the fibroconnective tissue and skeletal muscle.

2. RIGHT PARATHYROID, BIOPSY:
Cellular parathyroid tissue weighing 0.004 grams.

3. THYROID, TOTAL THYROIDECTOMY:
There is a poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma with a papillary component. The tumor is located in the isthmus of the thyroid and is not multifocal. There is no extrathyroidal extension or lymphovascular invasion. The resection margins are negative. The thyroid also shows extensive chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis consistent with Hashimoto's thyroiditis. There is metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma found in one lymph node in the central neck region without extracapsular extension.

4. RIGHT SUPERIOR PARATHYROID, BIOPSY:
No tumor is present in the lymphoid tissue. No parathyroid tissue is present.

5. LEFT SUPERIOR PARATHYROID, BIOPSY:
No tumor is present in the lymphoid tissue.

6. BILATERAL PARATRACHEAL AND MEDIASTINAL LYMPH NODES, DISSECTION:
Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma is found in five out of eighteen lymph nodes. Fragments of thyroid tissue with lymphocytic thyroiditis are also present.

The gross description of the specimens is also provided.

The pathology report describes a case of multifocal papillary thyroid carcinoma, with lymph node involvement and infiltration into the trachea. The dominant tumor was angioinvasive and widely invasive classical variant with focal dedifferentiation and tall cell change. The thyroid was totally excised, with surgical margins involved by carcinoma and extrathyroidal extension present. A secondary tumor of papillary carcinoma follicular variant was also found in the right lobe. The medullary carcinoma in the right lobe was positive for calcitonin, CEA, chromogranin, and TTF but negative for thyroglobulin. The tumor involved one lymph node. The patient underwent a total thyroidectomy. The report also notes the presence of additional papillary microcarcinomas and an adenomatoid nodule or nodular follicular disease. The tumor was staged as pT4a, pN1a, and cM0.

The report indicates that a total thyroidectomy was performed and the left lobe of the thyroid gland contained a 2.5 cm papillary carcinoma that was unifocal and had not spread to the lymph nodes or beyond the thyroid gland (pT2). The margins around the tumor were free of cancer cells and there was no evidence of venous or lymphatic invasion. The report could not assess for distant metastasis.

The pathology report is for a total thyroidectomy, with a 34 gram thyroid gland. There is a 28 cm oncocytic variant thyroid tumor, confined to the left lobe. There is evidence of vascular and lymphatic invasion with intraglandular spread. There was no significant fibrosis observed. Four lymph nodes were examined and showed no evidence of tumor. The pathologic stage is pT3a N0. There is nodular thyroid hyperplasia with a dominant oncocytic (multicellular) nodule measuring 1.2 cm, along with exuberant chronic lymphocyte infiltrates. Molecular pathology testing for mutations in BRAF, NRAS, HRAS61, KRAS12/13, and RET/PTC rearrangements did not identify any mutations. The report provides background information on the significance of mutations in these genes and their association with papillary thyroid carcinomas.

The pathology report describes the findings from a biopsy of the trachea, a lymph node, and a total thyroidectomy. The trachea biopsy shows benign respiratory mucosa. The lymph node biopsy reveals metastatic papillary carcinoma, with the node being 0.5 cm in size and the metastatic focus measuring 0.2 cm. No extranodal extension is seen. The pathology report indicates the presence of a papillary carcinoma in the right thyroid, with the tumor consisting of papillae covered by multiple layers of cuboidal epithelial cells. The tumor has invaded the capsule or vessels and benign tissue, and there is evidence of necrosis, fibrous tissue, and invasion of skeletal muscle. The size of the tumor is 2.5x2x1.8 cm. The pathology report describes a total thyroidectomy procedure, which involved the removal of the entire thyroid gland weighing 15 grams. The final diagnosis is papillary thyroid carcinoma, specifically the tall cell variant with extrathyroidal extension. There is no evidence of angiolymphatic invasion. The tumor was found to have spread to the right lobe (2.1 cm) and left lobe (0.3 cm) with extension beyond the resection margin. However, there was no involvement of the regional lymph nodes. The pathologic stage is pT3, NO. The report also mentions the presence of nodular thyroid hyperplasia and chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis. Molecular testing revealed a BRAF mutation in the right thyroid nodule. Overall, the report indicates the presence of papillary thyroid carcinoma with extrathyroidal extension but no lymph node involvement.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid carcinoma, classical variant, with a tumor size of 1.8cm, limited to the thyroid. Two out of three lymph nodes examined also showed involvement. The report notes a positive margin status due to the posterior margin being involved, while the anterior margin is very close. There were no lymphatic or perineural invasions reported. Additionally, a hyperplastic nodule was observed in the left thyroid lobe, while thymus and parathyroid gland samples were unremarkable. Information regarding the margin status was also included as it is recommended, but there are no data on the prognostic value of close margins. The pathology report describes a left hemithyroidectomy specimen for a patient who underwent total thyroidectomy with left levels 2 and 6 dissection. The diagnosis is angioinvasive poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma, widely invasive, arising in follicular variant papillary carcinoma, with a focus on the left hemithyroidectomy specimen measuring 9.6 cm. There were no pathological diagnoses for one lymph node dissection specimen and two lymph nodes in the other dissection specimen. The tumor was unifocal, with a greatest dimension of 9.6 cm, and a histologic grade of G3. There was partial capsule infiltration and focal extent of lymph-vascular invasion. The margins were uninvolved by carcinoma, and perineural invasion and extrathyroidal extension were not identified. The TNM descriptors were not applicable, and the pathologic staging was based on AJCC/UICC TNM 7th edition, which showed pT3 primary tumor and NO regional lymph node metastasis.

This pathology report describes the findings from a surgical resection of a papillary thyroid carcinoma in a patient. The report states that the patient had a total thyroidectomy, with the tumor located in the left lobe. The tumor is identified as a tall cell variant and measures 6.0 cm in size. There is also extracapsular extension present. The surgical resection margins are negative, although the tumor is seen 0.1 cm from the margins. One lymph node out of one examined shows metastatic carcinoma. The background thyroid parenchyma shows nodular hyperplasia. Molecular testing reveals a BRAF V600E mutation, but no mutations in NRAS61, HRAS61, or KRAS12/13. FISH testing shows negative results for RET/PTC rearrangement. The final diagnosis is papillary thyroid carcinoma, tall cell variant, with a tumor stage of pT3 N1a MX.

This pathology report summarizes the findings from various biopsies and specimens taken from a patient with papillary thyroid carcinoma. The report indicates the following:

- The right inferior parathyroid biopsy showed no evidence of malignancy.
- The right superior parathyroid biopsy showed benign normocellular parathyroid tissue.
- The left cricoid thyroid muscle biopsy showed metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma present in the muscle and soft tissue, along with dystrophic calcifications.
- The lymph nodes in the left neck at levels 2-4 showed one out of sixteen lymph nodes positive for metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma with extracapsular extension.
- The lymph nodes in the left neck at Level 6 revealed three out of six lymph nodes positive for metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma with extracapsular extension.
- The total thyroidectomy specimen showed papillary thyroid carcinoma with invasive properties extending into surrounding skeletal muscle. The tumor size was 2.5 cm, and there were two foci of papillary thyroid carcinoma present.
- The assessment of surgical margins showed involvement of the left anterior margin and within 1 mm of the left posterior margin. The anterior and posterior margins of the right lobe of the thyroid were negative.
- The thyroid gland away from the tumor showed non-neoplastic goiter with cystic degeneration and chronic thyroiditis.

In summary, the patient has papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to the lymph nodes and invasion into surrounding muscle and soft tissue.

The pathology report indicates that there was a right thyroid nodule that was positive for papillary carcinoma. Multiple nodules were seen on ultrasound. Biopsies were done on a jugular node, right paratracheal lymph node, and Delphian node, which were all found to be benign. A total thyroidectomy was performed, and the tumor type was identified as papillary carcinoma, tall cell variant. The tumor was found to be 1.4 cm in diameter and had positive margins. There was invasion into the perthyroidal fibroadipose tissue but no blood vessel invasion. The report also notes that there was nodular hyperplasia in the non-neoplastic thyroid and one benign perthyroidal lymph node identified. The frozen section consultations during the surgery confirmed benign tissue for the jugular node and right paratracheal lymph node.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has been diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma. The report includes the examination of various lymph nodes and the total thyroid. Metastatic carcinoma is found in several lymph nodes, with varying sizes and degrees of involvement. The tumor in the thyroid is described as multifocal, with different types of papillary carcinoma. The tumor is well differentiated and there is no evidence of mitotic activity or tumor necrosis. The tumor is partially and non-encapsulated, and there is no evidence of blood vessel invasion or extrathyroid extension. The report also mentions nodular hyperplasia in the non-neoplastic thyroid tissue and unremarkable parathyroid glands. In conclusion, the primary tumor is papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to multiple lymph nodes.

The pathology report describes the findings from a neck CT scan and the subsequent surgical removal of a portion of the thyroid. The diagnosis is papillary carcinoma, a type of thyroid cancer. The tumor is well-differentiated and has not spread to the surrounding tissues or blood vessels. The tumor is located in the left lobe of the thyroid and measures 1.3 cm in diameter. There is no tumor necrosis or extrathyroid extension. The surgical margins are free of tumor. The report also mentions the presence of nodular hyperplasia and the absence of parathyroid glands.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a total thyroidectomy for papillary thyroid cancer. The tumor was identified as tall cell variant of papillary carcinoma. Mitotic activity was not identified and tumor necrosis was not present. The tumor exhibited features of papillary carcinoma, including psammoma bodies. The tumor had focal invasion of blood vessels and extrathyroidal extension into perithyroidal fibroadipose tissue. The surgical margins showed microcarcinoma less than 0.5 mm from the cauterized margin. Multiple foci of papillary microcarcinoma were present in both the left and right lobes of the thyroid. No adenomas were identified. Non-neoplastic thyroid tissue showed nodular hyperplasia. One normal parathyroid gland was identified adjacent to the right lobe of the thyroid. Two benign perithyroidal lymph nodes were also found. Overall, the report confirms the presence of papillary thyroid cancer with certain pathological characteristics.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has thyroid carcinoma, specifically the tall cell variant. The report also mentions that a BRAF V600E mutation was identified, while mutations in NRAS, HRAS, and KRAS were not identified. The FISH test results were negative for RET/PTC rearrangement. The report states that the BRAF V600E mutation is associated with more aggressive behavior of papillary carcinoma. The report also mentions that mutations in RAS genes and PAX8/PPARg rearrangement occur in follicular thyroid carcinomas. The report concludes with the final diagnosis, which includes metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma in lymph nodes, extranodal spread, venous invasion, extrathyroidal extension in the tumor, and nodular thyroid with hyalinization and calcification. The pathologic stage is pT3, N1b, MX.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid cancer in a patient with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. The patient underwent a total thyroidectomy, and the surgical margins were free of tumor. The tumor was described as a tall cell variant of papillary carcinoma, with a size of 1.8 cm. There was no identification of tumor necrosis or blood vessel invasion, but there was invasion of the perithyroidal adipose tissue. The report also mentions numerous foci of papillary microcarcinoma in both lobes of the thyroid. Nodular hyperplasia was observed in the non-neoplastic thyroid tissue. The parathyroid glands were not identified in the specimen. Overall, the report indicates the presence of papillary thyroid cancer with a tall cell variant and the presence of microcarcinoma in multiple foci.

The report describes the pathology of a right thyroid lobectomy specimen. The specimen includes a 4.5 x 3 x 1.8 cm right thyroid nodule, which has a uniform hemorrhagic cut surface. The margins of excision are marked with black ink, and the tissue is submitted in its entirety in six cassettes. Microscopic examination of the sample shows nodular hyperplasia (multinodular goiter) and the presence of one parathyroid gland. A small incidental nodule (0.5 cm) is also identified, which is worrisome for papillary thyroid microcarcinoma. The diagnosis is confirmed through a follow-up addendum report.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has papillary thyroid carcinoma, conventional type, with extrathyroidal extension into skeletal muscle. The tumor has invaded the thyroid gland and has abutted the resection margin. Additionally, metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma has been found in three out of five lymph nodes in the right central neck with extracapsular extension. The biopsy from the right inferior parathyroid gland is negative for tumor. The report also provides details on the gross description of the specimens submitted for diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a total thyroidectomy specimen from a patient with a thyroid nodule. The final diagnosis includes the following findings:

- Papillary thyroid carcinoma, columnar cell variant with solid and microfollicular areas present in the left lobe, measuring 2.0 cm. The carcinoma is confined to the thyroid, with free margins.
- Angiolymphatic invasion is present.
- Three lymph nodes (2 left perithyroidal and 1 isthmic) were examined and found to be negative for tumor involvement.
- The pathologic stage is pT1bNO, based on the examination of the three lymph nodes.
- Exuberant chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis is also seen.
- The lesion is encapsulated, but capsular and vascular invasion are present, suggesting that encapsulation may not be relevant in this variant of papillary carcinoma.
- An immunostain for beta catenin shows cytoplasmic staining only, excluding the erlbriform morular variant.

Overall, the report indicates the presence of papillary thyroid carcinoma, columnar cell variant, with angiolymphatic invasion but no involvement of regional lymph nodes. The tumor is confined to the thyroid and has free margins. Chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis is also present.

The pathology report shows a diagnosis of papillary carcinoma of the left lobe of the thyroid, with the tumor being confined to the thyroid and margins of resection being free. The isthmus shows chronic inflammation, and three lymph nodes in the isthmus are identified, one of which has xanthogranuloma. No tumor is seen in the twelve lymph nodes of the right lobe. Additionally, there is a ruptured sebaceous cyst in the right neck. Immunoperoxidase studies were requested from the lymph nodes of the isthmus, with a supplemental report to follow. An addendum to the report confirmed the presence of metastatic carcinoma in three lymph nodes associated with the isthmus. No extracapsular extension was identified. The report's SNOMED codes suggest a diagnosis of thyroid cancer.

This pathology report is for a female patient who underwent a partial thyroidectomy for a right thyroid nodule suspected of being papillary carcinoma. The diagnosis confirms the presence of papillary carcinoma, classical type, predominantly well-differentiated with focal areas of tall-cell changes. Other notable findings include no evidence of tumor necrosis, involvement of the right lobe of the thyroid, a tumor diameter of 1.5 cm, no evidence of blood vessel invasion, and focal extrathyroid extension into soft tissue. All surgical margins are free of tumor, and there is no evidence of tumor multicentricity. The non-neoplastic thyroid shows no abnormalities, and no parathyroid glands are identified. Additionally, there is a fragment of atrophic thymus adjacent to the thyroid capsule. The report also mentions that representative slides were reviewed in consultation with another pathologist who agrees with the diagnosis. The specimen received is a partial thyroidectomy measuring 4 x 2 x 1.5 cm, with the cut surface revealing a well-circumscribed, indurated lesion measuring 1.5 x 1.5 x 1 cm. Both the tumor and the surrounding thyroid tissue were submitted for further analysis. This summary provides an overview of the main findings in the pathology report.

This pathology report is for a  year old female who underwent a partial thyroidectomy for a left thyroid nodule consistent with PTCA (Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma). The pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid carcinoma that involved both the left lobe and isthmus of the thyroid gland. The patient also had lymphocytic thyroiditis, benign Hurthle cell nodules, and metastases to lymph nodes in levels 2, 6, and the left modified radical neck dissection. The report does not include information on staging or treatment plans.

The pathology report describes three specimens received- a parathyroid biopsy, a right paratracheal lymph node excisional biopsy, and a total thyroidectomy specimen. The pathology report describes a case of thyroid cancer with multifocal bilateral papillary carcinoma and metastases to lymph nodes in various locations, including the right paratracheal lymph node at the thymus, left level 3 lymph node sites, and right level 2,3,4 lymph nodes. The pathology report describes a surgical pathology consultation for a patient with a left paratracheal node dissection and total thyroidectomy. The report also provides details about the size, weight, and other features of the specimen.

The pathology report reveals that the patient had a total thyroidectomy due to papillary thyroid carcinoma involving two left lobe and one right lobe tumor masses, the largest being 1.5 cm. The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a thyroid resection and completion thyroidectomy. The patient had a right thyroid mass and underwent a lobectomy. The pathology report revealed a combined follicular and papillary thyroid carcinoma. The tumor showed extensive capsular invasion and infiltration into the perithyroidal soft tissue. A small perithyroidal lymph node attached to the edge of the isthmic margin was also involved with metastatic papillary carcinoma. The lesion represents a rare example of a true mixed, or combined follicular/papillary carcinoma of the thyroid. The tumor was well-differentiated and did not show lymphatic/vascular invasion.

This is a pathology report for a patient who underwent a total thyroidectomy. The report shows that there is a 0.8 cm follicular variant microcarcinoma in the left lobe of the thyroid. The pathology report states that the patient underwent a total thyroidectomy and was diagnosed with papillary carcinoma with focal tall cell features in the left lobe of the thyroid. An adjacent parathyroid gland was involved as well.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid carcinoma with extensive intrathyroidal spread and lymphovascular invasion, as well as metastases to lymph nodes in the central compartment and midline. The pathology report describes a partial thyroidectomy performed on the left lobe of the thyroid. The patient has been diagnosed with metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma in multiple locations, including the left paratracheal tissue, central lymph node, and thyroid. The largest tumor nodule (inferior aspect of right lobe) measures 1.7 cm in diameter, and the carcinoma extends to the inked and cauterized surfaces of the resected thyroid gland. The pathology report reveals a diagnosis of multifocal papillary thyroid carcinoma in the left thyroid lobe with no extra-thyroid extension and no lymphovascular invasion. The pathology report describes a case of widely invasive papillary thyroid carcinoma with unusual features in a patient who also had severe chronic thyroiditis and atrophy. AJCC staging was not applicable.

This pathology report is for a patient with papillary carcinoma of the left thyroid. The report describes the findings from the specimens submitted, which include a right lobe hemithyroidectomy, left lobe hemithyroidectomy, and left paratracheal lymph node dissection.

Overall, the report confirms the presence of papillary thyroid carcinoma in the left thyroid lobe and metastatic involvement in lymph nodes. The right thyroid lobe shows chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis and nodular hyperplasia.

The pathology report describes the findings from a procedure done on a 72-year-old female with a thyroid nodule. The report includes the following details:

This pathology report describes the findings from a thyroid biopsy. The report states that there is a papillary carcinoma, classical type, in the left thyroid lobe and isthmus. The tumor is well differentiated and has a diameter of 2.5 cm. There is no encapsulation of the tumor, and it is noted to be present at the inked anterior margin. There are also two smaller foci of papillary microcarcinoma in the isthmus and left lobe measuring 0.7 cm and 0.25 cm, respectively. 

In the right thyroid lobe, there are three foci of papillary microcarcinoma ranging from 0.2 cm to 0.5 cm in size. There is no evidence of blood vessel invasion or extrathyroid extension. 

Lymph nodes in the left neck level six and seven show metastatic papillary carcinoma, with two lymph nodes involved. The largest lymph node has a size of 0.8 cm and the largest metastatic focus measures 0.6 cm. Extranodal extension is not identified.

The non-neoplastic thyroid exhibits nodular hyperplasia and mild chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis. Psammoma bodies, which are indicative of metastatic papillary carcinoma, are noted in the lymph nodes. 

There is no mention of any additional significant findings in the report.

The report describes the results of a right thyroid lobectomy specimen. The primary tumor is diagnosed as a papillary carcinoma with a size of 1.2 cm. The extent of invasion is limited to the thyroid, and no lymphatic invasion is identified. Metastasis is found in five out of nine regional lymph nodes in the central compartment of the neck. There is no involvement of surgical margins and additional pathologic findings. Parathyroid tissue is identified in both specimens.

The pathology report describes a total thyroidectomy and dissection of the central neck. The tumor, located in the isthmus lobe of the thyroid, is confirmed to be a papillary carcinoma with a size of 2.6 cm, unifocal and with minimal extrathyroidal extension. No lymph nodes were submitted for examination. Margins are uninvolved, but venous/lymphatic invasion is indeterminate. Parathyroid tissue was found attached to the inferior portion of the thyroid. The specimen was submitted in its entirety for examination.

The pathology report describes a left hemithyroidectomy specimen from a patient with papillary carcinoma, an oncocytic variant, with follicular nodular disease and follicular adenoma. Double adenoma, one chief cell type, and one clear cell variant are identified in the parathyroid gland. The tumor is unifocal and located in the left lobe of the thyroid with a size of 2.7cm. Margins are uninvolved by carcinoma, and there is minimal tumor capsular invasion. No lymphovascular or perineural invasions are identified, and there is no extrathyroidal extension. The primary tumor is classified as pT2, and regional lymph nodes cannot be assigned. Additionally, there is an adenomatoid nodule, nodular follicular disease, and focal (non-specific) thyroiditis.

This pathology report describes a case of metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma. The report details the size and involvement of various lymph nodes and describes the characteristics of the tumor itself, including size, location, and invasion. The report also notes the presence of nodular hyperplasia and chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis in the non-neoplastic thyroid tissue. The parathyroid glands are identified as unremarkable. Finally, the report mentions the successful surgical removal of the tumor with clear margins.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a total thyroidectomy due to papillary carcinoma in the right lobe of the thyroid gland. The tumor was 3.0 cm in size, and there was no evidence of lymph node metastasis or vascular invasion. The margins were uninvolved, and the extent of the tumor was limited to the thyroid gland. There was also mild lymphocytic thyroiditis and a single adenomatoid nodule in the right lobe.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had papillary thyroid carcinoma that had metastasized to four lymph nodes in the right neck contents and right paratracheal lymph nodes. The right and left thyroid lobes and isthmus were resected, and multifocal papillary thyroid carcinoma was identified in both lobes, but the margins were negative for tumor. Chronic lymphocytic (Hashimoto's) thyroiditis and nodular hyperplasia were also noted. No distant metastasis was identified.

The pathology report states that the patient has hyperparathyroidism, but it does not provide any information about the procedure performed. The report then discusses the findings of molecular testing on block 2A, which showed a BRAF mutation (p.V600E, c.1799T>A). Mutations in NRAS61, HRAS61, and KRAS12/13 were not identified. The FISH test results were negative for RET/PTC rearrangement. The report mentions that mutations in BRAF or RAS genes or RET/PTC rearrangements are found in more than 70% of papillary thyroid carcinomas, and that the BRAF V600E mutation is associated with more aggressive behavior of papillary carcinoma. The report also mentions that BRAF V600E mutation and RET/PTC and PAXA/PPARG rearrangements are overall specific for malignancy in the thyroid, although they have been reported with low frequency in benign thyroid lesions. The report then provides details about the methodology used for the mutational analysis, which involved DNA extraction, microdissection, real-time PCR, melting curve analysis, and sequencing. The report includes an addendum for block 1A, which identifies loss of heterozygosity at 1p, 10q, and 12q, and loss of heterozygosity of 13q.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid cancer in the right lobe. The tumor is classified as papillary carcinoma with focal oncocytic tall cell features. The tumor is well differentiated and no mitotic activity or tumor necrosis is identified. The tumor is located in the right lobe and measures 1.0 cm in diameter. There is no tumor encapsulation or blood vessel invasion. The surgical margins are free of tumor. Additionally, a papillary microcarcinoma measuring 0.6 mm is identified in the left lobe. Mild chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis is observed in the non-neoplastic thyroid tissue. No parathyroid glands are identified. The remaining sections of the thyroid are unremarkable.

The pathology report shows that a total thyroidectomy was performed and the specimen was found to have multifocal papillary carcinoma in both the right and left lobes of the thyroid. The tumor size in the right lobe was 3.0 cm. No lymph nodes were examined and the extent of invasion cannot be assessed. The primary tumor is classified as pT2, limited to the thyroid. Margins are uninvolved and there is no venous/lymphatic invasion identified. Additionally, parathyroid tissue was found in association with the right lower thyroid lobe.

The pathology report describes a case of widely invasive bilateral and multifocal papillary carcinoma in the thyroid gland, with extrathyroidal extension and focal thyroiditis. The dominant tumor is of the classical variant and measures 2.1 cm in the left lobe, while the second tumor is 1.7 cm in the right lobe and shows follicular papillary architecture. Vascular and perineural invasion are suspected but not unequivocally confirmed. The report also notes the presence of an additional papillary microcarcinoma of the follicular variant in the isthmus and infiltration of one of the parathyroid glands by papillary thyroid carcinoma. The report includes synoptic data and TNM staging information.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has bilateral thyroid nodules and a history of left lobe papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). The report shows that a total thyroidectomy was performed. The largest tumor focus is located in the right lobe, with tumor sizes ranging from 0.4 cm to 1.1 cm in greatest dimension. The tumor is classified as well-differentiated and there is no identified mitotic activity or tumor necrosis. The tumor is partially encapsulated and invades the perithyroidal adipose tissue and parathyroid gland. The surgical margins are free of tumor. Non-neoplastic changes include nodular hyperplasia and chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis. Two benign lymph nodes were identified. The report notes that special stains and immunohistochemical stains were negative. The frozen sections taken intraoperatively confirmed a benign thyroid issue near the left upper pole. The permanent diagnosis is the same.

The report describes a surgical pathology consultation for a patient who underwent a total thyroidectomy with left paratracheal neck dissection. Two tumors were found, one in the right lobe and one in the left lobe. The dominant tumor in the right lobe is a papillary carcinoma with three different histologic variants and capsular invasion. It exhibits positive staining for three specific markers, but no lymphovascular or perineural invasion nor extrathyroidal extension were identified. The second tumor in the left lobe is also a papillary carcinoma with two histologic variants, a partially encapsulated tumor with minimal capsular invasion. No lymphovascular or perineural invasion nor extrathyroidal extension was identified. The report also notes the presence of multiple papillary microcarcinomas and a branchial cleft-like cyst in the right lobe, as well as advanced thyroiditis. The report specifies that there are no regional lymph node metastases.

The pathology report describes a tumor in the right lobe of the thyroid gland that partially penetrated the tumor capsule and did not invade the lymphovascular space. The surgical margins were free of the tumor. No metastatic carcinoma was found in any of the 3 lymph nodes examined. Additionally, a benign follicular adenoma and a superior mid-thyroid mass were also present. The overall staging of the cancer was pTNM T1N0. Frozen section diagnosis confirmed the thyroid with no sign of parathyroid involvement. The report includes a detailed description of the specimens submitted for analysis.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid carcinoma in a patient who underwent a total thyroidectomy. The tumor was located in the right lobe and measured 4.2 cm in diameter, with minimal extrathyroidal extension. Resection margins were negative and no lymphatic or vascular invasion was identified. Six lymph nodes from the right paratracheal region were negative for metastasis. The left thyroid lobe was benign and there was mild lymphocytic thyroiditis present. The tumor was classified as stage pT3, pN0, and pM0. The report includes gross and microscopic descriptions of the specimen.

The pathology report states that the patient underwent a thyroidectomy for a thyroid nodule. The final diagnosis reveals that the left lobe of the thyroid gland had papillary thyroid carcinoma with dominant follicular growth pattern, while the right lobe had benign thyroid tissue. The carcinoma measured 3.3 cm and did not show extrathyroidal extension or vascular invasion. The cancer was 0.1 cm away from the margin. The pathologic stage was T2. The report also mentions that a previous fine needle aspiration of the left thyroid lobe showed a positive HRAS mutation.

The pathology report describes the results of a surgical pathology consultation. The report indicates that the patient was diagnosed with papillary carcinoma, follicular variant (2.2 cm) and mild follicular nodular disease and nonspecific chronic thyroiditis in the thyroid. No pathological diagnosis was made for lymph nodes and parathyroid glands. The report also includes information on tumor size, invasions, and staging based on AJCC/VICC TNM, 7th edition criteria. The specimens submitted for examination included a lymph node and the total thyroidectomy specimen, which consisted of the right lobe, left lobe, and isthmus.

The pathology report describes a case of a 46-year-old female with papillary thyroid cancer involving the right lobe of the thyroid gland and a small focus in the left lobe. The tumor size in the right lobe is 2.2 cm and there is capsular invasion with positive margins. A lymph node excision was negative for malignancy. Unremarkable parathyroid tissue was also excised. No extrathyroidal extension was observed.

The pathology report describes a tumor in the left thyroid gland. The tumor is consistent with papillary carcinoma, which is a type of cancer. The tumor size is 2x1.5x15 cm and it is unifocal, meaning it is confined to one area. There is no evidence of extrathyroidal extension, indicating that the tumor has not spread beyond the thyroid gland. No markers or special stains were used in the evaluation. There is no additional information or comments provided in the report.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had thyroid cancer. The report includes surgical pathology results for various specimens, including lymph nodes, thyroid lobes, and soft tissue. The right thyroid lobe was found to have benign parenchyma with a focal foreign body giant cell reaction and no evidence of carcinoma. The left thyroid lobe had papillary thyroid carcinoma, follicular variant, with the inked margin focally involved by carcinoma and infiltration of adjacent structures. The lymph node examined showed no evidence of malignancy. The specimen descriptions and gross descriptions are also provided.

The pathology report describes a total thyroidectomy that resulted in the diagnosis of papillary thyroid carcinoma. The largest tumor nodule measured 2.8cm, with two additional nodules detected in the isthmus and left lobe. The margins were negative but the tumor was 0.1cm from the closest margin. One out of four lymph nodes evaluated was positive for tumor. The tumor was found in a background of lymphocytic thyroiditis with germinal centers, which is compatible with Hashimoto's thyroiditis. The report includes tumor staging information and gross descriptions of the specimens examined.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has metastatic carcinoma in one lymph node and two types of neoplasms in the thyroid, including papillary thyroid carcinoma and a Hurthle cell neoplasm suspected to be a Hurthle cell adenoma. The report also notes the absence of evidence of fibrous capsule and capsular or vascular invasion in the Hurthle cell neoplasm and positive staining for thyroglobulin and negative staining for Calcitonin. The report mentions that immunoperoxidase and in-situ hybridization tests were performed and developed by the Laboratory of Pathology and that the laboratory is CLIA certified to perform high complexity clinical laboratory testing. The report also describes the gross features of the specimens received for examination. The reason for the supplemental report was to clarify the location of the lesions, and the diagnosis remains unchanged.

This pathology report describes the findings of a 1.5 cm papillary microcarcinoma thyroid nodule and a benign lymph node discovered during a total thyroidectomy of a 72-year-old male. The tumor was well-differentiated with tall cell features and did not show evidence of necrosis or mitotic activity. There was also a separate focus of papillary microcarcinoma (0.25 cm) in the right lobe. The surgical margins were free of tumor, and there was no evidence of extrathyroidal extension. The report also mentions nodular hyperplasia in the non-neoplastic thyroid tissue and does not identify any parathyroid glands. Overall, the diagnosis indicates a low-grade, non-aggressive form of thyroid cancer.

This pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid carcinoma. The tumor is located in the left lobe and isthmus of the thyroid gland. It is a single focus and measures 1.8x1.2cm in size. The tumor has invaded beyond the thyroid gland (extrathyroid extension) and the surgical margins are involved by the tumor. Angiolymphatic invasion is present, indicating spread of cancer cells into blood vessels and lymphatic vessels. Lymph nodes are negative for neoplasm. The TNM staging of the tumor is T3 NOMx.

The pathology report describes a case of metastatic carcinoma in a patient's neck. The report includes results from excisions of soft tissue in the neck as well as a thyroidectomy. The report indicates that the primary tumor has minimal extrathyroidal extension but that there are metastases in four out of eleven lymph nodes. The largest metastasis measures 2.4 cm. The report has been amended to include these findings.

The pathology report describes a right hemithyroidectomy specimen from a patient with multifocal papillary carcinoma with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis and mild follicular nodular disease. There are two tumors present, with the dominant tumor showing oncocytic mixed follicular and macrofolicutar variants, measuring 1.3 cm. The second tumor is a papillary carcinoma measuring 0.4 cm. The tumors have not invaded margins, the tumor capsule, lymphatic vessels, or nerves, and there is no evidence of extrathyroidal extension. Pathological staging is based on AJCC/UICC TNM, 7th Edition, with a primary tumor (pT) of 1b and no involvement of regional lymph nodes (PNX). The report also notes the presence of adenomatoid nodules or nodular follicular disease and normal parathyroid glands.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid carcinoma involving the right and left thyroid lobes. The tumor is multifocal with the largest focus measuring 3.2 cm in the left lobe. There is no evidence of invasion into surrounding structures or lymphovascular invasion. The surgical margins are negative, indicating that there is no tumor at the edges of the removed tissue. One out of three lymph nodes examined shows involvement by metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma. Other findings include multinodular hyperplasia and chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis. The pathologic stage is assessed as pT2 pN1. Intraoperative frozen sections were performed and showed no tumor in the lymph node or parathyroid tissue. The total thyroidectomy specimen weighed 27 grams and showed three distinct nodules, with the largest measuring 1.7 cm in the left lobe. The tumor is described as well-circumscribed and may contain focal calcifications.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a thyroid nodule and underwent a total thyroidectomy. The report confirms the presence of a follicular carcinoma with foci of transcapsular invasion measuring 2.5 cm in the right lobe. Additionally, two papillary microcarcinomas measuring 0.2 cm and 0.8 cm were found in the right and left lobes respectively. The report also includes information about molecular testing, which did not reveal mutations in BRAF, NRAS, HRAS, or KRAS genes, and RET/PTC rearrangement was negative. The report provides background information on the genetic alterations and their association with thyroid malignancy.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid carcinoma that was detected during a total thyroidectomy surgery. The tumor was multifocal with the largest mass located in the right thyroid lobe. The tumor showed features of "tall cell" variant of papillary carcinoma in some areas. There was lymphatic/vascular invasion, extensive capsular invasion, and invasion of perithyroidal soft tissue. The tumor was well-differentiated and classified as pT3NxMx. No tumor was seen in the Delphian lymph node biopsy.

The pathology report shows a diagnosis of multifocal papillary carcinoma, with a dominant oncotic follicular variant in the right hemisphere of the thyroid. The tumor is encapsulated, with minimal invasion of the tumor capsule. No lymph vascular or perineural invasion was identified, and there was no evidence of extrathyroidal extension. The report also notes chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis and multiple papillary micro-carcinomas. The primary tumor is staged as pT1b, with no regional lymph node metastasis.

The pathology report indicates that a total thyroidectomy was performed, and an encapsulated follicular variant tumor was found in the right lobe. There is no evidence of capsular or angiolymphatic invasion, and the tumor is confined to a size of 1-4 cm. There are no additional pathologic findings mentioned. The patient's history and clinical questions are not provided in the report. Further details about prior malignancies, chemoradiation, organ transplant, immunosuppression, and other diseases are also not mentioned.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a thyroid nodule and underwent a total thyroidectomy. The report states that mutations in certain genes (BRAF, NRAS61, HRAS61, KRAS12/13) were not identified, and a FISH test for RET/PTC rearrangement was negative. The report also mentions that there was a microcarcinoma in the left lobe of the thyroid and that molecular studies will be reported in an addendum. The final diagnosis reveals that the tumor in the thyroid was a papillary carcinoma, encapsulated follicular variant, with involvement of regional lymph nodes. The tumor size was 2.5 cm and there was no extrathyroidal extension. Margins were involved by carcinoma. Further details and information about the patient's medical history, such as prior malignancies, chemoradiation therapy, organ transplant, immunosuppression, and other diseases, were not provided or answered in the report.

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

- Right anterior scalene lymph node: Granulomatous inflammation, no tumor present.
- Right neck contents, level 2, 3, and 4: Benign-looking thyroid tissue metastatic to one level 2 lymph node and three level 3 lymph nodes. No tumor present in six level 4 lymph nodes.
- Left posterior carotid space mass: Thrombosed vessel, no tumor present.
- Submandibular ganglion: Ganglion and salivary gland, no tumor present.
- Left comprehensive neck dissection, right level 1: Invasive moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the mandible (4.5 cm). Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in one level 2 lymph node (6.0 cm) with extranodal extension. No tumor present in level 1, level 3, and level 4 lymph nodes. Focal mild dysplasia in the left floor of mouth margin.
- Right superior parathyroid gland: Parathyroid, no further information provided.
- Total thyroidectomy and paratracheal lymph node dissection: Small focus of follicular variant papillary carcinoma (3.0 mm). Multiple adenomatous hyperplasia.

The report also includes gross descriptions of the lymph nodes and other tissues examined.

The pathology report describes the case of a male patient who underwent a total thyroidectomy and left neck dissection. The report notes the presence of metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma in lymph nodes of the left lower neck and left tracheoesophageal gutter node. The report also identifies widely invasive classical variant papillary carcinoma with hobnail cell change and psammomatous dissemination in the left lobe of the thyroid. No pathological diagnosis was made for soft tissue in the left neck level VI or parathyroid left perthyroidal. The report suggests the dominant tumor is a 2.0 cm widely invasive classical variant which shows psammomatous dissemination throughout the left lobe. The tumor is partially encapsulated and shows no evidence of vascular invasion. Nine of the 34 regional lymph nodes examined showed metastases. The report suggests adenomatoid nodule(s) or nodular follicular disease but found no extranodal extension. The report recommends further examination to determine the extent of the tumor and metastasis.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of papillary thyroid carcinoma in a patient with a history of symptomatic palpable thyroid nodules and a total thyroidectomy was performed. The largest primary tumor was located in the right lobe and measured 1.1 cm. Capsular and vascular invasion were absent, and margins were negative. There was no evidence of extrathyroidal extension or lymph node metastasis. Six lymph nodes from the right level II and seven from level VI were dissected and found to be negative for neoplasm. The tumor was a well-differentiated follicular variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma. Frozen sections and permanent sections confirmed the diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a surgical consultation for a patient who underwent a total thyroidectomy and a biopsy of the right upper parathyroid gland. The report confirms the presence of papillary thyroid carcinoma in the left lobe of the thyroid with no evidence of capsular or vascular invasion. The tumor is unifocal and exhibits diagnostic features of low-risk papillary thyroid carcinoma. No lymph node metastasis or extrathyroidal extension is identified. The report also confirms the absence of pathological diagnosis in the right upper parathyroid gland and surrounding lymph nodes and thymus. The report concludes with additional information on the gross description of the specimens and a quick section diagnosis of the parathyroid tissue.

This pathology report summarizes the findings of a surgical procedure involving various tissues in the neck area. The main findings include:

1. Delphian lymph node:
- Benign lymph nodes

2. Left lower parathyroid:
- Benign parathyroid tissue

3. Left paratracheal tissue:
- Benign tissue

4. Total thyroidectomy:
- Papillary carcinoma of the thyroid, classical type
- Well-differentiated tumor with no mitotic activity or tumor necrosis
- Focal invasion into the capsule but no blood vessel invasion or extrathyroid extension
- Surgical margins free of tumor
- Two foci of papillary microcarcinoma in the left and right lobes
- No identified adenomas or non-neoplastic thyroid conditions

5. Preracheal tissue:
- Benign fibroadipose tissue

Overall, the report indicates the presence of papillary carcinoma in the thyroid, with well-differentiated features and limited invasion. The lymph nodes and parathyroid tissue examined were found to be benign.

The pathology report describes a total thyroidectomy specimen with a tumor localized in the right lobar isthmus. The tumor is a 0.2 cm papillary microcarcinoma and there is no evidence of lymphovascular invasion or extrathyroidal extension. Margin status is clear and there is no perineural invasion identified. The frozen section reveals the presence of parathyroid tissue. The final pTNM stage is pT2Nx.

The patient is a year-old with a left thyroid nodule, which was discovered during a routine physical exam. The entire thyroid gland was removed, and pathology confirmed a 2.3 x 2.1 x 1.8 cm papillary thyroid carcinoma within the left lobe, which was well encapsulated and did not infiltrate adjacent tissue. Two out of two lymph nodes excised from the left level VI area were positive for metastatic carcinoma consistent with papillary thyroid carcinoma. The final diagnosis is papillary thyroid carcinoma with lymph node metastasis and background lymphocytic thyroiditis.

The pathology report describes a specimen of a total thyroid gland measuring 6.0 x 5.5 x 3.0 cm with a multinodular tumor approximately 4 cm in size that predominantly shows the papillary and follicular variant of thyroid carcinoma. The report notes that the carcinoma invades the capsule and shows extra-capsular extension with focal tumor extension up to 0.05 cm from the inked margin. The report also mentions that no lymph nodes or parathyroid glands are identified grossly. A frozen section examination was performed during the surgery, which confirmed the presence of carcinoma.

This pathology report describes a case of thyroid cancer. The patient underwent a total thyroidectomy, and the pathology findings showed two foci of cancer in the thyroid, with the largest focus being in the right lobe. The cancer was identified as papillary carcinoma, encapsulated follicular variant. The cancer was confined to the thyroid and did not invade the capsule or blood vessels. The tumor was classified as pT3, meaning it had extended beyond the thyroid gland but had not spread to the lymph nodes or other organs. The parathyroid gland was also examined, and there were no significant abnormalities found. Overall, the margins of the excised tissue were free of cancer, and no lymphatic invasion was identified.

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

- A total thyroidectomy was performed.
- Papillary thyroid carcinoma was identified, which was multifocal and bilateral, with at least 7 foci ranging in size from less than 0.1 cm to 15 cm. There was also a focal tall cell feature present.
- Angiolymphatic invasion and microscopic extrathyroidal extension were found.
- The pathologic stage was determined to be pT3 NO.
- One lymph node was examined and found to be tumor-free.
- An oncocytic follicular (Hurthle cell) adenoma measuring 2.5 cm was identified in the right lobe of the thyroid.
- Chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis and nodular hyperplasia were also observed.
- Central compartment contents showed a normocellular parathyroid gland and unremarkable thymic tissue. No lymph nodes were present in this compartment.
- Molecular studies will be performed and reported in an addendum.

Overall, the report confirms the presence of papillary thyroid carcinoma with certain characteristics and provides information on the extent of the cancer and its involvement in surrounding tissues.

The pathology report shows the following findings:

1. Right paratracheal tissue biopsy: Benign fibroadipose tissue.
2. Right lower parathyroid biopsy: Benign enlarged hypercellular parathyroid gland.
3. Left paratracheal lymph node biopsy: Micrometastatic papillary carcinoma with no extranodal extension.
4. Total thyroid:
   - Tumor Type: Tall cell variant of papillary carcinoma.
   - Size: 5.7 cm in greatest dimension.
   - Mitotic activity: Not identified.
   - Tumor Necrosis: Not identified.
   - Location: Left lobe with invasion into perithyroid skeletal muscle.
   - Surgical margins: Free of tumor.
   - Multicentricity: Separate papillary carcinoma (1 cm) in the right lobe and papillary microcarcinoma (0.2 cm) in the left lobe.
   - No adenoma(s) identified.
   - Non-neoplastic thyroid exhibits nodular hyperplasia.
   - Parathyroid glands not identified.
5. Additional left paratracheal tissue biopsy: One lymph node positive for micrometastatic papillary carcinoma with no extranodal extension.

Overall, the patient has papillary thyroid carcinoma with metastasis to lymph nodes and invasion into perithyroid skeletal muscle. No mitotic activity or tumor necrosis are identified.

The pathology report states that the patient had a total thyroidectomy and excision of lymph nodes. The specific clinical question and outside tissue diagnosis were not answered. The report mentions that the patient has metastatic thyroid cancer. The addendum of the report discusses the results of molecular testing. It states that a HRAS codon 61 mutation was identified, but mutations in BRAF, NRAS61, and KRAS12/13 were not identified. The report provides information about the significance of these mutations in thyroid cancer. The sample preparation and procedure for the testing are also described. Additionally, the report states that loss of heterozygosity at chromosome 2 and fractional allelic loss of 9% were identified.

The pathology report shows that the patient has a papillary thyroid carcinoma, follicular variant in the left lobe of the thyroid gland with extrathyroidal extension and lymphovascular invasion. There are metastases in 2 of 13 lymph nodes in the central neck and in 4 of 42 lymph nodes in left levels 2A, 3, 4, and 5. The resection margins are negative. Additionally, a parathyroid tissue carcinoma is present. The report includes the gross description of the resected specimen and lymph nodes, as well as the SNOMED codes and diagnostic interpretation. Further treatment may be recommended based on these findings.

This pathology report describes a case of papillary thyroid carcinoma. The tumor measures 1.5 cm and is located in the isthmus of the thyroid gland. There is also an additional focus of papillary thyroid carcinoma measuring 0.3 cm in the left lobe. Vascular invasion is absent, and there is minimal extrathyroidal extension. The carcinoma is about 0.1 cm from the margin. Chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis is also noted. The overall stage of the tumor is pT3N0a. The report also mentions that metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma is present in six out of fourteen lymph nodes in the central compartment. Extracapsular spread is not present. In addition, a trichilemmal (pilar) cyst measuring 1 cm is found in the left abdominal wall. A biopsy of the right inferior parathyroid shows normal cellular parathyroid. Molecular testing of the right thyroid lobe reveals a BRAF p.V600E mutation.

The pathology report describes the findings of a surgical procedure for a thyroid nodule suspected to be papillary thyroid carcinoma. The specimens submitted for analysis include lymph nodes, thyroid tissue, and parathyroid gland tissue.

The report confirms metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma in the Delphian nodes and right paratracheal lymph nodes. The largest metastatic focus in the lymph nodes is 0.19 cm. There is no extranodal extension identified.

The pretracheal tissue in the midline also shows metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma, with the largest metastatic focus measuring 0.01 cm. Again, no extranodal extension is identified.

The biopsy of the right lower parathyroid gland shows benign and unremarkable tissue.

A total thyroidectomy was performed, and the dominant tumor nodule measured 2.0 cm in size. The tumor is classified as papillary carcinoma, diffuse sclerosing variant, and is well-differentiated. There are psammoma bodies present. The tumor is partially encapsulated but shows extensive invasion of blood vessels. It invades the thyrohippocytic tissue but has clear surgical margins.

The non-neoplastic thyroid exhibits chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, and the parathyroid glands were not identified.

The excision of the right paratracheal tissue reveals benign and unremarkable parathyroid gland tissue.

Overall, the pathology report confirms the presence of metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma in lymph nodes and surrounding tissues, with no evidence of extranodal extension. The total thyroidectomy showed a well-differentiated papillary carcinoma with some invasion but clear surgical margins. The non-neoplastic thyroid tissue shows chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis.

The patient has bilateral small thyroid nodules. The pathology report shows that the right-sided nodule is papillary thyroid carcinoma, classical type, with well-differentiated histologic grade. No mitotic activity or tumor necrosis is identified. The tumor is located in the left lobe and measures 1.1 cm in size. There is no tumor encapsulation or lymphovascular invasion identified. Entrathyroid extension is not present. The surgical margins show the tumor present at the inked and cauterized margin. Multiple foci of papillary microcarcinoma are present in both lobes ranging from 0.15 to 0.8 cm in size. No adenomas are identified. The non-neoplastic thyroid exhibits nodular hyperplasia. One unremarkable parathyroid gland is identified on the right side.

The pathology report describes a left hemithyroidectomy specimen with multifocal papillary carcinoma. The dominant tumor is a 1.2 cm follicular variant papillary carcinoma and an additional 0.05 cm papillary carcinoma was also identified. The margins were uninvolved by carcinoma and the tumor was totally encapsulated with no evidence of lymph-vascular invasion, perineural invasion, or extrathyroidal extension. The TNM staging was pT1b (tumor more than 1 cm but not more than 2 cm in greatest dimension, limited to the thyroid) and pNX (regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed). Adenomatoid nodules or nodular follicular disease were also noted. Frozen sections were taken and the remainder of the specimen was submitted for further examination.

The pathology report describes specimens received from a patient's right thyroid area, including a lymph node and thyroid tissue with multiple nodules. Multiple lymph node candidates were also noted. The report notes representative sections from each nodule were submitted for testing and the patient gave explicit written consent for the tissue to be used. No diagnosis or conclusion is provided in this report.

The pathology report confirms the presence of papillary thyroid carcinoma in the patient's thyroid gland, with involvement of the left lobe, isthmus, and lymph nodes in the neck levels 2, 3, and 4/6. There was also extrathyroidal extension and metastasis to several lymph nodes. A benign parathyroid gland was identified. The report is awaiting review for BRAF mutation analysis. The report provides detailed information on the location, size, and histological type of the tumors, as well as important descriptors for staging purposes.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of papillary thyroid carcinoma, follicular variant, with a tumor size of 3.3 cm. The tumor extends to the cauterized posterior resection margin and there is evidence of venous/lymphatic invasion. The regional lymph nodes and distant metastasis could not be assessed. An additional finding of nodular goiter is noted. Immunohistochemical stains for galectin 3 and HBME were negative.
