The extent of involvement of other organs is not seen. Lymph nodes are not involved. The tumor extends to the serosal surface but not perforating it. The woman has leiomyomata, and her ovaries and fallopian tubes are not significantly abnormal. The tumor is staged as pT1d Nx (FIGO 1).

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial cancer in a postmenopausal patient who underwent laparoscopic total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and pelvic lymph node dissection. The lymph nodes examined were negative for metastatic carcinoma. The primary tumor was well-differentiated endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, FIGO grade 1, with focal mucinous features. The tumor size was 3.5 cm and involved greater than 90% of the anterior and posterior endometrial cavity but invaded less than 50% of the myometrial thickness. No lymphovascular space invasion was seen, and there was no lymph node involvement. The report includes information on histologic grade, tumor size, depth of invasion, and lymph node involvement, and provides FIGO staging information.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial adenocarcinoma with FIGO grade 2 (of 3) in an 8.2 x 4.5 x 1.4 cm mass that involves the entire endometrial cavity, superficially invading the myometrium and deeply invading 1.4 cm into the endocervix with identified lymphovascular space invasion. Multiple leiomyomata are also identified. No tumor involvement is found in the bilateral ovaries, lymph nodes, or gonadal vessels. It is classified as AJCC pT2NO stage (7th edition, 2010). Frozen section consultation confirm the same and all lymph nodes are negative for tumor. The gross description includes an intact uterus with bilateral fallopian tubes and ovaries weighing 390.0 grams with no notable abnormalities.

The report describes a specimen received from a surgery to remove the uterus, cervix, ovaries, tubes, bilateral parametria, and upper vagina due to endometrial cancer. The gross description notes the presence of a tumor in the cervical canal and endometrial cavity, involving greater than 75% of the myometrium. The left ovary shows a cystic appearance with debris and no visible tubercle. The report also details the recovery of lymph nodes from the right pelvic area and right periaortic area, which are submitted in multiple blocks for further examination. No impressions about malignancy or staging are given in the report.

The pathology report indicates that there is a well-differentiated endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type with mucinous differentiation, located in the uterus. There was no cervical, vaginal, or adnexal involvement, and no invasion of contiguous structures. Lymphovascular and perineural invasions were not identified, and resection margins were free of carcinoma. There were 35 lymph nodes free of metastatic tumor. The report also notes moderate to severe squamous dysplasia and myometrial adenomyosis and leiomyoma. The right and left fallopian tubes and ovaries were grossly normal. The left pelvic lymph nodes and right caval lymph nodes were free of metastatic tumor. A small fragment from the right aortic lymph nodes contained no lymphoid tissue. The report concludes that the postoperative diagnosis is the same as the clinical diagnosis of endometrial cancer with pelvic organ prolapse.

The pathology report shows that the patient had surgery to remove the uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries, and omentum. The report indicates that the patient has high-grade serous carcinoma of the endometrium, which invaded the myometrium and cervical epithelium and stroma. The report also indicates that lymphatic invasion is present but no lymph nodes were identified with carcinomatous involvement. Multiple biopsies were taken, and no carcinoma was identified in any of the samples. The tumor size was 2cm, and the myometrial thickness was 19cm. The histological type of the tumor is serous papillary adenocarcinoma, and the grade is high. The report includes a detailed gross description with measurements and labels for the different specimens that were examined.

The pathology report describes the collection and analysis of various samples, including frozen tumor and blood samples. The final diagnosis of the resected tumor is well-differentiated adenocarcinoma (endometrioid type, FIGO grade 1) confined to the endometrium, with no evidence of invasion or lymphovascular invasion. Other findings include adenomyosis, leiomyomas, and benign tissue in the uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, and ovaries. Lymph nodes excised from various areas are all benign, except for one benign lymph node in the left aortic lymph nodes and two benign lymph nodes in the right aortic lymph nodes.

The report describes a surgical pathology exam of the patient's uterus, ovaries, and lymph nodes. The uterus and cervix were removed due to high-grade adenocarcinoma, with invasion of the myometrium and lower uterine segment, as well as vascular space invasion. The left fallopian tube was involved with high-grade papillary serous carcinoma, likely metastasized from the endometrial primary. The right ovary had evidence of malignancy, but no malignancy was identified in other lymph nodes or organs examined. The report does not provide any personal or medical history of the patient.

The pathology report identifies no malignancy in the peritoneal biopsy, omentum #1, omentum #2, left adnexa (except for serosal adhesions), and left periaortic lymph node. However, the report diagnoses primary endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type with myometrial invasion and lymphovascular invasion in the hysterectomy sample. The report also notes an organizing hemorrhage in the cul-de-sac and reactive mesothelial changes and organizing hemorrhage in the right uterosacral tissue. Additional findings include a calcified leiomyoma and an ovary with a benign surface epithelial inclusion cyst. The report indicates no metastatic carcinoma identified in the right pelvic lymph nodes, but the tumor may behave aggressively due to the extent of myometrial invasion and angiolymphatic invasion.

The pathology report describes the findings of a patient with endometrial cancer who underwent surgery (hysterectomy). The right and left tubes and ovaries showed acute salpingitis but were free of tumor. The uterus and cervix showed a well-differentiated endometrioid type of endometrial adenocarcinoma, with possible myometrial invasion identified grossly and confirmed microscopically. Lymphovascular invasion was not identified, and resection margins were free of involvement. No lymph node involvement was seen. Adenomyosis was also noted in the specimen. Frozen section interpretation suggested possible myometrial invasion.  The report documented the size and location of the tumor and other tissue measurements. Representative sections were submitted for further analysis.

The pathology report describes the findings of a hysterectomy and excision of ovaries, fallopian tubes, lymph nodes, and omentum. The left and right ovaries and fallopian tubes show corpora albicantia and serous cysts, with the presence of benign paratubal cysts on the right side. The uterus reveals a mixed pattern carcinoma with endometrioid and serous components, predominantly serous, with a histologic grade of 3, measuring 9.5 x 7.5 cm, and invading 1.7 cm into the myometrium. Lymphovascular space invasion is not identified, and margins are uninvolved. Common lymph nodes on the left and right sides show some metastatic carcinoma, while the left obturator lymph nodes reveal seven out of seven lymph nodes with positive metastasis, and the right obturator lymph nodes show one out of five lymph nodes with positive metastasis. The omentum is negative for malignancy. Appropriate immunohistochemical stains show majority of lesional cells positive for p53 and estrogen receptor, consistent with serous carcinoma. Overall, the diagnosis is mixed pattern carcinoma with serous components and lymph node metastasis.

The report describes a case of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, FIGO grade 3, in a patient who underwent a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The tumor measured 6.0 x 3.5 x 2.2 cm and invaded 1.7 cm into the myometrium, but did not involve the endocervix. Lymphovascular space invasion was identified, but there was no involvement of the bilateral ovaries, fallopian tubes, or lymph nodes (both pelvic and para-aortic, with a total of 33 lymph nodes examined). Multiple intramural leiomyomas were identified. The report notes that this is based on gross and microscopic examination, and any changes found on permanent section review will be reflected in a revised report.

The pathology report suggests that the patient underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy to remove the tumor from the endometrium. The tumor was found to be an adenocarcinoma with poor differentiation and extent greater than half the myometrium. The lymph nodes, lymphatic invasion, and venous invasion were not specified. The report confirms the absence of neo-adjuvant treatment and additional pathologic findings. The comment suggests that it is a grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma.

The pathology report states that the patient underwent a bilateral oophorectomy and hysterectomy. The report includes measurements and descriptions of the uterus, cervix, ovaries, and fallopian tubes, noting the presence of endometrial adenocarcinoma with no definitive invasion seen. The report also mentions the absence of carcinoma in several lymph nodes. A tumor was identified in the endometrium with the deepest invasion, and there were four identified growths in the specimen received. The report concludes by stating that an intraoperative consultation was conducted and the case was reviewed with another pathologist.

The pathology report describes the results of various biopsies and resections from different parts of the body. There is no evidence of metastatic carcinoma in any of the samples, except for the uterus which has a primary uterine carcinoma of adenosquamous type with myometrial invasion and lymphovascular invasion. The report also describes chronic inflammation, adhesions, reactive mesothelial changes, and benign findings in other soft tissue samples. Two lymph nodes showed extensive fibrosis and calcifications without metastatic carcinoma.

The pathology report reveals that the patient had endometrioid adenocarcinoma with spindle cell metaplasia in the endometrium, with myometrial invasion of the inner half and a depth of 3 mm. The tumor was found in the lower uterine segment but without stromal invasion in the cervical region or adnexa. There was no Lymphovascular Space Invasion (LVSI) and no lymph node involvement. The hormone receptor status was ER and PR positive (2-3+, 30%). The pathologic stage was pT1b pNO pMx with overall FIGO grade 3, based on architectural grade 2 and nuclear grade 3.  Other findings include an atrophic endometrial polyp and vascular calcifications in the myometrium. There were no significant pathologic abnormalities found in the ovaries or fallopian tubes.

The pathology report indicates that there is metastatic adenocarcinoma in the mesentery and anterior uterine serosa, with a larger tumor in the uterus that is identified as endometrial adenocarcinoma, serous type. Lymphovascular space invasion is not identified. Multiple lymph nodes in the left and right pelvic areas and para-aortic area are negative for tumor. Additionally, there is endosalpingiosis in the cul de sac, and endometriosis is present in the left tube and ovary. A benign epithelial cyst is found in the pyloric region, and the omentum is negative for neoplasm.

The pathology report describes the findings from a laparoscopic hysterectomy procedure performed on a patient with a pre-op diagnosis of malignant corpus. The uterus and attached cervix were removed and examined. The uterus had multiple subserosal and myometrial leiomyomas. Large, calcified, submucosal leiomyomas were found in the endometrial canal. The endometrium had a fungating lesion located primarily on the anterior side. The left and right ovaries and fallopian tubes were unremarkable. Pelvic lymph nodes were also examined and several were found with the largest measuring 3.0 x 1.0 x 0.6 cm. In an intraoperative consultation, the anterior uterine myometrium was noted to have adenocarcinoma with minimal myometrial invasion. The pathological stage was not provided in the report.

The pathology report describes the findings of a surgical procedure involving several lymph node regions, uterus and ovaries. The report reveals that the patient has a malignant condition called serous carcinoma, which is confined to a polyp within the endometrium and does not invade the myometrium. The lymph nodes that were examined all tested negative for tumor involvement except for one that was inconclusive. The ovaries showed an atrophic pattern, and the fallopian tubes were unremarkable. Some non-cancerous conditions were also noted. The report includes details about the specimen sizes, gross descriptions, and microscopic findings.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a surgical procedure for high-grade serous carcinoma, which involved the lower uterine segment and invaded the myometrial and lymphovascular spaces. There was also evidence of metastasis to lymph nodes in various areas, including the right external iliac, obturator, periaortic, and left external iliac regions. The ovaries and fallopian tubes showed no histopathological abnormality, and the omentum appeared normal. The report also includes details on the size and appearance of the various tissue samples and lymph nodes removed during the procedure.

The pathology report describes a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with node dissection for a malignant neoplasm in the corpus uteri. There is a mass at the fundus of the uterus extending into the anterior and posterior endometrium with full-thickness involvement of the anterior endometrium. There are also several cysts in the endometrium. The pathology stage is not specified, but multiple lymph node candidates are identified in the pelvic area and dissected for examination. An intraoperative consultation identifies adenocarcinoma consistent with invasion. Some tissue samples are sent for decalcification.

The surgery performed was a TAH-BSO with staging on a patient with endometrial adenocarcinoma, grade 1. The tumor was found in the uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes, and ovaries, but did not invade more than 50% of the myometrium and did not affect nearby structures or margins. Pelvic and aortic lymph nodes were also examined and showed no signs of metastasis. Three well-circumscribed myomas were also identified. Further testing is pending.

The pathology report describes the findings from a surgical procedure on an individual with a history of endometrial cancer. The report details the presence of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, grade 3, and extensive lymphatic invasion in the uterus and cervix. Metastatic endometrioid carcinoma was found in multiple lymph nodes, including the right par-aortic, right pelvic, left pelvic, IMA, cephalad IMA, and left PA lymph nodes. Mucinous neoplasm of borderline malignancy was identified in the appendix, and a tubular adenoma was found in the right colon's distal ileum. The report notes the presence of squamous metaplasia and clear cell change in the tumor. No tumor involvement was identified in the ovaries or fallopian tubes.

The pathology report describes a biopsy of the falciform ligament and resection of the omentum, both of which were negative for carcinoma. However, a salpingo-oophorectomy revealed a high-grade papillary serous carcinoma with clear cell carcinoma involving the right ovary and fallopian tube, as well as the left pelvic lymph node and paraaortic lymph nodes. There was also mixed papillary serous carcinoma and focal clear cell carcinoma involving the endocervix and vaginal cuff. There was lymphovascular invasion and involvement of leiomyomas by the cancer. The report suggests that it is difficult to establish the primary site, but it may originate from the endometrium. The report also mentions a small focal high-grade serous papillary carcinoma adjacent to the wall of the right gonadal vessel. Margins of the cervical and vaginal cuff were inked black.

The pathology report describes a 106-gram uterus with a 4.5x3.3x0.4 cm endometrioid adenocarcinoma primarily located in the posterior corpus, with no myometrial invasion and negative lymphatic/vascular invasion. Adjacent non-neoplastic endometrial polyps and atrophy are present. The cervix and serosa are not involved, and the specimen margins are not involved. The report also notes a smooth and intact right fallopian tube and ovary, and adhesions and a convoluting corpus luteum in the left fallopian tube and ovary. There is no information on any specimens submitted separately.

The pathology report indicates the presence of endometrial adenocarcinoma with invasion up to 50% of the myometrium. There is also involvement of the lower urinary segment and post-op evaluation is needed for potential involvement of the colon. Lymph nodes on both sides appear negative for carcinoma. Multiple sections of the uterus, ovaries, and fallopian tubes were submitted for analysis, as well as lymph nodes from both the right and left sides. Additional blocks were also taken from several structures.

The pathology report describes a surgical specimen of the uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes and ovaries taken from a patient with a pre-op diagnosis of endometrial cancer. The report confirms that there is endometrioid adenocarcinoma, grade 2, present in the uterus with a depth of invasion of 17% through the myometrial wall. The cervix is not involved in the cancer, and the margins of resection are clear. The report also confirms that there is no evidence of metastasis in any of the pelvic or periaortic lymph nodes sampled. The ovaries and fallopian tubes are uninvolved in the cancer.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrial cancer. The cancer was determined to be endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FLGO grade 1, and had invaded 60% of the syncytial wall. The lymph nodes removed during the surgery were negative for cancer. The report also notes the presence of adenomyosis and leiomyoma. Additional testing was ordered on block AFSI. The gross description outlines the size and structures of the uterus, ovaries, and fallopian tubes, as well as any lesions or abnormalities identified during the surgery. Several lymph nodes were also removed and examined.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had endometrial adenocarcinoma with grade 3 and nuclear grade 3. There was less than 60% invasion, and no lymphovascular invasion was identified. The tumor was present in the uterus, cervix, tubes, and ovaries. The right gutter implant, left pelvic lymph node, left aortic lymph node, and right pelvic lymph node were free of tumor. The right caval lymph nodes had two lymph nodes negative for metastasis. The patient had adenomyosis. The staging information revealed T2a, NO with no neural extension. Eighteen lymph nodes were negative for metastasis, and one lymph node was negative for metastasis. Representative sections, blocks B1-B13 were taken from the uterus and cervix. Blocks G1-C8 were taken from the left pelvic lymph node. Blocks D1-D2 were taken from the left aortic lymph node. The right pelvic lymph node had several pink-tan rubbery lymphoid nodules.

The surgical pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and a biopsy of the right external iliac lymph node. The uterus was diagnosed with a stage 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma with areas of squamous differentiation, while the right ovary had a separate 3cm adenocarcinoma. The lymph node biopsy revealed metastatic adenocarcinoma. The tumor invaded the myometrium and lower uterine segment, as well as the endocervical mucosa and lymphovascular space. The report also lists the tumor size, histopathologic type, FIGO grade, and other details. Further tests were pending.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a hysterectomy and salpingo-oophorectomy due to high grade carcinoma in the uterus, predominantly papillary serous carcinoma of the endometrium with focal areas of endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma. Papillary serous carcinoma was also found in the cervix. There were no tumors detected in the lymph nodes or surrounding tissues, although there was fibrosis and inflammation observed in some areas. Leiomyoma was found in the myometrium. No tumors were observed in the bilateral tubes and ovaries or in the omental biopsies. Fibroconnective tissue was found in the bladder peritoneum, anterior abdominal wall peritoneum, and cul-de-sac peritoneum, but there were no tumors present.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy specimen with a malignant neoplasm of the corpus uteri. The endometrium shows a well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma limited to the endometrium. Nodular masses are present in the myometrium, cervix, subserosa, left ovary, and fallopian tubes. The report also describes unremarkable lymph nodes and an immunohistochemical stain of the left ovarian nodule that supports a diagnosis of a hilus cell tumor.

The patient's uterus was removed and found to have a grade 1 endometrial adenocarcinoma, of the endometrioid and villoglandular type. The tumor was 2.5 x 2.0 x 0.7 cm in size and invaded 0.6 cm into the myometrium but did not involve lymphovascular spaces or the endocervix. The margins were negative for tumor. No abnormalities were seen in the left fallopian tube or left ovary. The right ovary and fallopian tube were also normal. A total of 34 lymph nodes were removed and none showed any evidence of cancer. Permanent sections will be reviewed for any substantive changes.

The pathology report describes the results of a surgical pathology report for a patient who had a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to adenocarcinoma in the lower uterine segment. The tumor invaded to a depth of 8mm and had focal lymphovascular invasion. The report also included a gross description of the specimen, which included a 280-gram uterus with attached cervix and bilateral adnexa, as well as normal ovaries and fallopian tubes. The malignant histologic diagnosis was adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type (FIGO grade 1) and serous type. The report notes involvement of the lower uterine segment, the endocervix, and lymphovascular space invasion.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrioid adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation in a patient who underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Lymph nodes were examined and found to be negative for carcinoma, except for one lymph node in the left internal iliac group. The report notes invasion of the myometrium by the carcinoma limited to the inner half, glandular involvement by endometrial adenocarcinoma in the cervix, and the presence of epithelial inclusion cysts and a paratubal cyst. The report also mentions a background of complex hyperplasia with atypia. The report does not indicate the stage of the cancer.

The report describes a surgical pathology report for a patient who underwent da Vinci hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with node biopsy. The report includes information about the size and location of various tissues and organs, as well as details about any tumors or abnormalities observed during the procedure. Specifically, the report notes the presence of a 1.5 cm. papillary, bulky, friable tumor in the right anterior and posterior endometrium that seems to track along the isthmus, but no unequivocal myometrial invasion is seen. The report also includes slide keys for various submitted samples. Tissue was submitted for research as requested.

The pathology report indicates that a hysterectomy was performed and the patient was diagnosed with endometrioid adenocarcinoma, a moderately differentiated tumor that has invaded more than half the thickness of the myometrium and involves approximately 50% of the endometrial cavity. There is also evidence of complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia, leiomyoma, and lymphovascular invasion. The pelvic and periaortic lymph nodes were negative for metastatic carcinoma. The final stage of the cancer is determined to be Ic.

The pathology report describes the findings of a surgical procedure that included removal of the right fallopian tube and ovary, which showed a benign serous cystadenoma in the ovary. The report also describes a hysterectomy conducted due to endometrial cancer, with the tumor being limited to the endometrium and no myometrial invasion identified. The tumor is diagnosed as endometrioid adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation, with a histologic grade of 1. No lymphovascular space invasion, serosal, or cervical involvement was identified. Lymph nodes removed showed no carcinoma in 0/37 examined. Other pathologic findings included benign endocervical polyp, adenomyosis, and endometriosis in other specimens. The report notes that information is pending regarding the tumor's estrogen and progesterone receptor immunohistochemistry, and further stages may change pending additional information and clinical review.

The pathology report describes a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy performed on a patient with uterine cancer and hepatitis B. The report shows that the patient had an endometrial adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type, grade 2, with tumor invasion present in 11% of the myometrial thickness. The report also describes adenomyosis and fibrous adhesions. Additionally, the report details the findings of lymph nodes excised from various locations, with no evidence of tumor involvement. The left ovary has a serous cyst, but no papillary excrescences were identified. The report also includes microscopic and gross descriptions of the uterus, cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes, and ovaries, including the tumor size and location. The report concludes with no evidence of regional lymph node metastasis.

The pathology report describes the results of biopsies and hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy of a patient with a pelvic mass. The report indicates the presence of metastatic high-grade Mullerian carcinoma in several lymph nodes, involving most of the endometrium and invading more than 50% of myometrium in the uterus, and benign findings in other organs examined. The report also notes the presence of neoplastic epithelium on the mucosal surface of the lower uterine segment and endocervix, which is likely artefactually displaced epithelium and not true involvement by the tumor. Lymphovascular invasion is also present. The report provides details of the macroscopic and microscopic findings and synoptic report. Pathologic staging indicates pTb and pN1. No involvement of other organs is noted. The report was ordered by a pathologist and received by an assistant.

The pathology report is for a 1-year-old female with endometrial adenocarcinoma. The report shows that there is invasive endometrial carcinoma, endometrioid type, with a grade 3 FIGO and nuclear grade 3. The report also states that there is no evidence of malignancy in lymph nodes. The tumor size is 5.2 cm with no evidence of myometal invasion. There was no endocervical involvement or other organ involvement. The report also includes other details such as histologic type, myometrial invasion, peritoneal ascitic fluid, margin, lymphovascular invasion, and pathologic staging. Prognostic markers were ordered for addendum image analysis report, and further information regarding the patient's clinical status and/or prior pathology should be reviewed before determining the final diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy performed for a FIGO grade I endometrioid adenocarcinoma that measures 3.4 x 2.4 x 1.0 cm and has invaded the myometrium to a depth of 1.0 cm. There is also a single leiomyoma present in the myometrium. Bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy shows no diagnostic abnormality, and multiple lymph nodes removed from various regions are negative for tumor.

The pathology report reveals the following findings:

(A) Omentum biopsy: Adipose tissue with suture granulomas and adhesions, no tumor present.

(B) Left ovary and fallopian tube: Fallopian tube with chronic inflammation, ovary with hemorrhagic cysts and multiple follicular cysts.

(C) Uterus: Multiple foci of endometrial endometrioid adenocarcinoma with superficial myometrial invasion and extension to the lower uterine segment. Background of extensive complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. Tumor extends into areas of adenomyosis. Uterine cervix, no tumor present.

Additional omentum: Adipose tissue with adhesions, no tumor present.

The clinical history is not provided.

The pathology report indicates that a 50-year-old female had uterine papillary serous carcinoma with myometrial invasion. A hysterectomy and bilateral salpingooophorectomy were performed. The tumor was 4.4 cm in size and involved the lower uterine segment. The cervix and parametrium were negative for malignancy, and the ovaries and fallopian tubes were negative for malignancy. Left pelvic lymph nodes and periaortic lymph nodes tested negative for malignancy, except for one lymph node in the right pelvic that tested positive for metastatic adenocarcinoma. The final diagnosis was serous adenocarcinoma of endometrium with a pTNM of pT1bNIMx. The left periaortic lymph node was negative for malignancy in adipose tissue and had no identified lymphoid tissue. A portion of omentum biopsy and representative sections of different areas were submitted for further testing.

The report states that the patient underwent a hysterectomy which showed the presence of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with a myometrial invasion of 0.2 cm. The tumor formed a polypoid mass at the left cornu and there was no invasion of lymphovascular space. The cervix is unremarkable. The left ovary had a fibroma and the right ovary was atrophic. Both fallopian tubes were unremarkable.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had metastatic adenocarcinoma consistent with endometrial primary cancer. The cancer affected various organs, including the bladder peritoneum, uterus, bilateral ovaries, and fallopian tubes. The tumor invaded 1.1 cm into the myometrium and showed angiolymphatic invasion. The left ovary had a large mass, while the right ovary had a microscopic focus of metastatic endometrial adenocarcinoma. The lymph nodes in the pelvis and para-aortic region were negative for tumor. The omentum was negative for tumor. The final pathology report was based on macroscopic examination and frozen section histologic evaluation of the specimens.

The pathology report describes a patient with endometrial cancer who underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and lymph node dissection. The report confirms the diagnosis of endometrial carcinoma with moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma and invasion of the lymphovascular space in the myometrium. The cancer is confined to the endometrium and there is no evidence of tumor in the ovaries, cervix, or lymph nodes. The pathological stage is pT1bN0. There are no grossly identifiable lesions seen in the abdomen. The report provides a description of the gross and microscopic findings of the excised tissues. Immune markers show high expression of p16 and p53, while estrogen receptors are weakly expressed. Overall, the immunoprofile is consistent with moderately differentiated endometrial carcinoma.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent hysterectomy due to primary endometrial cancer. The cancer is of the endometrioid adenocarcinoma type, with an overall FIGO grade 3 (architectural grade 3, nuclear grade 2-3). The tumor has invaded into the deep outer half and lower uterine segment, but has not extended through the serosal surface. Lymphovascular Space Invasion is also present. Adenomyosis and endometrial polyp are other pathologic findings. The patient's estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor immunohistochemistry results are pending. The right and left fallopian tubes, right and left ovaries, and lymph nodes have no tumor identified, and the patient's clinical history is of endometrial cancer.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy with removal of lymph nodes and ovaries in a female patient. The lymph nodes removed showed no signs of carcinoma. The uterus showed endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a grade of 3/3 and invasion into the outer third of the myometrium. Lymphatic space invasion was also present. Leiomyomata uteri and adenomyosis were also seen. The cervix and fallopian tubes showed no abnormalities. The left ovary showed serous cyst adenofibroma and cystic mesothelial adhesion. The right ovary showed bilateral surface papillary stromal hyperplasia. The adenocarcinoma was of architectural grade IV but had high-grade nuclear atypia (grade II) and a focal area of P53 positivity. The report also provides the pathologic staging and confirmation of the absence of distant metastasis and regional lymph node involvement.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the uterus with involvement of the cervix and inner half of the myometrium. Lymphovascular space invasion was present, but no regional lymph node metastasis was found. The tumor had both tubuloglandular and solid patterns, with the solid component showing high-grade cytologic atypia and undifferentiated appearance. Immunohistochemistry staining was positive for estrogen receptor and focally for progesterone receptor in the glandular areas and negative in the solid component. P53, synaptophysin, and chromogranin markers were negative. No tumor was found in the ovaries, but chronic salpingitis was present in the left fallopian tube. Adenomyosis and leiomyoma were also noted.

The pathology report indicates that specimens were submitted for a bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The report identifies a clear cell carcinoma in one of the ovaries, endometrial cancer in the uterus, and complex hyperplasia with atypia in the uterus. Additionally, multiple lymph nodes were removed, all of which were benign. The report confirms that the diagnosis is based on the reviewer's interpretation of the submitted materials and that they have reviewed and approved the results.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial adenocarcinoma, which has invaded the myometrial tissue up to a depth of 0.3 cm and has involved stroma of the lower uterine segment. The cervix has squamous metaplasia. Fibrous adhesions are observed in both ovaries and periovarian tissue but no malignancy is detected in any of the lymph nodes examined. The gross examination shows a polypoid endometrial mass on the posterior uterine wall, extending up to the endocervix and lateral anterior uterine walls. Bilateral fallopian tubes appear sclerosed and adhesed with the surrounding tissue, likely due to a previous procedure. Tumor and normal tissue are taken for a tumor bank, and the remaining samples are fixed in formalin for permanent storage.

The pathology report describes the results of a radical hysterectomy for a patient with endometrial adenocarcinoma. The tumor is grade 3 and has invaded half of the myometrium. Lymph nodes were negative for metastasis. Other findings include benign cysts in the ovaries and myomatous changes in the myometrium. No dysplasia or malignancy was found in the cervical tissue. The report notes the presence of hyperplastic endometrial polyps and squamous metaplasia. The report also mentions a separate submission for genomic research study.

The pathology report shows the presence of endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the uterus, which has invaded one centimeter into the myometrium. There is no lymphatic or vascular invasion, and the adjacent non-neoplastic endometrium is atrophic. The cervix and serosa show no pathological diagnosis. The report also includes information on the lymph nodes examined and the operations conducted. The patient is diagnosed with PT1b pNO pax stage adenocarcinoma.

The pathology report describes the examination of a 210 gram uterus, bilateral tubes, and ovaries received for frozen section. The report notes the presence of an endometrial adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation and FIGO grade I, originating from the lower anterior wall of the uterus and measuring 3.5 x 2.2 cm. There is no evidence of myometrial invasion or lymphatic/vascular invasion but there is adenomyosis in the remaining myometrium. The cervix and serosa are negative for tumor, and the specimen margins are not involved. Six lymph nodes from the right pelvic region and six from the left were also examined and found to be negative for carcinoma. The report concludes that the overall pathological stage is pIa pNO PMX.

This is a pathology report from a patient who underwent a hysterectomy along with removal and examination of multiple organs, including cysts and lymph nodes. Diagnosis of a benign cyst and follicular cysts was found in the right and left adnexa, respectively, with no tumor seen. Endometrial cancer was present in the uterus with myometrial invasion and lymphatic invasion, but negative margins and negative lymph nodes. There were also reactive lymph nodes in the left and right external iliac lymph nodes and para-aortic lymph node. The report notes additional sections may be submitted to identify additional lymph nodes. No clinical history was provided.

The pathology report describes the findings from a total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy procedure. The diagnosis was endometroid adenocarcinoma, NOS, with well-differentiated (FIGO 1) histologic and nuclear grades. The tumor measured 3.5 cm and invades 40% of the anterior and posterior endomyometrium with less than half the thickness of myometrium. There was no angiolympathic invasion, but complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia and adenomyosis were present. No lymph nodes were examined, and the pathological staging was recorded as pTib, BNx, and MX, with a FIGO stage of 8.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, with the diagnosis of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, FIGO grade 1 (of 3) identified in a 3.5 x 3.0 x 1.0 cm mass in the uterine fundus. The tumor invades 0.6 cm into the myometrium with no involvement of the endocervix. The background endometrium shows complex hyperplasia with atypia. The vaginal cuff margin is negative for tumor. Multiple left pelvic lymph nodes were negative for tumor. The report also notes the presence of multiple intramural leiomyomas and normal bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes.

The pathology report indicates that a 50-year-old female had undergone a robotic hysterectomy for endometrial cancer. The report states that there was no tumor identified in lymph nodes, and the uterus and cervix had endometrioid adenocarcinoma with focal squamous differentiation, with extensive invasion into the inner half of the myometrium. No involvement was detected in adnexal, lower uterine segment, or cervical areas. The report also mentions benign endometrial polyp, atrophic endometrium, Nabothian cysts, and leiomyomas in findings. The report concludes that the cancer is in Stage IA, Grade 3, and is subject to change with additional clinical review. The ovaries and fallopian tubes were benign, and no tumor was found in any of the lymph nodes examined.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has cervical cancer that has spread to various parts of the reproductive system, with surgical invasion and metastasis to lymph nodes in various areas including the iliac and para-aortic regions. The report indicates the presence of metastatic carcinoma in multiple lymph nodes. The report was reviewed and approved by Jed.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy specimen with a malignant neoplasm affecting the corpus uteri. The report details the dimensions of the uterus and the presence of a 3.4 cm exophytic, soft, friable mass on the anterior and posterior wall, invading 3 mm into the myometrium. The report also describes the appearance of the ovaries and fallopian tubes. Several lymph node candidates were identified in the left pelvic lymph node and 20 in the right pelvic lymph node. The report includes microscopic examination and a diagnosis of endometrioid carcinoma, Figo grade 3, invading 3 mm into the 15 mm wall. The pathological stage of the disease is pTib pNO pax.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, revealing serous carcinoma of the endometrium involving the anterior and posterior endomyometrium with extensive lymph-vascular space invasion present. The tumor size cannot be determined, but it invades 25 mm of 27 mm of myometrial thickness and extends to the lower uterine segment. There are also leiomyomata present and unremarkable uterine serosa. No tumor is present in the uterine cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes, or ovaries. There is metastatic carcinoma involving two of ten lymph nodes in the right pelvic and no tumor present in other lymph nodes or fibroadipose tissue resections. The report provides a pathologic staging of Stage IB1C1 with pT1b primary tumor and regional lymph node metastasis to pelvic lymph nodes. The report also indicates that immunohistochemistry was performed and showed the tumor's diffuse positivity with AE1/AE3, diffuse staining for p53 and p16, and no staining for BR, consistent with the diagnosis. The patient is described as being a  year old with endometrial carcinoma/postmenopausal bleeding. A tumor sample is submitted for further analysis.

The pathology report describes various specimens taken from the patient's reproductive system. The right ovary and fallopian tube were negative for malignancy. The left ovary had fibrous adhesions but no malignant findings. The uterus contained a 4.5 x 2.5 cm endometrial cavity lined by poorly differentiated carcinoma of endometrium that invaded the inner half of the myometrium but had negative surface and stromal invasion. The cervix#1 had an endometrioma and multiple cysts but was negative for malignancy, while cervix#2 had a 2.2 x 1.0 x 0 cm pedunculated leiomyoma but was also negative for malignancy. The report also notes the presence of adenomyosis and leiomyomas in the myometrium.

The pathology report describes findings from a surgical pathology exam of a patient who underwent a panniculectomy and a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The report includes information on the weight and characteristics of the tissue removed, as well as a diagnosis of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, that formed a 3.2 x 2.9 x 1.0 cm polypoid mass in the posterior uterine wall. The tumor had invaded 0.3 cm into the myometrium, but did not involve the endocervix. The report also notes the presence of a single intramural leiomyoma and adenomyosis, but no involvement of the bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes. Multiple lymph nodes were examined and found to be negative for tumor. The report concludes with a note that additional permanent section review may result in a revised report.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a glandular adenocarcinoma in the nose with one primary lesion. There is also involvement of the left lymph node. Further information about the size, extent, and grade of the tumor is not provided.

The pathology report confirms the pre-operative diagnosis of endometrial cancer. The tumor is a poorly differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a combined architectural and nuclear grade of 2. It measures 2.0 cm in its maximum dimension and involves 10% of the anterior endomyometrium and 30% of the posterior endomyometrium. The depth of myometrial invasion is less than 12 mm, and angiolymphatic invasion is present. Lymph node examination indicates no positive nodes. The final pathologic stage is T1aN0Mx (FIGO 1A classification). Immunochemical stains were performed for evaluation purposes. P16 is patchy positive, and P53 and 263 are negative. CD34, CK7, and D2-40 are positive in endothelial, lymphatic, and vascular channels. The report recommends additional clinical testing and follow-up.

The pathology report describes a case of high grade endometrioid adenocarcinoma in a patient with endometrial cancer. The report indicates involvement of the omentum, pelvic gutter, and bowel serosa by the cancer. The uterus and cervix were also affected, with the tumor located in the uterine fundus and invading the myometrium. The report notes no involvement of regional lymph nodes or adnexa. Other findings include chronic cervicitis, atrophic endometrium, and the presence of epithelial inclusion cysts in both ovaries. The tumor was positive for estrogen and progesterone receptor immunohistochemistry, had solid and cribriform growth patterns, and showed enlarged nuclei with prominent nucleoli and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. The cancer was classified as pT1b pNx pM21, corresponding to FIGO stage IVB. Surgical resection margins were free of tumor.

The pathology report describes the presence of endometrial adenocarcinoma in a polypoid form in the patient's uterus. The cancer is classified as FIGO grade 2 and there is evidence of very superficial myometrial invasion. The report mentions no pathological diagnosis for both ovaries and uterine tubes, and negative results for malignancy in paranetrium. A tumor sample was examined histologically, and MST testing was ordered. The clinical information states that the patient originally underwent biopsy for grade 1 endometrial adenocarcinoma with an ASCUS Pap.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy specimen from a patient with a FIGO 1 endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma and endometriosis. The gross examination showed a 3.1 x 2.1cm area of heaped-up endometrium in the myometrium, along with five firm, white, whorled nodules up to 1.7cm and a whorled submucosal nodule in the cervix. The report also notes adhesions and chocolate cysts in the adnexa and on the posterior surface of the uterus, with no definitive right ovary identified. Microscopic examination confirmed the diagnosis of endometrioid adenocarcinoma invading 2.6mm into the myometrium. Lymph nodes were also dissected for examination.

The pathology report describes the examination of tissue samples from a patient with endometrial cancer. The report includes findings from the left tube and ovary, uterus and cervix, a hernia sac, and left and right pelvic nodes. The left tube and ovary had a Leydig cell tumor with associated hilar cell hyperplasia and no evidence of carcinoma. The uterus and cervix had endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium in the posterior fundus with no myometrial invasion, absent lymphatic/vascular invasion, adjacent non-neoplastic endometrium showing atrophy, and letomyomata in the surrounding myometrium. The cervix was free of tumor, as was the serosa. The hernia sac showed no evidence of malignancy, and the right tube and ovary had simple paratubal cysts with no evidence of malignancy. The left pelvic nodes had no evidence of malignancy (0/6), and the right pelvic nodes had no evidence of malignancy (0/4).

The pathology report describes the examination of a specimen comprising the uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes, ovaries, left and right pelvic lymph nodes, and periaortic lymph node, with a pre-operative diagnosis of endometrial cancer. Gross examination reveals a 6 x 4.8 cm endometrial cavity containing fragmented pale-tan tumor, originating from the posterior wall, invading through 50% or more of the myometrial wall. Histologically, the tumor is an endometrioid adenocarcinoma with foci of squamous differentiation, classified as FIGO grade 2. Although the tumor involves the lower uterine segment posteriorly, it does not invade the cervix. Lymph nodes from the pelvic and periaortic regions are also examined and noted to have similar-appearing tissue and lymph nodes up to 4-4.5 cm in greatest dimension. All nodes submitted are negative for metastasis.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with a FIGO grade II (of III) identified forming a mass in the posterior uterine wall. The tumor invades 0.1 cm into the myometrium, with a total wall thickness of 2.2cm. The tumor does not involve the endocervix or cervix. Lymphovascular space invasion is not identified. The margins are negative for the tumor. The case involves a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, with unremarkable findings for the cervix, bilateral ovaries, fallopian tubes, and appendix. Multiple pelvic lymph nodes are negative for tumor.

The pathology report describes multiple specimens submitted from the uterus, ovaries, and lymph nodes. There is a finding of a fibrous tumor with calcifications and focal endosalpingiosis, as well as separate pockets of adenocarcinoma in the uterus and ovaries. The adenocarcinoma has aggressive features and is identified as a grade III tumor. There is invasion into the myometrium and surrounding tissues. However, lymph node involvement is limited. The report recommends further treatment and observation.

The pathology report describes a case of moderately differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the uterus and cervix of a patient with endometrial carcinoma. The tumor is based in the high endocervical canal and has extended to the lower uterine segment. The report notes invasion of the anterior endocervix and extensive stromal invasion of the cervix. There is no adnexal involvement, and the patient's lymph nodes appear to be unaffected. The report also includes clinical history and gross descriptions of the specimens received. Clinical correlation is advised, as it is unclear whether the tumor is a residual effect of previous therapy or a distinct primary endocervical tumor. The tumor is negative for estrogen and progesterone receptors, but positive for p16, although the significance of this finding with endometrioid histology is unclear. The pathology stage is classified as pT2b pNx pMx and FIGO stage IIB.

The pathology report indicates the presence of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, of FIGO grade I, in the uterus with a background of polypoid atypical hyperplasia. The adenocarcinoma is limited to the endometrium with no myometrial invasion, and there is no lymph-vascular space involvement. The report also mentions adenomyosis in the myometrium and unremarkable findings in the cervix, ovaries, fallopian tubes, and appendix.

The pathology report describes the diagnosis of a poorly differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the patient's uterus with involvement of the lower uterine segment and endocervical glands but no evidence of cervical stromal invasion. The maximum depth of invasion is 1.2 cm from the total thickness of 1.5 cm. The report also notes foci of adenomyosis and endometriosis in the left ovary. No evidence of malignancy is found in the bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy specimens and lymph nodes. The patient had undergone a total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node dissection.

The pathology report describes a surgical specimen inquiry of a female patient with adenocarcinoma in the uterus, tubes, and ovaries. The right and left parametrium showed no evidence of malignancy, but a single reactive lymph node was found in the right pelvic lymph node and four reactive lymph nodes in the left pelvic lymph node. The upper vagina was also found to have adenocarcinoma. The report includes details on lymph node sampling, tumor size, histologic type and grade, myometrial invasion, involvement of the cervix and other organs, lymph-vascular invasion, pathologic staging, and additional pathologic findings. The specimen received in three parts was each evaluated and submitted for further examination. The report includes gross descriptions, including measurements of the uterus, ovaries, and fallopian tubes, lymph nodes, and lesions found in the endometrium and myometrium. The final diagnosis was pT1a for the primary tumor with no involvement in regional lymph nodes and distant metastasis. The report also noted additional pathologic findings such as cervicitis, bilateral fallopian tubes without significant histopathologic change, bilateral ovaries without significant histopathologic change, and bilateral tubal ovarian adhesions.

The pathology report describes specimens from a patient who underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrial carcinoma. The report indicates a poorly differentiated mixed-type endometrial adenocarcinoma with both endometrioid and serous carcinoma components, invading more than 50% of the myometrium and showing squamoid differentiation. Leiomyomata were also present in the myometrium, whereas the fallopian tubes showed endosalpingiosis and the ovaries were atrophic with simple cysts. The report further noted metastasis to one of the one pelvic lymph nodes excised, measuring  0.5 cm with focal extranodal expansion. The final pathological stage was pT1bN0Mx.

The report describes a surgical pathology evaluation of a 61-gram uterus and its associated structures, including the cervix and fallopian tubes. The uterus contained a 2.6 cm tan-white tumor without myometrial invasion located in the corpus, which was diagnosed as a grade 1 endometrioid adenocarcinoma with adjacent non-neoplastic hyperplastic endometrium and leiomyomas in the remaining myometrium. The fallopian tubes contained mature cystic teratomas, and there was no pathologic diagnosis of the cervix. The report includes information on the pathology stage and the operative procedure, which is transmitted to the Institution's Cancer Registry for accreditation.

The pathology report is for a tumor sample taken from the uterus of a patient with endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The sample was collected during surgical resection, and the tumor was found to be T2 stage without bilateral disease. One lymph node was positive for cancer. The patient was 5.8 years old at the time of sample collection.

The pathology report describes a case of adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon with metastasis to lymph nodes including those near the aorta and iliac regions. A total of nine lymph nodes were positive for metastasis out of 23 examined. Five benign lymph nodes were also identified. The report suggests excision of affected lymph nodes and further treatment may be necessary.

The pathology report describes a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy of a patient with endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type with villoglandular features, FIGO grade 2. The polypoid mass was 5.4 x 3.7 x 2.6 cm in size and invaded 1.3 cm into the myometrium. However, there was no lymphovascular invasion, and the cervix was uninvolved. The bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes did not show any diagnostic abnormalities. The lymph nodes in the left and right pelvic region, left and right para-aortic region, and left and right gonadal vessels were negative for tumor.

The pathology report indicates the presence of metastatic serous carcinoma in multiple lymph nodes including pre-caval, right common and external iliac lymph nodes. The report also details the findings from a surgical pathology consultation report which includes the presence of serous carcinoma in the uterus, cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes, and ovaries. The report describes myometrial invasion by the carcinoma and the involvement of lymphatic and vascular spaces. The report also notes the absence of malignancy in the omentum. The histologic grade is described as poorly differentiated G3 and the carcinoma is present in lymphatic and vascular invasion. The report concludes with TNM staging classification and additional pathological findings that were not identified.

The patient had a uterus and cervix removed along with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrial cancer. The pathology report shows moderate differentiation of endometrioid adenocarcinoma involving almost 100% of the endometrial cavity with squamous differentiation. There is also endometrial hyperplasia, angiolympathic invasion, intramural leiomyoma, chronic cystic cervicitis, and tubo-ovarian adhesion. The left fallopian tube has a paratubal cyst and walthard rests, and the left ovary has endometriosis, hemosiderin-laden macrophages, and microcalcifications. The right ovary has epithelial inclusion and microcalcifications. The lymph nodes and margins are free of tumor. There is a pre-neoplastic condition of simple and complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. The tumor type is endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a moderately differentiated histological grade and a mitotic rate of 22/10 HPF. The tumor has invaded greater than or equal to 1/2 the thickness of the myometrium, but the vaginal margin is negative for tumor. The T stage is not given.

The patient underwent a hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymphadenectomy for endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with FIGO grade II (of III) and invasion into the myometrium, but no involvement of the endocervix or lymphovascular space. Multiple lymph nodes from various areas were negative for tumor. Estrogen and progesterone receptors were positive. Permanent sections may be reviewed for any substantive changes.

The patient underwent a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, specifically the endometrioid type, and with a histologic grade of 3. The tumor size was 50mm, with invasion of less than half of the myometrium thickness and a depth of invasion of 0.5 cm to an area of myometrium that was 4.3 cm thick. There was no involvement of lower uterine segment or cervical margins, and no neoplasm was identified in the bilateral fallopian tubes. In one of the 11 lymph nodes sampled, there was evidence of metastatic carcinoma confirmed with pancytokeratin immunostain. No neoplasm was identified in the remaining lymph nodes sampled. The report notes the presence of adenomyosis, but it is not clear if this is a significant finding. The gross description mentions the uterus, right parametrium, left parametrium, and fallopian tubes, but there is no significant information provided beyond what was already included in the diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a non-gynecological specimen that was acellular and non-diagnostic for interpretation. The clinical information indicates endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the uterus. An immunohistochemical staining (IHC) was performed to determine the presence or absence of protein expression for four proteins; MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2. The results showed normal protein expression and ruled out the possibility of a defective DNA mismatch repair function. However, additional testing may be required if there is a strong personal or family history of HNPCC-related cancers. The rest of the report describes the presence of poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma in the uterus with areas of high-grade nuclear changes and lymph node sampling results.

The pathology report shows the patient has endometrial adenocarcinoma that has invaded at least half of the myometrium. The tumor is grade 1 and nuclear grade 2, and is 9.4mm in size. There is no invasion of contiguous structures and no lymphovascular invasion. The patient had a TAH-BSO with staging, and the lymph nodes and ovaries are free of tumor. Eleven lymph nodes were negative for metastasis. Representative sections of tissue and lymph nodes were submitted for testing, but no special studies were requested.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had endometrial cancer, specifically endometroid adenocarcinoma with a well-differentiated histologic grade and nuclear grade 2. The tumor was 1.0cm in maximum dimension and involved 10% of both the anterior and posterior endomyometrium. However, there was no invasion of surrounding tissue or angiolympathic invasion. There was also a pre-neoplastic condition of complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia present, as well as an endometrial polyp and leiomyoma. No lymph nodes were examined, and the patient's pathological staging was eT1a, NX, MX, and FIGO stage I.

The pathology report describes the diagnosis of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, low-grade II, with myometrial invasion and lymphovascular invasion. The tumor size is 3.9 x 3.5 cm, and it involves approximately 55% of the uterine wall thickness. The cervix, vaginal cuff, and parametria are free of tumor, and there is no metastatic tumor in the ovaries or fallopian tubes. One lymph node in the right pelvic area is free of tumor, and six lymph nodes in the left pelvic area are also free of tumor. The report recommends primary tumor staging of pT1b, with no regional lymph node metastasis. Leyomyomas, endocervical polyp, squamous metaplasia, and focal epithelial hyperplasia are also noted.

The pathology report describes the diagnosis of endometrial adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type in the uterus with clear cell components. The carcinoma involves an endometrial polyp with minimal superficial invasion. The cervix has chronic inflammation, but no tumor is present. Adenomyosis and leiomyomas are present in the uterus. The left pelvic lymph node shows no tumor, while the left obturator has four lymph nodes with no tumor present. The left PA has three lymph nodes with no tumor present. The right pelvic lymph node has no lymph node found, and the right obturator lymph node has nine lymph nodes with no tumor present. Adipose tissue with fibrosis is present in the right P. P53 stain is negative, and the stage of the neoplasm is 1B, NO, Mx. The report also mentions an ill-defined yellow soft suspicious area in the ovary. Representative sections were submitted for analysis.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to invasive endometrial cancer of undifferentiated and endometrioid type in the uterus. The tumor was invasive and had infiltrated into the myometrium. However, the bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes were not involved. Lymph nodes in the pelvic area, para-aortic lymph nodes, omentum, and appendix were negative for the tumor. There was also a focal squamous cell carcinoma in situ present in the cervix. However, this area was initially diagnosed as atypical reserve cell hyperplasia at the transformation zone.  Nonetheless, further evaluation led to the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma in situ.

The pathology report is for a patient who had a total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node dissection. Nine specimens were submitted, including normal tissue, cervix, lymph nodes, and uterus with tubes and ovaries. The diagnosis is endometrioid grade I cancer, and the report includes descriptions of the specimens submitted for analysis. No grossly identifiable lesions were found, but representative sections were examined. There is a typographical error in the report, with the term "Adinorercinena, Indemelructh, Ws 834445 Sie Coke: Ladewettiim 054-1 yoy be" appearing at the top, which is unclear what it means.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had ovarian adenocarcinoma, endometrioid carcinoma of the uterus, and benign serous cystadenoma of the ovary. The report also mentions lymph node biopsies, which showed no evidence of cancer. The patient underwent a salpingo-oophorectomy and hysterectomy. The report has been reviewed and approved for accuracy.

The pathology report refers to a hysterectomy specimen of the uterus with bilateral adnexa and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The report states that there is a well-differentiated endometrial adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type with squamous metaplasia, FIGO grade 4, measuring 4.5 cm in greatest dimension. The tumor involves 80% of the anterior and 50% of the posterior endometrium and invades 36% of the myometrium. The tumor also involves the endocervical glandular epithelium without cervical stromal invasion, but no lymphovascular invasion is identified. Adenomyosis is present, but the ovaries and fallopian tubes are unremarkable. The report also includes results from lymph node dissections, all of which are negative for tumor. The final diagnosis is pT2a well-differentiated endometrial adenocarcinoma, FIGO stage not provided. The omentum and pelvic wash cytology specimens are negative for malignant cells.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had surgery for adenocarcinoma of the uterus, with a tumor size of 38cm and histologic grade of 3. The report notes greater than 50% invasion of myometrial thickness, as well as the presence of lymphovascular invasion. The report also describes the examination of lymph nodes, which were found to be negative for metastasis. The report mentions adenomyosis as another finding. Special studies are pending.

The pathology report indicates that there is cancer present in the ovary and that it has spread to nearby lymph nodes. The cancer is classified as adenocarcinoma and has invaded the endometrium, cervix, and nearby tissues. The grade of the cancer is not specified. Positive lymph nodes are found in the right hypogastric and common iliac areas, with negative nodes found in other areas. A total of five out of eleven lymph nodes examined are positive for metastatic carcinoma.

The pathology report describes the findings from a patient who underwent a hysterectomy due to poorly differentiated papillary serous carcinoma in the lower uterine segment that extended into the myometrium. There was also extensive lymphovascular space invasion by the carcinoma. The right Fallopian tube showed involvement by the same type of cancer, and no abnormalities were found in the right ovary. The left ovary and tube had mucosal psammomatous calcifications and chronic inflammation. The omentum showed reactive mesothelial hyperplasia, and no evidence of metastases was found. Intraoperative consultations were performed for the right ovary and uterus, both of which showed involvement by papillary serous carcinoma. A polypoid lesion was also noted in the endometrium. The report includes more detailed descriptions of each specimen received for analysis.

The pathology report describes the examination of various tissue specimens from a patient who had a pelvic mass. The hernia sac shows acute inflammation, abscess formation, and reactive granulation tissue, but no malignancy. The right ovary specimen shows a clear cell carcinoma that is high-grade and a part of an unremarkable fallopian tube. The right fallopian tube is benign, but with paratubal cysts. The left adnexa shows follicle cysts, inclusion glands, and cysts in the ovarian cortex, and an unremarkable fallopian tube. The uterus and cervix show endometrial carcinoma located in the lower uterine segment endometrium, confined to the endometrium involving only superficial myometrium, and a benign endometrial polyp. The chronic endocervicitis section of the cervix is mild, with unremarkable myometrium. The omentum biopsies, left pelvic lymph node, left periaortic lymph node, left obturator lymph node, and right pelvic lymph node are benign with no metastatic carcinoma. The right obturator and right periaortic lymph node, bladder biopsy, and appendix are negative for metastatic carcinoma, and there is appendiceal fibrosis with luminal obliteration. Overall, the patient has clear cell carcinoma of the ovary, high-grade, and endometrial carcinoma with clear cell features, well to moderately differentiated in the lower uterine segment endometrium.

The patient underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, revealing multifocal synchronous carcinomas in the endometrium, uterine serosa, and ovary. The endometrial carcinoma is a FIGO grade II endometrioid and secretory adenocarcinoma, with superficial invasion into the myometrium. There is also a microscopic focus of Undifferentiated carcinoma on the anterior uterine serosa associated with psammomatous calcifications and endometriosis. The right ovary has a FIGO grade I endometrioid adenocarcinoma with atypical complex hyperplasia, which may have arisen from an atypical endometrioid adenofibroma of the ovary or an endometriotic cyst. Immunohistochemical studies suggest that the cancer focus on the uterine serosa is higher grade than the intrauterine cancer. Gene testing is recommended to investigate the possibility of hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC).

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a radical hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node dissection for endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, FIGO grade II, which was invasive to a depth of 2.5 cm out of 40 cm of myometrium. The report also mentions the presence of leiomyomas and acute and chronic cervicitis in the cervix, without evidence of malignancy. The lymph node sampling did not show evidence of malignancy in any of the 28 lymph nodes examined. Overall, the report suggests that the cancer was confined to the uterus with no spread to the lymph nodes or other organs.

The pathology report describes the surgical removal and examination of lymph nodes and reproductive organs in a female patient with endometrial cancer. No signs of cancer were found in any of the lymph nodes examined. The endometrial cancer was identified in the uterus and was classified as endometrioid with a grade III on the FIGO scale. The tumor invaded the superficial myometrium but did not involve other regions. No lymphovascular space invasion was identified. Other findings included endometrial polyps and leiomyomata. The estrogen and progesterone receptor status of the tumor is pending. The final stage and treatment plan will depend on further clinical review and information.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a hysterectomy specimen with attached bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes weighing 80 grams. The report shows the presence of serous endometrial cancer with invasion of the myometrium, cervical stroma, right fallopian tube, and the pericolic soft tissue. There was also the presence of metastasis in the omentum and lymphatic vessels. The report also mentions invasion in several parts such as cul-de-sac tissue, right-sided small tissue, left adnexal tissue, right adnexal tissue, and pericolic soft tissue. The size of the tumor was 3.5 cm in its greatest dimension and there was a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy performed. The report also notes that there were no tumors seen at the resection margins of the specimen. Additionally, the report mentions the presence of metastasis in one lymph node and immunostaining was used on the tissue to confirm the presence of the tumor. Finally, the report shows that there was evidence of serous neoplasia in the sampled sigmoid tissue.

The pathology report describes multiple specimens removed during a surgery, including bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and hysterectomy. The report describes the appearance and measurements of the specimens, including masses, cysts, and nodules. The report also notes an intraoperative consultation finding of carcinoma in one specimen. Microscopic examination was performed, and the pathological stage was determined to be PT3a NX pM. This information was transmitted to the cancer registry.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of endometrial adenocarcinoma, grade 2, with invasion greater than 50% of myometrial thickness. The tumor was removed along with the uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes, and ovaries, and lymph nodes were tested for metastasis. Nine lymph nodes tested negative for metastasis. The report also includes details on the size and extent of invasion of the tumor. A fragment of a hernia sac was also examined and found to consist of fibromembranous tissue. Overall, the report indicates a diagnosis of endometrial cancer with further staging information pending.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial adenocarcinoma in a patient who underwent total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TAH-BSO) and lymph node sampling. The tumor is described as endometrioid type, grade 1-2, with no myometrial invasion identified. Five (6) lymph nodes that were sampled for metastasis were negative. The report also notes the presence of a nodule lesion in the upper endocervical wall, which was found to have no obvious invasive component upon gross examination. Additional sections of the endometrial lesion and other tissues were obtained for further analysis. The report provides information about the size and appearance of various organs and tissues, including the uterus, ovaries, and lymph nodes.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a pelvic mass excision and a fallopian tube and ovary removal. The diagnosis shows a presumed benign frosty tumor, no malignancy detected, with marked focal fallopian tube and ovarian surface dysplasia. There is a microscopic focus of atypical epithelium in the right fallopian tube and a similar focus on the surface of the ovary, which may be indicative of serous carcinoma. The report recommends treatment based on these findings. The lymph nodes and omentum were negative for malignancy, and the pathologic stage is OT, NO. Additionally, there is a single small negative lymph node present. The report provides a detailed description of the specimens received and examined.

The pathology report describes the diagnosis of a 4.2 x 3.6 x 1.1 cm mass of FIGO grade II endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, located in the right anterior uterine cavity, which has invaded 0.6 cm into the myometrium. The report also mentions the excision of the uterus, bilateral ovaries, fallopian tubes, and lymph nodes, which were negative for tumor, along with tissue from the abdomen. Additionally, the report notes the presence of endosalpingiosis in the left ovary and unremarkable findings in the right ovary and fallopian tubes.

The pathology report shows that the patient had benign fatty tissue in the omentum, high grade papillary serous carcinoma in the uterus that invaded more than 50% of the myometrial thickness with lympho/vascular invasion identified, and ovarian endometrioid carcinoma with mixed granulosa and Sertoli tumor features in the right ovary. The left ovary had fibroma/fibrothecoma, and the bilateral fallopian tubes were negative for tumor. The cervix had a tunnel cluster, Nabothian cyst, and no tumor involvement. Eleven left pelvic lymph nodes, four right pelvic lymph nodes, and five para-aortic lymph nodes were negative for carcinoma. The immunohistochemistry stains were positive for inhibin-alpha, WR, and CHROMOGRANIN A, and positive focal for CAM52 and P53. The cytology was negative. The pathological staging is pT 1bNOMx.

The pathology report describes a diagnosis of FIGO grade III endometrial adenocarcinoma of the uterus, endometrioid type, with invasion into the myometrium and lymphovascular space. Multiple intramural leiomyomata were also observed, but the bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes were atrophic and not involved. Lymph nodes in both the right and left pelvic regions were positive for metastatic carcinoma consistent with endometrial primary. The report notes that the tumor stage is pT1bN1 according to the 7th edition of the AJCC staging system.

The pathology report is for a patient who underwent a laparoscopic assisted vaginal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymphadenectomy for Grade 1 endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium. The tumor measures 3x2cm, invades the myometrium to a depth of 2.5mm and involves areas of adenomyosis. There is no lymphovascular space involvement or involvement of other tissues, and the lymph nodes are negative for malignancy. The patient also has uterine fibroids and endometrial polyps. Tissue has been submitted for estrogen and progesterone receptor assays, and results will be reported separately. The patient is staged as pT1a, with no evidence of metastasis. Pelvic washings and margins are negative.

The pathology report describes a total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to a leiomyoma (uterine fibroid) and twisted fallopian tube. The report also shows the presence of adenomyosis and endometriosis. A biopsy of the right para-aortic lymph node indicates the presence of lymphoid tissue. Additionally, there were benign lymph nodes and fibroids found in surrounding tissues. The report is signed by the examiner who conducted the examination.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy, oophorectomy, and lymphadenectomy performed on a male patient with malignant neocorpus uteri. The report details the gross examination of the removed tissues, including a soft gray-tan mass in the endometrial cavity and a second soft gray-tan mass in the underlining anterior lower uterine segment. Lymph nodes were also examined. The intraoperative consultation identified the mass at the fundus as adenocarcinoma mucinous features, FIGO grade 1. The pathological stage is pT1B pNO pMK. Information is transmitted to the Institution's Cancer Registry for accreditation.

The pathology report describes two specimens received for examination. The first is a 2020.0 gram portion of skin and subcutaneous tissue from an abdominal panniculectomy, and the second is a 145.0 gram uterus with bilateral tubes and ovaries received after a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The uterus shows a FIGO grade 2 endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, that is confined to the endometrium and does not involve the endocervix. The myometrium shows extensive adenomyosis forming a 4.5 x 4.1 x 3.1 cm well-circumscribed trabeculated myometrial nodule. The bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes are without diagnostic abnormality. Representative sections were submitted for examination.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, which revealed moderately differentiated endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with squamous metaplasia, FIGO grade 2. The tumor measured 5 cm and invaded approximately 53% into the myometrial thickness. Lymphovascular invasion was present, but the cervix was negative for tumor. Leiomyomata were also present. Left and right ovaries were negative for tumor, as were left and right fallopian tubes. Biopsies of the omentum and pelvic lymph nodes were negative for tumor. The final diagnosis is stage Ic endometrial cancer. A pelvic wash contained atypical cells, but other washing specimens were negative for malignant cells. A total of 17 lymph nodes were examined, and none were positive for tumor.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and was diagnosed with FIGO grade III endometrial adenocarcinoma with mixed endometrioid and clear cell types. The tumor has invaded 0.4 cm into the myometrium but does not involve the endocervix or lymphovascular space. The margins are negative for tumor.
