The left ovary and fallopian tube also show endometrioid carcinoma with tumor implants present on the right ovary and uterine cul de sac. Lymph nodes from the pelvic and para-aortic dissections are negative except for one lymph node in the right pelvic dissection that is positive for metastatic carcinoma on permanent section review. The report notes that any substantive changes from the initial report will be reflected in a revised report.

The pathology report describes findings from a surgical procedure involving the removal of the left and right fallopian tubes, uterus, and lymph nodes in the pelvic and common iliac areas. The left and right fallopian tubes exhibited chronic and minimal acute salpingitis with no evidence of metastatic carcinoma. The uterus showed primary uterine adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with associated squamous, eosinophilic, and secretory-like changes. The tumor had extensive involvement in certain areas, was exophytic/polypoid in some areas, and showed superficial myometrial invasion by carcinoma with secondary involvement of adenomyosis deeper in the uterine wall. No lymphatic or blood vessel invasion was identified, and the cervix and vaginal cuff were free of tumor. The lymph nodes, including the left pelvic, left common iliac, left obturator, right pelvic, and right common iliac nodes, were all reactive with no evidence of metastatic carcinoma. A follow-up addendum may include results from an immunohistochemical panel testing for potential microsatellite instability. The synoptic report summarizes the macroscopic and microscopic findings for each specimen type.

The report describes various tissue specimens received for analysis, including skin and subcutaneous tissue, uterus with attached tubes and ovaries, lymphatic tissue from pelvic and para-aortic nodes, and an omental biopsy. The uterus contains a 3.9 x 2.9 x 1.5 cm mass in the lower uterine segment with no leiomyomata identified. The right ovary measures 3.2 x 1.4 x 1.4 cm and the left ovary measures 2.8 x 1.4 x 1.4 cm with multiple paratubal cysts present. The lymphatic tissue from all nodes appears unremarkable. No masses are identified grossly in the omental biopsy. The report does not provide a diagnosis or suggest further course of action.

The report describes the results of a surgical pathology final report for a patient with endometrial cancer. The report confirms that the patient has endometrial adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type with FIGO grade 2 and focal mucinous differentiation. The report also provides details on the lymph nodes and ovaries removed during the procedure, confirming that there is no regional lymph node metastasis and no ovarian involvement. The surgical margins are uninvolved by invasive carcinoma. The report notes some additional pathologic findings, such as hyperplasia and leiomyoma with calcifications. Overall, the report indicates that the cancer is classified as pTla [IA].

The pathology report describes a case of a patient who underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to a pelvic mass and endometrial cancer. The report shows that there was a high-grade serous carcinoma in the endometrium and an endometrial polyp, with extensive lymphovascular invasion. Eighteen lymph nodes were examined, and 5 of them had metastatic carcinomas with extranodal extensions. The report provides details on the histologic type, grade, and extent of invasion of the cancer, as well as results of auxiliary tests. The clinical stage of the cancer was determined to be T1a, N2, M0, and the prognosis was poor.

The pathological report describes a case of endometrial cancer in an 85-gram uterus that was found to have a 1.6 x 1.5 x 1.0 cm polypoid adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type, FIGO grade 2-3 with superficial myometrial invasion (7% of myometrial wall thickness). The tumor is highly suspicious for lymphovascular invasion but does not involve the lower uterine segment or cervix. The left and right parametrial margins are negative for malignancy. Multiple lymph nodes were removed as part of the procedure and were negative for malignancy. Complex hyperplasia with atypia was identified in the lower uterine segment, and the fallopian tubes were unremarkable. The right ovary had a follicular cyst, and the left ovary had a hemorrhagic corpus luteum cyst.

The patient underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection. The pathology report indicates the presence of well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a tumor size of 4.5 cm and involvement of 10% of the anterior endomyometrium and 30% of the posterior endomyometrium. There was greater than 1/2 thickness of myometrium invasion. No angiolympathic invasion was noted, but the pelvic wash specimen was positive for malignant cells. The lymph nodes examined were negative for cancer. The final FIGO stage was determined as tA.

The pathology report describes a microscopic assisted vaginal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to a well-differentiated endometrioid type endometrial adenocarcinoma in an endometrial polyp, which involves approximately 20% of the posterior uterine wall. There is no lymphovascular invasion identified, and the vaginal and parametrium margins are negative for the tumor. The report also mentions an extensive complex atypical endometrial hyperplasia but no malignant cells found in the benign endocervical polyp, left and right ovaries, right fallopian tube with a paratubal cyst, and left ovary with an old suture granuloma. The tumor is categorized as T1a, N0, Mx stage, and the histologic and nuclear grades are well-differentiated (FIGO 1) and grade 2, respectively. The report also mentions that the tumor is confined to the endometrial polyp and there is no invasion.

The pathology report describes multiple biopsies taken from a patient with endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The tumor has invaded the myometrium to a depth of 3 cm and extends into the cervix and upper vaginal cuff. The surgical margins are free of tumor. The uterus contains a large calcified leiomyoma, and there is no tumor seen in the bilateral ovaries nor fallopian tubes. The report also includes information on the gross description and size of the tumor, as well as the histologic type and grade. The primary tumor is staged as pT3b (IIIB), and there is no regional lymph node involvement or distant metastasis detected. Multiple specimens were submitted for analysis, including fragments of tissues, a hemorrhagic material, and the uterus and surrounding organs with attached bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes.

The patient had a diagnosis of endometrial carcinoma and underwent a hysterectomy along with lymph node dissections. Four benign hyperplastic regional lymph nodes were found in the right periaortic lymph node dissection, and four hyperplastic regional lymph nodes were found in the left periaortic lymph node dissection. One solitary benign regional lymph node was found in the left pelvic lymph node dissection and three hyperplastic regional lymph nodes were found in the right pelvic lymph node dissection. The tumor was identified as endometrioid with moderate to poorly differentiated histologic grade and diffuse involvement in the groin cavity, measuring 4.8 x 4.6 x 2.2 cm. The tumor infiltrated the myometrium and invaded into both the endocervical mucosa and submucosa. Findings suggested the presence of lymphovascular space invasion, but no metastatic carcinoma was found in the 12 lymph nodes. The surgical margins were uninvolved. Additionally, benign bilateral fallopian tubes and ovaries exhibited paratubal cysts. The pTNM stage was determined to be pT2,NO.

The report describes surgical pathology findings from a patient who underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for high-grade serous adenocarcinoma. The tumor measured 4.7 x 2.4 x 0.8 cm and invaded 0.3 cm into the myometrium. Lymphovascular space invasion was not identified, and all lymph nodes examined were negative for tumor. Endometriosis was found in the cul-de-sac, and a single submucosal leiomyoma was identified. Other tissues and lymph nodes examined were negative for tumor. Gross descriptions of the specimens are included. The report notes that the final pathology report is based on gross/macroscopic examination and permanent sections, and any substantive changes identified on review will be reflected in a revised report.

The pathology report shows that the patient had endometrial adenocarcinoma, a type of uterine cancer. The cancer was found in the uterus, left ovary, and fallopian tube, but not in the right adnexa. The tumor was classified as endometrioid type and graded as 1-2, with minimal myometrial invasion and no lymphovascular invasion detected. The cancer had not spread to the lymph nodes. Other findings included benign stromal nodules, intramural leiomyomas, and adenomyosis. The patient's stage was classified as T1b, NO, MX; stage IB if MO. The right ovary was diagnosed with a mature cystic teratoma. The patient underwent a hysterectomy with bilateral salphingo-oophorectomy and lymph node removal.

The pathology report describes the results of a surgical procedure involving the removal of the uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries along with lymph nodes and omentum. The report confirms the presence of invasive high-grade papillary serous carcinoma and non-invasive high-grade papillary serous carcinoma within an endometrial polyp. Multiple benign leiomyomata and calcified nodules were also identified. The report shows that the removed lymph nodes and omentum were negative for any cancerous cells. The report is based on macroscopic and microscopic evaluations of the specimen.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrial adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type. The tumor was grade II and formed a 3.4 cm x 2.7 cm x 1.6 cm polypoid mass in the posterior and right lateral wall of the endometrial cavity, invading 0.2 cm of myometrial wall. The lower uterine segment was not involved, and the cervix, ovaries, and fallopian tubes showed no abnormalities. Lymph nodes from the pelvic region and para-aortic region were negative for tumor. A separate panniculectomy specimen was also received.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial cancer with lymph node metastasis. The uterus, cervix, tubes, and ovaries were removed, and the tumor was found in the endometrium, with myometrial invasion and involvement in lymphovascular spaces. The cancer had a mixed histologic type of serous adenocarcinoma and high-grade endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The lymph nodes in several locations were also affected by metastasis. The woman was estrogen receptor-positive but progesterone receptor-negative. The cancer was assigned a stage of pTla pN2 and FIGO Stage grouping IIIC2. Adenocarcinoma was also present within the lumens of the fallopian tubes but had not yet invaded them.

The pathology report describes a surgical removal of uterus, bilateral ovaries, and fallopian tubes due to invasive endometrial adenocarcinoma. The tumor, of endometrioid type, measured 8.5 x 2.6 x 1.1 cm and invaded 0.7 cm into the 1.8 cm myometrial thickness. The cervix was not affected. Endometriosis was detected in the right ovary, while the left ovary and both fallopian tubes showed no abnormalities. Biopsy from the pelvic peritoneum showed inflamed fibroconnective tissue, and multiple lymph nodes were removed from the pelvis and left para-aortic regions. One of the pelvic obturator lymph nodes was positive for metastatic adenocarcinoma, while the remaining lymph nodes were negative for tumor spread.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma in a female patient. The tumor involves the uterus, cervix, bilateral ovaries, and fallopian tubes, with extensive angiolymphatic invasion present. The report notes positive lymph nodes and negative omentum. The tumor is classified as pT3a N1 Mx, and the histologic grade is G3. Several biopsies and excisions were taken, with positive right pelvic and periaortic lymph nodes and negative left pelvic lymph node. The omentum was negative for tumor. The gross description details the size and appearance of the uterus, fallopian tubes, and ovaries.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy specimen that was analyzed for a tumor in the uterus. The tumor was found to be an endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a size of 3 x 2.5 x 1 cm and a moderately differentiated histologic grade. The tumor involved less than half of the myometrium and showed evidence of lymphatic invasion. Venous invasion was not specified, and there was no mention of neo-adjuvant treatment or other notable pathological findings.

The pathology report describes a case of cancer identified as Odinecarcenmea, PULTE, located in the cervix, fallopian tubes, ovaries, and uterus. Metastatic carcinoma was found in various lymph nodes, with varying degrees of involvement. The report indicates that the material has been reviewed and approved. Further information on treatment and prognosis is not included in the report.

The pathology report is for a patient who underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for endometrial cancer. The cervix showed acute and chronic cervicitis but was negative for malignancy. The endometrium had adenocarcinoma (endometrioid type, FIGO grade I of III) with focal superficial myoinvasion (less than 1/3 of the inner myometrium). Endosalpingiosis was found in the left ovary, but both ovaries were negative for malignancy. The lymph nodes from pelvis and periaortic area were negative for malignancy. The AJC Pathologic stage was pT1b/pNx.

The report describes a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy performed on a 50-year-old woman who was diagnosed with a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type, FIGO grade 3, with spread to the left pelvic lymph nodes. There were no abnormalities found in the right pelvic or common periaortic lymph nodes, or in the omentum. The report also notes the presence of leiomyoma and subserosal endosalpingiosis in the uterus, and ovarian adhesions. The left fallopian tube contained an endocervical polyp. No abnormalities were found in the right fallopian tube or the left and right ovaries. The report includes gross descriptions of each specimen received in the laboratory. An intraoperative consultation was also noted.

The pathology report indicates that there was a total hysterectomy and ovarian removal due to papillary serous type endometrial adenocarcinoma. The tumor invaded the myometrium and vaginal area. There were benign adipose tissue and lymph nodes found during the surgery. Further tests and treatment may be needed.

The pathology report describes the case of a man who underwent surgical removal of a uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes, and ovaries for endometrial cancer. The gross description of the removed tissue indicates the presence of numerous fibrous nodules, some of the nodules occupying the endometrial canal. The report confirms the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. Samples from several lymph nodes and the omentum were also taken and submitted for analysis. The report suggests that the cancer has spread beyond the uterus and lymph nodes, indicating advanced stage disease.

The pathology report relates to a 2 cm endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium and a 1.4 cm cervical adenoid basal carcinoma. The endometrial cancer has invaded the cervical stroma and has a FIGO grade 3 histologic type with a myometrial invasion inner half, while the cervical adenoid basal carcinoma has invaded deeply into the cervix. The report mentions that the cervix also had high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion present. The report states that a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-cophorectomy have been performed. No involvement of regional lymph nodes or adnexa is identified. The patient is clinically diagnosed with endometrial cancer, and the gross description identifies a pear-shaped uterus with a weight of 135 grams. The cervix is 3.5 cm in diameter with a 1 cm slit-like cervical os. The report states that the pathologic stage assessment is based on information available at the time of this report and is subject to change pending clinical review and additional information.

The pathology report describes a total abdominal hysterectomy with a diagnosis of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, nuclear grade 3 and architectural grade 1, involving approximately 60% of the endometrium. There is no evidence of endocervical involvement, but there is a very superficial invasion of the myometrium. Other findings include endometrial hyperplasia, leiomyoma, tubal epithelial hyperplasia, and various lymph nodes with no evidence of metastatic neoplasm. Focal fat necrosis and granulomatous reaction are present in the sigmoid epiploica, and focal mesothelial hyperplasia and surface fibrosis with microadhesions are observed in the omentum. There is also atypical endometrioid mullerianosis in the right fallopian tube and atrophy in the squamous epithelium of the cervix with mild squamous atypia. The report was left on the ordering physician's voicemail.

The pathology report describes a case of malignant neoplasm of the corpus uteri. The report details the gross examination of various lymph nodes and the uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, and ovaries. The uterus has a 4.6 cm polypoid mass that involves both the anterior and posterior endometrium and has a glandular type architecture suggestive of possible adenomyosis. Additional smaller polypoid endometrial lesions are also found. The report recommends microscopic examination and provides the pathologic stage as well as details of the lymph node sampling.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy for endometrial cancer where the tumor is a mixed serous and endometrioid adenocarcinoma of FIGO grade 3 and has invaded the inner half of the myometrium, with 33% infiltration, but with no involvement of the serosa, lower uterine segment, or cervix. Adnexal involvement is identified in the right fallopian tube, and right-sided and left-sided pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy show no carcinoma in the nine dissected lymph nodes. The estrogen and progesterone receptor status is ER 2-3+, 60%, and PR 2-3+, 20%. Ovaries are normal. Chronic cervicitis, adenomyosis, and leiomyomata are additional pathological findings. The final diagnosis is pT3a pNO endometrial cancer.

The pathology report shows that the patient had a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrial adenocarcinoma. The tumor was of endometrioid type with a nuclear grade III and invaded the underlying myometrium to a depth of 0.4 cm out of a total myometrial thickness of 2.2 cm. There was lymphovascular emboli present, but all surgical margins were free of tumor. The diagnostic comment suggests that it was suspicious for superficial myometrial invasion. The final pathologic staging was determined to be pT2a pNO pMx. The patient's omentum and pelvic lymph nodes were free of tumor.

The pathology report describes the excised tissues from a patient who underwent a radical hysterectomy. The report includes descriptions of the lymph nodes in the left and right pelvic areas, which were entirely submitted for analysis and found to be negative for malignancy. The report also describes the uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, and ovaries, including the presence of a pink-tan fungating mass that invades 1.2 cm into a 1.8 cm thick pink-tan fibrous myometrium. The mass is identified as a tumor, but no myometrial nodules or lesions were found. The final diagnosis includes the negative findings for malignancy in the lymph nodes and the presence of a tumor in the uterus, which remains unspecified in the report.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy specimen from a patient with uterine cancer. The uterus shows primary uterine adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with associated squamous changes. The tumor extensively involves the mucosa of the uterine fundus and corpus, and extends into the lower uterine segment. Myometrial invasion by the tumor is present superficially, and dislodged fragments of the tumor are present within some endothelial-lined spaces, including veins. The report suggests that an iatrogenic process is favored over true lymphovascular invasion. The cervix, including the surgical margin, is negative for tumor. Several benign uterine findings are also present, including uterine leiomyomas and adenomyosis. The report notes mild epithelial hyperplasia in both fallopian tubes without significant atypia. The lymph nodes show no evidence of metastatic carcinoma. The pathologic tumor stage is assigned as pT1b, NO.

The report describes a surgical sample that includes the uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries, and vaginal margins. The diagnosis is primary uterine adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type with associated squamous changes and focal secretory changes, FIGO grade 3, nuclear grade 2. The report notes extensive involvement of adenocarcinoma in the endometrium and an endometrial polyp. There is also evidence of invasion of myometrium from the posterior lower uterine segment and adenomyosis. The report notes that there is no unequivocal lymphatic or blood vessel invasion by carcinoma, no invasion of the endocervix, and the vaginal cuff is free of tumor. The report also notes that the left fallopian tube has foci of hyperplasia without significant cellular atypia, subserosal endometriosis, and calcification. There are also senescent changes and relative cortical stromal hyperplasia with associated hyperthecosis in both ovaries.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the uterus, with involvement of the upper endocervix and myometrial invasion up to a depth of 6 mm. Metastases were identified in the right ovary but not in the left ovary or in any of the lymph nodes examined, except for isolated involvement of the left common iliac lymph node. The tumor is classified as pT3a NO Mx. The report also includes a gross description of the specimen and its dimensions.

The pathology report describes a sample of tissue collected from a uterine endometrial mass through surgical resection. The histology of the sample shows endometrioid adenocarcinoma with up to 50% squamous/transitional differentiation. The tumor size and lymph node involvement are not specified in the report.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomies due to a biopsy showing Grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The uterus, cervix, bilateral ovaries, and fallopian tubes were removed. The histologic type was endometrioid adenocarcinoma, with a histologic grade of FIGO grade 3 (architectural grade 2, nuclear grade 3). The tumor was located in the primary endometrial cancer site, with myometrial invasion in the outer half, and a depth of 11 mm. The lower uterine segment had involvement, but cervical and adnexal involvement were not identified. Regional lymph nodes were negative for tumor. The AJCC Pathologic Stage was pT1b pNo, and the FIGO (2009 classification) Stage Grouping was IB, grade 3. Leiomyomas and a benign endocervical polyp were also present. No tumor was identified in lymph nodes removed during regional lymph node dissection.

The pathology report describes the examination of a surgically removed uterus, cervix, and ovaries. A 3.1 cm tumor was found in the posterior part of the uterus with multiple nodules in the surrounding tissue. The largest nodule was 3.6 cm with focal calcifications. The report concludes that the patient has a malignant neoplasm of the corpus uteri, specifically endometrial adenocarcinoma grade 2, with superficial invasion at most and no involvement of the lower uterine segment. The left adnexa had a cerebriform cyst, an unremarkable mesentery, and fat. The right adnexa had a pelvicolonic segment with no ovary or fimbria. Lymph nodes were also examined, and the largest lymph node found was 2.6 cm in greatest dimension. The report includes the pathology stage (pTlb pNO pMx) and surgical procedure (hysterectomy and left salpingo-oophorectomy) as required for cancer registry accreditation.

The pathology report shows that the patient underwent hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrial carcinoma. The tumor was located in the corpus, fundus, and lower uterine segment and measured 7.7 cm. It was grade 1 (well-differentiated) and had invaded 0.5 cm into the myometrium. No lymphovascular invasion was identified. Leiomyoma, cervix with Nabothian cysts, ovaries with epithelial inclusion cysts, and fallopian tubes with paratubal cysts were also observed, but there was no evidence of malignancy. Seven lymph nodes from the right pelvic dissection and three lymph nodes from the left pelvic dissection had no evidence of malignancy. A soft tissue pelvic nodule underwent excision. The final pathologic staging was pT1b, pNO.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a radical hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to the presence of serous carcinoma involving an endometrial polyp, submucosal leiomyoma, and a mixture of serous and endometrioid carcinoma in the endometrium. There was focal superficial invasion but no lymphovascular space involvement, and the endocervix and cervix were uninvolved. The left ovary had a 1.5 cm simple cyst, and the right ovary was atrophic, as were the fallopian tubes. Omentum, lymph nodes, and surrounding soft tissues were negative for tumor.

The report describes a case of uterine papillary serous carcinoma (UPSC) with extensive involvement of the uterus, cervix, and fallopian tubes. The left fallopian tube shows tubal intraepithelial carcinoma, while the right fallopian tube and ovary show metastatic adenocarcinoma with lymphatic space invasion. The omentum also shows metastatic UPSC. The report suggests a poor prognosis due to the extensive spread of the cancer.

The pathology report describes the results of a surgical consultation for a patient who had undergone a hysterectomy and lymph node biopsies. The report notes the presence of serous carcinoma in the endometrium and adenocarcinoma in the myometrium of the patient's uterus. No malignancy was found in the patient's lymph nodes or ovaries. The report also includes measurements of the specimens, and specific details about the appearance and characteristics of the cancerous tissue.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has endometrial carcinoma of the endometrioid type. The tumor extends from the outer cervix to the lower uterine segment, and there is lymphovascular space invasion. The report also notes the presence of adenomyosis. The immunohistochemistry shows that the tumor cells are positive for ER and negative for PSS and p18. Of the lymph nodes examined, four out of twenty-four pelvic nodes and one common iliac node tested positive for carcinoma. The report includes descriptions of the uterus, ovaries, fallopian tubes, and lymph nodes, as well as details about the tissue sections analyzed.

The pathology report indicates that there is endometrial cancer present, with lymph nodes also affected. The tumor size is 30x21.5mm and has a high-grade appearance. Multiple lymph nodes have been removed and tested for cancer. The report also provides detailed measurements for various tissue samples and describes the shape and size of the tumor and surrounding tissue. The report suggests that further treatment may be necessary and provides information for future reference.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary serous carcinoma in the uterus, with lymphovascular invasion present. The tumor extends into the posterior lower uterine segment and is close to the serosa, with a maximum myometrial thickness of 1.5 cm. The report also notes small foci of high-grade serous carcinoma in the bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes, which may represent independent primaries rather than metastasis from the uterine cancer. One lymph node in the left periaortic region and one in the left para-aortic lymph nodes are positive for metastatic carcinoma, while no tumor is present in the right external iliac lymph nodes or the left and right pelvic lymph nodes. The report provides gross descriptions of the specimen and includes codes for the submitted sections.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial cancer with involvement of the ovaries and fallopian tubes. There is no evidence of cancer in other organs or lymph nodes, except for some lymph node involvement in the pelvic area. A tumor measuring 15cm is detected in the endometrium with myometrial invasion. The report also mentions the presence of leiomyomata (fibroids) and a few specific details about the appearance and characteristics of the various tissues and organs examined. An immunohistochemical stain for p53 is positive consistent with serous carcinoma. Overall, the report provides a detailed analysis of the patient's condition and the presence of cancer in various parts of her reproductive system.

The pathology report includes the results of several containers received in formalin containing various specimens, including lymph nodes and tissue samples. The report confirms the presence of an endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the uterus and notes that the tumor has invaded nearby lymphovascular spaces. The report also indicates that the lymph nodes tested are benign, and immunohistochemistry staining for DNA mismatch repair enzyme proteins was intact. However, clinical signs suggest possible Lynch Syndrome, so further testing is recommended. The report provides detailed information on the size, location, and number of lymph nodes tested from various areas. Additionally, the report notes that the margins are unwotted, and there is no involvement in the lymph node status.

The pathology report shows that the patient had a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, which was moderately differentiated and involved 70% of the endometrial surface and less than 5% of the myometrium. There was also a background of atypical complex hyperplasia and focal lymphovascular space involvement. The cervix and pelvic lymph nodes were negative for tumor. The ovaries had stromal hyperplasia and a small adenofibroma. The size of the tumor was 40mm, and there was less than 1/2 thickness of myometrium invasion with angiolympathic invasion. The pre-neoplastic condition was simple endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. The patient had 0 positive lymph nodes out of 6 examined. The stage and grade of cancer were not specified.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrioid adenocarcinoma with focal squamous differentiation in the uterus, cervix, left fallopian tube, and ovary. The tumor has invaded the inner half of the myometrium and presents lymphovascular space invasion. There is no involvement of the serosal, cervical, or adnexal areas. The patient is ER and PR receptor positive. The AJCC Pathologic stage is pT1a pN0 pMx, and the FIGO stage grouping is 1A. The lymph nodes removed during surgery did not show any metastatic carcinoma. The diagnosis has been amended to invasion into the inner half (33%), and the original stage of pTlb has been amended to pT1a. There is also the presence of a Nabothian cyst and chronic cervisitis in the cervix. The left fallopian tube presents peritubal cysts and hydrosalpinx, and the atrophic ovary shows no malignancy.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a Robot assist total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral Salpingo-oophorectomy and pelvic lymph node dissection due to endometrial cancer. The report reveals that no metastatic adenocarcinoma is identified in the lymph nodes, except for bilateral peritubal and ovarian involvement by metastatic adenocarcinoma. The uterus is affected by chronic endocervix with Nabothian cysts, microscopic adenocarcinoma externally involves the deep subface of cervix, and background leiomyomas. Serous endometrial adenocarcinoma of nuclear grade 3 extends through the full thickness of the myometrium with serosal involvement. Lymphovascular space invasion is present. The mitotic rate is not provided, and the patient had no distant metastases. The report further indicates that the patient is staged as pT3a and has no residual tumor.

The pathology report describes a reactive lymph node with sinus histiocytosis in the left obturator lymph node. The report also indicates a high-grade endometrial carcinoma with endometrioid adenocarcinoma and foci of serous carcinoma that invaded 2.2 mm of myometrium, and into the upper endocervical stromal connective tissue. The tumor had not spread beyond the uterus or to any of the lymph nodes examined. Immunostaining for ER was positive in the endometrioid areas and p53 staining was strong and diffuse in the endometrioid areas while negative in the areas of serous carcinoma.

This is a pathology report for a 67-year-old female with endometrial carcinoma. The report shows that the patient has metastatic adenocarcinoma in the lymph nodes of the right and left para-aortic and pelvic areas. The tumor is endometrioid adenocarcinoma and has a histologic grade of overall FIGO grade 3. The tumor is located in the anterior and posterior corpus and lower uterine segment. The myometrial invasion is in the inner half, and the depth is 1.1 cm. The lymphovascular space invasion is extensive. Leiomyomas with hyalinization are also observed in the myometrium. The cervix shows Nabothian cysts, acute and chronic cervicitis, tubal metaplasia, and benign mixed endocervical/lower uterine segment endometrial polyp. The adnexal, right and left ovaries, and right and left fallopian tubes are all atrophic, with no tumors seen. The stage of the cancer is IIIC2. The report is subject to change with additional information.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the corpus uteri that has invaded 0.1 cm into the myometrial wall. The pathology report indicates multiple sites of metastatic serous adenocarcinoma of primary uterine origin, including a soft tissue mass in the abdominal wall, left salpingo-oophorectomy, uterus and cervix, omentum, and various pelvic soft tissue masses and lymph nodes. The tumor is a high-grade serous adenocarcinoma with extensive lymphovascular space invasion, myometrial invasion, and cervical involvement. A frozen section consultation was also performed for an abdominal wall tumor, which was diagnosed as high-grade papillary serous carcinoma invading the peritoneum.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type (FIGO grade II) that measured 4.7 x 3.2 x 1.7 cm and invaded 0.3 cm into the myometrium without involving the endocervix. The gross/macroscopic examination found a 160-gram uterus with attached bilateral tubes and ovaries, as well as several aggregates of adipose and lymphatic tissue labeled as lymph nodes, all of which were negative for tumor.

The pathology report indicates the presence of endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma grade 2 that has invaded 0.4 cm with 2.3 cm myometrial thickness and involves endocervical glands and stroma. Lymph nodes and omentum show no evidence of tumor, while the left fallopian tube has paratubal cysts. The report includes detailed descriptions of the gross specimens obtained during surgery.

The pathology report shows a marked epithelial nabothian cyst in the uterus with poorly differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma that has invaded to a depth of 8 mm. The report also describes the size and characteristics of the tumor and lymph nodes that were examined. Further treatment may be necessary based on the findings.

The report describes a laparoscopic-assisted vaginal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for a patient with endometrial adenocarcinoma, papillary endometrioid type, FIGO grade I. The tumor size is 4.0 x 3.0 x 3.0 cm and involves the lower uterine segment but not the cervix. Vascular invasion is present. The myometrial invasion is greater than or equal to one-half, with a depth of invasion of 0.7 cm and a myometrial thickness of 1.1 cm. Lymph node sampling shows no regional lymph node metastasis, and several lymph nodes are negative for tumor (0/7). One lymph node is identified in the omental biopsy but is negative for tumor (0/1). The report also describes leiomyomas, endometriosis, and xanthomatous salpingitis present in some of the sampled tissues. No tumor is observed in the pelvic sidewall biopsy or lymph node excisions. The report provides detailed information on the size, involvement, and staging of the cancer and describes other findings in the sampled tissues.

The pathology report shows that the patient underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy and unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to primary uterine adenocarcinoma. The tumor is predominantly endometrioid with associated secretory, eosinophilic and squamoid changes, focal mucinous type, and possible minor component of tumor with clear cell features. The tumor has invaded the myometrium and involves greater than 50% of the uterine wall thickness in the deepest area of invasion. The report also notes adenomyosis, benign uterine leiomyomas, hyperplasia with atypia, and cervical inflammation. No evidence of metastatic carcinoma was found in the lymph nodes. The left ovary shows atrophic changes, and the right ovary shows relative cortical stromal hyperplasia with associated hyperthecosis.

The pathology report shows that the patient underwent a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to suspected endometrial hyperplasia. The report revealed the presence of adenocarcinoma of endometrial origin with endometrioid type, FIGO grade 1, and nuclear grade 2. The tumor invades the inner half of the myometrium, and lymphatic vascular invasion is absent. The cervix showed benign ectocervical and endocervical components with no evidence of dysplasia, malignancy, or tissue invasion. The serosa of the uterus had no evidence of malignancy, while the ovaries showed physiologic changes and no malignancy. The lymph nodes were benign with no evidence of metastasis, and there were no large or small vessel invasions. The report suggests that the tumor is well-differentiated, with no distant metastasis. The doctors requested an additional portion of the right fallopian tube and tumor mass for further research.

The pathology report is for a patient who underwent a robot-assisted laparoscopic hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and pelvic lymph node dissection for endometrial carcinoma. The pathology report describes the findings from multiple specimens. The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, endometrioid type with extensive squamous differentiation and necrosis, grade 3, stage 1C. The report describes a diagnosis of endometrial carcinoma, endometrioid type, with invasion into the myometrium, but not into the endocervix or lymphovascular spaces. The patient underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to FIGO grade III endometrial adenocarcinoma. The report describes the examination of various tissue samples and biopsies taken from a patient with endometrial cancer. The patient had endometrial cancer and underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The patient underwent a laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to a grade 2 to 3 endometrial neoplasm. The pathology report describes the examination of lymph nodes and reproductive organs from a patient with endometrial cancer. The report also notes minor abnormalities in the cervix and calcifications in the vascular system. The right and left ovaries and fallopian tubes were atrophic without malignancy identified.

The report describes a patient with endometrial carcinoma who underwent a hysterectomy and partial omentectomy. The pathology report describes the results of several surgical procedures, including omentectomy and hysterectomy, which identified the presence of endometrial cancer in the uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, and ovaries. The report mentions other findings related to atrophy and the absence of DNA mismatch repair proteins, but it is unclear whether these are significant in the context of the patient's cancer diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a case of serous papillary adenocarcinoma of the endometrium with a tumor size of 13.7 cm and full thickness myometrial invasion. The patient underwent a hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and omentectomy with lymph node dissection. One lymph node was found to be positive for metastasis. The pathological stage was pT3b pN1 pA according to the AJCC 7th Edition. The report provides details on the gross examination of the anatomy of the reproductive organs, as well as the microscopic examination of the tissue samples.

The pathology report shows that the patient had a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrial adenocarcinoma (endometrioid type) with myometrial invasion and involvement of the lower uterine segment. The tumor did not invade lymphovascular spaces and there was no lymph node involvement or distant metastasis. The report also indicates the absence of carcinoma in residual ovary, lymph nodes, and soft tissue samples. The tumor is classified as G3 with solid growth of more than 50%. The gross description shows a hemorrhagic mass in the left fundus with central areas of necrosis and a friable papillary lesion in the posterior lower fundomyometrium. The patient's cervix and fallopian tubes did not show evidence of carcinoma.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, which revealed stage 3 endometrial carcinoma, serous type, that had invaded completely through the myometrium to uterine serosal soft tissues. The tumor also involved the cervix/endocervix, but lymphovascular space invasion was not identified. Multiple intramural leiomyomata were also identified. One of 20 left pelvic lymph nodes was positive for a microscopic focus of metastatic serous carcinoma. Multiple right pelvic lymph nodes, as well as right and left para-aortic lymph nodes, were negative for tumor. The omentectomy was negative for tumor, and the appendix was benign. The right diaphragm biopsy was also negative for tumor. The gross examination revealed a 6.4 x 6.2 x 2.8 cm exophytic friable mass filling the endometrial cavity, grossly invading 1.7 cm. The myometrial thickness was 1.7 cm. Representative sections of the uterus, bilateral fallopian tubes and ovaries, left pelvic lymph nodes, right pelvic lymph nodes, omentum, appendix, right para-aortic nodes, left para-aortic nodes, and right diaphragm biopsy were submitted for evaluation.

The pathology report describes the specimen received for tissue procurement labeled as uterus, bilateral tubes and ovaries, cervix, which presents a 4.5 x 3.9 cm uterine cavity containing a pale tan tumor measuring 2.5 cm in thickness grossly involving the upper one-third of the myometrium anteriorly. Some well-circumscribed rubbery whorled intramural leiomyomata and normal-appearing endometrium are also present. The analysis includes representative sections of the lesion and endometrium, as well as the right and left pelvic and periaortic lymph nodes, which show several slightly rubbery tan-pink-gold tissues keeping with lymph nodes. Bilateral ovaries are unremarkable. The patient had a pre-op diagnosis of endometrial carcinoma.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy surgical procedure for endometrial carcinoma. The report provides information on the histopathological features of the carcinoma, including high grade adenocarcinoma with many solid poikilocytotic areas, many mitoses and some clear cell features. The staging of the carcinoma is also described. The report notes the presence of numerous cysts and lymphoid aggregates in the posterior cervix, as well as fibrovascular adhesions in the uterine serosa. The report describes various biopsy specimens and sections, including omentum biopsies, a biopsy of the cul de sac, and a biopsy of the right uterosacral ligament. The gross characteristics of various specimens, including the uterus, tubes and ovaries, are also described in detail.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to the presence of endometrioid adenocarcinoma with morular squamous metaplasia of the endometrium. The tumor is classified as grade T, with solid growth that constitutes less than 5% of the total tumor. The tumor is limited to the endometrium, with no endocervical invasion observed. Complex hyperplasia with atypia is observed in the endometrium, and endometriosis and adhesions are present in the left ovary and fallopian tube, respectively. 

Several lymph nodes were excised, including the left lateral external iliac, left obturator, right lateral external iliac, and common iliac lymph nodes, with no evidence of cancer in most of the nodes. However, three positive lymph nodes were found in the right common iliac adipose tissue, indicating the presence of metastatic cancer. A medical professional personally examined the slides and agrees with the diagnosis.

The pathology report is regarding a tumor sample (type: endometrial mass) collected from the uterus of a patient (TCGA-DF-AIKV-034). The tumor was diagnosed as endometrioid adenocarcinoma that was moderately differentiated (Grade 2). There was no evidence of cancer spread to the nearby lymph nodes (Pathological N: NO, Number of Nodes Positive: 0) and distant sites (Clinical M: N/A). The report does not provide information on the patient's age, surgical procedure details, or any further treatment recommendations.

The pathology report indicates that a patient underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy, right salpingo-oophorectomy, and left salpingo-oophorectomy. The right ovary showed atrophic changes without malignancy, while the left ovary showed atrophic changes with fibrous adhesions but no malignancy. The uterus had endometrial adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type with invading carcinoma involving the anterior and posterior walls and lower segment. The tumor invaded the outer half of the myometrium with extensive lymphovascular invasion present. The cervix showed benign components. Lymph nodes from different regions were found benign except for a benign lymph node with endosalpingiosis. Additionally, the hernia sac showed benign tissue. The patient also had incidental findings of endosalpingiosis involving lymph nodes and uterine subserosal tissue, along with endometrial atrophy.

The pathology report describes the case of a female with serous endometrial cancer. The report includes the diagnosis of uterine serous carcinoma, tumor size, invasion depth and lymphovascular space invasion present. Two pelvic lymph nodes were found to be involved by the neoplasm. Other specimens, including lymph nodes, peritoneal washings, and diaphragm were submitted and found to be negative for neoplasm. The final staging was T2N0M0 (FIGO N).

The pathology report describes a tumor found in the omentum and several lymph nodes that were removed and examined for metastatic disease. The lymph nodes were negative for metastasis. The tumor was identified as high-grade endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a tumor size of 0.7 cm to 2.8 cm and involved the myometrium. The surgical margins were clear, and the patient was diagnosed with pT1aN0 (FIGO I) stage cancer. The report also notes the presence of myomectomy, an attached ovary with stromal hyperthecosis, and separate ovaries and fallopian tubes without evidence of malignancy. Additional immunochemical stains were performed on the biopsy samples.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of endocarcinoma of the endometrium, with spread to the lymph nodes and other areas of the body. Several biopsies were taken, with varying numbers of benign and cancerous lymph nodes found in each sample. No lymph nodes were identified in one of the biopsies. The report was based on a personal examination of the slides by the examining physician.

The report describes the presence of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type in a patient who had undergone a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The tumor is grade II (of III) FIGO and extends into the uterine fundus, anterior endometrium, and transformation zone of the cervix. Lymph nodes in the left pelvic area and one in the right pelvic area contain metastatic adenocarcinoma, while other lymph nodes in the pelvic area and para-aortic lymph nodes are negative for tumor. The bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes are without diagnostic abnormalities.

The report describes a diagnosis of papillary serous adenocarcinoma with clear cell features in the uterus and cervix of a 60-year-old female. The tumor has invaded the myometrium, lower uterine segment, and cervix. There is also microscopic involvement of the left ovary and lymphovascular space invasion. One lymph node out of 16 in the left pelvic region shows focal metastatic adenocarcinoma. Immunohistochemistry results for tumor estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor are pending, but the tumor is MSH2 positive, MSH6 positive, and MLH1 positive. The report provides information on the histologic type and grade, extent of invasion, involvement of other sites, and AJCC stage. There are also findings of adenomyosis, calcification of vessel walls, and a hemangioma in the endocervix. Two containers labeled as ovaries showed no evidence of malignancy, and there was no metastatic carcinoma identified in most of the examined lymph nodes.

The pathology report describes the findings from a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy surgery. The uterus, ovaries, and fallopian tubes were removed due to the presence of an endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with FIGO grade II (of III) and measuring 4.0 cm x 2.7 cm x 2.7 cm in the fundus. The tumor invaded superficially, 0.2 cm into the myometrium, but did not involve the endocervix. Lymphovascular space invasion was not identified, and margins were negative for the tumor. The bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes were unremarkable and uninvolved. Multiple lymph nodes from both pelvic regions were excised, and all of them were negative for tumor.

The pathology report describes a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy specimen with a diagnosis of high-grade endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the uterus, stage TA, with poorly differentiated components and invasion of 35% of the myometrium. Lymphovascular invasion is identified and there is adenomyosis involvement. The cervix and bilateral ovaries are negative for tumor. Pelvic and common lymph nodes are negative for tumor. The omentum is also negative for tumor. The tumor is positive for CAM 5.2 and AET/AES and Vimentin, and negative for CD10 and desmin. The maximum dimension of the tumor is 40 mm and it involves 80% of the posterior endometrial surface and 15% of anterior endometrial surface. The histologic grade is poorly differentiated (FIGO 3) with a nuclear grade of 3.

The pathology report describes the findings from a hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node biopsy in a patient with serous carcinoma uterus. The report includes details of the size and location of various nodules and lesions, including a submucosal uterine lesion that extends to the inner third of the myometrium and a 0.5 cm ovarian cyst. The report also notes the presence of metastatic carcinoma in a right common iliac node. The pathology stage is pT3a.

The pathology report shows that the patient had endometrial cancer with endometrioid adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, grade 2 nuclear grade. The tumor measured 4.6 cm in its largest dimension and involved 75% of the anterior and posterior endomyometrium. The tumor did not invade more than half the thickness of the myometrium, and there was involvement of the endocervical glands. The report also notes the absence of lymph node involvement and distant metastases. The final stage of the cancer is not reported, and the residual tumor is listed as "RK." The peritoneal washing was negative for malignant cells. Additionally, the report mentions the presence of pre-neoplastic conditions, including simple endometrial hyperplasia with atypia, complex endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, adenomyosis, and leiomyoma.

The pathology report shows that the patient had a laparoscopic vaginal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to poorly differentiated endometrial carcinoma. The tumor invaded the endometrial mucosa to a depth of 0.5cm and had a nuclear grade of high grade. There was lymphovascular invasion but no cervical or myometrial involvement was seen. There were no lymph node or distant metastases identified. The patient also had adenomyosis. The report includes additional information on the specimen received and its measurements.

The pathology report describes a fresh frozen sample of a uterine mass on the posterior wall collected in 2018. The patient was between 0-3 years old at the time of the sample collection. The sample was a surgical resection of the uterus, and the histology showed endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The tumor size was 4.3cm, and the grade/differentiation was not specified. The pathological T was T1b, and there was no evidence of nodal involvement (N0). The clinical M status was not specified. Overall, the report suggests a diagnosis of endometrial cancer.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has high-grade serous adenocarcinoma with endocervical stromal invasion and myometrial invasion present at 12.5%. There is no evidence of carcinoma in the ovaries, tubes, or omentum. The report includes lymph node examination results revealing no evidence of malignancy in any of the nodes examined. The report also includes additional information on tumor site, dimensions, invasion, margin status, and immunohistochemical staining. The report concludes that the case has been reviewed by one or more pathologists and lists the clinical information obtained from laparoscopic surgery. The specimens received for examination include cervix, uterus, tubes, ovaries, and omentum, and an inclusion cyst was present in the right ovary.

The pathology report describes multiple tissue samples taken from various areas including the uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes, ovaries, lymph nodes, and abdominal scar. The report describes an irregular mass in the posterior wall of the uterine cavity measuring 2.5x1.0x1.5 cm and two smaller polypoid masses on the anterior wall of the uterine canal. Multiple lymph nodes were also examined in various locations. Additional details about the appearance and size of the tissue samples are provided in the report.

The report describes a surgical procedure involving removal of lymph nodes and a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for a patient with grade 3 endometrial cancer. The pathology report shows that no tumors were seen in the lymph nodes examined and that the endometrial cancer was confined to the mucosa with no serosal involvement and involving the mucosa only in the lower uterine segment. No other sites were affected, and the cervical/vaginal margins were widely free of tumor. The report also notes the presence of leiomyomas in the uninvolved endometrium. Additional information on estrogen and progesterone receptor immunohistochemistry and final tumor staging is pending.

The pathology report indicates the presence of FIGO grade II endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with squamous and mucinous metaplasia. The tumor is identified as a 4.0 x 3.0 x 1.0 cm polypoid mass located in the fundus, invading 0.2 cm into the myometrium. Multiple (3) intramural leiomyomata and a benign endometrial polyp are also identified. The bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes are not involved in the tumor. The pathology report includes a description of the gross/macroscopic examination and the frozen section histologic evaluation of the specimen(s). The report concludes with a block summary of the examined tissues.

The pathology report describes the presence of metastatic serous carcinoma in the peritoneum, right gutter, and omentum as well as in the uterus and cervix, where the tumor type is classified as serous adenocarcinoma. The histologic grade is noted as grade 3 and includes extensive lymphovascular space invasion. Adnexal involvement is present in both ovaries, with one exhibiting a poorly differentiated serous adenocarcinoma. The frozen section biopsy taken from the peritoneum, right gutter, is positive for high-grade serous adenocarcinoma. The tumor is positive for estrogen receptors and weakly positive for progesterone receptors. The overall stage is classified as pT4a pNx pMx, or Stage IVA according to FIGO classification. The clinical history indicates the patient was diagnosed with endometrial cancer and had serous adenocarcinoma of the endometrium.

The pathology report is for a patient with endometrial adenocarcinoma who underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The report describes the size and location of the tumor, invasion of the myometrium and lymphovascular space, and involvement in nearby lymph nodes. The report also includes descriptions of the lymph nodes that were processed for research purposes, which were negative for malignancy. Overall, the report provides details about the extent and characteristics of the patient's cancer.

The pathology report describes the findings from multiple excisions and partial omentectomies, salpingo-oophorectomies, hysterectomy, and lymph node excision in a patient. The report shows the presence of mild chronic inflammation, adhesions, and focal reactive mesothelial proliferation in the omentum, with no evidence of metastatic carcinoma. The left adnexa shows chronic inflammation and an atrophic ovary with a cystic mesothelial inclusion, while the right adnexa shows an atrophic ovary with cystic epithelial inclusions and focal epithelial hyperplasia with associated atypia/dysplasia. The uterus reveals primary uterine carcinoma with serous, clear cell, and undifferentiated features, nuclear grade 3, with myometrial and lymphovascular invasion. The lymph nodes excised show no evidence of metastatic carcinoma. The report mentions additional findings like reactive lymph nodes, myometrial inflammation, and calcific sclerosis of regional arteries. An addendum is included to report additional findings in slide E2-1 related to the right adnexa.

The first report describes the pathology findings for a patient who underwent a hysterectomy and lymph node dissection. The histologic type of the tumor was papillary serous adenocarcinoma with high grades. The tumor invaded the myometrium up to 20 mm with no lymphovascular invasion present. The patient had 0/16 positive para-aortic nodes and 9/37 positive pelvic nodes for regional lymph node metastasis. The ER stain was negative, and the PR stain was low positive. The patient was at Stage IA0.

The second report describes the pathology findings for a patient who underwent a total hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and biopsy. The tumor was endometrial carcinoma with invasion of approximately 30% of the myometrium. There were also multiple leiomyomas present. The patient had a 4.2 cm, well-circumscribed mass located next to the left ovary. Representative sections were submitted for further examination.

The patient had a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrioid type endometrial adenocarcinoma involving 60% of the endometrial surface and invading 28% of the hyometrium, along with complex atypical hyperplasia in the background. The left fallopian tube had metastatic adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type FIGO grade 1 nuclear grade 2, and invasive poorly differentiated adenosquamous carcinoma involved the cervix. Lymphovascular invasion by adenosquamous carcinoma was present. The tumor invaded 5mm of the cervical wall thickness and superficially spread over 11mm. Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 3 and adenocarcinoma in situ were present. The patient had negative lymph nodes in all collected areas except for one lymph node from the left fallopian tube with metastases. Foreign body giant cell reaction was found in ventral hernia sac excision. The appendix was negative for metastatic tumor.

The report describes a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy procedure for a patient with a malignant neoplasm in the corpus uteri. The gross examination shows a 2.8 cm adenocarcinoma of the endometrium with 0.5 cm maximum depth of myometrial invasion and lymphatic/vascular invasion present. The tumor is poorly differentiated with a FIGO grade of 3 out of 3. The remaining myometrium is a leiomyoma measuring 3 cm. The cervix and serosa are free of tumor, and the specimen margins are not involved. The right and left ovaries have benign serous cysts and adhesions, and the left fallopian tube and ovary are unremarkable. Microscopic examination confirms the diagnosis of metastatic poorly differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the cul-de-sac nodule. The report includes information on the pathology stage and operative procedure and is transmitted to the institution's cancer registry. The tumor is unreactive for synaptophysin and chromogranin.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of endometrial cancer, involving the entire uterine cavity and extending to the lower uterine cavity, with invasion of 0.5 cm into the myometrium. A single intramural leiomyoma is also identified. Metastatic adenocarcinoma is identified in the peritoneum and small bowel serosa, consistent with endometrial primary. However, the report states that lymph nodes and other tissues show no evidence of tumor. Immunoperoxidase stains for DNA mismatch repair enzymes were performed and showed intact expression, suggesting no defective DNA mismatch repair.

The report describes a patient who underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingooophorectomy, and omentectomy due to invasive poorly differentiated endometrial carcinoma of the endometrioid type. Fourteen pelvic lymph nodes, one paraortic lymph node, and thirteen lymph nodes from the omentum were negative for malignancy. The ovaries and fallopian tubes were also negative for tumor involvement. The report also describes multiple leiomyomas, but they were not involved with the tumor. A large 3.5 cm tumor was found and examined in detail. It was determined to be a metastatic tumor, and samples were submitted for further testing. Overall, the patient's diagnosis indicated endometrial carcinoma, and the report provides detailed information about the extent and nature of the tumor.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy and salpingo-oophorectomy specimen from a patient with a clinical history of endometrial hyperplasia. The uterus weighs 256 grams and is diffusely trabeculated, with a diffusely thickened, shaggy endometrial lining and an unremarkable myometrium. The cervix exhibits multiple pink wart-like nodules and a flap of unremarkable vaginal epithelium is attached to the posterior cervix. The left and right fallopian tubes and ovaries exhibit unremarkable serosal surfaces; however, the right ovary contains a predominantly smooth-walled ovarian cyst with rare scattered tan nodules, and the left ovary consists of several cortical serous fluid-filled cysts. A piece of pink-tan tissue from the posterior vagina is also present. Intraoperatively, 1 mm myometrial invasion is observed in a 2.5 cm thick wall of the anterior endomyometrium, indicating a Pathologic Stage of pT1B pNX pax. The report concludes by noting that information on pathology stage, as well as the operative procedure, will be transmitted to the institution's cancer registry.

The pathology report shows that a patient underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to moderately differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium. The cancer invaded the inner half of the myometrium and the lower uterine segment, but did not involve the endocervix. There was no evidence of angiolymphatic invasion. The cervix with parakeratosis and bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes were negative for tumor. There was also the presence of leiomyomata and focal adenomyosis. Lymph node dissection showed negative results for tumor in all nodes examined.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with invasion into 25% of the myometrial thickness. The report also indicates the presence of benign cervix, adenomyosis, and endometrial polyp. Lymph nodes from multiple regions were negative for carcinoma. The tumor was found to have intermediate to high-grade nuclei, and the final FIGO score was 2. Age and other details about the patient are not mentioned in the report.

The pathology report indicates that the patient was diagnosed with endometrial adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type with low-grade and FIGO grade 1. The tumor has invaded the uterine serosa into the parametrial tissue, and lymphovascular invasion is present. The anterior bladder flap, pelvic node, and parametrial tissue are involved with metastatic adenocarcinoma. The report also mentions the presence of a benign epithelial-tined polyp and a uterine fibroid. The report concludes that a hysterectomy was performed, and the tumor size was 3.5 cm in the greatest area. One lymph node out of two received is positive for adenocarcinoma, while the other is free of the tumor.

The pathology report describes the results of a biopsy and total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The bladder flap and uterine serosa biopsies were negative for malignancy. However, the uterus with cervix and bilateral adnexa showed endometrioid type adenocarcinoma located on the anterior aspect of endometrium with exophytic growth and invading myometrium. No lymphovascular invasion was noted. The report also mentions proliferated endometrial polyp, myometrium with leiomyoma, mild endocervicitis in cervix, and benign Mullerian glands in both ovaries. The lymph nodes were examined, and no metastatic carcinoma was found. The final diagnosis is primary uterine endometrial tumors, with endometrioid adenocarcinoma (FIGO grade 2). The tumor size was 3cm with less than half the thickness of myometrium involved. Complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia was also observed. Further pathological staging was not provided in this report.

The pathology report describes the results of a surgery to remove a patient's uterus, tubes, and ovaries due to endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type. The report confirms myometrial invasion, the presence of lymphovascular space invasion, and involvement of one lymph node. However, there is no carcinoma involved in the non-cancerous endometrium and other organs and lymph nodes tested negative for cancer. The report also provides details on the size and dimensions of the tumor, histological grade, and depth of myometrial involvement. The report indicates that further evaluation for distant metastases is needed.

The pathology report describes the examination of a uterus and bilateral adnexa that were removed during a hysterectomy, oophorectomy, and lymphadenectomy. The patient had an EES neoplasm of the corpus uteri and abnormal bleeding. The gross examination revealed a 6 x 4 x 1.1 cm exophytic tumor involving both anterior and posterior endometrial surfaces with myometrial invasion of 0.6 cm in a 2.3 cm thick wall. The tumor extends to within 1.5 cm of the anterior section of the cervix and 2.5 cm from the posterior endocervical. The left and right ovaries and fallopian tubes were unremarkable, but the serosal had a leiomyoma and powder burn mark. Microscopic examination revealed endometrioid adenocarcinoma with FIGO grade 2, and adjacent non-neoplastic endometrium was atrophic. The remaining myometrium had adenomyosis and a leiomyoma of the maximum 0.6 cm. The cervix was involved with a 2 mm nodule at the tip of endocervical polyp. There were no signs of lymphatic/vascular invasion. The pathology stage was pT2, pNO, pM.

The pathology report describes multiple findings in a pelvic tumor, including degenerative changes, chronic cervicitis with reactive endocervical cells, endocervical polyp, focal dystrophic calcification, and nabothian cysts. The left ovary has surface epithelial nuclear cysts and physiologic changes, while the right fallopian tube has reactive epithelial changes and metastatic tumor cells involving one of four lymph nodes. The omentum (a fatty tissue layer in the abdomen) is negative for carcinoma. The report includes a comment on the high-grade endometrial cancer and suggests a complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia. The tumor stage is reported as pT1bN1Mx, indicating a small primary tumor with regional lymph node involvement, but no distant metastasis was identified. The tumor is identified as endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a grade of 3 (out of 3), which is an aggressive form of cancer.

The pathology report describes the findings from a surgical pathology examination of a uterus, bilateral ovaries, and fallopian tubes from a patient who underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The report indicates the presence of microscopic foci of superficially invasive endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, with a background of complex atypical hyperplasia forming a polypoid mass circumferentially involving the endometrium. The tumor has invaded superficially into the myometrium, but lymphovascular space invasion is not identified, and the endocervix is not involved. The report also notes bilateral corpus luteal cysts in the ovaries and chronic inflammation in the umbilical hernia sac with two benign reactive lymph nodes with dermatopathic changes. Representative sections of the relevant tissues were submitted for analysis.

The pathology report indicates that the patient, a female named Khana, had uterine carcinoma. The tumor was identified as serous adenocarcinoma of the endometrium. The report also shows the presence of metastatic carcinoma, with lymph nodes positive for the disease. The patient underwent surgery, including the removal of the uterus, cervix, bilateral ovaries, and fallopian tubes, as well as lymph node procedures. The report confirms negative findings for malignancy in the collected specimens, except for the primary tumor and metastatic carcinoma in the lymph nodes. Additionally, immunohistochemical staining on a specific block confirms the presence of serous carcinoma.

The pathology report pertains to a patient named Toker who underwent a surgical procedure for cervical cancer. The report includes the findings of lymph nodes and tissues removed during the procedure. The addendum indicates the presence of poorly differentiated endometrial tumor (equivalent to Grade 3 endometriold adenocarcinoma). The tumor information includes the extent of invasion, nuclear and histologic grade, and involvement of surrounding tissues. The report also includes staging information and gross descriptions of received lymph nodes and tissues. The report concludes that all lymph nodes were free of metastatic tumor except for the left parametrium. The posterior vaginal margin is free of tumor. A comment section indicates that the findings were concurred with by a SRI.

The patient's postoperative diagnosis is uterine cancer, specifically endometrial adenocarcinoma that has metastasized to multiple lymph nodes including a left suprapubic mass, left pelvic lymph nodes, deep left pelvic lymph nodes, and left common lymph nodes. The tumor is described as being grade 3 and has invaded more than 50% of the myometrial thickness with lymphovascular invasion present. The report also includes a detailed description of the size and characteristics of the tumor and affected lymph nodes. The staging information indicates the cancer has spread to other parts of the body. Special studies were requested but are not specified in the report.

The pathology report describes findings from various tissue samples taken during surgery for uterine cancer. Samples from the right fallopian tube and ovary show benign cysts and endosalpingiosis but no evidence of cancer. Samples from the uterus, left fallopian tube and ovary show primary endometrial adenocarcinoma with minimal invasion into the uterine wall and no lymphatic or blood vessel invasion. Non-neoplastic endometrium shows areas of hyperplasia with varying degrees of cytologic atypia. There are also leiomyomas, serosal adhesions, calcific sclerosis of uterine arteries, and cervical inflammation present. Lymph nodes and soft tissue samples show no evidence of metastatic carcinoma. Some neoplastic endometrial cells exhibit positive staining for synaptophysin and rare endometrial tumor cells stain positively for chromogranin, indicating a possible minor neuroendocrine component. Further immunohistochemical staining will be performed for confirmation. A preliminary finding was discussed with the physician, and additional findings have been incorporated into the diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a 55.5-gram uterus with bilateral adnexa that was removed from a patient with a malignant neoplasm of the corpus uteri. A tan exophytic endometrial tumor diffusely involves the entire cavity and invades 1.2 cm into the 1.7 cm thick myometrium. The tumor extends to within 0.2 cm of the internal cervical os. The right ovary and fallopian tube contain a 0.6 cm ovarian surface nodule and multiple cysts, while the left ovary and fallopian tube are unremarkable. Three lymph node candidates are found in the left pelvic node and two in the right pelvic node, but no tumor is found in them. The omentum is grossly unremarkable. Pathologic stage, based on the current tissue specimen, is PT1c pNO pMx with endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The report notes that the information provided is solely based on the current tissue specimen being evaluated and should not be confused or substituted for a clinical stage.

The pathology report describes the findings from a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. A primary uterine adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type with serous changes, FIGO grade 11 is present. The tumor involves the endometrium of the posterior fundus, posterior uterine corpus, and posterior lower uterine segment, with exophytic portions of the tumor being polypoid in some areas and showing focal villous glandular features. The surface of the tumor is focally eroded in secondary inflammatory changes with hemorrhages and necroses present. Myometrial invasion by the carcinoma is superficial and involves less than 20% of the uterine wall thickness. There is no evidence of lymphatic or vascular invasion by the tumor, and there is no extension of the tumor into the cervix. The vaginal cuff is free of tumor, and there is no involvement of parametrial soft tissues by the tumor. There is no evidence of metastatic carcinoma involving ovaries or fallopian tubes. Benign inflamed endocervical polyps, acute and chronic inflammation, and reactive epithelial changes are present in the cervix. The diagnoses suggest endometrial cancer with no lymphatic or vascular invasion (stage IA1).
