Containers D-F contain specimens from a hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and adnexal biopsies. The uterus contains a 1.5 cm endometrioid adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation and spindle cell metaplasia, with anaplastic and focal mucinous features. The cancer has invaded the outer half of the myometrium with a depth of 1.3 cm. The cervix, adnexa, and other sites are free of tumor. One out of eleven right pelvic lymph nodes shows small lymph node metastasis, while all other regional lymph nodes are negative for malignancy. The patient is diagnosed with stage IIIC1 endometrial cancer.

The pathology report shows that a  year-old female had high grade uterine papillary serous carcinoma with associated calcifications that involved the omentum, uterus, cervix, and bilateral adnexae. The tumor had deep myometrial invasion and lymphovascular space invasion, and there were small foci in each ovary with ovarian surface involvement as well as parenchymal involvement. The report suggests that this serous carcinoma is of endometrial origin. Several leiomyomas and chronic cervicitis were also present. AJCC Pathologic Stage was pT3a pNx.

The pathology report describes the findings from a surgical procedure of a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to the presence of a 3.6 x 2.9 x 2.0 cm mass in the posterior uterine wall. The mass was identified as an endometrial adenocarcinoma with mixed endometrioid and clear cell types, forming a tumor that invaded 0.1 cm into the myometrium. Lymphovascular space invasion was not identified, and the margins were negative for the tumor. Multiple lymph node biopsies from various locations were negative for the tumor, and other peritoneal biopsies were also negative. The report concludes with a diagnosis of endometrial adenocarcinoma with available surgical material pTlaNO. A preliminary frozen section consultation was also performed to evaluate myometrial invasion and histological subtype. Leiomyomas were also identified in the uterine tissue.

The report describes a case of serous adenocarcinoma in a patient's endometrium. The various specimens received for evaluation, including lymph nodes, omentum, uterus, cervix, tubes, and ovaries were found to be negative for carcinoma except for the endometrial tumor. The tumor was classified as high grade and had invaded less than 50% of the myometrium, but with no involvement of the cervix or lymphovascular space invasion. None of the lymph nodes examined - periaortic, pelvic or left - showed any involvement of the carcinoma. There were no distant metastases. No neo-adjuvant treatment was applied. Histological grading indicates a Tumor invades less than one-half of the myometrium. The report includes specific details about the sizes and numbers of the various tissue and tumor samples submitted for examination and the related procedures.

The individual underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and was diagnosed with FIGO grade I endometrioid carcinoma in the left uterine wall, invading 0.2 cm into the myometrium but not involving the endocervix. A polyp of non-invasive FIGO grade I endometrioid carcinoma was also identified. Extensive adenomyosis was present. No diagnostic abnormalities were found in bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes. Multiple lymph node excisions were performed, and all lymph nodes were negative for tumor. A previous diagnosis of a benign endometrial polyp was corrected to non-invasive endometrioid carcinoma.

The pathology report describes a case of cervical cancer, specifically an adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type. The tumor has invaded the cervical stroma but has not spread to the parametria or lymph nodes. Residual endometrium is present but cannot be clearly defined, and the myometrium thickness is normal. Immunohistochemical testing shows positivity for HR and Vimentin, possibly indicating a tumor originating in the lower uterine segment.

The patient underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy due to endometrial carcinoma. The pathology report indicates that the carcinoma was well to moderately differentiated and of the endometrioid type with squamous differentiation, with invasion into the myometrium by direct extension. There was no lymphovascular space invasion identified. Adenomyosis was also present. The left ovary and fallopian tube showed no abnormalities, while the right ovary showed no histopathologic abnormalities but the right fallopian tube showed mild hydrosalpinx. Eighteen lymph nodes were identified in the left pelvic, right pelvic, and right periaortic areas, with eight showing adenocarcinoma and three showing no adenocarcinoma. No lymph nodes were present in the left periaortic area. The report was based on microscopic examination of the submitted specimens.

The pathology report is from a patient who had abnormal uterine bleeding after a post-pregnancy sal procedure. The report indicates the presence of malignant neoplasia corpus uteri. The uterus has a mass that is not grossly invasive but appears to grossly invade the myonetrin. The left fallopian tube has a section that is dilated and contains yellow-red fluid. The report includes block summaries for representative sections of lymph node candidates in the right and left pelvis. Microscopic examination confirms an endometrioid adenocarcinoma diagnosis for the uterus.

The pathology report is for a hysterectomy specimen showing endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, FIGO grade II. The tumor involves the fundus of the uterus, invading 0.4 cm into the myometrium, but the lower uterine segment is uninvolved. There is also focal superficial involvement in the endocervical mucosa, but lymphovascular space invasion is not identified and the resection margins are negative for tumor. A single subserosal leiomyoma is also present. Bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is performed without diagnostic abnormality bilaterally, and multiple left and right pelvic lymph nodes are negative for tumor.

The pathology report describes a tumor sample collected from a posterior endometrial mass in the uterus. The histology showed endometrioid adenocarcinoma, poorly differentiated with squamous differentiation and focal areas of well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma. There was also evidence of metastatic adenocarcinoma of endometrial origin in the bladder flap. The report does not provide information on the stage or prognosis of the cancer.

The pathology report is pending for a patient with a suspected endometrial adenocarcinoma. The operative procedure involved a TAHBSO with staging. The histologic grade is Grade 3 with invasion present and extends through the myometrium to the serosa. Metastatic carcinoma is present in various sites including the adnexa, ovaries, cul de sac tissue, pelvic tumors, left pelvic sidewall, left and right pelvic lymph nodes, and omentum. Special studies were done upon request. The gross description details the specimens submitted for examination, including enlarged ovaries with nodular and multicystic surfaces, a polypoid tan mass in the endometrial cavity, and fragments of hemorrhagic tissue. Consultation was obtained and agrees with the interpretation of the report. Multiple immunostains were done to identify the disease further.

The pathology report describes the gross examination of various specimens received from a bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, hysterectomy, omentectomy, and peritoneal biopsies, along with an intraoperative consultation. The report includes detailed descriptions of the size, color, and consistency of the specimens, as well as representative sections submitted for further examination. The report notes the presence of a soft, papillary tumor in the endometrial cavity that does not invade the uterine wall and several small leiomyomata. The pathology stage is reported as TxNx¥x (uncertain primary origin site).

The pathology report is for a sample of a uterine endometrial mass. The sample was collected via surgical resection and determined to be endometrioid adenocarcinoma, with no bilateral disease detected. The tumor size was not specified, but there were no positive lymph nodes detected. The patient was 55 years old at the time of sample collection.
The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of endometrial cancer in a Caucasian patient. No further details or information about the severity of the cancer are provided.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy procedure done for a preoperative diagnosis of complex hyperplasia with atypia. The report specifies that the right ovary and fallopian tube, as well as the left ovary and fallopian tube, were excised, revealing small benign cysts. The uterus showed endometrioid adenocarcinoma, grade 2, with myometrial invasion, measuring 5.5 cm. No other organs were affected. Lymph nodes excised from various locations were negative for metastatic disease. The omentum and right parous lymph nodes were excised and were negative for a tumor. One polypoid lesion was found within the endocervical canal. No other significant findings were mentioned. The final diagnosis was pT1a NO FIGO IA endometrioid adenocarcinoma.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a salpingo-oophorectomy on both the left and right ovaries, revealing no significant pathological changes in the ovaries but with paratubal cyst present in both fallopian tubes. The uterus and cervix were removed and showed no malignancy in the cervix but "adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, endometrioid type, FIGO grade I of III" present in the endometrium, which has invaded half of the myometrium. There was no angiolymphatic invasion identified, and the serosa is negative for malignancy. The patient also underwent excision of pelvic lymph nodes, which were both negative for malignancy. The AJC Pathologic Stage is pT1c/pNO. No other gross lesions were identified. Immunohistochemical tests were performed but have not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

The pathology report indicates the following findings for TSS Namettt:

- Site: Endometrium (uterus)
- Diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma of endometrium, exometriod type, with papillary features, grade II (solid growth), nuclear grade 3
- Invasion: the tumor has invaded more than half of the myometrium
- Lymph node involvement: microscopic metastatic adenocarcinoma found in one out of five para-aortic lymph nodes
- Other findings: follicular cysts in the right ovary, otherwise, all adnexa are unremarkable
- Hormone receptor status: the tumor expresses PR, but not HR or p53
- Beta-catenin shows a congruent pattern of immunoreactivity, and the MIB-1 labeling index is moderate-high.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has endometrial cancer of the endometrioid type with focal squamous differentiation and FIGO grade I, with early-stage myometrial invasion. The report also indicates that there are no indications of tumor in the lymph nodes, except for lymph node material identified in the left external iliac lymph nodes which showed mature fibroadipose tissue, and the right ovary having a serous cystadenoma. The report further suggests that there is slight chronic cervicitis and adenomyosis. There is no distant metastasis, and no large/small vessel invasion. The gross description involves the analysis of multiple lymph nodes, ovaries, uterus, and fallopian tubes.

The pathology report describes the findings of a surgical specimen of uterus, bilateral ovaries, and fallopian tubes, indicating the presence of endometrial adenocarcinoma with a polypoid mass (3.0 x 2.3 x 1.0 cm) of endometrioid type that is confined to the polyp and immediately adjacent endometrium and does not involve the endocervix. Lymphovascular space invasion is not identified. The report confirms FIGO grade II (of III) endometrial adenocarcinoma with negative margins and no involvement of bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes. There are also multiple uterine intramural leiomyomas observed along with the other structures. Representative sections were submitted for further evaluation.

The pathology report indicates that there is a malignant tumor in the serous lining of an unknown location (not mentioned in the report), with no evidence of it spreading to nearby lymph nodes or tissues, except for one lymph node in the right para-aortic region which had cancer cells present. The tumor cells were positive for keratin and negative for LCA. The report has been reviewed and electronically signed off.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and bilateral pelvic and para-aortic lymph node dissection. The report shows that the patient had endometrial cancer (specifically, endometrioid and serous adenocarcinoma) with myometrial invasion and lymph node involvement was not seen. The report also shows that the cervix, fallopian tubes, and ovaries were not involved in the cancer. Bilateral chronic salpingitis was noted. The report indicates that the cancer was staged as pT1a (IA) and that the margins were uninvolved by invasive carcinoma.

The pathology report describes a surgical pathology consultation for a patient who underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and partial omentectomy. The omentum shows no malignancy, while the uterus, cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes, and ovaries show endometrial adenocarcinoma with invasion into the myometrium and glandular involvement in the cervix. The ovaries have epithelial inclusion cysts, but the fallopian tubes show no abnormality. The report includes macroscopic and microscopic details of the specimens and provides information on the staging of the cancer.

The pathology report describes the findings from a laparoscopic cholecystectomy and a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The gallbladder shows chronic cholecystitis with porcelain gallbladder and cholecystolithiasis. The uterus and cervix show chronic cervicitis with squamous metaplasia, reactive epithelial atypia, and calcifications associated with metaplastic glands. There is also moderate differentiated adenocarcinoma of endometrium, endometrioid type, with invasion of 75% of myometrium and nearly 100% of the endometrial surface. Lymphovascular invasion is identified focally. The left ovary has inclusion cysts, but the right ovary is unremarkable. A lymph node dissection is performed, with one lymph node negative for metastatic carcinoma in the left external iliac region, two lymph nodes negative in the left obturator region, two lymph nodes negative in the right external iliac region, and no lymph nodes identified in the right obturator and right common iliac regions. The pathological stage is pT1c, NO, MX. The report also includes information about the tumor size, depth of invasion, involvement of endometrial surface, and lymph node status. The report suggests that the companion pelvic wash fluid cytology is negative.

The pathology report is for a patient with endometrial cancer who underwent laparoscopic-assisted vaginal hysterectomy, right salpingo-oophorectomy, left salpingectomy, and node sampling. The report shows moderately differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma involving about 68% of the endometrial surface and penetrating up to 8% of myometrial thickness, with no lymph node involvement observed. The peritoneal cytology is negative for malignant cells. The final diagnosis is endometrioid adenocarcinoma with FIGO stage IB. The report also includes synoptic information about the tumor type, histologic grade, percent of endometrial surface involvement, depth of invasion, and lymph node involvement.

The pathology report shows that the patient had endometrial cancer (adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type) with myometrial invasion measuring 5mm and involvement of 29% of the myometrium in the uterus. The report also shows that there was no lymph node or vascular space invasion. Biopsies of various lymph nodes were taken, and all of them were negative for tumor. The report states that the patient had adenomyosis, chronic cystic cervicitis, and endometriosis involving the deep cervical stroma. The bilateral ovaries showed atrophic pattern with focal hyperthecosis, and a benign serous cystadenofibroma was found on the right ovary. The report concludes that the tumor is categorized as endometrioid adenocarcinoma, not otherwise characterized with a stage IB.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has a high-grade carcinoma with features of both serous and high-grade endometrioid carcinoma. The tumor cells tested positively for BR and were consistent with a serous carcinoma. Metastatic carcinoma was found in all three lymph nodes removed during the surgery. Additional testing was conducted but has not been cleared or approved by the FDA for clinical purposes. The report is approved by the examiner who examined the slides.

The pathology report describes the presence of primary uterine adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type with associated squamous changes, grade II in the endometrium biopsy and benign endocervical tissue in the endocervix curettage. The report also includes details of the surgical specimens, including uterus, ovaries, and fallopian tubes, which have been removed due to endometrial carcinoma. There is tumor-associated necrosis and secondary acute and chronic inflammatory changes in the endometrium biopsy. The report mentions that there is no evidence of metastatic carcinoma in the fallopian tubes and ovaries. The report also provides information on the tumor's histologic grade, grade 2, and staging, PT1B [IB]. The surgical margin is free of tumors, and no lymphovascular invasion is identified. There is simple hyperplasia with atypia and complex hyperplasia with atypia in the additional pathological findings.

The pathology report describes the findings from a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for endometrial cancer with myometrial invasion. The tumor is endometrioid with squamous differentiation and associated calcifications, classified as FIGO grade 2. The tumor invades the inner half of the myometrium to a depth of 3 mm and involves the anterior and posterior lower uterine segment. Adnexal involvement is present, with metastatic endometrioid adenocarcinoma identified in the right fallopian tube and free fragments of the tumor in the left fallopian tube. Lymph nodes from both the periaortic and pelvic regions showed no evidence of metastatic carcinoma. Immunohistochemistry for estrogen and progesterone receptors showed positive staining in tumor cells. The final pathological stage is pT3a pNO, corresponding to FIGO stage IIIA.

The pathology report describes a specimen of uterus, cervix, bilateral ovaries, and fallopian tubes resection. The histologic type of the tumor is papillary serous carcinoma of the endometrium. The tumor size is 7.5 cm with a myometrial invasion of <1/2 and a depth of invasion of 8 mm. The cervical mucosa is not involved, but stromal invasion involving the inner 1/3 is present. The cervical lymphovascular space invasion is not identified. There is a small focus of adenomyosis, calcified uterine leiomyoma, and squamous metaplasia with Nabothian cysts in the cervix. The bilateral atrophic ovaries are negative for malignancy, and the bilateral fallopian tubes are without histopathologic abnormality. The pathologic stage is PT2b NI(TTIc) Mx. The right periaortic lymph nodes are negative for malignancy, while eight out of the right pelvic lymph nodes and one out of the four left pelvic lymph nodes have metastatic carcinoma. The report has been verified by the pathologist, and the microscopic description of the slides is not available. The gross description shows a yellow, papillary endometrial tumor measuring 7.5 cm with no gross lymphatic or vascular invasion. The thickness of the myometrium is 1.5 cm, and one firm white nodule measuring 0.3 x 0.3 cm is seen in one section. The ovaries and fallopian tubes are unremarkable.

The report describes the presence of adenocarcinoma in the ileum (a part of the small intestine), along with cancerous lymph nodes in the right external iliac area. Six nearby lymph nodes were benign, while three lymph nodes in the same area had cancerous involvement. Further testing was conducted with immunohistochemistry markers A41/AE9 and ABL/AK3. Additional cancerous involvement was found in one lymph node in the left obturator area. No evidence of cancer was found in the two remaining lymph nodes in that area.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a previous diagnosis of endometrial cancer and underwent abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and omental biopsy. A biopsy of a nodule found in the abdominal wall showed infarcted appendices epiploicae with calcification. The biopsy of the omentum showed benign fibroadipose tissue. The report confirms the presence of adenocarcinoma in the endometrium, which includes clear cell and endometrioid components. There is no evidence of tumor invasion in the background endometrium, myometrium, or other anatomical structures. The report concludes that there is no lymph node involvement, and the stage of the cancer is not given.

The patient had a TAH-BSO with node sampling for endometrial adenocarcinoma. The lymph nodes in the left and right pelvic and aortic regions were negative for metastasis. The tumor was endometrioid, grade 3, less than 50% invasive, and had no lymphovascular invasion. The cervix was grossly unremarkable, and there was no involvement of contiguous structures. The right ovary was grossly unremarkable, but there was evidence of a previous tubal ligation. The left tube and ovary were not grossly identified, and there were no metastatic deposits in the lymph nodes. The tumor was 4.9 mm from the cervical margin. Additionally, the patient had adenomyosis. Further examination is pending to determine the final pathology report.

The patient, a 51-year-old female, underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy with right salpingo-oophorectomy and pelvic lymph node dissection due to papillary serous adenocarcinoma, which was found to be confined to the endometrium with identified lymphovascular space invasion. The tumor also involved the enocervical glands. The report confirmed the presence of adenocarcinoma in the specimens received, but no abnormalities were found in the right ovary and soft tissue with organizing thrombus. Results of the lymph node dissection showed no carcinoma identified in five lymph nodes on the right pelvic and left pelvic, and two lymph nodes on the right periaortic. However, no carcinoma was identified in four lymph nodes on the left periaortic. The gross description showed the organ's size, color, and external appearance, and the microscopic examination substantiates the diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a case of uterine corpus (endometrial) cancer with myometrial invasion and lymphovascular invasion. The histologic type is serous papillary carcinoma with the tumor size measuring 4.0 cm in greatest dimension. The report also notes the involvement of other organs like the mesentery, sigmoid, omentum, bladder, and periculdle gutter implant. Lymph node sampling showed no regional lymph node metastasis, with no lymph node involved amongst the 11 lymph nodes examined. Ancillary studies mentioned the positive expression of ER and HER-2 and the lack of expression of PR. The operation performed was a total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-cophorectomy, and pelvic lymph node dissection.

The pathology report indicates the presence of adenocarcinoma in the cervix (specifically in the endocervical canal) and the presence of benign lymph nodes in various locations. The report also mentions cervical wall thickening and endometrial atrophy, but does not identify any evidence of sarcoma. The diagnosis is based on the pathologist's personal examination of the samples provided.

The pathology report describes the findings from surgical pathology procedures on various pelvic organs. The report includes descriptions of nodules in pelvic lymph nodes, as well as an examination of the uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, and ovaries. The final diagnosis reveals that there were no signs of metastatic carcinoma, with the lymph nodes showing reactive histiocytosis and fatty infiltration.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a malignant neoplasm in the uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes, and ovaries. A soft white-gray mass is present in the endometrial cavity and extending into the myometrium. Intramural nodules are also present. Lymph node sampling was performed in various locations, and the report indicates no evidence of metastasis. Pathologic staging using the AJCC 6th edition is pT2 pNO pMx. Further information on the operative procedure is not provided.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial cancer in a patient who underwent abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral pelvic and para-aortic lymph node dissection, and pelvic biopsies. Molecular testing on both endometrial and ovarian tumors identified loss of heterozygosity (LOH) in both tumors at chromosomes 144. The endometrial tumor was a moderately differentiated endometroid adenocarcinoma with maximum dimension of 114mm and less than 1/2 thickness of myometrium invasion. The tumor involved 9% of the anterior endomyometrium and 85% of the posterior endomyometrium. The endocervical glands and cervical stroma were also involved, but there was no angiolympathic invasion. The primary ovarian tumor was a high-grade serous carcinoma (pT2c) with marked cytomorphologic atypia and a ruptured tumor capsule. The maximum dimension of the tumor was 70mm, and there was no evidence of vascular invasion. None of the lymph nodes examined were positive for cancer. The patient's LMP date was not available, and there was no prior malignancy or chemoradiation therapy. The overall FIGO stage was high, but no specific clinical question was provided.

The report indicates that no tumors were found in the lymph nodes or ovaries. However, a 5.7 x 3.1 x 1.6 cm endometrial tumor was discovered in the uterus. The tumor is classified as an endometrioid adenocarcinoma, with a FIGO grade of 3 (architectural grade 2, nuclear grade 3). The tumor has invaded the outer half of the myometrium but does not involve the serosa or cervical margin. The pathology stage is pT1c pNO pMx, and the FIGO stage grouping is 1B. Immunohistochemistry results for the tumor estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor are pending. The report also mentions additional findings such as adenomyosis in the myometrium.

The pathology report is for a patient with endometrial cancer who underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and lymph node dissection. The report shows that cancer was present in the uterus and had invaded more than half of the myometrial thickness. The tumor was identified as endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a grade 3 histologic type. There was evidence of lymph node metastasis on the right side, but not on the left, and no tumor was found in the ovaries or fallopian tubes. The total staging of the patient is reported as TIe, N4 (Stage IIc). Inflammation was found in the pelvic biopsies and abdominal wall biopsies, but no tumor was identified. The diagnosis is pending further pathology examination.

The patient had a malignant tumor in the uterus that measured 6 x 4.5 cm and invaded the myometrium. The tumor was low-grade adenocarcinoma and could not completely exclude serous adenocarcinoma. The patient underwent a hysterectomy, oophorectomy, and lymphadenectomy. The pathology stage was determined to be pTib, pNO, pMK. The report includes additional information on the lymph nodes and other tissues examined during the surgery. Information on pathology stage and the operative procedure was transmitted to the Institution's Cancer Registry.

The pathology report describes a case of poorly differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma found in the uterus, with no evidence of carcinoma in the bilateral fallopian tubes and ovaries. The neoplasm measures 8.5 cm in maximum dimension and invades less than 50% of the myometrium. Angiolymphatic invasion is present, but there is no involvement of the endocervix/ectocervix, and margins are negative for carcinoma. Seventeen total lymph nodes show no evidence of carcinoma. The report has been corrected to include a statement about discussion on separate tissue within the container.

The patient has a grade 1 endometrial carcinoma, a tumor in the lining of the uterus. A 7 x 4 x 0.7 cm mass was identified and removed, with no grossly identified involvement of nearby tissue. A leiomyoma, a benign tumor, was also identified in the fundic area of the uterus. No malignant cells were found in the right or left ovaries or fallopian tubes, or in the lymph nodes. The patient underwent a hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node sampling. No lymph node involvement was identified. The pathology stage is pt1B pwo px.

The pathology report indicates the presence of adenocarcinoma with deep invasion into the myometrium of the uterus. The cervix and lower uterine segments are uninvolved. Lymph node dissection was performed, identifying multiple lymph node candidates, with some submitted for further analysis. The remaining specimens from the hernia sac, ovaries, and aortic lymph node were unremarkable.

The pathology report is for a surgical pathology evaluation. There were biopsies taken from various sites in the abdomen, including the colic gutter, omentum, and pelvic sidewall. All of the biopsies showed no evidence of malignancy. 

The report also includes the results of a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TH/BSO), which revealed the presence of endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a histologic grade of G2 in the endometrium of the right side of the uterus. The tumor was 3.5cm in size and had less than 50% myometrial wall involvement. The report includes information about the pathologic staging of the cancer as well.

There were also additional findings in the report, including squamous metaplasia and nabothian cysts in the cervix, adenomyosis, fibroids in the uterus, and a benign Brenner's tumor in the right ovary. Lymph nodes in the pelvis and para-aortic regions were negative for malignancy. The appendix was also negative for malignancy.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has a high-grade endometrial tumor that has invaded the myometrium to a depth of 2.8 cm. There is no involvement of the cervix or any other organ, and there is no lymphovascular invasion. The surgical margins of the uterus, parametria, and cervix are uninvolved, but some lymph nodes were positive for metastatic carcinoma, including one of the pelvic lymph nodes. The omentum is negative for malignancy. The pTNM stage is pT1N1, and the patient had a total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and lymph node dissection. No significant pathologic abnormalities were found in the ovaries and fallopian tubes.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation in the uterus. The tumor had a size of 6.5 cm and invaded more than 50% of the myometrium and the endocervical stroma. Lymphovascular space involvement was also present. The report states that the ovaries were negative for carcinoma but endometriosis was found in the left fallopian tube. Multiple lymph nodes were examined and found negative for carcinoma. The tumor is classified as grade 3, and its stage is pT1c (IC), meaning it invades one-half or more of the myometrium. No regional lymph node metastasis was detected, and no distant metastasis was observed. The report shows no additional pathologic findings.

The pathology report describes a case of malignant neoplasm in the corpus uteri, specifically a grade 2 endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The uterus is enlarged and the cervix shows some discoloration and friability. The tumor primarily involves the anterior wall of the uterus and partially extends onto the posterior wall. The right fallopian tube is dilated and contains a cystic liquid. Multiple lymph node candidates are identified in both the left and right pelvic areas and periaortic region. An intraoperative consultation confirmed the presence of tumor in the uterus and depth and size measurements were taken. The final diagnosis is endometrioid adenocarcinoma.

The pathology report describes findings from various tissue samples taken from a patient with papillary serous endometrial carcinoma. The report includes descriptions of a sigmoid nodule, pelvic biopsy, uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries, lymph nodes, and other tissues. The report notes the presence of adenocarcinoma but does not provide more detailed information on the tumor's characteristics or staging. The report also mentions the presence of intramural leiomyomas and invasion into the endometrial wall. More specific findings are listed in the block summary section.

The pathology report describes a case of adenocarcinoma in the uterus with superficial invasion of the myometrium and extension into the cervical stroma. There was no evidence of nodal metastases in four pelvic lymph nodes or six lymph nodes from the left pelvic and periaortic regions. The appendix was incidentally removed and found to be benign. No other significant findings were reported. Frozen section diagnosis revealed serous adhesions in the uterus, tubes, ovaries, and omentum. The report does not include information about the age, sex, or other personal details of the patient.

The pathology report describes a specimen consisting of the uterus, cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes, and ovaries. The uterus has a large 12.5 x 8.3 x 2.4 cm hemorrhagic tumor that invades 3.0 mm into the myometrial layer and 2.0 mm into the cervix with lymphovascular invasion present. A myometrial nodule consistent with leiomyoma is present on the lateral wall. No tumors are found in the ovaries, fallopian tubes, pelvis, omentum, or paraaortic lymph nodes. A 0.6 cm cystic lesion is found in the left ovary, and a 0.6 cm surface cyst is found in the right ovary. The left tube has a paratubal cyst, and the right fallopian tube contains hemorrhagic material but no other lesions. The report suggests a high-grade endometrial cancer and recommends further treatment.

The pathology report suggests that the patient had endometrial adenocarcinoma with an invasive histologic type and grade 3 nuclear grade. The tumor was found to be 23mm invasive, with no involvement in any other organs. The lymph node analysis showed no evidence of metastasis. There were also multiple lymphoid nodules found in the left and right pelvic and aortic lymph nodes. The entire sample was submitted for examination. The report confirms the diagnosis of endometrial cancer.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had invasive, well-differentiated endometrial adenocarcinoma with mucinous, secretory, and squamous differentiation, with a Nuclear Grade 1 and FIGO Stage 1. The tumor invaded 1.0 cm into 1.3 cm myometrium and lymphovascular invasion was identified. Complex atypical hyperplasia was also present. Metastatic carcinoma was found in the fimbriated end of the left fallopian tube and adenomyosis. The cervix was free of tumor, and the bilateral ovaries and right fallopian tube were negative for tumor. The patient's pathologic stage was T2a NO MX, FIGO IIA. Pelvic lymph nodes, common lymph nodes, and para-aortic lymph node were negative for metastatic carcinoma. Omentum was negative for metastatic carcinoma. The tumor was of endometroid adenocarcinoma, NOS type, with a histologic grade of well-differentiated (FIGO 1). The tumor size was 6.5 cm, with greater than 1/2 thickness of myometrium depth of invasion. The patient had complex endometrial hyperplasia with atypia, and the lymph nodes examined were negative. The patient's pathologic stage was pT3a, N0, Mx.

The pathology report describes a sample from a uterine endometrial mass that was surgically resected. The tumor is identified as an endometrioid adenocarcinoma, with bilateral disease and a primary site in the endometrium. The size and dimensions of the tumor are given as well. Days to procedure and diagnosis are also included.

The pathology report indicates the presence of adenocarcinoma in the endometrium with a grade 2 nuclear grade, and invasion to less than or equal to half the thickness of the uterus. The report also mentions various surgical specimens including the uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, and ovaries, as well as lymph nodes which were found to be benign. No further information is provided on the other specimens.

The surgical pathology report describes a total hysterectomy specimen with a mass lesion located at the fundus, which has invaded approximately 0.8 cm into the myometrium. There are also additional lesions in the posterior lower uterine segment, including a polypoid lesion and two white, whorled nodules. The cervix appears grossly unremarkable. The right ovary has a serous-filled cyst on the adjacent fallopian tube, while the left ovary and tube are unremarkable. A fragment of fibroadipose tissue containing six lymph node candidates was also identified and submitted for analysis. One of these candidates was bisected. One lymph node candidate showed evidence of cancer. The report does not provide information on the type or stage of cancer identified.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has endometrial adenocarcinoma, involving the uterus, tubes, and ovaries. The cancer is of the endometrioid type, grade 2, with invasion of the myometrium up to a depth of 2 cm. There is no lymph node metastasis identified in the right common iliac and right pelvic lymph nodes, while the left para-aortic and left pelvic lymph nodes have metastases. The report also indicates the presence of a tumor, its size, and the absence of venous/lymphatic invasion. The report suggests an initial diagnosis of endometrial carcinoma with considerations for further clinical evaluation and treatment.

The pathology report describes a uterine mass consistent with grade 1 endometrial adenocarcinoma that invades 0.4 cm into the myometrium. The report also noted the absence of lymphovascular space invasion and negative margins for the tumor. The right ovary showed an unremarkable ovarian tissue and a paratubal cyst, while the left ovary and fallopian tube showed unremarkable findings except for hemorrhagic adhesions that were grossly suspicious for endometriosis.

The pathology report describes the findings of a surgical biopsy of various tissues in a patient. The report indicates that there is no evidence of metastatic carcinoma in the omentum, uterus (right cornua), fallopian tube and ovary (left), and fallopian tube and ovary (right). However, a primary uterine adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type with associated squamous changes, was found in the uterus (total abdominal hysterectomy). The tumor involves the endometrium of the uterine fundus, anterior and posterior uterine corpus, lower uterine segment, and myometrial invasion by carcinoma is present and involves the full-thickness of the uterine wall. The tumor also penetrates the uterine serosa, and lymphovascular and perineural invasion by carcinoma is present. The cervix shows severe dysplasia, squamous cell carcinoma in situ, focal microinvasive carcinoma, and koilocytic cervical squamous atypia consistent with human papillomavirus infection. There is no evidence of microinvasive carcinoma at surgical margins, and no lymphatic or blood vessel invasion. Other findings include endocervical nabothian cysts, recent subepithelial hemorrhages, and focal endometriosis in the outermost wall. There were reactive lymph nodes with no evidence of metastatic carcinoma.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral adnexectomy. The uterus weighed 28 grams and had leiomyomas. The report shows that there was a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, with involvement of up to 100% of the endometrial surface. The report also states the presence of a mature cystic teratoma in the left ovary and a high-grade poorly differentiated carcinoma in the left fallopian tube. The right pelvic lymph nodes showed no tumors but significant inflammation. The report concludes with a diagnosis of primary uterine endometrial carcinoma and carcinosarcoma, with a tumor size of 130 mm. The report recommends further treatment and follow-up.

The pathology report describes a case of papillary serous carcinoma (cancer) in the uterus that had invaded 0.3 cm into the myometrium. However, the cervix and lower uterine segment were uninvolved. The right and left ovaries and fallopian tubes did not show any abnormality. Lymph node excisions of the right and left pelvic, right and left para-aortic, and an additional right para-aortic below the inferior mesenteric artery showed no tumor. No malignancy was found in the bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes. One lymph node each in the left and right pelvic regions was examined and found to be negative for cancer. An omental biopsy was unremarkable, but additional studies are pending for a better characterization of a suspicious cell group found. The report also notes the presence of a hyalinized leiomyoma with calcification and endometriosis arising from simple endometrial hyperplasia in the bladder peritoneum. The diagnosis pending additional study is not specified.

The pathology report describes a surgical specimen from an abdominal tissue, salpingo-oophorectomy of both adnexa, and total abdominal hysterectomy with cervix. The report shows unremarkable skin and fibroadipose tissue, an ovary with physiologic changes and endometriosis in the left adnexa, and an ovary with physiologic changes and negative for tumor in the right adnexa. The uterus with cervix shows endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma with myometrial invasion less than 50% and superficial depth of invasion, and negative lymphovascular invasion. The gross impression indicated a leiomyoma which was histologically found to be present. The report also states that no malignant cells were found in the pelvic wash specimen. The patient's BRCA mutation history is noted and the report provides details on the tumor type, histological and nuclear grades, tumor size, margins of resection, lymph nodes examined, pathological stage, and Figo stage. The report recommends immunostain interpretation and mentions that a specimen labeled 38 "pannus tissue" was discarded after a prescribed period of time.

The pathology report is for a patient who underwent a hysterectomy and lymph node dissection. The diagnosis is extensive superficially invasive well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma with minimal myometrial invasion and no lymphovascular invasion. The tumor measured 12 cm maximum dimension. The ovaries and tubes are consistent with age, and mild chronic cervicitis was noted. All pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes examined were negative for metastatic carcinoma. The frozen section was consistent with endometrial carcinoma superficially invasive as per. The final diagnosis remains the same as the preoperative diagnosis. The report also includes macroscopic and microscopic descriptions of the specimen. The histologic grade is G1.

The pathology report describes the examination and diagnosis of tissues and organs from a patient's uterus, ovaries, fallopian tubes, omentum, lymph nodes, and appendix. The patient had grade III papillary carcinoma forming a polypoid mass in the lower uterine segment, without invasion, and a benign endometrial polyp in the anterior fundus. The report also identified a single subserosal leiomyoma, a single intramural fibroid, and corpus luteal and endometriotic cysts in the ovaries, as well as benign paratubal cysts in both fallopian tubes. The lymph nodes and staging biopsies were negative for malignancy. The neoplastic cells from the uterus were positive for p53 and negative for wr-1.

The pathology report shows that the patient underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to the presence of a polypoid mass in the endometrial cavity. The mass is a grade A (of 3) endometrioid adenocarcinoma with extensive squamous differentiation. The tumor has invaded 0.6 cm into the myometrium, but the cervix and serosal surface are not involved. The report also indicates that the lymph nodes, omentum, and gonadal vessels are negative for tumor, and all staging biopsies are negative for tumor as well. A preliminary frozen section consultation suggests that the patient has grade III (of III) endometrial carcinoma of the endometrioid type with focal clear cell features and extensive squamous differentiation, but the diagnosis needs to be confirmed on permanent sections.

The pathology report indicates the presence of endometrioid carcinoma in the uterus with surface adhesions on the right ovary. Lymph nodes in the pelvis and abdomen were examined and some showed metastasis, while others did not. Additional examination of one lymph node is pending. Further information regarding the stage and treatment plan is not provided in this report.

The report describes a patient with uterine cancer, specifically serous papillary adenocarcinoma that extended from the endometrium with stromal invasion. They underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The pathology report showed invasive carcinoma invading the myometrium to a depth of 6mm. The report also describes that no malignancy was found in any lymph nodes or tissues removed during the surgery. The report includes a detailed description of the specimen received for analysis.

This is a pathology report for a patient with a malignant neocorpus uteri, which was surgically removed with a hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, and lymphadenectomy. Gross examination revealed a 3.5 x 3.5 cm yellow-tan exophytic tumor at the junction of the posterior endomyometrium and the fundus, which penetrated 1.4 cm into the myometrium. The tumor did not involve the cervix or lower uterine segment. The report also mentions multiple intramural leiomyomata and well-circumscribed leiomyoma. The report notes that lymph nodes were examined, and microscopically examined. The final pathologic stage is pT1c pN0.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has adenocarcinoma, a type of cancer that originates in glandular tissue, in the cervical region. The cancer has spread to nearby lymph nodes and surrounding tissues. The report also mentions surgical procedures that were done on the patient, including a total hysterectomy and bilateral oophorectomy. The report includes details about the extent of the cancer and the lymph nodes involved. Additional slides and materials were reviewed by the pathologist.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial cancer in a patient, with various lymph node dissections performed. Benign lymph nodes were found in the left para-aortic, right common iliac, and left pelvic regions, while a benign lymph node and fibroadipose tissue were found in the right para-aortic and left common iliac regions, respectively. The uterus, tubes, and ovaries were removed via hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and the endometrium was found to have high-grade serous carcinoma with 2.5 mm invasion of the inner half of the myometrium. Lymphovascular invasion was present, and there was evidence of endometrial intraepithelial carcinoma in the cervix and lower uterine segment. The ovaries and fallopian tubes did not show any significant abnormality or signs of malignancy. The report includes a checklist for the endometrial carcinoma and notes the extent of invasion and involvement of lymph nodes. The pathologic stage is designated as PT2a NO Mx.

The pathology report describes the findings from the surgical removal of the patient's left and right tubes and ovaries, uterus, sigmoid adhesion, and various lymph nodes, along with biopsies from the right colon and umbilical hernia repair. The report shows that the left ovary has endometrioid adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation, while the right ovary is benign. The uterus has endometrioid adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation involving the upper endocervix, lower uterine segment, and uterine corpus. Intravascular tumor cells are also observed, and there appears to be a single intramural leiomyoma. The report also notes the presence of benign fallopian tubes, tubo-ovarian serosal adhesions, reactive mesothelial reaction, and negative malignancy results for different samples. The report comments on the presence of endometrial carcinomas in the left ovary and endometrial tumor involving the endocervical mucosa and stroma. The report also shows that selected slides were used to determine the presence of an ovarian tumor, endocervical stromal invasion, and possible lymphovascular invasion. The report concludes with a histologic type, grade, tumor site, and size determined for the endometrioid adenocarcinoma present in the uterus.

The pathology report describes findings from a surgery involving the removal of the uterus, cervix, bladder, fallopian tubes, and ovaries. The report indicates the presence of complex hyperplasia with atypia, adenomyosis, and multiple leiomyomata. There is uncertainty regarding the involvement of adenoacanthoma. No evidence of metastatic tumors is found through staining and examination of lymph nodes. The report is signed and approved by a medical professional who conducted a personal examination of the materials.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy specimen of uterus, right ovary with a 8.1 cm segment of right fallopian tube, left ovary with a 7.2 cm segment of left fallopian tube, right and left pelvic lymph nodes, right and left para-aortic lymph nodes, and left gonadal vessel. The uterus has endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, FIGO grade I that invades into the myometrium at a depth of 1.0 cm. No diagnostic abnormality is observed in the cervix, ovaries, and fallopian tubes. The lymph nodes and gonadal vessel are negative for tumor.

The pathology report is for a patient named Jeb who underwent a uterus, tubes, and ovaries hysterectomy and salpingo-oophorectomy surgery. The report indicates a grade II endometrial adenocarcinoma found on the right posterior of the uterine fundus, invading 0.4 cm of myometrium with a 2.2 cm myometrium thickness. The lower uterine segment and cervix are not involved in the tumor. The report also notes multiple lymph node excisions that are all negative for tumor, as well as an unremarkable left and right gonadal vessels.

The patient, a 65-year-old with a history of postmenopausal bleeding, underwent total laparoscopic hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node dissection for endometrial adenocarcinoma. The tumor was found to be endometrioid type, FIGO grade 3, with dimensions of 4 x 4 x 1.5 cm. It extended into the lower uterine segment and had invaded 36% of myometrial wall thickness, with a depth of 0.8 mm. There was lymphovascular space involvement, and the endocervix mucosa was positive for tumor. The uterine serosa was negative for tumor, as were the right and left parametrium, right ovary and fallopian tube, and left ovary and fallopian tube (although there was an inclusion cyst of the left ovary). Immunohistochemical stains were performed and were supportive of the above diagnosis. Lymph node dissection showed no tumor identified in the lymph nodes examined.

The pathology report shows a diagnosis of FIGO grade II endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, which has invaded 1.8 cm into the myometrium and involves the left and right tube, but not the bilateral ovaries. One lymph node above the IMA and one below the IMA are positive for tumor, while the other three lymph nodes are negative for tumor. The surgical margins are negative for tumor. An immunohistochemical stain for p53 was negative in tumor cells. The gross description shows a 6.1 x 2.4 x 1.9 cm mass involving the entire endometrial cavity and diffuse adhesions on the uterine serosa. The report suggests that any substantive changes identified on permanent section review will be reflected in a revised report.

The pathology report describes excisions of multiple lymph nodes and tumors in various areas of the body. The identified cancer is adenocarcinoma, endonetriotd type. No metastases were found in lymph nodes examined. Benign adipose tissue was found in some areas. The report suggests that further tests are needed to determine the architectural and nuclear grades of the cancer.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the endometrium, with superficial invasion of myometrium. The tumor shows inner half myometrial invasion with a depth of 2 mm and a wall thickness of 19 mm, and is classified as FIGO grade 2. The cervix/vaginal margin is free of carcinoma and lymphovascular space invasion is not identified. There is no involvement of regional lymph nodes. The patient underwent a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingooophorectomy, and no carcinoma is identified in the lymph nodes or other specimens examined. The pathology stage is pT1b pNO pMx, and the tumor cells show strong nuclear staining for estrogen and progesterone receptors. There are also other findings, such as stromal hyperthecosis in the ovaries and endocervical polyp with chronic inflammation and squamous metaplasia in the cervix. Regarding adnexal involvement, no carcinoma is identified.

The pathology report describes the results of a surgical biopsy of a patient's uterus, cervix, and pelvic lymph nodes. The patient was diagnosed with moderately differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma that has invaded the outer half of the myometrial wall and involved the lower uterine segment mucosa, with focal lymphovascular space invasion and tumor necrosis. The patient underwent a radical hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy. The report indicates that no tumor was found in the removed lymph nodes. The gross description includes detailed measurements and physical characteristics of the tissue specimens submitted for testing. Multiple tissue blocks were taken for further investigation.

The patient underwent a hysterectomy due to a mass identified in the uterus. The pathology report states that she has endometrial adenocarcinoma Type FIGO grade 1 (of 3) that is 1.9 cm in size and has invaded 0.5 cm into the myometrium. The tumor has been identified in the superficial endocervical canal with no lymphovascular space invasion identified. The ectocervical margin is negative by 1.5 cm. The report also states that she has no diagnostic abnormalities in both ovaries and fallopian tubes. Multiple lymph node biopsies have been performed and have tested negative for tumor. The final diagnosis is endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a revised pT1b NO MO staging.

The pathology report indicates the presence of endometrial, endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a FIGO grade of 3. The tumor has invaded the myometrium to a depth of 5.0 mm, and lymphatic/vascular invasion is detected within the myometrium. There is no involvement of the cervix, ovaries, or fallopian tubes. Lymph nodes are non-necrotizing, indicating the possibility of sarcoidosis, and clinical ruling out of infectious causes is suggested. A polypoid mass measuring 5.0 x 4.0 x 2.6 cm and involving the anterior wall of the uterus is also present. The maximum thickness of the myometrium is 3.3 cm. No other lesions are identified.

The pathology report describes findings from a hysterectomy with pelvic and para-aortic lymph node dissection for a patient with malignant neocorpus uteri. The report describes the gross examination of multiple organs and tissues, as well as the microscopic examination. The report notes the presence of endometrioid carcinoma grade II with approximately 50% invasion in the posterior wall of the uterus, as well as nodal involvement. The pathology stage is reported as pT1e pN1 pM. Further details about the extent of the cancer and lymph node involvement are provided in the report. The tissue specimens submitted for evaluation were received fresh and grossed accordingly. The report concludes with additional information required for accreditation by the Commission on Cancer.

The pathology report indicates a malignant neoplasm in the corpus uteri classified as FIGO I endometrioid adenocarcinoma. A supracervical hysterectomy specimen revealed an exophytic 6 x 6 cm brown mass invading 0.1 cm into the myometrium. A well-circumscribed 3 x 3 x 2.7 cm intramural nodule was also noted in the myometrium. The right ovary and fimbriated fallopian tube were received attached, and the surface of the ovary had a lobulated white-tan appearance upon sectioning, with a brownish mass present inside. The left adnexa was received unattached and showed a fimbriated fallopian tube with a white ovary. A smooth exocervix and unremarkable endocervical canal were observed in a 14-gram amputated cervix. Lymph nodes and peritoneal tissue were also received. An intra-operative consultation confirmed mucinous adenocarcinoma in both the unattached and attached ovaries, and FIGO grade I endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the endomyometrium. Pathologic stage is reported as pT3a pNX pMx. The report emphasizes that pathology stage should not be substituted for clinical stage, and only applies to the current tissue specimen evaluated.

The pathology report describes the examination of tissue removed during hysterectomy for endometrial cancer. The report details the examination of lymph nodes and uterine tissue. The lymph nodes dissected from both sides were benign. The tumor in the endometrial cavity was identified as endometrial cancer, with an invasion of more than half of the myometrium. No evidence of lymphovascular space invasion was seen. The cervical margin was negative. The report recommends genomic studies for a yellow tan nodule.

The pathology report describes a case of high-grade serous adenocarcinoma that has spread to various parts of the body, including the ileal mesentery, small bowel serosa, uterus, bilateral ovaries, fallopian tubes, omentum, and peritoneal lining. The cancer has not spread to certain lymph nodes, gonadal vessels, or vaginal margins. The report notes that the cancer is confined to a polyp within the uterus and has not invaded the myometrium or endocervix. Additionally, there are no definite signs of lymphatic/vascular invasion. The report indicates that all surgical resection margins are negative for tumor, and any substantive changes identified on permanent section review will be reflected in a revised report.

The pathology report is for a male patient with endometrial cancer, who underwent a hysterectomy. The report shows that the patient has a G3 serous adenocarcinoma, with more than 50% non-squamous solid growth. The tumor has invaded the outer one-third of the myometrium, and there is venous/lymphatic (large/small vessel) invasion. There are multiple lymph nodes excised for evaluation, and none of them show evidence of malignancy. The omental nodule was cutting poorly during the intraoperative consultation. Overall, the report indicates the presence of an aggressive form of endometrial cancer.

The pathology report describes the presence of a high-grade Mullerian-derived endometrial adenocarcinoma with associated malignant squamous changes in the uterus and cervix. The tumor has invaded more than 50% of the myometrium and is staged as pT1b NO. The report mentions various other findings including benign adnexa, leiomyomas, adenomyosis, and benign endometrial polyps. The lymph nodes and omentum are free of metastatic carcinoma. Surgical margins are uninvolved by invasive carcinoma, and there is no involvement of other organs. The pathology report includes synoptic information and a macroscopic and microscopic description of the specimen.

The patient has undergone a hysterectomy due to a malignant neoplasm in the corpus uteri. The pathology report indicates the presence of endometrioid adenocarcinoma in the endometrium with no myometrial invasion or vascular invasion and a size of 0.3 x 3.5 x 0.4 cm. The tumor has also extended to the cervix but there is no stromal invasion. The report also states that there were no malignancies found in the peritoneal biopsy, bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes, or lymph nodes. The pathology stage is pT1aN0.

The pathology report describes the examination of a uterus, cervix, fallopian tubes, ovaries, and pelvic lymph nodes of a 55-year-old woman with stage I endometrial carcinoma. The report reveals the presence of multiple leiomyomata, a neoplasm composed of irregular glands with prominent desmoplastic stromal reaction, and endometriosis in the examined organs. The endometrial adenocarcinoma is graded FIGO 2/3, with myometrial invasion limited to less than 1 194 of the thickness of the myometrium and no vascular invasion or cervical involvement. All surgical margins are free of tumor, and no evidence of malignancy is found in the examined lymph nodes.

The pathology report is discussing the results of immunohistochemical studies for p16 and p53 on a patient with endometrial adenocarcinoma. The report also details the final diagnosis of the patient's total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, which revealed endometrial adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type, FIGO grade 1, invading 15 cm of a 2 cm-thick myometrium. The report lists the involvement of other organs and lymph nodes and mentions the absence of metastatic carcinoma in pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes, with one group of carcinoma cells in a lymphatic space noted. The report also includes the absence of carcinoma and the presence of cystitis cystica-like inverted papilloma in a bladder biopsy. The primary tumor is classified as pTlb (IB), and no regional lymph node metastasis is present.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymphadenectomy for a patient with poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the corpus uteri. The uterus contained multiple tumor nodules that appeared to invade full thickness of the myometrium. Lymph node specimens were also taken and two of three right paraaortic lymph nodes were positive for metastatic carcinoma. The left ovary contained two pale nodules and both fallopian tubes had paratubal cysts. The report includes block summaries and information on the pathology stage, which was reported as pr2 pN2 pMK. The report notes that the pathology stage is based solely on the current tissue specimen being evaluated and should not be confused with or substituted for the clinical stage.

The pathology report describes a diagnosis of invasive endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, FIGO grade I. The cancer has invaded 0.6 cm into the myometrium but has not spread to the lymph nodes or surrounding tissues. The report includes information on the size and location of the tumor and provides details on the surgical resection margins and lymph node dissection. Gross and microscopic descriptions are also included.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a robotic-assisted radical hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and pelvic lymphadenectomy due to endometrioid adenocarcinoma. The tumor was found on the posterior uterine surface and measured 4.0 cm in its greatest dimension with 10% myometrial invasion and a depth of invasion of 2 mm. The histologic grade was FIGO grade 1. There was no involvement of the cervix or other organs. One reactive lymph node was found in the right side parametria, and three reactive lymph nodes were found in both left and right pelvic lymph node dissections. The report suggests that the tumor was contained in the uterus and staging was determined as pT1a with no lymph node involvement. Other additional pathologic findings included cervicitis, leiomyomas, and ovarian/tubal tube adhesions.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, in a hysterectomy specimen. The tumor measures 6.6 x 6.2 x 1.6 cm and invades the myometrium to a depth of 0.8 cm. Lymphovascular space invasion is not identified and the margins are negative for tumor. The report also mentions excision of multiple pelvic lymph nodes, which are negative for tumor. Overall, the diagnosis is FIGO grade I (of III) endometrial adenocarcinoma.

The pathology report describes a malignant tumor in the uterus, identified as endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type, that has invaded 0.5 cm into the myometrium and circumferentially involves the endometrial cavity. Lymphovascular space invasion is not identified, and the margins are negative for tumor. There is also a benign strumal carcinoid in the left ovary and a leiomyoma in the uterus. The lymph nodes tested are negative for tumor. The report includes gross descriptions of the tissue samples received for analysis.

The pathology report describes a surgical consultation for a patient with adenocarcinoma in their left fallopian tube and ovary, with less than 50% myometrial invasion and no regional lymph node involvement. No distant metastases were found, and there were no additional pathological findings. Adjuvant treatment history of the patient is unknown. The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of serous adenocarcinoma of the endometrium in stage 2, with lymphovascular invasion and involvement of approximately 85% of the myometrium. There was also invasion of endocervical glands and cervical stroma. None of the examined lymph nodes showed evidence of tumour metastasis, and the omentum was negative for tumour, with a focal mesothelial proliferation that was suspicious for malignancy. The tumour had a nuclear grade of 3 and involved 80% of the endometrial surface. The report also mentions the absence of lymph node tissue in some of the examined areas.

The pathology report describes the results of a laparoscopic-assisted vaginal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and excision of soft tissue masses in a patient with primary uterine adenocarcinoma of endometrioid and high-grade serous types. The tumor involves mainly the uterine fundus and corpus with minimal myometrial invasion and no lymphatic or blood vessel invasion. There is no evidence of metastasis in the ovaries or fallopian tubes. Other findings include leiomyomas, adenomyosis, benign endocervical polyp, and atrophic changes in the ovaries and fallopian tubes. The correction was made to remove a redundant phrase and a typographical error.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial adenocarcinoma with mixed endometrioid and serous types, FIGO grade 3, detected within a polypoid mass in the posterior wall of the uterus along with multiple sessile lesions on the anterior and lateral walls also showing endometrioid and serous adenocarcinoma, superficially invading the myometrium to a depth of 0.1 cm. A benign endometrial polyp is also present. The report confirms that the lymph nodes, gonadal vessels, and omentum are negative for tumor infiltration. The report indicates that the final diagnosis was made with the help of both gross/macroscopic examination and tissue histology, which involved the use of Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) staining. The report also notes that any substantive changes will be reflected in a revised report, based on the permanent section review.

The pathology report indicates the presence of invasive carcinoma in the uterus, left fallopian tube and ovary, with a tumor invading more than half of the myometrium. No carcinoma is found in any of the lymph nodes that were examined, including those in the external and internal iliac, obturator, and para-aortic regions. The report also notes excision of soft tissue tumors in the right para-aortic region and left myfogastric lymph node, both negative for carcinoma. The report is electronically signed by the pathologist who examined the slides and materials.

The patient presented with severe anemia and menometrorrhagia, and a possible diagnosis of endometrial cancer. The pathology report confirms the diagnosis of endometrial adenocarcinoma with involvement of the cervix, parametrium, and pelvic lymph nodes. The tumor is a poorly differentiated carcinoma with a grade 3 FIGO score and a size of 11x5x3 cm. The myometrium is invaded more than 2/3 of its thickness, and there is lymphovascular invasion. Frozen section analysis of implants in the omentum and ileum show benign cysts and fibrous tissue with keratin granulomas, respectively. The right and left ovaries and tubes are negative for malignancy. The final staging is 3a, N1, M1, Stage VB.

The patient has been diagnosed with uterine cancer, specifically an invasive endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a histologic grade of FIGO grade 3. The tumor is located in the anterior and posterior endometrium, including the lower uterine segment, with extension to involve the endocervix. The cancer has a solid growth pattern in more than 5% of the tumor, with maximal depth of invasion of 1.1cm. Endocervical stromal invasion and lymphatic invasion are seen. Parametrial tissue does not appear involved. The bilateral ovaries and fallopian tubes are uninvolved by tumor and demonstrate atrophic features.

The pathology report describes the findings of a surgical procedure on the patient's lymph nodes, uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes, and bilateral ovaries. Several poorly defined nodules are found in the lymph nodes, while the uterus and cervix are moderately distorted by nodules. The report also describes the size and appearance of the organs and tissues evaluated during the procedure. Some nodules have a fibrotic cut surface, while others are tan-yellow with fatty cut surfaces. The report provides instructions for the submission of tissue samples for further analysis.

The report describes a case of adenocarcinoma in the uterus, cervix, tubes, and ovaries in a patient who underwent a hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node sampling. The tumor was categorized as high-grade and grade 3 and had invaded through more than half of the myometrium. Six intramural nodules and paratubal cysts in the left and right tubes were also noted. Multiple lymph nodes were biopsied, including from the pelvic and aortic regions. The report includes information on the size, location, and color of various specimens and blocks of tissue that were submitted for analysis. The pathologic stage was determined to be pTIb pN2 paw, based on the current tissue specimen being evaluated.

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

- Adenocarcinoma is also present in the myometrium through direct extension and leiomyomas are identified.
- No carcinoma is detected in the vagina, right ovary, and right fallopian tube.

- The omentum shows no carcinoma.

- Resection margins are free of tumor.

The pathology report reveals a diagnosis of residual endometrial adenocarcinoma, endometrioid type with mucinous differentiation, located in the left cornu and posterior aspect of the uterine fundus with myometrial invasion. No residual papillary serous component is identified, and lymphovascular space invasion is not identified. The report also mentions a peritoneal inclusion cyst in the right ovary and a serous cystadenoma in the left ovary with unremarkable fallopian tubes. The preliminary frozen section consultation confirms invasive endometrial adenocarcinoma. The report includes a block summary of the sections submitted.

The pathology report describes a surgical pathology examination of a cervical tumor removed from a patient. The tumor was found to be a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with focal squamoid differentiation and extensive lymph-vascular invasion. The cancer was diagnosed as endometrioid adenocarcinoma from the lower uterine segment with infiltration of the cervical stromal connective tissue and no distant metastasis. The report includes information on the size, extent, and margins of the tumor, as well as immunohistochemical patterns. The patient underwent a radical hysterectomy and lymph node dissection, with all lymph nodes reported as benign. The report also notes the presence of follicular cysts, adenomyosis, and a paratubal cyst. The report suggests a possible association between endometrial carcinoma of the lower uterine segment and Lynch syndrome.

The pathology report describes the excision of a uterus with right ovary, 3cm of right fallopian tube, left ovary, 5cm of left fallopian tube, lymph nodes, and mesentery biopsies. The uterine mass is determined to be an endometrial adenocarcinoma of the endometrioid type with squamous differentiation, FIGO grade III. The tumor has invaded through the myometrium to a depth of 1.5 cm. The lower uterine segment and cervix are also involved by the tumor. Metastatic carcinoma is present in a single right obturator and a single left external iliac pelvic lymph node. Multiple other lymph nodes and biopsies are negative for tumor. Immunohistochemical stains and HPV in situ hybridization confirm the neoplastic cells are positive for estrogen receptor and vimentin, negative for progesterone receptor and pCEA, and negative for HPV. The ovaries and fallopian tubes are without diagnostic abnormalities.

The pathology report describes a case of primary endometrial cancer in a  year-old female who underwent a hysterectomy. The cancer is identified as endometrioid adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation and a FIGO grade 3. The tumor invades mostly the inner half of the myometrium, with a depth of 3mm and a percent of 20. No involvement was identified in the serosal, lower uterine segment, cervical, and adnexal areas, and no tumor was identified in the adnexal and lymph nodes removed during the surgery. The frozen-section diagnosis confirmed the presence of endometrioid adenocarcinoma with a FIGO grade 2. The right and left ovaries, fallopian tubes, and lymph nodes did not contain any tumors. Adenomyosis is present, and no other pathologic findings are noted.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial cancer involving the uterine corpus with no evidence of cervical or adnexal involvement. The tumor is a well-differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma with squamous differentiation, limited to the endometrium and with focal extension into superficial adenomyosis. Myometrial invasion, serosal involvement, and lymphovascular space invasion are not identified. Lymph nodes from the pelvic and periaortic regions are negative for carcinoma, and other non-neoplastic findings are present, including adenomyosis, leiomyoma, and secretory endometrium. Immunohistochemistry for estrogen and progesterone receptor status is pending. The final pathology stage is pT1a pNO pMx, with a FIGO Stage grouping of 1A. The report also includes descriptions of gross appearances and findings from various specimens submitted for examination.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent surgery to remove the fallopian tubes and ovaries due to suspected malignancy. The report confirms the presence of endometrial tumor invasion in the myometrium. Several lymph nodes were also removed and tested, with several found to be benign. Overall, the diagnosis is based on the exam and other materials reviewed by the pathologist.

The pathology report describes the findings from a surgical resection of the uterus, ovaries, and fallopian tubes. The right ovary had a mature cystic teratoma, while the left ovary had a microscopic mature cystic teratoma. The report notes the presence of moderately differentiated endometrioid adenocarcinoma that involves approximately 90% of the endometrial surface and has penetrated up to 80% of the myometrial thickness. Four pelvic lymph nodes and one left periaortic lymph node were free of tumor. The report provides information on the histologic grade, architectural grade, tumor size, and depth of invasion, and notes the presence of atypical hyperplasia. The report does not provide a FIGO stage.

The pathology report describes findings from a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy procedure for a patient with endometrial adenocarcinoma. The report indicates that the cancer is grade 1 and has invaded the myometrium and blood vessels. Lymph node biopsies were taken from multiple sites, including the obturator lymph nodes, iliac lymph nodes, para-aortic lymph nodes, and common iliac lymph nodes. Overall, there were multiple benign lymph nodes, but also a few lymph nodes that showed no evidence of cancer. An addendum confirms the diagnosis based on the pathologist's personal examination of slides and other materials.

The report describes a surgical procedure for endometrial cancer. A frozen section sample of omental biopsy suggests carcinoma, which is confirmed by subsequent tests. The gross description reveals yellow-tan fatty tissue with no nodules or lesions. The uterus, cervix, adnexa, ovaries, and fallopian tubes are also examined with representative samples submitted for genomic studies. Lymph nodes are also examined from the pelvic and aortic regions. Further details are provided on the size and location of the tumor, the involvement of myometrium and fibrous nodules, and depth of invasion.

The report describes a uterine mass measuring 5x3x3 cm that appears to be a tumor extending from the endocervical canal into the lower uterine segment and exhibiting tumor extension into the deep cervical stroma which abuts the paracervical soft tissue margin. The tumor extends and involves the external cervical os. In addition to the mass, there is an endometrial polyp located at the fundal region and multiple intramural myomatous nodules measuring up to 0.6 x 0.6 x 0.5 cm.
