One benign lymph node was found in the right external iliac region, and the omentum (a fatty tissue in the abdominal cavity) was negative for metastatic tumor cells. The report confirms the diagnosis made based on examination of tissue samples, and no evidence of malignancy was found in the stains performed for hormones and markers.

The pathology report is from a surgical procedure performed on a female patient with suspected carcinosarcoma. The specimen included the uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries, upper vagina, and lymph nodes from various locations. The report confirms the presence of malignant mixed Mullerian tumor (carcinosarcoma) in the endometrial polyp, with predominantly carcinomatous areas. There is also a focal uterine intraepithelial serous carcinoma. No abnormality was found in the left fallopian tube, and the right fallopian tube was found to have hydrosalpinx. Benign fibroconnective tissue with endosalpingiosis was found in the rectovaginal septum. No malignancy was found in any of the lymph nodes except for the small bowel mesentery node, which was negative for malignancy. The report includes a history of the patient's diagnosis and a summary of the surgical procedure, and identifies the received specimens for examination.

The report describes a case of carcinosarcoma with heterologous elements affecting the uterus and characterized by diffuse tumor site, a tumor size of approximately 10 x 8 x 2 cm, and lymphatic/vascular invasion. The tumor is present within 1 mm of the serosal surface, and while there is no myometrial invasion evident, a similar point of closest approach is seen. The cervix is negative for tumor, as are both the right and left ovaries and fallopian tubes. The malignancy is consistent with the carcinomatous component of a mixed mullerian tumor. The posterior vaginal margins are negative for malignancy. Clinical correlation is needed.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a malignant neoplasm in the corpus uteri and a cervical mass with high-grade sarcoma. The uterus tumor is a carcinosarcoma, with dimensions of 7x6.5x5 cm and a maximum depth of invasion of 1.2 cm in a 3.2 cm thick wall. There is no lymphatic/vascular invasion, and the mitoses rate is 1/10 HPFs. The endometrium is quiescent with a small leiomyoma. There is a 1 mm tumor metastasis in the deep wall just at the junction of the lower uterine segment and cervix. The specimen margins are not involved. Metastatic/implanted tumors were found in the pelvic sidewall, bilateral ovaries, and extensive omentum. The tumor has various histologies, including areas resembling clear cell cancer, alveolar soft part sarcoma, and undifferentiated sarcoma with few osteoclasts.

The pathology report shows that a person identified as Leos-B has been diagnosed with high-grade carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Mullerian tumor) in their uterus. The tumor fills the endometrial cavity and invades the lower uterine segment and cervical canal. The tumor is also found to invade 2.5 cm into the myometrium and angiolymphatic invasion is identified. The report also mentions the presence of a calcified subserosal leiomyoma. The preliminary frozen section consultation suggests that the high-grade carcinoma is likely serous vs carcinosarcoma, and further examination is required to classify it on permanent sections.

The pathology report describes a case of malignant mixed mesodermal tumor (MMMT) involving the uterus, bilateral tubes, and ovaries. The tumor has extensively invaded the uterine wall, penetrated the serosa, and also involved other tissues such as the left parametrium and omentum. The right ovary has a focal parenchymal involvement, and the right fallopian tube shows surface involvement and foci of epithelial dysplasia. The left ovary has surface fibrin and detached tumor cell clusters, and the left fallopian tube shows adhesions with foci of atypia and mild hydrosalpinx. The diagnosis includes a malignant epithelial component of mixed high-grade serous and endometrioid adenocarcinoma along with a sarcomatous component of high-grade pleomorphic sarcoma with features suggestive of a rhabdoid differentiation and fibrosarcomatous-type differentiation. The stage of the cancer is pT3a Nx Mx.

The pathology report describes the case of a patient who underwent a total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and the specimens submitted included the cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes, ovaries, and lymph nodes. The diagnosis was a malignancy of the endometrium, specifically a carcinosarcoma, which invaded more than half of the myometrium with no endocervical invasion. The lymph nodes located in the right obturator, left external iliac, left common iliac, and right hypogastric were negative for metastatic tumor except for two benign lymph nodes in the right hypogastric lymph node and one benign lymph node in the right external iliac lymph node. There are pending deeper sections of the left common iliac lymph node. An addendum report was added concerning the examination of the uterine tissue at the request of the clinician but specific information is not provided.

The report is a clinical case report for the collection of cancerous tissue. The patient has presented with symptoms of vaginal bleeding and the clinical findings indicate blood in the vaginal area. The report includes the patient's medical history, medications, social history, family medical history, and diagnostic studies, as well as the surgical treatment and pathological staging. The report notes the presence of lymph nodes and indicates the distance to NAT (not available) and the time to LNZ (lymph node zone). The report does not indicate a specific diagnosis.

The pathology report shows that the patient had a hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to endometrial carcinosarcoma with heterologous elements (chondrosarcoma) limited to the endometrium. The report also indicates lymph node dissections in various regions, with only benign lymph nodes identified. The tumor has not invaded the myometrium or vascular space, and there is no involvement of other organs or distant metastasis. Pathologic staging shows PT1a NO. The report includes additional information about the size, location, and histologic type of the tumor, as well as special stains and procedures used. Several lymph nodes were examined and found to be benign, with no involvement by invasive carcinoma or lymphovascular invasion identified.

The pathology report outlines a diagnosis of adenocarcinomas present in multiple organs, including the sigmoid nodule, uterus and cervix, fallopian tubes, ovaries, cul-de-sac, and omentum. The high-grade component is predominantly serous with focal clear cell areas. There is extensive lymphovascular invasion by the high-grade carcinoma, and the adenocarcinoma extends into the cervical stroma. Despite the presence of adenocarcinoma in multiple sites, the appendix appears unremarkable. Several lymph nodes were examined, with varying degrees of metastatic carcinoma identified. The pathological stage is pT3 pN2 Mx. The breast tumor immunohistology results showed positive hormone receptors for estrogen and progesterone. The synoptic summary indicates the tumor type is a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor with a carcinoma and carcinosarcoma component and involves several structures. The lymph node status is not clear, except for the presence of metastatic carcinoma in several lymph nodes.

The report states that the omentum (a tissue layer in the abdomen) removed during surgery was benign (not cancerous). However, the uterus and bilateral adnexa (tissues connected to the uterus, such as ovaries and fallopian tubes) showed a malignant mixed mullerian tumor (carcinosarcoma) with two large tumors measuring 8.5 x 5.2 and 3.1 x 3.0 cm. The tumors showed a polypoid growth pattern with invasion of 35% of myometrium depth and lymphovascular invasion. Squamous metaplasia was noted in the cervix without tumor involvement, as well as a leiomyoma (a benign smooth muscle tumor) and adenomyosis (a benign condition where endometrial tissue grows into the muscle of the uterus). Surgical margins were clear of cancer. The left and right ovaries showed benign serous cystadenofibroma and the right fallopian tube had a hydrosalpinx while the left fallopian tube had paratubal cysts. Biopsies of the pelvic lymph nodes showed no metastatic malignancy. The tumor was confirmed by immunostains and was classified as a carcinosarcoma. The uterus had a maximum dimension of 8.5 cm and involved 60% of the anterior endomyometrium and 90% of the posterior endomyometrium. The depth of invasion was less than 1/2 of the myometrium thickness and there was angiolympathic invasion. The report states a pathologic T stage of "ori," pathologic N stage of "ph," and pathologic M stage of "pMX," with a FIGO stage of 8. The diagnosis was carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed mesodermal tumor).

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial cancer in a  year-old female with no tumors identified in the examined lymph nodes. The tumor was found to be a carcinosarcoma with heterologous elements, specifically mixed serous and endometrioid adenocarcinoma and undifferentiated sarcoma, with myometrial invasion into the inner half and mild lymphovascular space invasion present in rare foci. The gross examination revealed leiomyomata, adenomyosis, and vascular calcifications. The cancer was staged as pT1la pNO and FIGO (2008 classification) Stage grouping: IA. The report also states that the immunostains performed on a representative section of the tumor failed to show staining for myogenin and therefore do not support a rhabdomyosarcomatous component to the tumor.

The pathology report describes the diagnosis of a patient's uterine cancer. The report indicates that the patient had a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and the pathology examination revealed a tumor exhibiting carcinomatous and sarcomatous differentiation consistent with carcinosarcoma with heterologous elements. The tumor involves the lower uterine segment and cervix. The AJCC pathologic stage is pT2 pNx, and the FIGO stage grouping is II. The report also notes the presence of a small focus of glandular tissue suspicious for carcinoma in the cervix. The estrogen and progesterone receptor immunohistochemistry results are pending. The report concludes with a description of the gross specimen received, including the size, weight, and appearance of the specimens.

The pathology report describes a malignant mixed tumor (MMMT) of the endometrium, consisting of a high-grade endometrioid carcinomatous component and a homologous sarcomatous component. The tumor involves greater than 30% of the endometrial surface with extensive necrosis and endocervical mucosa involvement. Lymphovascular space invasion is present, and the pelvic washing is positive for tumor cells. Pelvic lymph nodes and periaortic lymph nodes are negative, and the omentum biopsy shows benign fibroadipose tissue. The tumor is moderately differentiated, grade 3, and has a maximum dimension of 10 cm, with posterior and anterior endomyometrium involvement. The immunohistochemistry report shows the positivity of actin, muscle-specific, angi/aB3, cam 5.2, desmin, and vimentin antigens/antibodies associated with the carcinomatous and sarcomatous components of the tumor. The FIGO stage is A.

The pathology report describes a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor with heterologous differentiation found in a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy specimen. The tumor was 7.5 x 7.0 x 2.0 cm in size, invading 50% into the myometrium and confined to the uterus. No involvement of lymphovascular spaces was found. The margins were negative for tumor. Severe epithelial atypia was found in both fallopian tubes, but the ovaries were unremarkable. Multiple lymph nodes were examined, and all were negative for tumor. Frozen sections were taken and were consistent with the final diagnosis. A permanent review of the specimen is recommended.

The pathology report reveals a diagnosis of malignant mixed Mullerian tumor involving about 70% of the endometrial surface and extending into the lower uterine segment and right lateral endocervical canal with full thickness penetration into the serosa and right parametrium. The report also notes involvement of the vaginal margin, uterine serosa, and lymphovascular permeation. Metastasis of the tumor is found in the soft tissue of the right parametrium with extracapsular extension and in the lymph nodes of the right common iliac, right periaortic, and right external iliac regions. The report also indicates the presence of endometrial polyp, adenomyosis, and leiomyomas. The tumor is classified as carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Mullerian tumor), poorly differentiated with a nuclear grade of 3 and involving the cervical stroma and vagina. The pathology also reports positive margins for the vaginal margin and parametrium. The patient has stage IIIC1 carcinosarcoma according to the Figo staging system.

The pathology report shows that the submitted lymph node was found to have two benign lymph nodes and metastatic serous adenocarcinoma to the omentum. The patient had undergone a total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy for adenomyosis.

The pathology report indicates the presence of metastatic carcinosarcoma in multiple lymph nodes, including the left external iliac lymph node, right obturator lymph node, and one of two lymph nodes in the left pelvis. The lymph nodes also show marked follicular hyperplasia, and further testing is being done to classify the carcinomas. Benign fibroadipose tissue was found in other areas, and some lymph nodes were negative for carcinoma. Various molecular studies were conducted, and the pattern is consistent with reactive changes.

The pathology report describes a case of a uterine carcinosarcoma, homologous type, with grade 3 histologic characteristics. The tumor is located in the posterior endometrium and shows myometrial invasion with lymphovascular space involvement. The report also mentions the absence of involvement in other areas such as the serosa, lower uterine segment, cervical, and adnexal areas. The cervix is described as having Nabothian cysts and chronic inflammation. The report provides information on the pathology stages and lymph node involvement, and notes the presence of multiple leiomyomas and benign inclusion cysts in the reproductive organs. Immunohistochemistry shows weakly-positive estrogen receptor and positive progesterone receptor in the epithelial component of the tumor. The report also includes a description of the macroscopic features of the specimen.

The pathology report describes a case of stage IIIC2 endometrial cancer in a 51-year-old female. The tumor was found to be a malignant mixed mullerian tumor with heterologous elements and Grade 3 histologic type. There was minimal myometrial invasion but extensive lymphovascular space invasion and lymph node involvement. The tumor was present in the posterior endometrium but not in the lower uterine segment or cervix. There was no serosal involvement and the cervical/vaginal margins were widely negative. The report also noted the presence of leiomyomata and endometrial intraepithelial carcinoma. The patient underwent hysterectomy and right salpingo-oophorectomy, and multiple lymph node dissections were performed, with a total of 13 lymph nodes involved out of 18 examined. The patient's right fallopian tube and ovary showed age-related changes and benign inclusion cysts, with prior tubal ligation evident on the right fallopian tube.  An immunohistochemical stain for myogenin was performed and was supportive of the diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a patient with metastatic carcinosarcoma in the left paracolic gutter nodule and malignant mixed Mullerian tumor in the uterus, left and right fallopian tubes, and ovaries. Lymphovascular space invasion is identified and there are multiple leiomyomas in the myometrium. The lymph nodes in the left and right pelvic, right para-aortic, and left para-aortic areas, as well as the gonadal vessels, are negative for tumor. A metastatic carcinosarcoma is also found in the mesentery sigmoid. The appendix does not show any diagnostic abnormality. The final pathology report is subject to revision pending permanent section review.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor of the endometrium with heterologous elements (high-grade carcinosarcoma). The tumor invades more than half of the myometrium, and extensive vascular invasion is observed. No endocervical or lower uterine segment invasion is identified. The report also notes the presence of leiomyomas, atrophy of the uninvolved endometrium, and chronic cervicitis with squamous metaplasia in the cervix. In addition, the right and left adnexa do not show evidence of malignancy. The final stage is determined to be pT1eNxMx, based on the material examined. Further deeper sections were examined, and representative sections were taken for each specimen.

The report is a pathological diagnosis of a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, indicating the presence of a carcinosarcoma with serous carcinoma and homologous sarcomatous component in multiple locations including the endometrium, lower uterine segment, and posterior upper endocervix. The tumor size ranges between 6.5 x 6.4 x 4.5 cm and 9.2 x 8.9 x 3.0 cm. Myometrial invasion is present in the outer half with a depth of 6.5 mm and a wall thickness of 1.3 cm with 50% involvement, and lymphovascular space invasion is present. The report also notes one lymph node with metastatic serous carcinoma. Recommendations for further correlation with operative procedures and immunohistochemistry stains have been made. Other findings include mild acute and chronic cervicitis, nabothian cyst, hyalinized leiomyomata, atrophy and chronic endometritis in endometrium, and medial calcification of vessels in the adnexal area. Clinical history indicates that the patient is a 71-year-old female with endometrial cancer.

The pathology report describes a case of malignant mixed Mullerian tumor involving the uterus, cervix, right fallopian tube, and right ovary. The tumor has invaded the myometrium to a depth of 17mm and the cervical glands and stroma with maximal cervical invasion of 15mm. Lymphovascular invasion is present. The report also notes additional findings such as leiomyomas, endosalpingiosis in left pelvic lymph nodes, and an unremarkable left obturator lymph node. The carcinomatous component of the tumor consists predominantly of high-grade endometrioid carcinoma with sex cord-like differentiation and focal papillary serous carcinoma. The stromal component consists predominantly of unclassified high-grade sarcoma with focal cartilaginous differentiation. A parovarian cyst is present in the right ovary. The report includes a detailed gross description of the pathology and a comment on the tumor's composition.

The pathology report states that the patient has a uterine malignant mixed Mullerian tumor with invasion of 80 mm into a 240 mm thick myometrium. Lymphovascular invasion is also present. The report describes no tumor present in the cervix, bilateral ovaries and tubes, and lymph nodes. The tumor is predominantly a high-grade carcinoma composed of undifferentiated carcinoma and high-grade serous carcinoma. The sarcomatous component has heterologous elements (malignant cartilage), and the myoinvasive component is exclusively composed of carcinoma. The report includes the gross description and section code of the uterus, cervix, bilateral ovaries and tubes, pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes, and omentum. The report also provides clinical history and SNOMED codes.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a hysterectomy due to a borderline malignant mixed Müllerian tumor that invaded over half of the myometrium in the uterus, with endocervical invasion. Biopsies of various lymph nodes and organs were also taken, with benign findings in most areas, except for metastatic carcinoma in 3 out of 2 lymph nodes. Additional staining and tests were done on some of the lymph nodes and there was no evidence of metastatic tumor. An addendum was made to the report reflecting this information.

The pathology report describes the diagnosis of a malignant mixed Müllerian tumor/carcinosarcoma with cartilaginous elements in the uterus, cervix and bilateral adnexa of a 54-year-old female who underwent hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and omentectomy due to a pelvic mass. The tumor invaded the outer half of the myometrium and had a thickness of 1.8 cm. Lymphovascular invasion was present, but adnexal involvement was absent. The cervical/vaginal margin was widely negative, and there were no significant findings in the fallopian tubes, ovaries or lymph nodes. The pathology stage was pT1b pNX pMX, and the FIGO stage grouping was 1B. Additionally, benign Nabothian cysts were found in the cervix, and atrophic pattern was observed in the endometrium. The omentum showed a lipoma with fat necrosis and calcifications, but no malignancy was identified.

The pathology report is for a patient who has undergone a removal of uterus, cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes, ovaries, and lymph nodes. The tumor type found in the uterus is carcinosarcoma with homologous myometrial invasion. The tumor has a high proliferative index and is negative for immunostains of Synaptophysin and Chromogranin. The lymph nodes removed during surgery showed no evidence of metastasis. The report also states that the immunchistochentstry and ISM tests were conducted for clinical purposes only and should not be regarded as investigational or for research. The report was reviewed and approved.

The pathology report describes a case of a 73-year-old woman who underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node dissection due to a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor (MMMT) with heterologous differentiation involving the lower uterine segment. The tumor also extended to the cervix and invaded to a depth of 13 mm into the myometrial layer. Lymphovascular invasion was identified along with metastasis to 2 out of 6 pelvic lymph nodes, with extracapsular extension. However, no malignancy was found in the ovaries and left lymph nodes. A skin excision showed only a dermal scar. Overall, the report indicates a high-grade malignancy with aggressive behavior and a potential for metastasis.

The pathology report describes a case of uterine carcinosarcoma with a homologous sarcoma component and endometrioid carcinoma with squamous differentiation and serous carcinoma. The tumor had invaded the outer half of the myometrium with up to 63% involvement and had not spread to regional lymph nodes. No other sites were affected by the tumor. The estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor status of the tumor was negative in the serous carcinoma component and positive in the endometrioid component. The patient had postmenopausal bleeding and was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma on PAP and endometrial biopsy with carcinosarcoma. Some benign changes were noticed in the ovaries and fallopian tubes, but these areas were not affected by cancer.

The pathology report indicates the presence of metastatic high-grade serous carcinoma in the omentum, uterus, left tube and ovary, and on the bladder peritoneum. The report also suggests the presence of a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor originating from the endometrium with less than 50% depth of myometrial invasion and necrosis. Additionally, the report identifies the presence of lymphovascular invasion and uterine angiomyolipoma. The report suggests that the tumor has invaded superficial myometrium, but cervical involvement is not identified. Lymph nodes were not sampled, and it appears difficult to assess the margins of the specimen. Paritoneal cytology was positive, indicating tumors present in the peritoneum. Finally, the pathology report presents measurements and provides a gross description of the specimens.

The pathology report describes a laparoscopic total hysterectomy with salpingo-oophorectomy for a malignant neoplasm in the corpus uteri. The tumor is described as a 4.5 x 4.4 x 1.5 cm exophytic and polypoid mass that invades through the entire myometrium to the serosal surface, with focal features suggestive of carcinosarcoma. Myometrial invasion is present to 2.1 cm into a 2.1 cm thick myometrium. There are multiple well-circumscribed nodules in both the anterior and posterior uterus, ranging from 0.3 cm to 1.6 cm in greatest dimension. The cervix and endocervix are grossly uninvolved. The serosa is smooth, tan, and glistening with no tumor implants grossly apparent. Right and left ovaries are grossly uninvolved, with the right fallopian tube diffusely enlarged and the left fallopian tube appearing fimbriated with a pinpoint lumen. Lymph nodes from the left obturator and left external iliac are identified and submitted for analysis. Special studies were not prospectively ordered.

The pathology report describes the examination of a 186-gram uterus with endometrial cancer and a tumor that has arisen from the anterior wall. The tumor is a 6.0 x 3.5 x 1.0 cm carcinosarcoma with a depth of invasion of less than 2 mm in a 2.3 cm thick wall. There is no lymphatic or vascular invasion, and adjacent non-neoplastic endometrium is absent. The cervix has a nodule of tumor on the mucosa but is not invasive into the wall. Additionally, multiple lymph nodes and the ovary are examined, but no significant findings are noted other than a small ovarian cyst. The report suggests that there is likely a need for further treatment and monitoring for the endometrial cancer.

The pathology report details the diagnosis and findings of surgical samples taken from a female patient who underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The report notes the primary diagnosis of a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor involving multiple areas of the uterus, including the cervix and endometrium, as well as metastatic tumors in the omentum and vagina. No abnormalities were found in the ovaries or fallopian tubes. The report also notes the lack of definitive cervical tissue in the multiple sections examined. Samples from the prolapsed cervical tumor showed no definitive cervical tissue, and samples from the uterus and cervix showed a polypoid mass measuring 6 x 6 x 5 cm with a predominance of sarcomatoid elements and glandular patterns.

The pathology report indicates the presence of endometriotic cysts in both the right and left ovaries. Biopsies of lymph nodes in various locations were conducted, and no metastatic nodes were found. The lymph nodes in the external iliac, obturator, and hypogastric regions were examined. A biopsy of the right breast tissue was performed but is not included in this report. The report was reviewed and approved.

The pathology report describes a case of uterine malignant mixed mullerian tumor with a high-grade carcinomatous component of mixed endometrioid and papillary serous carcinoma, as well as a high-grade sarcomatoid carcinoma with no heterologous elements identified. The tumor invaded greater than or equal to one-half of the myometrium and had lymphovascular invasion. The report also describes lymph node sampling, with no evidence of malignancy in the pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes. Further findings include leiomyomas and a tumor with large areas of necrosis. Immunohistochemistry studies were conducted, with mixed results. Representative samples were received for further analysis. Overall, the patient was diagnosed with stage PT1b uterine cancer, with no regional lymph node metastasis.

The patient underwent a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy due to a malignant mesodermal tumor. The tumor invaded the myometrium and was composed of high-grade serous carcinoma with a component of rhabdomyosarcoma. Metastatic carcinoma was found in the lateral ovaries, fallopian tubes, bladder peritoneum, omentum, and rectal serosa. The report includes findings from multiple biopsies, and lymph node involvement is noted. The report also includes information on the appearance and size of the specimen.

The pathology report describes a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor (carcinosarcoma) in an endometrial polyp, with superficial myometrial invasion present. The tumor extends to the lower uterine segment, but does not involve the cervix, and there is no lymphovascular space invasion identified. The report also notes that there is no tumor present in the bilateral ovaries, lateral fallopian tubes, or any of the lymph nodes sampled (pelvic and para-aortic). A few other findings, such as adenomyosis and an intramural fibroid, are also mentioned. The report includes a detailed description of the specimen and how it was sectioned and submitted for analysis. Two specific tissue blocks (A18 and A27) are recommended for future molecular diagnostic testing if needed.

The pathology report describes the findings of a hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and lymph node excisions. The report indicates the presence of endometrial carcinoma, with invasion of the endocervix and some lymph nodes. The cervix is unresectable, but the ovary shows an inclusion cyst. Tissue stains are still being analyzed for further details. Lymph nodes excised show mostly benign findings.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor, also known as carcinosarcoma, invading 18% of the myometrial thickness in the uterus. The tumor measures 7.2 cm in the largest dimension and is present as a polypoid mass in the endometrial cavity. There is no lymphovascular space invasion identified, and the cervix is negative for tumor. The omentum and adnexae are negative for tumor, and lymph nodes in several areas are also negative. The background endometrium is inactive and leiomyomas are present in the myometrium. The appendix shows benign fibrous obliteration of the lumen. The final diagnosis is primary uterine endometrial carcinoma and carcinosarcoma. The tumor size is 72mm, and the depth of invasion and lymph node involvement is not present.

The pathology report indicates that a total hysterectomy was performed on the patient, revealing a malignant mixed Müllerian tumor of the endometrium with interglandular elements consisting of leiomyosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, and malignant mesenchymal tumors invading the myometrium to a thickness of 9 mm. The report also notes superficial invasion of the endocervical stroma (<1 mm) and metastatic carcinosarcoma in the right external iliac lymph node. Further examination of the pelvic diaphragm, peritoneum, and left external iliac lymph nodes is recommended.

The pathology report describes a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor (carcinosarcoma) in the uterus, cervix, parametrium, both tubes, and both ovaries. The tumor invades 40mm into an 18.0mm thick myometrium and 14mm into a 150mm thick cervical stroma with lymphovascular invasion present. One left parametrial lymph node has metastatic carcinoma, while the right para-aortic lymph node has one lymph node without a tumor present and one with metastatic carcinoma. The tumor is composed of 60% carcinomatous and 40% sarcomatous elements, and the gross description includes a necrotic and hemorrhagic polypoid mass in the uterine cavity and a cystic polyp in the posterior lower uterine segment. Samples are submitted to the tumor bank for further examination.

The pathology report describes a total abdominal hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy of a uterus with cervix and bilateral adnexa. The specimen shows a mixed malignant Mullerian tumor (carcinosarcoma) measuring 5.5 cm that has invaded the posterior myometrium (100%) and forms a nodule on the serosal surface. No definite lymphovascular invasion is identified, and the cervical tissue is not seen in the specimen grossly or microscopically. The left and right fallopian tubes and ovaries are negative for tumor. The right ovary has inflammatory adhesions, and the left external iliac lymph node biopsy shows a lymph node with small granuloma formation but negative for tumor. The tumor is biphasic, with a high-grade serous carcinoma component and a high-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma component. The specimen is diagnosed as a mixed malignant Mullerian tumor (carcinosarcoma) with a pT3a pN0 ptx (FIGO stage INA) pathologic stage. The pelvic wash specimen, SIRIMRSREN, is negative for malignant cells. Immunohistochemistry is performed with selected antibodies, and microscopic examination substantiates the diagnosis.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has malignant mixed Mullerian tumor, consisting of papillary serous carcinoma and sarcoma. The cancer has spread to the left and right ovary and fallopian tube, myometrium, cervix, and lymph node. The tumor size is 12x10x8cm with greater than 50% myometrial invasion and invasion of cervical stromal connective tissue. The report also notes extensive vascular invasion. The patient presented with vaginal discharge. Gross examination revealed a disrupted and shaggy capsule surface on both ovaries with attached blood clot and fibrous adhesions. Representative sections were submitted for each specimen.

The pathology report describes a case of endometrial malignant mixed Mullerian tumor (MMMT) in a patient who underwent a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The tumor has invaded the superficial myometrium (1 mm/12 mm) without lymphovascular invasion. The report also mentions metastatic carcinoma identified in one of one right common iliac lymph nodes, and no tumor present in other lymph nodes analyzed. The carcinomatous components of the tumor consist of mixed high-grade endometrioid and high-grade serous carcinoma, while the sarcomatous component is undifferentiated with extensive rhabdoid features. Other samples, including the cervix, bilateral tubes, and ovaries, showed no pathological abnormalities except for the presence of an angiomyolipoma in the myometrium. A portion of the specimen is pending decalcification, with further results to follow.

The pathology report indicates the presence of malignant tumors in multiple areas of the patient's body. These include a malignant mixed tumor of the endometrium, metastatic carcinoma in a rectal serosal tumor, a tumor from the transverse colon, and a metastatic carcinoma in lymph nodes in the right supradiaphragmatic region. Additional benign findings were also noted in some excised tissue samples.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent surgery to remove a carcinosarcoma of the uterus with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The tumor was confined to the endometrium and did not involve the endocervix. There was no lymph node involvement or spread to other areas of the body. Multiple (2) intramural leiomyomata were present. All other biopsied tissues were negative for tumor. The report notes that the diagnosis was based on gross/necropsy examination and frozen section histologic evaluation, with confirmation by permanent section review.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has a malignant mixed Mullerian tumor of the endometrium with heterologous elements (including hardonyoblastic and cartilaginous components) and myometrial invasion with a thickness of 2.5 mm. There was no cervical invasion. Two of the two pelvic lymph nodes and five of the six benign lymph nodes were negative for cancer. The report also notes excision of lymph nodes in other areas with benign results. The report was approved by the examining pathologist.

The pathology report indicates a metastatic carcinosarcoma with homologous differentiation having components of endometrial cell carcinoma and adenosarcoma. The tumor measures 5 cm in maximum depth and has spread to the left external iliac lymph node. No cervical invasion is identified. The myometrium exhibits atrophy and adenomyosis. Multiple leiomyomata are also present. Further immunohistochemical stains will be performed to confirm the diagnosis. A small bowel adhesion specimen shows inflamed fibroadipose tissue with reactive mesothelial change. Pelvic peritoneum biopsy reveals benign fibroadipose tissue with reactive mesothelial change. Examined lymph nodes show benign lymph nodes. The omentum is benign with reactive mesothelium and no tumor is seen. Chromogranin, deamin, and myogenin tests are negative.

The pathology report describes a case of uterine carcinosarcoma with heterologous elements in the posterior fundus of the uterus, with a maximum depth of myometrial invasion of 0.6 cm. Lymphatic/vascular invasion was present. The adjacent non-neoplastic endometrium was not hyperplastic, and the cervix and serosa were negative for carcinoma. The right and left ovaries were positive for poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, while the fallopian tubes were negative. The omentum contained adipose tissue with extensive poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma. The report also includes information on the gross examination and block summary of the specimens submitted for evaluation, as well as the pathologic stage and diagnostic evaluation conducted by the pathologist.

The pathology report shows that the specimen submitted is a malignant mullerian mixed tumor of the ovary with teratologic differentiation. No vascular invasion is identified, and the endometrium exhibits atrophy while the uterus exhibits multiple leiomyomata. The right ovary and fallopian tube show metastatic carcinosarcoma with mucinous cystadenoma, and the left adnexa shows the same. The report also includes excisions of lymph nodes in various locations, all of which show benign lymph nodes except for one with metastatic carcinosarcoma. Additional testing was ordered for a lymph node in the common iliac region, which later showed no evidence of metastatic tumor.

The report describes the examination of various tissues and organs, including lymph nodes, a peritoneal nodule, and the uterus with adnexa. Multiple lymph node candidates of various sizes are identified and submitted for analysis. The uterus shows a protruding, rubbery, exophytic mass within the endometrial cavity that appears confined to the endometrium and overlies a thick myometrium containing several homogenous nodules of varying sizes. The left and right fallopian tubes and ovaries are normal. No definitive diagnosis is provided in the summary.

The pathology report describes a hysterectomy and salpingoophorectomy procedure that was performed on a patient with a malignant neoplastic uterus. A 6 x 5 x 3.8 cm pedunculated soft yellow tan mass was located within the posterior endometrial cavity and appeared to invade the lower uterine segment endocervical canal. Three intramural nodules were identified, but no areas of hemorrhage or necrosis were found. The report includes information on the pathology stage (pr2a pNO pHx) and the lymph node dissection. Two lymph node candidates were identified in the left pelvic region, four in the right pelvic region, and two in the para-aortic region. The lymph nodes ranged in size from 0.6 cm to 4.5 cm in greatest dimension.

The report describes the findings from a hysterectomy, which includes the uterus, tubes, ovaries, and cervix. The report states that there is a carcinomatous component and diffuse vascular invasion. There is a leiomyoma on the surface and a tumor mass in both the right and left fallopian tubes. Lymph node excisions were performed, and metastatic carcinoma was found in several lymph nodes, including the left lateral iliac, left obturator, right external iliac, right obturator, and right preaortic lymph nodes. The report concludes that the diagnosis is based on the examiner's personal examination of the slides.

The pathology report indicates that multiple biopsies were taken from different areas of the tongue. These biopsies show no evidence of malignancy, except for the biopsy taken from the right posterior of the tongue, which shows a well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor measures 2.1 cm and has invaded the muscle. No angiolymphatic invasion or bone invasion is identified. The surgical margins are free of tumor. Lymph nodes from the right neck were also examined, and metastatic squamous cell carcinoma was identified in one out of three lymph nodes in Level 2. No evidence of malignancy was found in the other lymph nodes examined. Overall, the revised diagnosis is pT2 pN1 squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue.

The pathology report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma of the right lateral tongue. A hemiglossectomy was performed, and the tumor was found to infiltrate into the tongue muscle with a depth of 1.3 cm. There was evidence of perineural invasion, but no vascular or bone/cartilage invasion was observed. The tumor was moderately differentiated.

Lymph node dissections were also performed at various levels in the right neck. One lymph node in level I was found to contain metastatic squamous cell carcinoma, while the remaining lymph nodes at levels II, III, and IV were negative for cancer.

The report confirms the intraoperative findings of tumor invasion and provides information about the involvement of lymph nodes in the neck. The margins of resection were free of tumor.

This is a pathology report for a lesion excision in the larynx. The clinical diagnosis was a tumor of the larynx. The surgical specimen included the larynx, hyoid bone, and part of the trachea. The tumor was 3.2x2.4x2.5 cm in size and located in the subglottal region, invading the false vocal cords and the thyroid cartilage. The histopathological diagnosis is invasive carcinoma planoepitheliale keratodes, pT3. Excision lines were found within healthy tissues. The report advises contacting the doctor with this information.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had squamous cell carcinoma of the right tongue. The report describes the findings from various tissue samples taken during the surgery and indicates that the tumor was moderately differentiated and invasive. Perineural invasion was present, but there was no angiolymphatic invasion. The margins were free of tumor. The report also mentions that there was no tumor present in other parts of the tongue or in the lymph nodes dissected from the right neck. Additionally, there was evidence of chronic sialadenitis in the submandibular gland. Further studies will be performed and reported as an addendum.

The pathology report describes a partial glossectomy specimen (surgical removal of part of the tongue) that shows invasive squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor is moderately differentiated and invades the surrounding tissues, including blood vessels. The report also mentions that there is metastasis to one out of 35 lymph nodes examined. No tumor is present in the other lymph nodes. Lastly, there is a mention of a skin tag in the left neck, but no further information is provided.

The pathology report describes the findings from the examination of a surgical specimen obtained from a patient with a left tonsil tumor. The specimen received is divided into different sections for analysis. 

Section A consists of soft tissue from level II and level III of the neck containing multiple lymph nodes. Representative sections are submitted for further evaluation. 

Section B consists of two irregular soft yellow fatty tissues with potential lymph nodes. All are submitted for analysis. 

Section C is a composite resection that includes soft tissue and bone measuring 7.0 x 6.0 x 4.0 cm. The bone appears to be a portion of the mandible. On the medial aspect, there is an irregular soft tissue partially covered with pink mucosa. A round lobule of normal appearing salivary gland is seen on the anteroinferior aspect. In the center, there is an irregular ulcer measuring 3.5 cm x 3 cm x 1.3 cm. The ulcer is located close to the margins of the resection. No intact tonsil is identified. The attached salivary gland appears unremarkable. The soft tissue margins consist of irregular tissue including muscle, connective tissue, and fat. The tumor is not identified on the surgical margins. A small hemorrhagic polyp is noted on the posterolateral surface of the tonsil. Various sections representing different margins and the tumor itself are submitted for analysis.

This pathology report describes a case of moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the floor of the mouth in a male patient. The report indicates that there is invasion of the mandibular bone and perineural invasion. There is no angiolymphatic invasion seen, and the resection margins are free of tumor. Two deep lymph nodes in the floor of the mouth are also free of tumor. However, metastatic squamous cell carcinoma is found in three out of sixteen left cervical lymph nodes. The report concludes with the pathological staging of the cancer as N2b MX. Additional testing for EGFR, P16, cMET, and HPV is recommended. The gross description section provides details about the tumor and the submitted specimens.

The pathology report describes a case of invasive squamous carcinoma, poorly differentiated, involving the mandibular bone. The tumor was partially removed through a glossectomy and resection of the floor of the mouth, anterior mandible, and bilateral neck dissection. The resected margins were free of tumor. The report also mentions the absence of tumor in the left inferior alveolar nerve and salivary glands, as well as in the right neck lymph nodes. However, 1 of the 6 level 7 lymph nodes in the left neck showed metastatic squamous carcinoma, while the other lymph nodes in the left neck were free of tumor. The report indicates that the tumor mass in the floor of the mouth measures 4.2 x 4.5 x 4.5 cm and comes close to the resection margins but is not present at the true margin. Additional information about the mandibular bone is pending.

The pathology report describes a fragment of tongue tissue with a gray-pink tumor measuring 4.5 cm in diameter and 0.8 cm thick. The tumor is predominantly localized near the base of the tongue. The microscopic examination reveals squamous cell carcinoma, keratinizing subtype, grade 1, with ulceration. Lymph nodes were examined and some showed reactive follicular hyperplasia and sinus histiocytosis, while one lymph node showed metastasis of the squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor features an ulcerated appearance and is localized in the oral cavity, specifically the tongue base. Venous invasion is absent and margins are uninvolved. The tumor is well differentiated. No further diagnosis details or comments are provided in the report.

The pathology report describes a case of HLH (hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis) and the findings related to the tongue region. The macroscopic examination reveals a thick and short lesion on the tongue, covered with mucous membrane. The lesion is slightly nodular and ulcerated. Microscopic examination shows sections of excised tissue with non-keratinized epithelium, muscle, and normal serous glands. The underlying tissue shows extensive formation of atypical squamous epithelium with varying degrees of keratinization. The tumor cells have irregular configurations, pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, enlarged nuclei with partially atypical mitoses, and evidence of polynuclear cells. The tumor is surrounded by a desmoplastic stroma reaction and inflammatory infiltrate composed of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and neutrophil granulocytes. The lateral/deep soft tissue resection margin is marked, and other resection margins are negative. The report also mentions the excision of tissue from the mucosa with hyperparakeratosis and low-grade chronic recurrent inflammation.

Summary:

This is a pathology report regarding a resected tumor of the tongue. The clinical diagnosis was a tumor of the tongue. The size of the tumor was 3.1 x 1.7 x 0.9 cm. The minimum margin of normal tissue around the tumor was 0.2 cm at the base and 0.5 cm on the side. The histopathological diagnosis is Carcinoma planoepitheliale with a keratosis grade of G3. The tumor does not have keratosis. The macroscopic examination shows normal tissue margins.

The pathology report describes the findings of a biopsy of the anterior commissure, as well as a total laryngectomy and near total thyroidectomy. In the biopsy of the anterior commissure, fragments of moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma are present. In the posterior wall of the esophagus, squamous mucosa with no tumor is detected. In the larynx, invasive moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma (2.4 cm) is observed on the right true vocal cord, with extension into the right supraglottic region (submucosa of false cord) and subglottic region. The tumor also crosses the midline to involve the left anterior vocal cord and invades the right paraglottic space. No lymphatic/vascular invasion is identified, and the margins are free of tumor. The thyroid is free of tumor as well. Further examination of sections of the thyroid cartilage is pending.

This pathology report describes a case of well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the right tonsil. The report confirms the presence of cancer and provides details about the tumor size, location, and spread. The surgical margins are positive in the posterior lateral aspect, indicating that cancer is present in that area. However, the other surgical margins are negative. Lymph node involvement is seen in the right level 2A lymph nodes, with four out of eight nodes being positive. No lymphovascular invasion is noted. The final stage of the cancer is categorized as T2, N2b according to the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging system. The report also includes information about the frozen section diagnosis, clinical information, and gross description of the specimen.

This pathology report provides information about a left neck dissection and surgical resection of various structures. The lymph nodes in level 1 and 3 of the left neck were negative for tumor. The left maxillary gingiva and soft palate mucosal margins were also negative for tumor. However, the report confirms the presence of invasive moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma in the left partial maxilla tuberosity, left partial glossectomy, left segmental mandibulectomy, and left partial pharyngectomy specimen. The tumor is described as ulcerating, with a size of 3.2 cm in its largest dimension and depth of 0.8 cm. The tumor border is infiltrative with thick cords. The report notes that perineural invasion and vascular invasion were absent. The lymph nodes in level 2A were negative for tumor, but the report mentions that decalcification is pending for bone/cartilage invasion assessment. Skeletal muscle and fragment of bone in the medial pterygoid plate were negative for tumor. The lateral buccal mucosal margin was redacted, and the report does not provide information on tumor presence in that area. The gross description describes the aggregate of fibroadipose tissue in level 1 and level 2A of the left neck dissection, as well as the composite resection of various structures. The bone underlying the ulcerated area in the composite resection specimen shows fine pitting and deformity. Representative sections are submitted for further analysis, including decalcification of the bone.  Overall, the report provides information about the tumor presence and its characteristics, as well as assessments of lymph nodes and margins.

This pathology report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma in the larynx. The report includes information about lymph node involvement and metastasis, as well as details about the tumor's size, grade, invasion, and presence of ulceration. It also mentions the absence of vascular invasion and the presence of chronic thyroiditis.

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

1) The deep margin and superficial margin of the tongue excision are negative for tumor.
2) There is metastatic squamous cell carcinoma involving one out of six lymph nodes in level 2 of the neck dissection.
3) In the left side of the neck, levels 3 and 4 of the dissection show no tumor involvement in seven lymph nodes in level 3 and eight lymph nodes in level 4.
4) In the right side of the neck, levels 2-4 of the dissection show metastatic squamous cell carcinoma involving one out of seven lymph nodes in level 2. Nine lymph nodes in level 3 are negative for tumor, and eleven lymph nodes in level 4 are negative for tumor.
5) A total laryngectomy was performed, with the tumor site being located in the supraglottis. The histologic grade of the squamous cell carcinoma is moderately to poorly differentiated. There is metastatic carcinoma in two out of forty-eight lymph nodes. Presence of venous/lymphatic invasion and absence of perineural invasion are noted.
6) The margins of the primary tumor are uninvolved, with a distance of invasive carcinoma from the nearest margin being 2mm. The extent of invasion into the preepiglottis is identified. The presence of distant metastasis cannot be assessed.

Overall, the report indicates the presence of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in lymph nodes, involvement of the preepiglottis, and absence of tumor in the margins of the excised tissues. The tumor is moderately to poorly differentiated, and further assessment for distant metastasis is needed.

The pathology report indicates that there is squamous carcinoma involving the mandibular bone. The report also mentions metastatic squamous carcinoma in 2 out of 22 lymph nodes in the right neck dissection, with no tumor present in the left neck dissection and other areas such as the anterior margin and tongue margin. The tumor is moderately differentiated and shows vascular and perineural invasion. The resection margins are free of tumor. Grossly, the report describes the size and appearance of the specimens submitted for analysis. Overall, the report confirms the presence of squamous carcinoma in the mandibular bone and provides information on lymph node involvement and margin status.

The pathology report describes a tumor in the left oral tongue that is ulcerated, protruded, and measures 2.5x2x2 cm. The tumor tissue shows the presence of malignant cells that form keratinized pearls. The nuclei of these cells are enlarged with variability in size and shape. Mitotic figures are common. The tumor has invaded the lower muscle propria and there is infiltration of inflammatory cells in the stroma. The diagnosis is squamous cell carcinoma, Grade II, infiltrating the muscle propria. Lymphovascular invasion is present, but perineural invasion is absent. Lymph nodes were examined, with 4 out of 9 lymph nodes in the left cervical area affected. The margins are uninvolved.

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

- Biopsies of the right, left, posterior, and deep margins are negative for in situ or invasive carcinoma.
- The biopsy of the anterior margin shows mild dysplasia of squamous epithelium and minimal stroma for evaluation.
- A lymph node in the right level 1 shows metastatic carcinoma without extranodal extension, along with a benign salivary gland.
- The tumor removed from the mouth's anterior floor and left level 1 is diagnosed as a moderately differentiated, keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. It measures 4.2 cm and extends into the sublingual salivary gland and large muscle fibers of the oral tongue. No CIS or angiolymphatic space invasion is identified.
- Surgical margins are negative, with the closest margin being 3 mm from the tumor.
- Other lymph nodes tested in different levels show metastatic carcinoma in some of them, with the largest metastatic focus measuring 1.3 cm. Extranodal extension is absent.
- A fragment of benign salivary gland is found in one lymph node.
- A skin sample from the left neck shows a benign epidermal inclusion cyst.
- The frozen section diagnoses are confirmed, and no tumor is seen in the frozen sections of the margins.
- The patient's clinical history indicates stage TV SCCA of the mouth.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has invasive squamous cell carcinoma in the left retromolar trigone and in the left oropharynx/tonsil. The tumor is grade 2 (moderately differentiated) and has invaded the lamina propria. The report also mentions lymph node involvement and extracapsular extension in one set of lymph nodes. The margins of resection show involvement on the lateral margin but are negative on the remaining margins. Other findings include no dysplasia present. The stage of the cancer is pT2N2a, Stage IVA according to the AJCC staging system. There are also comments about additional areas of involvement and lymphovascular invasion.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a biopsy that confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the left lateral tongue with leukoplakia. The report describes the size, location, and characteristics of the tumor. Multiple sections of the tongue and surrounding tissue were taken for frozen section control. The report also mentions the presence of possible lymph nodes in the neck, which were also sectioned and examined for carcinoma. The final section report states that all sections were negative for carcinoma.

The pathology report describes the findings of a surgical excision performed on the anterior and posterior mandibular margins, medial and anterior mucosal margins, posterior buccal mucosa margin, anterior buccal mucosa margin, posterior mucosa margin, and skin. The report indicates that there is no tumor present in any of these margins.

The report also states that a partial mandibulectomy was performed, targeting a tumor in the oral cavity of the right mandible. The tumor measures 4.5cm in its greatest dimension. The histological analysis reveals the presence of squamous cell carcinoma, specifically a moderately differentiated variant.

Further examination shows the invasion of the tumor through the cortical bone and the involvement of multiple ipsilateral lymph nodes. Six out of thirty-seven examined lymph nodes are affected by metastatic squamous cell carcinoma, with extracapsular extension of the tumor. Additionally, there is indeterminate involvement of blood/lymphatic vessels, and perineural invasion is present.

In the right neck, metastatic squamous cell carcinoma is found in one out of thirteen lymph nodes with a tumor deposit measuring 1.5cm. Levels 3 and 4 of the neck have no evidence of tumor involvement in the twelve and six lymph nodes examined, respectively.

It is important to note that these results are unofficial and not to be filed in the patient chart. The report suggests contacting medical records for an official chart copy.

The pathology report indicates that no dysplasia or invasive carcinoma was identified in multiple biopsies taken from different areas of the tongue, floor of mouth, and neck. However, a 2.4 cm diameter poorly differentiated invasive squamous carcinoma was identified in the floor of the mouth, with close negative surgical margins. Additionally, squamous carcinoma in situ was found. No metastatic carcinoma was identified in the lymph nodes. The final diagnosis is pT2 pNO pMx. Frozen section consultations confirmed the absence of tumor in the biopsy samples.

This pathology report is a supplemental report for a patient who underwent a total laryngectomy. The report confirms the presence of moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma of the larynx, involving various structures in the right supraglottic region. The margins of resection are free of tumor, but the diagnosis for the hyoid bone and thyroid cartilage is still pending after decalcification. The carcinoma measures 1.5 x 1.3 x 0.7 cm in size and shows focal perineural invasion and focal vascular channel invasion.

The pathology report indicates that the patient was admitted with a clinical suspicion of cancer in the larynx and lower pharynx. The material submitted for examination was the larynx, specifically the marked margin. The histopathological diagnosis revealed invasive non-keratinising squamous cell carcinoma (G3) with involvement of the excision line. The tumor was described as whitish and lobular in the cross section, measuring 6 x 3.7 x 2.5 cm. The report advises contacting the doctor with this information.

The pathology report describes the findings from a surgical history case. The following diagnoses were made:

(A) Right Pyriform: Squamous mucosa with mild atypia
(8) Epiglottis: Invasive squamous carcinoma, grade 2
(©) Right Lymph Node: Lymph node, no tumor
(D) Right Jugular Branch: Squamous carcinoma in fibroconnective tissue
(E) Left Spinal Accessory Node: Two lymph nodes, no tumor
(F) Left Level 2B Nodes: Three lymph nodes, no tumor
(G) Superior Pharyngeal Margin: Squamous mucosa with mild dysplasia
(H) Laryngectomy and Bilateral Neck Node Dissection: Invasive squamous carcinoma invading perineural spaces and lymphatics, involving multiple areas including the right pyriform sinus, supraglottis, peri-epiglottic space, and glottis. Margins of resection were free of tumor. Metastatic squamous carcinoma was found in 2 out of 5 left cervical lymph nodes and 2 out of 13 right cervical lymph nodes, with extracapsular invasion.
(1) Left Proximal Jugular Vein Branch: No tumor present in blood vessel.

The gross description of the specimens is also provided.

The pathology report shows that the patient had a right extended modified radical neck dissection, revealing metastatic moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma in the subdigastic and upper posterior cervical lymph nodes with extracapsular extension. The report also mentions several margins and tissues that were examined, including the lateral nasopharyngeal margins, buccal mucosa and retromolar trigone, lingual, tongue, floor of mouth margins, vallecula margin, base of tongue, left soft palate, nasopharyngeal roof margin, and right hard palate margin, and no tumor was found in any of these areas. Additionally, the patient underwent a partial glossectomy, partial maxillectomy, partial pharyngectomy, total resection-nasopharyngectomy, which revealed invasive moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma involving the tongue, right retromolar trigone, hypopharynx, uvula, and soft palate, with a maximum depth of invasion of 1.4 cm and focal perineural invasion. The deep margin of resection was free of tumor. Fifteen teeth were also examined.

This pathology report describes a total laryngectomy specimen that was removed from a patient. The report indicates that the specimen shows invasive poorly differentiated squamous carcinoma, which means that there is an aggressive type of cancer involving the squamous cells in the larynx. The tumor has extensive perineural invasion, meaning that it has spread along the nerves, and vascular lymphatic invasion, meaning that it has spread through the blood vessels and lymphatic vessels. The tumor involves the piriform sinus and left supraglottic region. The margins of resection, meaning the edges of the removed tissue, are free of tumor.

In addition, a section of the left base of the tongue was also examined, and there was no tumor present. The report also includes a gross description of the laryngectomy specimen, indicating the size and location of the tumor.

The report also mentions the ink color used to mark the margins during the procedure, and provides a detailed section code for the different areas of the specimen that were examined. The SNOMED codes at the end of the report are standardized numerical codes used in pathology to classify and record diagnoses.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a biopsy and radical resection of the floor of the mouth and mandible due to a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor invaded the anterior floor of the mouth and sublingual gland, with perineural invasion present. However, there was no angiolymphatic invasion or bone invasion. The margins were free of tumor. The lymph nodes removed during the neck dissection showed no evidence of tumor spread. The submandibular gland had no significant abnormalities, except for chronic sialadenitis. The final pathological stage was pT2, indicating a moderately advanced tumor.

The pathology report describes a case of squamous carcinoma in the buccal mucosa. The tumor has invaded the mandibular bone and extends into the submandibular gland and soft tissue. The resection margins are free of tumor and there is no evidence of vascular invasion. There is also metastatic squamous carcinoma found in one of the cervical lymph nodes. The report mentions that decalcification and sectioning of the mandibular bone and left clavicle are pending further analysis. The specific margins and muscles examined are listed, and no tumor is present in those areas. The report also mentions the presence of multiple teeth with enamel caps, but only for gross examination.

This pathology report describes the findings of a patient with carcinoma of the pharynx involving the larynx. The patient underwent a laryngopharyngectomy and bilateral neck dissection. The report includes the following information:

- Part 1: Excision of lymph nodes in the right neck, level IIB. One out of three lymph nodes (1/3) was found to have metastatic squamous cell carcinoma, with no extracapsular spread identified.

- Part 2: Dissection of lymph nodes in the right neck, levels II and IV. Three out of twelve lymph nodes (3/12) were found to have metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. Positive lymph nodes were found in levels II and III, with extracapsular spread present in a level II lymph node.

- Part 3: Dissection of lymph nodes in the left neck, levels II, III, and IV. Four out of thirty lymph nodes (4/30) were found to have metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. Positive lymph nodes were found in levels II, III, and IV, with extracapsular spread present in levels III and IV.

- Part 4: Laryngopharyngectomy and thyroidectomy. Infiltrating squamous cell carcinoma of the right pyriform sinus was found, moderately differentiated, with invasion into the paraglottic space and thyroid and cricoid cartilages. Perineural invasion was seen. The thyroid gland was free of tumor but showed areas of fibrosis and inflammation. No involvement by tumor was found at the tracheostomy site. The final margins of resection were free of tumor. The pathological stage is pT4a, N2c, Mx.

- Part 5: Excision of the esophageal margin. No tumor was seen, and one benign lymph node was found.

- Part 6: Excision of the right base of tongue. Infiltrating squamous cell carcinoma, moderately differentiated, was found.

- Part 7: Excision of the upper pharyngeal wall. No tumor was seen.

- Part 8: Additional excision of the right base of tongue. No tumor was seen.

- Part 9: Excision of a lymph node in the right neck, level II. Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma was found in one lymph node, with extracapsular spread present.

The pathology report describes a surgical case of total laryngectomy with right selective and left radical modified neck dissection. The main findings are:

- Invasive poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma involving mainly the supraglottis lesion, left piriform sinus, and extending to the epiglottis and involving the false and true vocal cord. The tumor size is estimated to be 5.0 x 3.0 cm, and it invades the anterior space. Lymphovascular permeation is present, but the margins of resection are free of tumor.

- Left modified radical neck dissection reveals 5 out of 42 positive lymph nodes with macrometastasis. There is no extracapsular extension present. Positive nodes are found in level 2 (2-19 positive nodes), level 3 (2 out of 5 positive nodes), and level 4 (1 out of 9 positive nodes). Further evaluation is pending for additional deeper sections. 

- Right selective node dissection shows 20 benign lymph nodes (0/20) pending additional sections.

- The gross description of the surgical specimen includes measurements of the laryngectomy specimen, left neck, and right neck. There is an ulcerated, excavated mass involving the left pyriform sinus and extending to the left supraglottis and epiglottis. The tumor does not involve the margins of resection. The right side neck dissection shows multiple lymph nodes, while the left modified radical neck dissection includes the sternocleidomastoid muscle and jugular vein, as well as levels 2, 3, 4, and 5.

- SNOMED codes T-24100 and M-80703 are provided for reference.

- An addendum notes that additional deeper sections reviewed did not show evidence of metastatic carcinoma.

Overall, the report describes the extent and characteristics of the invasive squamous cell carcinoma and provides details about lymph node involvement and the absence of macroscopic metastasis in the deeper sections reviewed.

This pathology report describes the findings from various tissue samples taken from the patient. 

The report states that in the lymph nodes in the right neck (levels 2, 3, and 4), there is metastatic squamous cell carcinoma present in 15 out of 19 nodes. There is extranodal extension present in this area. In the lymph nodes in the left neck (levels 2, 3, and 4), there is metastatic squamous cell carcinoma present in 3 out of 37 nodes. There is no extranodal extension present in this area. 

In the tongue base on the left side, there is a squamoproliferative lesion with keratosis, but no carcinoma is present. The report indicates that immunostains for p53 and Ki-67 are not increased in the squamoproliferative areas. 

In the left lateral pharynx, no tumor is present. In the larynx, there is invasive moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma present in the right "marginal" supraglottic/hypopharyngeal area. There is also invasive squamous cell carcinoma present in the left glottic area. Angiolymphatic and perineural invasion are noted. The final pathological stage is pT3 N2c for the right supraglottic/hypopharyngeal carcinoma and pT1 for the left glottic carcinoma. The final margins are free. The thyroid tissue is unremarkable. 

The report also includes a gross description of the received specimens, including the lymph nodes and other tissues that were sampled. The report mentions that additional immunohistochemical stains for p53 and Ki-67 will be reported separately.

The pathology report describes a biopsy of the larynx, specifically the right aryepiglottic fold and right pyriform sinus. The diagnosis for both sites is invasive moderate to poorly differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. The patient has a history of carcinoma of the medial right pyriform sinus. The gross description provides measurements and characteristics of the tissue samples. The light microscopy confirms the presence of the squamous cell carcinoma.

The pathology report describes the findings from the examination of various tissue specimens. 

1. Left neck dissection: Five lymph nodes at level 1, two lymph nodes at level 2, and fifteen lymph nodes at level 11 were found to be free of tumor. One lymph node at level 11 contained a nonkeratinizing granuloma.

2. Right neck dissection: All lymph nodes at level 1 and level 11 were free of tumor.

3. Composite resection of the chin, jaw, floor of mouth, and tongue: A 6.5 cm invasive hybrid verrucous and conventional moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma was found. The tumor had a depth of invasion of 3.2 cm. The tumor border was predominantly pushing and focally infiltrative. There was no perineural or vascular invasion observed.

The report also provides a gross description of the specimens received, including the size and characteristics of the lymph nodes and other tissues. Additional testing and processing are mentioned, with results to be included in a supplemental report.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a partial glossectomy (removal of part of the tongue) due to the presence of a moderately differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor measures 1.5 x 1.4 x 0.9 cm and shows an infiltrative and discontinuous pattern of growth. It has invaded skeletal muscle bundles and has present perineural and lymphovascular invasion. The mucosal and soft tissue margins of the tumor are negative for carcinoma. 

Other excisions of different parts of the tongue were performed, and they were negative for high grade dysplasia and invasive carcinoma. Lymph node dissections were also performed, and most of the lymph nodes were negative for carcinoma. However, one out of seven lymph nodes in level II of the neck dissection showed metastatic carcinoma without extracapsular spread. The remaining lymph nodes in that level and the lymph nodes in other levels were negative for carcinoma.

The pathology report indicates that the lymph nodes in the neck (specifically levels 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3A, and 4) were examined and no tumors were found in any of them. The report also mentions that there is chronic sialadenitis with periductal fibrosis and atrophy in the lymph nodes in levels 1B, as well as an unremarkable parotid tissue. The mandible marrow margins on both the left and right sides show no tumors. The posterior and deep tongue margins on both the right and left sides also show no tumors. The mylohyoid, floor of mouth (both right and left), and anterior mandibular composite with hemiglossectomy margins show no tumors. However, invasive squamous cell carcinoma is present in the floor of mouth on the left side. The report also states that there is extrinsic tongue muscle involvement, but no bone involvement. The margins of the excised tissues are free of tumor. Additionally, there is metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in one of the thirty-three lymph nodes in the left neck zone 2A, 2B, 3A, and 4, with extracapsular extension. The gross description portion of the report details the sizes and appearances of the received specimens.

This pathology report is for a patient who underwent a total laryngectomy with neck dissection for laryngeal cancer. The report includes findings from the dissection of lymph nodes in the left and right neck, as well as biopsies of the left superior laryngeal nerve and various margins. The final diagnosis reveals a moderately differentiated invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx, which has invaded through the thyroid cartilage and into the anterior soft tissue. Vascular invasion is present, but perineural invasion is absent. The tracheal and anterior soft tissue margins are free of carcinoma. The pathology stage is pT4a No MX. A focus of invasive squamous cell carcinoma is seen on permanent section of the right superior margin, but the original frozen section slides show no carcinoma. No tumor is seen in the left laryngeal wall margin, left inferior wall margin, left superior wall margin, or right superior wall margin. The gross description includes details of the submitted specimens, including lymph nodes and the laryngectomy specimen.

The pathology report indicates that multiple specimens were collected from various areas of the oral cavity and surrounding structures. The report confirms that there is no tumor present in the deep right tongue base, left nasopharynx, left pharynx, deep midline hard palate, right soft palate, and the vallecula, among others. The pathology report indicates the following findings:

- Molecular anatomic pathology testing on block 3K revealed an HRAS mutation (p.Q61K, c.181C>A).
- Mutations in BRAF, NRAS61, and KRASI2/13 were not identified.
- The FASH test for RET/PTC rearrangement is pending.
- DNA extraction was sufficient for testing.
- Mutations in BRAF or RAS genes and RET/PTC rearrangements are commonly found in papillary thyroid carcinomas.
- The BRAF V600E mutation is associated with more aggressive behavior in papillary carcinoma.
- RAS mutations and PAX8/PPARg rearrangements occur in follicular thyroid carcinomas with lower frequency in oncocytic carcinomas.
- BRAF V600E mutation and RET/PTC and PAX8/PPARg rearrangements are overall specific for malignancy in the thyroid.
- RAS mutations occur in both malignant and benign thyroid tumors.
- The correlation between genetic alterations and microscopic manifestation and prognostic characteristics of thyroid carcinoma is important.
- The mutational status analysis showed high aggressiveness in papillary thyroid tumors.
- Manual microdissection was performed for analysis of paraffin-embedded surgical specimens.
- Real-time PCR and PCR product sequencing were used to detect and confirm mutations.
- In-situ hybridization and immunohistochemistry were performed on invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx, showing negative results for HPV and Pi6 and positive for EGER 3.
- Final diagnosis includes no tumor present in lymph nodes levels 2-4, metastatic squamous cell carcinoma with spindle cell features in one of fourteen lymph nodes, and invasive poorly differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma with focal spindle cell features in the larynx.

In summary, the pathology report indicates that there is no tumor present in the skin at the stoma site. In the lymph nodes of the left neck levels 2-4, no tumor is present in twenty lymph nodes. The parotid gland tissue is unremarkable. There is also involvement of the paraglottic space and pre-epiglottic space. Angiolymphatic invasion is present but there is no perineural invasion. The resection margins are free of carcinoma. The pathology stage is pT3 N2B. No tumor is present in the post cricoid margin, left lateral pharyngeal margin, right lateral pharyngeal margin, or right base of tongue margin.

This pathology report describes the findings from a patient with carcinoma of the floor of the mouth. The report includes information about lymph node involvement, the extent of the tumor, and the presence of any metastases. Here are the key findings:

- Part 2: Tracheal lymph nodes - Three benign lymph nodes were excised.
- Part 3: Left Level 18 lymph node - A questionable lymph node was found to have squamous cell carcinoma involvement, along with five additional benign lymph nodes.
- Part 4: Right Level 1B lymph nodes - Three of six lymph nodes were found to have metastatic squamous cell carcinoma, with extracapsular spread seen in one node. Additionally, the right submandibular gland showed duct ectasia and acute and chronic sialadenitis.
- Part 5: Anterior floor of the mouth, anterior mandible, and overlying skin - Invasive squamous cell carcinoma (acantholytic type) involving the floor of the mouth, mandible, and adjacent soft tissue/subcutaneous tissue interface of the skin. Extensive perineural invasion was noted, involving the inferior alveolar nerve. All margins, including bone, mucosa, soft tissue, and skin, were free of tumor. One additional lymph node was found to have metastatic squamous cell carcinoma, with no extranodal spread.
- Part 6: Right Level 2 lymph nodes - Ten benign lymph nodes were excised.
- Part 7: Right Level 3 lymph nodes - Eight benign lymph nodes were excised.
