- Part 10: Left Level 4 lymph nodes - Thirteen benign lymph nodes were excised.
- Part 11: Additional posterior margin of soft tissue - No tumor was present.
- Part 12: Teeth - Nine teeth were extracted, showing caries.

The report also mentions that the tumor in Part 5, involving the floor of the mouth, could be classified as acantholytic (pseudoglandular) squamous cell carcinoma rather than adenosquamous carcinoma, based on the negative mucicarmine stain.

Overall, based on the findings in this report, the patient is staged as T4a N2c MX.

This pathology report describes the findings from a surgical resection of a tumor in the tongue. The report confirms the presence of invasive moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma in the left pyriform sinus with extension into the left aryepiglottic fold, preepiglottic space, and subepithelial connective tissue of the left true vocal cord. The tumor also extends focally to the subepithelial connective tissue of the left inferior lateral pyriform sinus margin. The margins of resection in the trachea, soft tissue, and other mucosal areas are free of tumor. The left thyroid lobe does not have any tumor, but there are two metastatic squamous carcinomas found in the cervical lymph nodes out of 26 nodes examined. Additional information regarding the tumor and underlying thyroid cartilage, as well as the hyoid bone, is pending decalcification and will be provided in a supplemental report.

The pathology report describes the findings from a right maxillectomy for a patient with squamous cell carcinoma in the oral cavity. The tumor measures 2.2 cm in its greatest dimension and is moderately differentiated. The margins of the tumor are negative for malignancy, meaning there is no tumor present within 0.5 cm of the margins. There is no lymphovascular invasion or perineural invasion identified. Additional sections of bone are pending for examination. Biopsies of the deep mucosal, posterior, and medial margins are all negative for malignancy. The synoptic report confirms the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma and provides information on tumor size and grade. There is no vascular or perineural invasion noted, and no other pathological findings identified. The T stage is deferred until the bone sections have been examined. The gross description of the specimen confirms the location and extent of the tumor, including involvement of the bone. Representative sections are submitted for further analysis. The addendum comment reveals that the tumor is present adjacent to the bone but without invasion, and the bone margins are negative for tumor. The tumor is staged as pT2, indicating a tumor greater than 2 cm but not more than 4 cm in its greatest dimension.

The pathology report describes the findings from a patient's biopsy and neck dissection procedure. The patient had a laryngeal mass, which was found to be an invasive basaloid squamous cell carcinoma. The lymph nodes in the neck were also examined and it was determined that one lymph node was free of tumor and 29 lymph nodes were also free of tumor. However, four lymph nodes were found to have metastatic basaloid squamous cell carcinoma. There was no extracapsular extension seen. The larynx was removed and the tumor was found to have invaded the left pyriform sinus and nearby areas. The resection margins were free of tumor. In addition, there was a hypercellular left parathyroid gland and one level VI lymph node with metastatic carcinoma. The final pathological stage was determined to be T3 N2b MX. The report also mentions that the right cervical lymph nodes contained tissue consistent with benign thyroid inclusions, but further evaluation of the right lobe of the thyroid is recommended. Additional studies for EGFR, c-MET, HPV, and p16 have been ordered and will be reported in an addendum.

The pathology report describes findings from a variety of neck dissections and other specimens taken during surgery. In general, no tumors were present in the lymph nodes examined except for one lymph node in the right neck dissection at level II "A", which showed metastatic squamous carcinoma with extracapsular extension. The report also mentions congestion and vascular ectasia in one lymph node, as well as infiltration of invasive squamous carcinoma in a total glossectomy specimen. No tumors were present in the right lingual nerve or the right base of tongue. The report includes descriptions of the size and number of lymph nodes identified in each dissection. Teeth fragments were also detected. The mucosal margins were clear.

The pathology report is incomplete and does not provide a detailed summary of the findings. The report mentions the collection of frozen tumor samples and fresh tumor samples, as well as blood samples. There are also weight measurements and timestamps provided. However, the report does not provide specific details about the tumor samples or any pathology findings.

This pathology report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma in the oral cavity of a teenage patient. The report indicates that the cancer has spread to the lymph nodes in the neck. The tumor is poorly differentiated and has basaloid features. The resection margins around the tumor are positive for tumor cells. The TNM stage of the cancer is pT2 N2b Mx. The report also notes the presence of perineural invasion and carcinoma in situ. The final diagnosis recommends further treatment based on the findings.

This pathology report describes the findings from a surgical biopsy of the left true vocal cord and a biopsy of an anterior tracheal lymph node in a patient with clinical squamous cell carcinoma. 

The diagnosis for the true vocal cord biopsy is invasive moderately differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. However, additional testing for pl6 IHC and high risk HPV ISH stains is pending and will be reported in an addendum.

The tracheal lymph node biopsy did not show any tumor (0/1 lymph node).

The report also includes a brief description of the gross appearance of the specimens and the respective measurements.

In an addendum to the report, it states that the carcinoma is negative for plé by immunohistochemistry and negative for high risk HPV by in situ hybridization. Appropriate controls were performed.

This pathology report is for a patient who underwent a surgical resection of a lesion in the larynx. The clinical diagnosis was a tumor of the larynx, specifically a circular proliferation covering 2/3 of the front part of both vocal folds, both laryngeal vestibules, and the anterior commissure. 

The macroscopic examination of the surgical specimen revealed a tumor sized 3.8 x 2.1 x 2.6 cm, infiltrating into the supraglottal, subglottal, and infrahyoid regions. The tumor spreads over all levels of the larynx, thyroid cartilage, and a small part of the thyroid gland. The surgical incision lines were free of neoplastic proliferation, with a minimal margin of less than 0.1 cm at the front. 

The microscopic examination confirmed the presence of an invasive keratinized squamous carcinoma of the larynx, specifically categorized as carcinoma planoepitheliale keratodes invasivum G2. The final histopathological diagnosis is carcinoma planoepitheliale keratodes invasivum laryngis, indicating an invasive keratinized squamous carcinoma of the larynx, with a grade 2 tumor (G2) and a stage Téa. The report advises the patient to contact their doctor with this report.

The pathology report is for a patient who underwent a partial glossectomy for squamous cell cancer in the right tongue. The tumor is moderately differentiated with deep invasion of the lingual musculature. Perineural invasion is also seen. The margins of resection are free of tumor, although the deep margin is less than 4mm from the tumor. No tumor is seen in the dorsal and deep margins that were excised separately. The report also mentions the gross description of the specimen and includes information about ink codes and cassette codes used during the examination. A frozen section was taken for intraoperative consultation. The microscopic examination confirms the diagnosis. The report concludes with a statement about the laboratory's certification and capabilities, and includes synoptic data for primary upper aerodigestive tract and salivary gland tumors. The size of the tumor is not specified in the report.

This pathology report describes the examination of multiple specimens from the oral cavity and neck. 

Specimens 1, 2, and 3 from the oral cavity, specifically the tongue and buccal regions, are negative for malignancy. 

Specimen 4, from the right floor of the mouth and tongue, shows the presence of squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor is moderately differentiated and measures 4.1 cm in maximum dimension and 1.0 cm in thickness. Perineural invasion is present, and the tumor is close to the deep margin. All other margins are negative for tumor. 

Specimen 5, a perifacial lymph node on the right side, is negative for malignancy. 

Specimen 6, the left submandibular gland, does not show any pathological changes and is negative for malignancy. 

Specimens 7, 8, and 9, from different levels of the right neck, show varying findings. Level 1 shows mild chronic inflammation in the submandibular gland but is negative for malignancy. Level 2 shows the submandibular gland and four lymph nodes, all negative for malignancy. Level 3 shows metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in two out of ten lymph nodes, with the largest involved node measuring 1.5 cm. No extracapsular extension is present. 

Specimen 10, another perifacial lymph node on the right side, is negative for malignancy. 

The synoptic data provides additional information about the tumor, including the histologic type (squamous cell carcinoma), size, grade (moderately differentiated), and involvement of lymph nodes. 

Overall, the report indicates the presence of squamous cell carcinoma in the right floor of the mouth and tongue, with involvement of nearby lymph nodes but negative margins in most areas.

The pathology report indicates the presence of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in lymph nodes of the right supraomohyoid neck dissection. The report also mentions the absence of tumor in the gingival labial margin, mucosal tongue margin, deep tongue margin, and anterior floor of the mouth. Additionally, the report includes gross descriptions of the specimens received for examination.

This pathology report is for a case involving squamous cell carcinoma in the right true vocal cord. The carcinoma is invasive and classified as grade ITI. Lymphatic invasion is present, and the tumor is found at the deep margin of resection and in the left anterior commissure. The tissue overlying the arytenoid cartilage also shows squamous carcinoma in fibrovascular tissue. However, there is no tumor in the false cord margin, posterior commissure margin, posterior subglottic, anterior subglottic, new arytenoid margin, new anterior commissure margin, or thyroid cartilage. The report contains SNOMED codes for classification.

The pathology report describes a case of invasive squamous carcinoma in a specimen from a patient who underwent a Cheniglossectomy, maxillectomy, mandibulectomy, partial pharyngectomy, and neck dissection. The tumor infiltrates the mandibular bone, but the resection margins are negative for tumor. The report also mentions fragments of well-differentiated squamous carcinoma in the excised buccal mucosa and a nodule in the submental area, which were negative for tumor. The tumor is moderately differentiated and involves the buccal mucosa, gingiva, pharynx, and tongue. It extends to the lateral soft tissue resection margin. Perineural invasion is present, but there is no tumor involvement in the submandibular gland or the examined lymph nodes. The mandibular bone is still being decalcified, and a supplemental report will follow. The report also mentions a remnant of the uvula, which was negative for tumor.

The pathology report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma in the larynx. The tumor is moderately differentiated and involves the infraglottic, glottic, and supraglottic regions, as well as the right hypopharynx. The size of the tumor is 4.5 x 4.0 x 3.5 cm. The tumor has extended to the thyroid cartilage and right paralaryngeal skeletal muscle. Additionally, there is in situ squamous cell carcinoma present, and moderate stromal dysplasia. However, there is no evidence of perineural or lymphovascular invasion. The margins are uninvolved by carcinoma. There are a total of 12 lymph nodes on the right and 10 lymph nodes on the left, all of which show no evidence of metastatic carcinoma. The pre-epiglottic fat tissue shows no evidence of neoplasia.

This pathology report describes a case of poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma involving the right buccal mucosa, mandible, floor of mouth, and soft tissues. The tumor measures 8.5 x 8.5 x 8.0 cm and has invaded the pterygoid muscles and lateral pterygoid. Perineural invasion is present. There is also metastatic squamous carcinoma involving 14 out of 24 lymph nodes. However, the decalcified sections of the anterior mandibular resection margin and the condyle of the right mandible are free of carcinoma. Additional sections are pending decalcification. The final pterygoid margin of excision is free of tumor, but two initial pterygoid margins were positive. The largest lymph node metastasis completely replaces a 5.0 cm lymph node, with extranodal extension present. Gross examination of other tissues, such as the tongue margin, right palate margin, teeth, and right maxillary tuberosity, did not show any tumor.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a right partial glossectomy for an invasive squamous carcinoma on the tongue. The tumor is moderately differentiated, ulcerating, and measures 2.2 cm in its largest dimension. It has invaded to a depth of 1.0 cm and has an infiltrative border with thick cords of more than 4 cells. There is no evidence of perineural or vascular invasion, but there is mild lymphocyte infiltration. The mucosal margin is negative for invasive carcinoma, but the deep margin is close (<2mm) and there is no dysplasia at the margin.

Additionally, several lymph nodes and other tissue samples were examined. The right external jugular lymph node, as well as skeleta muscle and nerve tissues, did not contain any tumor. The right neck dissections at levels 1, 2A, 28, and 3 did not show any tumor in the lymph nodes, except for one lymph node in level 3 that contains metastatic squamous carcinoma. There is no extranodal extension observed. The tooth was examined grossly only.

In summary, the patient has invasive squamous carcinoma on the tongue with lymph node metastasis in one lymph node in the right neck dissection. No tumor is present in the other lymph nodes or additional tissue samples examined.

This pathology report describes the findings from a left level I neck dissection and a total glossectomy, total laryngectomy, and bilateral neck dissection. In the neck dissection, four lymph nodes were found, all of which were negative for carcinoma. A benign salivary gland was also present. In the glossectomy/laryngectomy, a 6.5 cm invasive, keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma was identified in the right base of the tongue, extending into skeletal and submandibular gland tissue. The resection margins were free of carcinoma. Two out of 29 lymph nodes showed metastatic squamous cell carcinoma with extranodal extension. Multiple areas of mild to moderate dysplasia and atypia were found in the soft palate, posterior pharyngeal margin, and right gingivial margin. Additional sections from various structures and lymph nodes were also examined.

Summary:

This pathology report describes the findings from the examination of lymph nodes and tissues from the floor of the mouth. Here are the key points:

- Left - Level IIA lymph nodes: 5 lymph nodes were examined and found to be uninvolved by cancer.
- Right - Level IIB lymph nodes: 10 lymph nodes were examined and 1 was found to be involved by metastatic squamous cell carcinoma.
- Left - Level IB lymph nodes: 2 lymph nodes were examined and found to be uninvolved by carcinoma.
- Left - Level III lymph nodes: 6 lymph nodes were examined and found to be uninvolved by cancer.
- Right - Level III lymph nodes: 2 lymph nodes were examined and found to be uninvolved by cancer.
- Right - Level ILA lymph nodes: 10 lymph nodes were examined and 2 were found to be involved by metastatic squamous cell carcinoma with capsular involvement.
- Level 1A lymph nodes: 2 lymph nodes were examined and found to be uninvolved by cancer.
- Right - Level IB lymph nodes: 2 lymph nodes were examined and found to be uninvolved by cancer.
- Pelvi-Glosso-Mandibulectomy: The tumor in the floor of the mouth was found to be invasive well differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with a size of 6.0 cm and depth of 4.0 cm. Lymphatic invasion was present, but perineural invasion was not detected. The anterior mucous margin was involved by the neoplasia, but other mucous margins were uninvolved.
- Marginal central mandibulectomy: The osseous tissue was found to be uninvolved by neoplasia.

Overall, the report indicates the involvement of lymph nodes and the extent of the neoplasia in the floor of the mouth.

The pathology report indicates that the patient, Nanc Copath, underwent surgery for a right buccal tumor. The diagnosis of the tumor was squamous cell carcinoma, moderately differentiated. The tumor measured 2.5 cm in maximum dimension and 0.7 cm in maximum thickness. Perineural invasion was present, but no lymphovascular invasion was identified. The surgical margins were negative for malignancy. Additionally, the report mentions lymph nodes in the right neck that were negative for malignancy, as well as negative findings in the submandibular gland and skeletal muscle. The report provides details about the gross description of the specimens and the histologic type, grade, and staging of the tumor.

Final Diagnosis:
- Moderately-differentiated keratinizing invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the right lateral floor of mouth, measuring 5.3 cm in greatest dimension.
- Tumor invades through the anterior mandible and into the subcutaneous soft tissue.
- All margins are negative for tumor.
- No tumor identified in the soft tissue or mandible of the left side.
- AJCC pathologic stage: pT4a pNO.

Lymph Nodes:
- Right level 1A and 1B lymph nodes: All five lymph nodes are negative for tumor.
- Right level 2A and 3 lymph nodes: All fourteen lymph nodes are negative for tumor.

- Left level 2A and 3 lymph nodes: All five lymph nodes are negative for tumor.

This pathology report describes the findings of a biopsy performed on a patient's tonsils. The report includes the following information:

1. Left tonsil (Part 1): Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, predominantly non-keratinizing. No blood or nerve vessel invasion seen. Tumor-free resection margins. Pathologic stage is pT2Nx.

2. Right tonsil (Part 2): Hyperplastic tonsil with saprophytic bacteria.

3. Left tonsillar fossa (Part 3): No significant pathologic changes or presence of tumor.

Immunoperoxidase staining and in-situ hybridization for human papillomavirus were performed on a prior biopsy of the tumor, and both were positive.

The gross description of the specimens includes details about the size, appearance, and resection margins.

Intraoperative evaluation was performed, and representative tumor samples were procured for further study.

An intraoperative consultation confirmed the diagnosis of invasive squamous cell carcinoma in the left tonsil.

Microscopic examination confirmed the diagnosis and indicated that all necessary ancillary studies were conducted.

The report also includes information about the testing performed and its compliance with regulatory requirements.

The pathology report describes the following findings:

- Lateral margin of resection is free of tumor

The pathology report reveals that there is invasive moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma in the left pyriform sinus. The tumor has also extended into other areas such as the left aryepiglottic fold, esophagus, left paraglottic space, left paratracheal/para-esophageal soft tissue, and left thyroid. Vascular and lymphatic invasion is present. The surgical margins are free of tumor. Metastatic squamous carcinoma is found in 11 out of 53 left cervical lymph nodes and 5 out of 29 right cervical lymph nodes. One out of the 2 perithyroidal lymph nodes also contains metastatic cancer. No tumor is present in the submandibular glands, jugular vein, vagus nerve, or parathyroid gland. The report also mentions the presence of marked solar elastosis and acute inflammation in the anterior neck subcutaneous tissue. The tumor in the left pyriform sinus measures 9.5 cm in greatest dimension and the largest lymph node involved measures 2.5 cm. Extranodal extension measuring at least 3.0 mm is observed.

The pathology report describes the findings of a left neck dissection and left oral resection. The main findings are as follows:

- Submandibular gland with no pathologic changes.

- Left posterior margin: Negative for tumor.
- Left anterior margin: Negative for tumor.
- Left lateral mucosa margin: Negative for tumor.
- Deep muscle margin: Negative for tumor.
- Surgical waste: Skin and soft tissues with no pathologic changes.

- Left neck III lymph node: Soft tissues with no pathologic changes.
- Left facial lymph node: Two lymph nodes negative for tumor.

Overall, the report suggests that the patient has metastatic squamous cell carcinoma involving lymph nodes in the left neck and oral cavity. The tumor shows moderate differentiation and perineural invasion. The margins of the resected tissue are negative for tumor.

The pathology report describes the findings from a right neck dissection at level 1A. The report provides information on various tissue samples obtained during the surgery:

1. Surgical waste: No pathological changes observed in adipose tissue (only gross examination).

2. Mental nerve (right neck): Positive for squamous cell carcinoma.

3. Buccal mucosa: Excision revealed moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Perineural invasion is present, but lymphovascular invasion is absent. Tumor is close to the infero-anterior soft tissue margin.

4. Buccal fat: Fibroadipose tissue with chronic inflammation, no tumor identified.

5. Modified dissection of the right neck: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma involving six out of forty-six lymph nodes. The largest involved lymph node measures 3.5 cm. Extensive extracapsular extension is present. The submandibular gland shows no pathological changes.

6. Inferior alveolar nerve (right neck): No pathological changes observed.

7. Floor of mouth mucosa (margin): Negative for tumor.

The synoptic data provides additional information on tumor characteristics:

- Tumor site: Oral cavity
- Histologic type: Squamous cell carcinoma, conventional
- Tumor size: Greatest dimension is 8.0 cm
- Histologic grade: Moderately differentiated (G2)
- Venous/lymphatic invasion: Absent
- Perineural invasion: Present
- Margin involvement: Supero-anterior buccal and lip mucosal margins are involved
- Pathologic staging (pTNM): pT3, pN2b (metastasis in multiple ipsilateral lymph nodes, none more than 6 cm in greatest dimension)

The report also mentions the presence of a metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in a peri-submandibular gland lymph node, without invasion of the salivary gland itself.

The gross description of the specimens is provided, including the size and characteristics of each tissue sample.

In summary, the report indicates the presence of squamous cell carcinoma in the mental nerve, buccal mucosa, and multiple lymph nodes in the right neck. There is involvement of the supero-anterior buccal and lip mucosal margins. Perineural invasion is present, but lymphovascular invasion is absent.

The pathology report describes the findings from a right marginal mandibulectomy, which is a surgery to remove part of the mandible (jawbone) on the right side. The main diagnosis is in-situ and invasive squamous cell carcinoma, moderately differentiated, with a maximum tumor dimension of 1.8 cm. The report also mentions the presence of carcinoma in-situ at the anterior margin and notes that all other margins are negative for in-situ and invasive carcinoma. Bone sections are still pending decalcification and will be reported later. Other findings include negative results for tumor in the right medial margin, right posterior margin, right lateral margin, and right deep muscle margin. Lymph nodes in various levels of the right neck were negative for tumor, and there were no pathological changes in the submandibular gland. The gross description of the specimens confirms the presence of the tumor in the oral cavity and provides details about the size and location.

This pathology report describes the findings from a surgical pathology examination of a tongue biopsy. The main diagnosis is invasive squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor is moderately to poorly differentiated and located in the right posterior lateral area of the tongue. The report also mentions the presence of tumor necrosis.

The report includes information about lymph node involvement. Out of 16 lymph nodes examined, 2 are positive for carcinoma with extension into hilar fat. There is also 1 positive lymph node out of 3 in Level 24 and 1 positive lymph node out of 8 in Level 3. The report indicates that there are negative lymph nodes in Level 18 and Level 28.

Additionally, several margin biopsies were taken, and they all show no evidence of in situ or invasive carcinoma. The report mentions biopsies of the posterior superior margin, posterior margin, floor margin, anterior margin, anterior/superior margin, and deep posterior margin, all of which show mild squamous atypia but no carcinoma.

The report also includes information about a right neck dissection, with negative findings in the submandibular gland and two lymph nodes in Level IB. However, 1 lymph node out of 3 in Level 2A is positive for metastatic carcinoma, while 1 lymph node out of 8 in Level 3 is negative for metastatic carcinoma. Three lymph nodes in Level 28 are negative for metastatic carcinoma.

The clinical diagnosis and history indicate right tongue cancer.

Overall, the report provides information about the extent and characteristics of the invasive squamous cell carcinoma in the tongue, as well as lymph node involvement and margin status.

Summary:

The pathology report indicates the presence of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in the right neck level IIA, with one out of nine lymph nodes showing involvement. There is also evidence of chronic inflammation in the submandibular gland. 

Additionally, a squamous cell carcinoma is found in the right glossectomy specimen, with a tumor size of 5.5 cm and a thickness of 3.6 cm. Perineural invasion is present, but there is no lymphatic or vascular invasion. The medial and lateral pharyngeal margins are positive for tumor, while the remaining margins are negative. 

Other specimens, such as the deep tonsil margin, posterior tongue base, anterior tongue base, anterior deep margin, and posterior deep margin, are all negative for tumor. The left level II lymph node is negative for tumor, as well as the left level III lymph node and revision right parapharyngeal space. 

The overall pathologic staging is pT3, indicating a tumor or lip or oral cavity larger than 4 cm in size, and pN2a, indicating metastasis in a single ipsilateral lymph node. The report does not mention any distant metastasis.

This pathology report describes a case of invasive moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma in the larynx, base of tongue, and surrounding structures. The tumor measures 5 x 4.5 x 1.7 cm and involves the base of the tongue, epiglottis, supraglottic mucosa, and pre-epiglottic space. It has invaded up to 1.7 cm of a total 1.8 cm. The tumor also involves the left lateral pharyngeal margin and the anterior soft tissue resection margin, although it closely approaches the latter margin (less than 0.1 cm). No lymphovascular invasion is identified. 

Metastasis is found in 1 out of 25 right neck lymph nodes and in 2 out of 20 left neck lymph nodes. The single positive right lymph node measures 4.0 cm in greatest dimension with 1.2 cm of extranodal extension. The two positive left lymph nodes have metastatic foci measuring approximately 5 mm and 3.0 cm, with 4 mm and greater than 1.0 cm of extranodal extension, respectively. 

No tumor is present in the hyoid bone, submandibular glands, new left lateral pharyngeal margin, or tendon excision site.

This pathology report describes a case of invasive squamous cell carcinoma, moderately differentiated, keratinizing. The tumor measures 11.0 mm in thickness. There is perineural invasion and vascular/lymphatic invasion present. There are metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in 8 of 30 lymph nodes. Multiple tumor nodules in fibroadipose tissue are present, likely representing replaced lymph nodes. The report also mentions chronic inflammation in the salivary gland with no tumor present.

The pathology report states that the patient underwent a partial glossectomy (surgical removal of part of the tongue) on the right side. The diagnosis of the removed tissue is squamous cell carcinoma, a moderately differentiated, keratinizing type. The tumor measures 1.2 cm in its largest dimension and has a maximum depth of invasion of 6 mm. The margins of the resected tissue are free from tumor cells, with the closest margin being 9 mm away. No lymphatic or vascular invasion or perineural invasion is identified in the sample.

A sentinel lymph node (the first lymph node to receive drainage from the tumor site) from right neck level 2 was also removed and examined. It showed metastatic carcinoma, with the presence of cancer cells measuring 3.5 mm in its largest dimension. No extracapsular extension (spread of cancer beyond the lymph node capsule) is identified.

The tumor classification according to the AJCC (American Joint Committee on Cancer) system is pT1 (primary tumor stage 1) and pN4(sn) (sentinel lymph node metastasis stage 4). The report indicates that an immunohistochemical stain for p16 will be performed and results will be issued later. The clinical information provided is "tongue cancer."

The report also includes information on the gross appearance of the resected tissue and the procedure performed by the lab to examine it.

The pathology report describes an invasive squamous cell carcinoma in the larynx, which measures 5.0 cm in size and has invaded the pre-epiglottic soft tissue. Lymphovascular invasion is present, but perineural invasion is not identified. The resection margins are free of tumor. No tumor is found in the lymph nodes in the left neck, one paratracheal lymph node, or the central compartment lymph nodes. Additionally, no tumor is present in the right laryngeal margin, posterior cricoid mucosa, left pyriform sinus, superior vallecula margin, or left laryngeal margin. The report also mentions that the thyroid gland shows no diagnostic abnormality, and the lymph nodes in the central compartment and neck show no tumor. Frozen sections taken from the tracheal margin and right laryngeal margin both show no tumor.

The pathology report includes the following findings:

1. Glottis, right, biopsy: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma.
2. Thyroid, left lobe, lobectomy: Slight nodular thyroid hyperplasia.
3. Thyroid, right lobe, lobectomy: Slight nodular thyroid hyperplasia.
4. Larynx, total laryngectomy:
   A. Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, moderately differentiated, involving the supraglottic region with right glottic and anterior commissure involvement.
   B. Paraglottic and pre-epiglottic space involvement.
   C. Clear margins, but tumor is within 0.05 cm of preepiglottic soft tissue margin.
   D. Angiolymphatic invasion present, no perineural invasion.

   G. Pathologic stage: pT3N2b.
   H. Papillary thyroid microcarcinoma involving isthmic portion of thyroid.

5. Right retrofacial lymph nodes: Squamous cell carcinoma in soft tissue, no lymph node tissue present.
6. Right pharyngeal margin excision: No tumor present.
7. Left pharyngeal margin excision: No tumor present.
8. Base of tongue margin excision: Mild dysplasia, no tumor present.
9. Paratracheal lymph nodes: Normocellular parathyroid tissue, no lymph node tissue present.

In summary, the report describes invasive squamous cell carcinoma in the glottis, with involvement of the thyroid, larynx, and lymph nodes. There is also a papillary thyroid microcarcinoma. The tumor has invaded surrounding tissues but has clear margins in some areas. The overall stage of the squamous cell carcinoma is pT3N2b.

This pathology report describes the surgical removal and examination of various tissues and lymph nodes from a patient with right oral cavity cancer. The report states that no tumor was seen in the right anterior muscle, right middle muscle, right lateral muscle, right posterior mucosal margin, right posterior middle margin, right anterior mucosal margin, right posterior deep margin, right middle deep margin, and right anterior deep margin. Additionally, benign salivary gland tissue with focal atrophic changes was noted in the right anterior and right lateral floor of the mouth. No tumor was seen in the left neck level I lymph nodes, two lymph nodes in the right neck level 1, three lymph nodes in the right neck level 2, and twelve lymph nodes in the right neck level 3. The histologic tumor type was determined to be squamous cell carcinoma, and it was moderately differentiated. The tumor was found to invade into the bone of the mandible. No presence of carcinoma in situ (CIS), angiolymphatic space invasion, perineural space invasion, or tumor in the surgical margins and lymph nodes was identified. Other significant findings were not reported. The report concludes by stating that the staging of the cancer is not available at the time of the report and pending clinical review. The frozen section analysis confirmed that no tumor was seen in the examined tissue specimens.

The pathology report indicates that there is squamous carcinoma present in the tongue, measuring 1.7 cm in maximum dimension and invading to a depth of 0.7 cm. The posterior margin of resection is positive for carcinoma. A total of 32 lymph nodes that were sampled are negative for metastatic carcinoma.

The pathology report describes a resection of a specimen from the left mandible and base of the tongue. The report confirms the presence of poorly differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the tongue, with lymphatic and vascular invasion. The tumor is ulcerated and measures 1.5 cm in thickness. The margins of the lesion are free of tumor. 7-9. Tongue and posterior margins: No malignancy was found.

10. Oral cavity, anterior floor of mouth, ventral tongue, and marginal mandibulectomy: Squamous cell carcinoma was diagnosed, measuring 3.6 cm and moderately differentiated. There was no perineural or lymphovascular invasion, and the margins were negative for tumor. One lymph node tested negative for carcinoma.

11. Left level II tissue: No pathologic changes were observed.

Summary: The pathology report indicates the presence of Warthin's tumor in the parotid gland and nearby lymph nodes, as well as metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in one lymph node in the neck. Additionally, squamous cell carcinoma was found in the anterior floor of mouth and ventral tongue, but there was no evidence of malignancy in the tongue and posterior margins or left level II tissue.

The pathology report describes the findings of a partial glossectomy (surgical removal of part of the tongue) for a tumor in the oral tongue. The tumor is identified as a moderately differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, with a size of 4 cm. The report also mentions lymph node involvement, with metastasis found in multiple ipsilateral lymph nodes, but not exceeding 5 cm in size. The report notes that extracapsular extension of the tumor is present. The margins of the resected tissue are uninvolved by tumor, except for a 1 mm distance from the deep aspect of the medial margin. The report also mentions metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in lymph nodes in the left neck. In conclusion, the tumor in the oral tongue is squamous cell carcinoma with metastasis to lymph nodes.

This pathology report is for a laryngectomy surgery and right hemi thyroidectomy. The tumor involves the right pyriform sinus (hypopharynx) with involvement of the right true vocal cord and right false cord. The tumor is classified as squamous cell carcinoma and has a size of 3.0 cm. It is poorly differentiated (G3). No lymph nodes were submitted for examination and the presence of distant metastasis cannot be assessed. Margins are uninvolved. The tumor shows perineural invasion. The carcinoma extends into skeletal muscle and soft tissue adjacent to the right pyriform sinus and beyond the thyroid cartilage, with focal involvement of the right thyroid lobe.

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

1. Left neck level I: One out of four lymph nodes examined is positive for metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. Extranodal invasion is present. No pathologic changes are seen in the submandibular gland.

2. Left neck level II: Eleven lymph nodes examined are negative for tumor.

3. Left neck level III: Three lymph nodes examined are negative for tumor.

4. Left neck level IV: Twelve lymph nodes examined are negative for tumor.

5. Pterygoid muscle: Negative for tumor.

6. Oral cavity: Left buccal tumor resection: Squamous cell carcinoma is present with a maximum tumor diameter of 4.4 cm and tumor thickness of 2.6 cm. No lymphovascular invasion or perineural invasion is noted. Tumor is present at the deep margin of the specimen, but the remaining margins are negative for tumor.

7. Intertemporal fossa fat: Negative for tumor.

8. Interior maxillary margin: Negative for tumor.

9. Anterior buccal margin: Negative for tumor.

10. Posterior inferior mucosal margin: Negative for tumor.

11. Inferior anterior mucosal margin: Negative for tumor.

12. Inferior alveolar margin: Negative for tumor.

13. Posterior mucosal margin: Negative for tumor.

Overall, the tumor is diagnosed as a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with a maximum diameter of 4.4 cm and tumor thickness of 2.6 cm. Perineural invasion is present, but no lymphovascular invasion is noted. The margins of the resected specimen are uninvolved by tumor. One lymph node in the left neck level I is positive for metastasis, with extranodal invasion. No metastasis is identified in other lymph nodes examined. The gross description of the specimens indicates the size and presence of lymph nodes in each level of the neck. The report does not mention any distant metastasis.

The pathology report describes findings from various tissue samples taken from the patient. The report indicates the presence of invasive, poorly differentiated non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma in the left radical tonsillectomy specimen, measuring 1.8 cm in greatest dimension. The margins of the tonsillectomy specimen are free of carcinoma, and no perineural invasion is seen. Metastatic carcinoma is present in two out of thirty-two lymph nodes in the left neck dissection specimen. The largest metastatic focus measures 4.5 cm. No extranodal extension is identified. The report also mentions the presence of chronic sialodenitis in the salivary gland. The tumor cells in the tonsillectomy specimen are positive for keratin, CK5/6, p63, and negative for HLA-DR. They also exhibit positive staining for p16, but MPV testing by in situ hybridization is still underway. The rest of the lymph nodes, including those in the left neck dissection and level 2B, do not show evidence of carcinoma. The report states that the margins of the invasive carcinoma in the tonsillectomy specimen are uninvolved, and the tumor is classified as pT2 (tumor 2 cm or less in greatest dimension) and pN2b (metastasis in multiple ipsilateral lymph nodes, none more than 6 cm in greatest dimension) according to the pathologic staging.

The pathology report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma involving the mandible. The tumor is abutting the anterior margin of the mandible and is within 2 mm of the posterior margin. Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma is also found in the left neck dissection lymph nodes, with tumor present in 1 out of 5 nodes. In level I, II, III, and V of the neck dissection, metastatic squamous cell carcinoma is present in 3 out of 16 lymph nodes. No tumor is found in the salivary gland or other sites such as the medullary cavity, anterior floor of the mouth, lateral floor of the mouth, anterior tonsillar pillar, retromolar trigone, buccal mucosa, labial mucosa, or right medial pterygoid. The squamous cell carcinoma involving the mandible is poorly to moderately differentiated and is deeply invasive, however, the mandible itself is still pending decalcification to confirm the extent of invasion. Multiple lymph nodes with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma are identified in the neck dissection levels. No tumor is found in the salivary gland or other sites such as the medullary cavity, anterior floor of the mouth, lateral floor of the mouth, anterior tonsillar pillar, retromolar trigone, buccal mucosa, labial mucosa, or right medial pterygoid.

This pathology report summarizes the findings from a lymph node biopsy and other excision samples from various parts of the neck. The report indicates that there are reactive changes in the lymph nodes, likely in response to metastatic carcinoma, but these findings do not alter the initially rendered diagnosis. Additional immunohistochemical stains were performed to evaluate the lymph node, and the specific results are provided in a table. The report also states that there is metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in three lymph nodes on the right side of the neck and involvement of other structures in the larynx. However, all surgical margins are free of tumor.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a history of oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma and underwent a glossectomy. The report provides details about the margins and lymph nodes examined during the procedure. Multiple lymph nodes were identified in the submandibular glands and in neck levels 1 and 2, some of which showed possible involvement of tumor. The report also mentions the presence of tumor in various margins including the posterior left base of the tongue, dorsal tongue, and lateral margin. Photographs were taken for documentation. Overall, further analysis and evaluation of lymph nodes and margins are required to determine the extent of the disease and plan the appropriate treatment.

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

- Specimens received include sections of various parts of the tongue, oral cavity, and neck lymph nodes.
- Lateral, anterior, posterior, deep, and alveolar margins all show no evidence of malignancy.
- The left sublingual gland shows mild chronic sialadenitis but no malignancy.
- The left tongue and floor of the mouth show poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, with a tumor dimension of 2.8 cm and thickness of 0.9 cm. There is no perineural or lymphovascular invasion.
- Moderate to severe squamous dysplasia is present.
- Additional pathologic findings are not identified.
- Margins are uninvolved by tumor, with a distance of 0.4 cm from the closest margin.
- The tumor is classified as pT2, indicating a tumor of more than 2 cm but not more than 4 cm in greatest dimension.
- No regional lymph node metastasis is observed in the examined 29 lymph nodes.
- Distant metastasis cannot be assessed.
- Gross descriptions of the submitted specimens are included.

The pathology report describes the findings of a biopsy of a specimen labeled "right oral tongue and floor of mouth." The specimen consists of a portion of the tongue with a central irregular mass measuring 4.2 cm by 3.8 cm. The remaining mucosa is pale tan and slightly edematous. The mass is located 1.9 cm from the superior mucosal margin, 0.4 cm from the anterior mucosal margin, and 0.2 cm from the inferior mucosal margin. There is a superficial area of ulceration less than 0.1 cm from the inferior mucosal margin. The specimen is serially sectioned and reveals white cut surfaces with a maximum tumor depth of 1.2 cm. The tumor is moderately differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma that invades salivary gland tissue, with angiolymphatic and perineural invasion. The tumor extends to within less than 1.0 mm of the inferior specimen margin but no carcinoma is identified at the inked margins.

The pathology report describes the findings from a surgical procedure on the neck and tongue. In the right supraomohyoid neck dissection, metastatic squamous carcinoma was found in one of 13 regional lymph nodes, with extension into extranodal connective tissue. No tumor was present in the submental/submandibular lymph nodes, midjugular lymph nodes, or submandibular gland. In the right base of the tongue, there was focal mucosal ulceration with no diagnostic evidence of malignancy. A subtotal glossectomy was performed, and invasive grade I-II squamous carcinoma was found. The resection margins were free of tumor. The report also mentions morphological features suggestive of lymphovascular invasion by the tumor. Overall, the findings indicate the presence of squamous carcinoma in the lymph nodes and tongue, with some invasion and ulceration, but with no evidence of malignancy in the submandibular gland. The resection margins were clear of tumor.

The pathology report describes a case of poorly differentiated squamous carcinoma in the anterior mandible. The tumor has invaded the bone, but the margins of resection are free of tumor. There is also fibrous inflammation of the submandibular gland, but no tumor is present in five lymph nodes. The report states that the tumor is close to the margin of resection and that a supplemental report will follow once the bone is decalcified. The gross description indicates the presence of lymph nodes in adipose tissue and an irregular exophytic area involving the floor of the mouth and anterior soft tissue. The margins of the lesion are described, and the mandibular bony margins are unremarkable. SNOMED codes indicate the type of cancer and tissue specimen.

This pathology report describes the findings from a neck dissection in a patient with invasive squamous cell carcinoma. The report states that lymph nodes from various levels in the neck were examined, and all were negative for tumor involvement (0/3, 0/6, 0/9, 0/5, 0/7, 0/5, 0/3, 0/14, 0/8, 0/3). The report also mentions negative findings for tumor in the floor of mouth, lateral and dorsal tongue margins, alveolus, and composite resection of the ventral tongue and floor of mouth. The squamous cell carcinoma is described as moderately differentiated, with an ulcerating gross appearance, a size of 4 cm, and invasion depth of 1.2 cm into skeletal muscle. Other tumor features, such as perineural invasion and vascular invasion, were absent. The report also notes the presence of a mucocele in the minor salivary gland. The gross description section provides details about the specimens received and the sizes of lymph nodes in each section.

The pathology report describes the findings of a surgical resection of a tumor in the left floor of the mouth. The tumor is diagnosed as moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. The report mentions that there is no tumor seen in various biopsies taken from different sites, including the bone marrow, floor of mouth, vestibule of mouth, lingual nerve margin, soft tissue on the left face, proximal nerve margin, and proximal inferior alveolar nerve margin. There is an epithelial inclusion cyst identified in the soft tissue biopsy, but no malignancy is found. The report also mentions that the tumor has invaded the bone and is 0.1 cm from the closest margin. Lymph nodes are examined and no tumor is seen in any of the lymph nodes removed. The report concludes with the pathological TNM stage of the tumor as pT4a pNO, indicating a locally advanced tumor without lymph node involvement. Additional information or clinical review may impact the final staging.

This pathology report is related to a male patient with a clinical suspicion of cancer on the left side of the tongue. The histopathological examination revealed invasive squamous carcinoma of the tongue, partially keratinizing and ulcerating (G2) with completed excision. There were no neoplastic lesions found within the wire-marked margins. The surgical specimen measured 4.5 x 4 x 2cm with a flat raised, ulcerated tumor measuring 3.5 x 2.0 x 0.8cm. This report advises the patient to contact their doctor with the findings. The specific type of cancer mentioned is carcinoma planoepitheliale partim keratodes invasivum exulcerans (G2).

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

1. Total laryngectomy:
- Squamous carcinoma in the perichondrium (cartilage had no tumor present).

2. Right thyroid:
- Nodular goiter.

3. Skin thyroid:
- Nodular goiter.

4. Total laryngectomy, partial pharyngectomy:
- Bilateral transglottic poorly differentiated squamous carcinoma.
- Extensive vascular invasion.
- Tumor involving three epiglottic and paraglottic spaces and skeletal muscle of the neck.
- Tumor in vascular spaces at submucosa close to the margins of excision (less than 1 mm).

5. Skin of neck:
- No tumor found in subcutaneous tissue.

Comment:
- Tumor invaded the blood vessels of the right and left mucosal margins, although it was only 1 mm from the margin of excision.

The pathology report is from a patient who had a partial glossectomy (surgical removal of a portion of the tongue) for a tumor. The diagnosis is invasive squamous carcinoma, which is a type of cancer that arises from the squamous cells lining the surface of the tongue. The tumor is well differentiated, meaning that the cancer cells resemble normal cells to some extent. The tumor is exophytic, meaning it grows outward from the surface of the tongue. It measures 7.2 cm in its largest dimension and has invaded to a depth of 0.6 cm. The tumor has infiltrative borders but does not show perineural or vascular invasion. The lymphocyte infiltration is absent. The margins of the tumor resection are negative for invasive carcinoma and dysplasia. The report also mentions left neck dissection at three levels (levels I, II, and III) with multiple lymph nodes examined, all of which show no evidence of tumor. The report does not provide any clinical history for the patient.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent surgery for the removal of a tumor in the right neck and partial glossectomy. The tumor is diagnosed as invasive squamous carcinoma, moderately differentiated, with a size of 2.5 cm. The tumor is infiltrative with thick cords and shows no perineural invasion or vascular invasion. There is moderate lymphocyte infiltration. The mucosal and deep margins are negative for invasive carcinoma. Dysplasia is present at the margin. Lymph node dissections show no tumor present in levels 1A, 1B, and 3, but metastatic carcinoma is identified in 1 out of 8 lymph nodes in level 4. The posterior lateral margin shows no tumor present. The clinical history and additional information are not provided in the report.

The pathology report shows that the patient had a subtotal glossectomy (removal of a portion of the tongue) and left level 1 neck dissection. The main finding is invasive moderately differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, measuring 5.2 cm, in the tongue. The tumor extends to the deep left lateral margin of the specimen. Perineural invasion is not present. No malignancy is seen in the lymph nodes examined. Other areas examined, including the lingual nerve, lingual artery, floor of mouth, base of tongue, pharyngeal mucosa, and alveolar ridge, also show no malignancy. The failed free flap shows no malignancy. The tip of the tongue shows squamous mucosa with keratosis.

This pathology report is for a patient who underwent surgical treatment for a tumor in the mouth area. The report provides the following findings:

- Lymph node submental: No pathological changes present, no lymph nodes present.
- Right neck level I: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma found in one out of four lymph nodes. The involved lymph node measures 0.8 cm. No extracapsular invasion noted. Mild non-specific chronic inflammation found in the submandibular gland.
- Right neck level II: No tumor present in six lymph nodes.
- Right neck level III: No tumor present in one lymph node.
- Left neck level I: No tumor present in six lymph nodes. No tumor found in submandibular gland.
- Left neck level II: No tumor present in four lymph nodes.
- Left neck level III: No tumor present in five lymph nodes.
- Anterior gingival tissue: No tumor present.
- Oral cavity (anterior marginal mandibulectomy and floor of mouth): Keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, moderately differentiated, with maximum tumor dimension of 2.0 cm and tumor thickness of 0.9 cm. Perineural invasion present, but no lymphovascular invasion. Margins are negative for tumor, except for the anterior gingival mucosal margin which is very close to the tumor (0.3 cm).
- Right posterior margin: No tumor present.
- Anterior tongue: No tumor present.
- Left posterior margin: No tumor present.

In summary, the report indicates the presence of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in some lymph nodes, as well as the primary tumor in the oral cavity. The tumor is moderately differentiated and has invaded the perineural space. The margins around the tumor are mostly negative, except for the anterior gingival mucosal margin which is close to the tumor. Further examination of bone tissue is pending.

The pathology report describes a surgical specimen that was received for examination. The specimen includes various fragments of tissue from the tongue, gingival margin, floor of mouth, and lymph nodes. The report mentions a right lateral tongue lesion that measures 1.9 cm in dimension and extends into the attached floor of mouth. The tumor is well-circumscribed and displays a central hemorrhagic area. The report also mentions the presence of intact lymph nodes in both bilateral level 1A and right level 18.

This pathology report describes a lesion excision of a tumor on the right lower lip. The macroscopic description states that a partial resection of the lower lip was performed, resulting in a specimen measuring 1.5 x 2.0 x 1.0 cm, containing a papillar tumor measuring 1.5 x 1.0 x 0.5 cm. 

The microscopic description reveals that the tumor is a carcinoma planoepitheliale keratodes G2, with the largest diameter measuring 1.5 cm. The report also mentions the minimal margins of normal tissue from the lateral side and bottom of the resected material, measuring 2 mm and 1 mm, respectively.

The histopathological diagnosis is given as carcinoma planoepitheliale keratotes cutis G2; pT2 invasive planoepithelial carcinoma keratodes of the skin. It also mentions excision lines within healthy tissues.

The pathology report describes the findings of a lower jugular lymph node biopsy, as well as a total laryngectomy with partial pharyngectomy and bilateral neck dissection. The report indicates the presence of a squamous cell carcinoma involving the left vocal cord, left ventricle, and left supraglottic area. The tumor measures 2.0 cm in thickness and extends 2.5 cm in the supraglottic region. The margins of resection are free of tumor. Additionally, there is a nodular goiter in the right thyroid without tumor involvement. Multiple cervical lymph nodes are examined, with 25 on the right and 39 on the left, all of which show no tumor involvement. The report also mentions specific sections and blocks submitted for further examination, including mucosal margins, lymph nodes, and nodules found in the left pyriform sinus and right thyroid lobe. Frozen section analysis does not show evidence of malignancy.

Summary:

- The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent multiple biopsies and dissections of the floor of mouth, lymph nodes, and glands.
- In the biopsy of the floor of mouth, invasive squamous cell carcinoma was found, moderately differentiated.
- One of seven lymph nodes in the left level 1 had metastatic squamous cell carcinoma, while all four lymph nodes in the right level 1 showed no tumor presence.
- Perineural invasion was present in the tongue and floor of mouth resection.
- Margins were free of tumor.
- The pathologic stage was determined to be pT2 NI.
- Chronic sialadenitis (inflammation of salivary glands) was seen in the submandibular and sublingual glands.
- No tumor was present in the lymph nodes from left level 24 or right level 24.
- A biopsy of the right anterior margin of the tongue showed keratosis but no tumor.
- Ancillary studies will be performed to provide additional information.
- The gross description of the specimens includes details about the sizes and appearances of the tissues and lymph nodes submitted for analysis.

This is a pathology report for a patient who underwent surgery for suspected laryngeal carcinoma. The diagnosis is invasive keratinising squamous cell carcinoma (G3) of the larynx. The tumor was found in the glottal region and invaded the subglottal region, glottis, supraglottal region, and left aryepiglottic fold. The surgical margins were free of neoplastic lesions. The pathology report recommends contacting the doctor for further discussion.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a total laryngectomy and bilateral neck dissection for invasive squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor is moderately differentiated and involves the left false vocal cords, left pyriform sinus, left epiglottis, and also extends to the left aryepiglottic fold. The tumor measures 5.5 cm in its largest dimension with an invasion depth of 2.0 cm. The tumor has a pushing border and there is no evidence of perineural or vascular invasion. The report also mentions the presence of mild dysplasia at the tracheal margin.

The report confirms negative margins for invasive carcinoma in terms of the mucosal and deep margins. The tracheostomy site and thyroid gland are both free of tumor. The report mentions hypercellular parathyroid but does not indicate any tumor in the paratracheal lymph nodes or in the lymph nodes of both right and left neck dissections.

Overall, the report suggests successful removal of the tumor with clear margins and absence of tumor involvement in the lymph nodes examined.

The pathology report describes the findings from the excision and dissection of the tongue and neck lymph nodes in a patient. The report states the following:

1. Base of tongue, left, excision: No tumor present.
2. Tongue, left, hemiglossectomy: Moderately differentiated invasive squamous cell carcinoma (4.7 cm) with perineural invasion. Severe dysplasia/carcinoma in situ at lateral margin, but final margins free of invasive carcinoma. Pathologic stage is pT3 N2b.
3. Additional deep margin excision: No tumor present.
4. Lymph nodes, left neck level 2 selective dissection: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in one of thirteen lymph nodes (1/13) with extracapsular spread. Parotid tissue is unremarkable.
5. Lymph nodes, left neck level 3-4 selective dissection: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma in two of nine lymph nodes (2/9) without extracapsular spread.
6. Lymph node, left neck level 1A and B selective dissection: No tumor present in eight lymph nodes (0/8). Submandibular gland is unremarkable.
7. Additional posterior margin excision: No tumor present.

Overall, the report indicates the presence of squamous cell carcinoma in the tongue, with involvement of nearby lymph nodes. The tumor has invaded the surrounding tissue and shows perineural invasion. However, the margins of the excised tissue are free of invasive carcinoma. The patient is staged as pT3 N2b.

The pathology report describes the findings from a laryngectomy procedure on a patient with a malignant neoplasm of the larynx. The report includes the following findings:

- Lymph nodes, right and left, at levels 2, 3, and 4: Sixty-one benign lymph nodes were found in the right lymph nodes, and thirty-six benign lymph nodes were found in the left lymph nodes.

- Larynx and thyroid gland: The larynx showed an invasive, moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the supraglottic region, predominantly on the right side. There was also invasion of the pre-epiglottic space. Acute abscess formation was present. The margins were free of tumor, and no perineural invasion was seen. A tracheostomy was present. The right thyroid lobe showed focal fibrosis. 

- Larynx margins: No tumor was seen at the right lateral, left lateral, inferior, right superior, and left superior margins of the larynx.

- Gross description: The received specimen included nodules from the lymph nodes at different levels in the neck, as well as the larynx and right thyroid lobe.

Overall, the report indicates the presence of a malignant neoplasm in the larynx with involvement of lymph nodes at different levels in the neck. The cancer showed invasion of surrounding tissues but did not involve the surgical margins.

This pathology report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma in the right base of the tongue. The tumor is moderately differentiated and invasive, with a depth of 0.5 mm. The lymph node submitted for analysis did not show any signs of neoplasm. Additionally, the report mentions the presence of skeletal muscle with scar, inflammation, and foreign body reaction in the soft tissue of the right neck.

This pathology report is for a patient named Abus Eld who has been diagnosed with squamous cell carcinoma in the buccal mucosa. The report describes the involvement of various lymph nodes and tissues in the right side of the patient's mouth. 

The margin of the inferior alveolar nerve is uninvolved by the neoplasia. In level IIB, two lymph nodes are identified and found to be uninvolved by the neoplasia. The skeletal muscle tissue is also uninvolved. In level IIA, one out of eight lymph nodes is found to have metastatic squamous cell carcinoma without capsular involvement. In level IIL, three lymph nodes are dissected and found to be uninvolved. In level IB, one lymph node is dissected and found to be uninvolved.

The report also mentions that the retromolar area and right palatine tonsil are infiltrated by moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. There is ulceration and infiltration present, but perineural invasion is not identified. The surgical margins are uninvolved. 

An addendum states that the neoplasia infiltrates the osseous tissue by contiguity, but the osseous tissue margin is uninvolved by the neoplasia.

The pathology report summarizes the findings of a surgical case involving a total laryngopharyngectomy (removal of the larynx and pharynx) and bilateral neck dissection. The diagnosis indicates the presence of invasive squamous cell carcinoma (a type of skin cancer) that is moderately to poorly differentiated and measures 8.5 cm in size. The tumor involves the left pyriform sinus and extends through the thyroid cartilage into the anterior soft tissue. Perineural and lymphovascular invasion is identified, indicating that the cancer has spread to nerves and blood vessels. The margins of resection are free of tumor, meaning that no cancer cells were found at the edges of the removed tissue. 

In the neck lymph nodes, five out of forty-two on the left side were positive for tumor, indicating lymph node involvement. The affected lymph nodes were found in level 3 of the left neck, and there is extranodal extension of the tumor present, meaning that cancer cells extend beyond the lymph node tissue. None of the lymph nodes on the right side had tumor involvement. 

The gross description of the surgical specimen provides details on the size and extent of the tumor. Separate tumor nodules were also noted in the anterior soft tissue component. The report further specifies the sections of the specimen that were submitted for examination.

The clinical history section states that no clinical information was provided for the patient.

Overall, the report confirms the presence of squamous cell carcinoma in the laryngopharynx, with lymph node involvement on the left side and an absence of tumor in the resection margins and right-sided lymph nodes.

This pathology report describes the findings of a surgical specimen from the patient's floor of the mouth. The main findings include:

1. No malignancy seen in the middle suprahyoid, left suprahyoid, or right suprahyoid regions.
2. No malignancy seen in the floor of mouth.
3. No malignancy seen in the left lateral border, right posterior border, or middle deep regions of the tongue.
4. Moderate differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma detected in the floor of the mouth, invading the underlying connective tissue, salivary gland, and bone.
5. Negative soft tissue resection margins.
6. Involvement of five out of thirteen lymph nodes in the neck, with focal extracapsular extension.
7. Pending bone resection margins.
8. Perineural invasion present.
9. No malignancy seen in the left level 5 lymph node, right level 5 lymph node, right level 28 lymph node, or left side level 14 (salivary gland).

The report also includes details about the tumor size, histologic type and grade, lymphovascular invasion, and the pathological TNM staging. Additional immunostain was performed to confirm metastatic carcinoma in one lymph node. Overall, the report suggests a moderately advanced local disease with metastasis to lymph nodes.

The pathology report states that the patient underwent a direct laryngoscopy with biopsy. The post-operative diagnosis was laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma. The pathology report also includes information on lymph nodes in the neck, which were found to be benign. Additionally, a total laryngectomy and right thyroid lobectomy were performed. The tumor was predominantly on the right side and measured 2.4 cm. It invaded the thyroid cartilage but did not show angiolympathic invasion or perineural invasion. The resection margins were free of tumor. One lymph node was found to be benign. The right lobe of the thyroid had benign follicular nodules. The final pathologic stage was pT4a NO Mx. The report also mentions a soft tissue specimen, which was normocellular parathyroid tissue. The gross description of the specimens is also included in the report.

This pathology report describes a case of invasive poorly differentiated squamous carcinoma found in the base of the tongue, supraglottic larynx, and subdigastric compartment. The report also mentions lymph node involvement in the neck. No tumor is found in the connective tissue overlying the left internal jugular vein or in the sublingual and submandibular glands. The report also mentions that there is no tumor present in the pharyngeal margin, soft palate, and nasopharynx. However, the tumor is extensive and invades various structures in the throat, including the vallecula, epiglottis, and palatoglossal arch. There is also a second tumor nodule present on the left aryepiglottic fold.

The patient had a excision of a base of tongue tumor. The tumor was poorly differentiated invasive squamous cell carcinoma with basaloid features. The size of the tumor was 1.7 cm in its greatest dimensions. There was no associated squamous cell carcinoma in situ identified. Angiolymphatic invasion was present, but perineural invasion was not identified. The new lateral margin was negative for tumor. The lymph nodes in levels 4 and 5 of the left neck were negative for tumor, but there was involvement of one lymph node in level 3 and involvement of soft tissue by poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. The overall stage of the tumor was T1,N1.

The pathology report describes a patient who presented with hoarseness and was found to have a large right-sided laryngeal lesion. The final diagnosis is invasive transglottic squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor is moderately differentiated and measures 3.8 cm. It invades through the thyroid cartilage and anterior soft tissue. There is no evidence of perineural or angiolymphatic invasion. All surgical resection margins are free of tumor. The lymph nodes in the right and left cervical regions (levels 2-4) are free of tumor. The pathologic stage is pT4a, NO, MX. No significant pathologic changes were observed in the right thyroid gland. A total laryngectomy was performed, as well as bilateral neck dissection and right thyroid lobectomy. The gross description of the specimen confirms the presence of the tumor and its involvement of surrounding structures. Several sections of the tumor, soft tissue margins, and lymph nodes were submitted for examination. Intraoperative consultation confirmed the involvement of the anterior soft tissue margin by the tumor.

The pathology report indicates that:

1. The superior mucosal margin (salivary gland) is negative for tumor.
2. The lateral margin (oral mucosa) is negative for tumor.
3. The inferior margin (oral mucosa) is negative for tumor.
4. The lymph nodes show metastatic carcinoma involving two out of nine nodes, with extracapsular extension identified.
5. Level III lymph nodes show metastatic carcinoma involving one out of seventeen nodes. Skeletal muscle is unremarkable.
6. Level IV lymph nodes and associated fibroadipose tissue are negative for tumor.
7. Level V lymph nodes are negative for tumor.
8. In total, metastatic carcinoma involves four out of fifty-two lymph nodes.
9. The left tonsil and soft palate (excision) show infiltrating poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma (3 cm) that extends to a depth of 3 cm with invasion of deep skeletal muscle. There is infiltrating carcinoma present within 1 mm of the deep margin. All other surgical margins are negative for tumor. Extensive angiolymphatic invasion is identified.

This pathology report describes the findings from a surgical biopsy of a patient with invasive squamous cell carcinoma. The report notes that the tumor is moderately differentiated and involves the mandibular bone, floor of mouth, ventral tongue, lower lip, mental skin, and bilateral lymph nodes. The surgical margins are negative for carcinoma, but perineural invasion is present. The report also mentions the presence of metastatic carcinoma in one lymph node and extranodal extension is not identified. In addition, the report mentions the presence of Actinomyces organisms consistent with actinomycosis in the mandibular bone. The report also includes information about the status of other excised tissues and lymph nodes in the neck, all of which are negative for carcinoma except for one lymph node in the right level 4, which shows metastatic carcinoma. The report concludes with a synoptic worksheet providing more detailed information about the specimen, tumor characteristics, and pathological staging.

The pathology report describes the findings from a surgical procedure and lymph node dissections. The main diagnosis is invasive squamous cell carcinoma in the larynx. On the right breast and axillary lymph nodes, a modified radical mastectomy showed invasive high-grade sarcomatoid (metaplastic) carcinoma, with areas of matrix-producing carcinoma. The invasive tumor measured 96 mm in diameter and showed lymphatic invasion near the periphery. Resection margins were free of invasive carcinoma, except for a margin located 40 mm inferiorly. Twenty-two axillary lymph nodes were examined and showed no tumor.

The pathologic tumor staging is as follows:
- Type and grade of invasive carcinoma: High-grade sarcomatoid carcinoma with areas of matrix-producing carcinoma
- Primary tumor stage: pT3
- Regional lymph node stage: pNO
- Distant metastasis stage: pMX
- Pathologic stage: IIB
- Lymphovascular invasion identified near periphery of tumor
- Margin status: Negative (RO)

The majority of the invasive carcinoma is characterized by solid sheets of high-grade malignant cells, with areas showing spindle cell morphology and anaplastic nuclear features. Tumor-associated necrosis is present, and glandular differentiation is not evident. This indicates the presence of sarcomatoid (metaplastic) carcinoma. Immunohistochemical staining supports the designation of metaplastic carcinoma and shows positive staining for p63, CKS/6, and smooth muscle actin. Staining for ER and PR is negative.

The invasive carcinoma is seen in association with a fibroepithelial neoplasm, likely a fibroadenoma with some features of a phyllodes tumor. High-grade malignant cells are seen lining the ducts/clefts of the fibroadenoma, suggesting invasion. However, it is less likely that the carcinoma has arisen from the epithelial component of the fibroadenoma.

Sarcomatoid carcinoma is a highly malignant tumor with the potential for distant metastasis.

The patient is a female with a diagnosis of left breast cancer (CA c50.3). She underwent left nodal radical mastectomy with procurement by surgical procedure. The pathological report states that the tumor mass was close to the anterior margin, with a possible tumor close to the interior margin. The tumor was analyzed for HER-2/neu amplification using fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and the ratio of HER-2/neu signals to chromosome 17 centromere signals was determined to be 2.09, indicating amplification of the gene. The final diagnosis also includes the results of estrogen and progesterone receptor assays and HER-2/neu staining. The estrogen receptor was interpreted as positive, the progesterone receptor as borderline positive, and HER-2/neu staining as nearly positive. There is mention of the assays being performed using FDA-approved methods, and the performance characteristics of the progesterone receptor assay were determined by the Department of Pathology. The final diagnosis is ductal carcinoma with focal lobular features.

Patient: Female, age not stated
Specimen: Sentinel node, right axillary; Right breast tissue

Final Diagnosis:
A. Sentinel node, right axillary: One lymph node negative for metastatic carcinoma.
B. Right breast tissue: Infiltrating ductal carcinoma, not otherwise specified, multifocal. Nottingham Grade: III/III. Nottingham Score: 8/9. Tumor size: Mass #1 - 1.0 cm, Mass #2 - 0.5 cm, Mass #3 - 1.2 cm. Tumor necrosis and microcalcifications present. No venous/lymphatic invasion identified. Margins involved. Intraductal component: Ductal carcinoma in situ, nuclear grade 3 (solid and comedo types). Estrogen and progesterone receptors positive. HER2 NEU negative. Pathologic stage: pT1c NO MX.
