Pathological report for a patient who underwent a total mastectomy of the left and right breast due to invasive ductal carcinoma. In the left breast, the carcinoma is poorly differentiated, with high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and no lymphovascular invasion. The invasive carcinoma measures 1.2 x 1.0 x 1.0 cm, with widely free margins. No tumor is present in the left axillary sentinel lymph nodes. In the right breast, the carcinoma is also poorly differentiated with high-grade DCIS and the presence of focal lymphovascular invasion. The invasive carcinoma measures 1.4 cm in greatest dimension, and there is no tumor present in the right sentinel lymph nodes. Further immunohistochemistry testing is required to evaluate the HER-2/neu gene copy level. The estrogen receptor is low positive, the progesterone receptor is negative, and the HER-2/neu overexpression is negative with focal 5% positivity. Additional sections are submitted for further evaluation.

The pathological report is for a patient who underwent a right mastectomy for breast cancer. The report states that the surgical margins were negative but close. Microscopic examination showed infiltrating ductal carcinoma, grade 3, measuring 4.3 cm. Sentinel lymph node #1 and #2 were examined and no evidence of metastasis was found in 3 lymph nodes from each specimen. No vessel invasion or calcification was identified. Ductal carcinoma in situ was not identified. The gross description of the mastectomy specimen indicates a large tumor measuring 4.3 cm and close proximity to the inked deep margin. No additional abnormalities were identified.

Summary:
The pathological report indicates that the patient's right axillary lymph node biopsy showed metastatic carcinoma in one out of one lymph node. The metastatic focus measures 3.5 cm and extracapsular extension is present. Additionally, the patient underwent a modified radical mastectomy, revealing infiltrating lobular carcinoma with pleomorphic and classical subtypes. The tumor measures 7.0 cm with a Nottingham score of 8/9. The tumor is multifocal and multicentric, present in different quadrants of the breast. Lobular carcinoma in situ is also present, comprising less than 5% of the total tumor volume. No lymphovascular invasion is identified. Margins are free of invasive carcinoma, but the tumor extends into the nipple without ulceration or pagetoid extension. Atypical ductal hyperplasia and previous biopsy site changes are observed. Of the ten axillary lymph nodes dissected, eight are positive for metastatic carcinoma. The largest dimension of the metastatic focus is 2.0 cm with extracapsular extension. The tumor is estrogen receptor-positive, progesterone receptor-positive, and HER-2/NEU-negative. The patient has stage pT3 disease, pN2a nodal involvement, and Mx metastasis status.

Summary:

This is a pathological report for a female patient with breast cancer. The cancer sample obtained from the right breast shows infiltrative ductal carcinoma, with a histological description. The tumor is located in the primary site, and the specimen is frozen. The patient has undergone a radical mastectomy, and the tumor is classified as grade 3, stage 2, with no evidence of spread to lymph nodes (N stage) or distant metastasis (M stage). The patient has not received any treatment yet. A normal blood sample was also obtained for analysis.

Pathological Report Summary:

The patient underwent a wide local excision in the right breast. The pathology report revealed infiltrating ductal carcinoma, Nottingham grade III, forming a mass measuring 2.3 x 1.9 x 1.8 cm. Ductal carcinoma in situ was not present. There is no angiolymphatic invasion. The surrounding non-neoplastic breast tissue showed nonproliferative fibrocystic changes. All surgical margins were free of tumor.

Lymph node dissection revealed that 3 out of 6 sentinel nodes were positive for metastatic carcinoma. Additionally, 2 out of 13 axillary lymph nodes were positive for metastatic carcinoma, with extranodal extension present.

Further testing for Her-2/NEU has been ordered on the tissue sample.

The final diagnosis is as follows:

1. Right breast segmental mastectomy with needle localization: There is a grade 3 invasive tumor measuring 2.1 cm in size. There is also ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) with a solid pattern, grade 3 nuclear grade, constituting about 5% of the total tumor volume. The resection margins are negative for carcinoma, with the invasive carcinoma being 1.5 mm to the closest anterior margin. There is no lymphovascular invasion noted. Foci of microcalcifications are associated with the invasive carcinoma. Fibrocystic change is also present. The invasive carcinoma is ER positive, PR positive, HER2/neu weakly positive, and there is no amplification by FISH analysis.

2. Axilla #1 sentinel lymph node, right, biopsy: One lymph node examined and found to be negative for metastatic carcinoma.

Overall staging: pT2 (pathologic T stage), N0 (pathologic N stage), MX (pathologic M stage).

Furthermore, the tumor is classified as ductal adenocarcinoma, not otherwise specified (NOS), with a Nottingham score of 9 (nuclear grade 3, tubule formation 3, mitotic activity score 3), resulting in a Nottingham grade of 3. There is no angiolymphatic invasion, dermal lymphatic invasion is not applicable, and calcifications are present in malignant zones. The surgical margins are not involved by the invasive or in situ components.

In this pathological report, the doctor received multiple specimens for analysis. These include a sentinel lymph node from the left axilla, a mastectomy specimen from the left breast, and a fragment from the upper outer quadrant of the left breast.

Upon gross examination, the sentinel lymph node was found to be firm and underwent sectioning and preparation. The mastectomy specimen weighed 1,184 grams and had multiple tumors present, with the closest tumor measuring 1.5 cm from the inferior/anterior aspect. The upper central and upper outer quadrants of the breast contained a grey-white, firm, stellate mass measuring 6.0 x 5.5 x 4.0 cm. Another lesion was found in the 7 o'clock position measuring 6.8 x 0.6 x 0.5 cm. An ill-defined nodular area was also identified 4.5 cm superior to the second lesion. Sections of the breast specimen were taken for further analysis, but no distinct lesions corresponding to the 12 o'clock and 10 o'clock positions were observed.

The fragment from the upper outer quadrant of the left breast did not reveal any grossly identifiable lesions and consisted mostly of yellow lobulated adipose tissue interspersed with grey-white fibrous tissue.

The doctor also made an amendment to the report to include final results for estrogen receptor/progesterone receptor and HER2/neu. The intraoperative consultation diagnosis revealed that the sentinel lymph node biopsy was positive for carcinoma.

Further analysis and examination of the specimens will be necessary to determine the extent and characteristics of the tumors and to provide a concrete diagnosis.

The gross description of the pathological report indicates the presence of a 3.5 cm tumor in a quadrant of the breast, with lymph nodes showing no abnormal features in the fatty tissue. The microscopic examination reveals an intraductal papillary adenocarcinoma with invasion, classified as G-2. The examined lymph nodes demonstrate lipomatosis. The diagnosis details indicate that the tumor features are indeterminate, with a tumor extent of T2 (size more than 2 cm but not more than 5 cm). There is no venous invasion, and margins are absent. The treatment effect is not specified. The Nottingham Histologic Score and additional pathologic findings are not determined or specified. There is no evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment. Overall, a moderately differentiated infiltrating papillary adenocarcinoma in the breast with lymph node involvement is reported.

The pathological report states that a histopathological examination was performed on a patient who underwent multiple organ resection, specifically of the left breast and axillary tissues. The examination revealed a tumor in the upper quadrant of the left breast, with measurements of 6.0 x 6.0 x 3.5 cm. The tumor was found to be invasive ductal carcinoma, with a histologic grade of NHG3 (3 + 2 + 3) and 35 mitoses per 10 high power fields. The examination also showed lesions of mastopathia fibrosa et cystica in the glandular tissue. Metastases of the carcinoma were present in the lymph nodes. Immunohistochemical examination showed the presence of estrogen receptors in 10-75% of neoplastic cell nuclei and progesterone receptors in over 75% of neoplastic cell nuclei. The HER2 protein was found to be negative in the invasive cancerous cells. It is recommended that the patient contact their doctor with this report.

Summary:

The pathological report indicates that a 52-year-old female patient underwent surgery for breast cancer. The diagnosis is infiltrative ductal carcinoma, indicating cancer that has spread from the milk ducts into the surrounding breast tissue. The tumor was located in the right breast and its grade is 2. There is no evidence of cancer spread to other parts of the body (lymph nodes or distant metastasis) at this stage. The patient has not undergone any treatment yet. A normal blood sample was also taken for comparison.

Summary:

The lumpectomy revealed an infiltrating poorly differentiated ductal carcinoma, measuring 2.4 cm in size, with clear resection margins and lymphovascular invasion. The tumor tested positive for estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR), and negative for HER2. The right breast tissue showed fibrocystic changes with stromal fibrosis, adenosis, and microcalcifications. The tumor is classified as invasive ductal carcinoma, with a histologic grade of III and a Nottingham Score of 8-9. No metastases were detected in the lymph nodes examined. The margins were free of invasive carcinoma, and there was evidence of venous/lymphatic invasion. The report also includes details about the gross appearance of the specimens received. An addendum to the report states that a keratin immunostain was negative for carcinoma.

The pathological report indicates a diagnosis of invasive lobular carcinoma grade 1 in the right axillary lymph node, along with lobular carcinoma in situ. The pathological report shows a tumor in the breast tissue measuring 2.5x2.3 cm. The lymph nodes are also affected. The biopsy confirms infiltrating ductal carcinoma. - The sentinel lymph node in the left axilla showed no tumor.
- In the left breast lumpectomy, there was invasive ductal carcinoma with a high grade and focal necrosis, as well as associated lymphocytic infiltrate. Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) was also present and associated with the invasive carcinoma.

- There was no evidence of blood vessel or lymphatic invasion, and the axillary lymph nodes were negative for tumor.

- The pTNM staging of the tumor was pT2, NO(sn), MX.

The pathological report describes a right breast partial mastectomy performed on a 50-year-old female with a 1.4 cm tumor. The tumor is described as grade 2, and the staging indicates that it is a primary tumor with no lymph node involvement or distant metastasis. The pathological report describes a lumpectomy of the left breast. The specimen contains two areas of concern marked 1 and 2, with area 2 being a regular mass with well-defined borders. Microscopic examination reveals an infiltrating ductal carcinoma, poorly differentiated, with areas of high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ. The tumor is single focus and measures 1.9 cm. The Nottingham combined histologic grade is 8-9, indicating poor differentiation. No neo-adjuvant treatment is evident. Additional pathologic findings are not specified, and there are no comments.

The pathological report indicates the presence of carcinoma in the patient. The report also includes information about the patient's medical history, diagnostic studies, and staging of the tumor. Further details about the tumor's size and extension, lymph node involvement, and distant metastasis are provided. The patient is a 30-year-old female who underwent a mastectomy for right breast cancer. Additionally, there is a concomitant DCIS (Ductal Carcinoma In Situ) of malignancy grade I, with the procomponent of the tumor being less than 10%. The tumor is classified as G2 (moderately differentiated), pT1c (size category), pNO (no lymph node involvement), MX (distant metastasis cannot be assessed), and RO (minimum width of dorsocranial safety margin is 1 cm). The report includes unique identifying codes and references to other technical information.

3. Gross description: The received specimen consists of a 3.5 x 1.1 x 0.4 cm piece of soft tissue containing a lymph node. The left breast excision specimen is a 4.1 x 3.2 x 3 cm lumpectomy without radiographs, inked per protocol. The slice sections reveal a 1.9 x 1.4 x 1.3 cm firm tan circumscribed mass closest to the medial margin at less than 0.2 cm.

The margins are negative, with a distance from the closest margin of 0.2 cm. Tubular score is 3, nuclear grade is 2, mitotic score is 3, and the Modified Scarf-Bloom-Richardson grade is 3. Necrosis is absent, and there is no vascular/lymphatic invasion or lobular neoplasia. Only sentinel lymph node was identified, and it was negative for metastases (0/1).

Overall, the left breast excision specimen shows invasive ductal carcinoma with high grade features, and there is no evidence of tumor in the additional margins or lymph nodes sampled.

The pathological report indicates that the patient underwent a wide local excision of the right breast and a dissection of the right axillary contents. The examination revealed invasive ductal carcinoma, poorly differentiated with apocrine features, and several foci of microinvasion associated with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). The tumor measures at least 3 cm in size and is 2 mm from the deep margin. Extensive lymphovascular invasion is present. The DCIS is solid type, nuclear grade 3, with necrosis and associated lymphoid infiltrate, involving lobules. It is present at the lateral margin and within 1 mm of the anterior/medial and anterior margin, and within 2 mm of the deep margin. Axillary dissection showed metastatic carcinoma in 2 out of 25 lymph nodes, with the largest metastasis measuring 4 cm. No extracapsular extension is seen. The margins of the excised breast tissue are negative. The ER and PR receptors are negative, and HER2 is positive.

The pathological report indicates that the breast resection sample shows a 1.8 cm moderately differentiated tubulolobular carcinoma with an intraductal tumor component. The tumor has a minimum margin of 5 mm at 12 o'clock, over 10 mm at 3 o'clock, and about 1 mm at 6 o'clock (well over 10 mm at 9 o'clock). There is no evidence of lymph vessel invasion. The tumor classification is M-8500/3, grade 2, pT1e, pLO, pSNO (0/2), pMx, stage I. R0.

The patient's pathological report reveals the following findings:

- The invasive carcinoma covers an area of approximately 3 cm.
- The invasive carcinoma extends to within 3.0 mm of deep, 3.0 mm of inferior, and 5.0 mm of superficial margins.

5. Left axilla, level 1 and 2 lymph nodes, excision:

- The metastatic carcinoma measures 2.8 cm in greatest dimension.
- Extranodal extension up to 3.0 mm present.

6. Left axillary level 3 lymph node:
- No tumor present.

Additionally, a radial scar and cyst were identified.

Gross description:

- Left breast implant and partial capsulectomy: A tan-yellow plastic breast implant devoid of contents, with an irregular piece of tan-yellow fibroadipose tissue attached to its surface.

Further investigation and treatment may be required based on these findings.

The pathological report indicates that the patient underwent a simple mastectomy for breast cancer. Multiple nodules of infiltrating lobular carcinoma were identified in the upper outer quadrant of the breast. The cancer shows HER2/neu protein overexpression and has metastasized to the right axillary sentinel lymph node. Another lesion was found in the same quadrant, but there is no evidence of metastasis to the lymph nodes. Extensive ductal carcinoma in situ is also present. The non-neoplastic breast tissue shows benign fibrocystic changes. The surgical margins are negative for tumor. Only one out of 12 axillary sentinel lymph nodes is positive for metastatic carcinoma. HER2/neu amplification was not demonstrated by fluorescence in situ hybridization. Further testing will be done to confirm HER2/neu amplification.

The pathological report describes a case of breast cancer. The report indicates the presence of multiple areas of invasive papillary carcinoma in the right breast, with the largest area measuring 0.8 cm. The report also mentions the presence of metastatic carcinoma in the lymph nodes. The cancer is graded as grade 1 based on the tumor size and other factors. No evidence of skin involvement or nipple involvement is observed. The report also mentions the surgical procedures performed, including a mastectomy and sentinel node mapping. The frozen section analysis confirmed the presence of carcinoma.

The pathological report indicates the following findings:

- The sentinel lymph node in the left axilla shows metastatic ductal carcinoma in a 2 cm focus.
- Two out of fourteen lymph nodes in the left axilla show metastatic ductal carcinoma.
- No tumor is found in one lymph node in left axilla level III.
- The left breast, which underwent modified radical mastectomy, shows invasive ductal carcinoma, ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), high-grade with micropapillary and cribriform patterns.
- Invasive carcinoma is present at the inked anterior-superior resection margin.
- Microcalcifications are seen in the DCIS.
- Non-proliferative fibrocystic change with apocrine metaplasia and microcysts are present.
- A benign sclerosing papilloma is found.
- The excised anterior/superior/medial margin of the left breast shows invasive ductal carcinoma, SBR grade 3, close to the inked margin.
- The skin nodule on the left breast shows invasive ductal carcinoma, SBR grade 3, in the dermis, subcutaneous tissue, and fibrous tissue, possibly originating from a scar.
- No significant pathologic abnormality or tumor is found in the newest anterior/superior/medial margin of the skin.
- The biopsy of the left nipple margin shows benign lactiferous ducts without tumor.
- No tumor is detected in two non-sentinel lymph nodes in the dissection.
- No tumor is detected in one non-sentinel lymph node biopsy.
- The tumor in the main mastectomy specimen is characterized by infiltrating trabeculae, nests, and glands of cells with clear cytoplasm and pleomorphic nuclei. Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is present but only in scattered foci mixed with the invasive tumor.
- Invasive carcinoma is found at the inked anterior-superior margin of the main specimen, while the additional margin shows narrowly excised invasive tumor.
- The skin nodule contains invasive ductal carcinoma within the subcutaneous tissue, dermis, and beneath the epidermis. It is close to the excision margin and involves an area of fibrosis suggestive of a skin scar.
- Immunohistochemical studies indicate that the tumor does not support a diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma but supports renal tumor.

The pathological report indicates that the patient has ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) as well as invasive carcinoma in the right breast. DCIS accounts for less than or equal to 25% of the total tumor mass and is accompanied by the invasive component. The invasive carcinoma is located in the lower outer quadrant of the breast. There is no involvement of the nipple by either in situ or invasive carcinoma. Calcifications are present in the invasive carcinoma. Vascular invasion is also present. The surgical margins are not involved by either in situ or invasive carcinoma. No lymph node metastasis is identified. The results of special stains for estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor are included, showing positive staining for estrogen receptor and negative staining for progesterone receptor in 90% of the tumor cells. Further testing for HER2 overexpression is recommended.

B. Sentinel node #1: One lymph node positive for metastatic lobular carcinoma.

D. Left breast tissue: Invasive lobular carcinoma, grade 2, with no lymphovascular invasion or ductal carcinoma in situ.

Note: This information is transmitted to the institution's Cancer Registry for accreditation purposes. The pathology stage is based solely on the current tissue specimen and does not incorporate other relevant data. It is only a component to be considered in determining the clinical stage.

The surgical pathology report indicates that the procedure performed was an excision of lymph node #2 and resections in the right breast. The diagnosis for the lymph node shows isolated cytokeratin positive cells. In the right breast, there is a 2.6 cm invasive lobular carcinoma that extends to involve the inferior and lateral margins. Microscopic examination was performed and no metastasis was seen on staining. The carcinoma is classified as invasive lobular cancer with an overall grade of 2. The pathological report indicates that the patient underwent a HER2 gene amplification test using dual in situ hybridization. The results showed that the patient is negative for HER2 gene amplification. The test was performed as a reflex test after the HER2/NEU immunostain was scored as 2+. The specimen used for the test was a formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue slide. The assay allows for co-hybridization and visualization of the HER2 gene and Chr17 centromere on the same slide. The HER2 gene is detected using a dinitrophenyl labeled probe, while the Chr17 centromere is targeted with a digoxigenin labeled probe. Slide scoring was performed, and if the HER2/Chr17 ratio falls within 1.8-2.2, additional nuclei scoring is recommended. The HER2 gene status is reported as non-amplified if the ratio is less than 2.0, or amplified if the ratio is greater than 2.0.

In addition, immunohistochemical evaluation was performed on the tissue for estrogen receptors, progesterone receptors, and HER-2NEU in invasive mammary carcinoma. The results showed 99% positivity for estrogen receptors and 40% positivity for progesterone receptors. The staining intensity for both receptors was reported as moderate. HER-2NEU scoring was equivocal with a score of 2+. The immunohistochemical studies used monoclonal antibodies and control sections for proper evaluation. The reactivity of estrogen and progesterone receptors was determined based on the percentage of positive cells, with reference values indicating positivity if nuclear staining is present in 1% or more of invasive carcinoma cells. The staining intensity for HER-2NEU was evaluated according to CAP scoring guidelines.

Summary of Pathological Report:
This report is for a 77-year-old female patient with breast cancer. The diagnosis is infiltrative lobular carcinoma. The cancer sample was taken from the right breast during surgery. The tumor is grade 2 and at stage 1 with no spread to nearby lymph nodes or other organs. The patient has not received any treatment yet. A normal blood sample was also taken. The report confirms the presence of infiltrative lobular carcinoma in the breast tissue. The TCGA team has classified it as ductal. Further testing and treatment recommendations are needed.

The final diagnosis is as follows: 

1. Left axillary sentinel lymph node #1: biopsy shows metastatic breast carcinoma.
2. Breast: left, modified radical mastectomy reveals multifocal infiltrating mixed ductal and lobular carcinoma. Tumor measures 6.0x5.5x250mm and is located in multiple quadrants (multicentric tumor). Angiolymphatic invasion is identified. Lobular carcinoma in situ accounts for 10% of the tumor and is admixed with the tumor. All margins are negative for invasive mixed ductal-lobular carcinoma and lobular carcinoma in situ. The nipple has focal invasive carcinoma in the deep stromal tissue, with duct ectasia and chronic inflammation in the nipple and skin of the breast. Estrogen receptor positive, progesterone receptor positive, HER-2NEU negative. Biopsy site changes, fibrocystic changes with ductal epithelial hyperplasia, columnar cell changes, and microscopic peripheral ductal papilloma are also present.
3. Left pectoralis minor muscle excision shows striated skeletal muscle free of tumor confirmed by immunostain.
4. Left axilla, level 3, lymph node excision reveals six lymph nodes. All nodes are positive for metastatic carcinoma with extra capsular spread.

Summary: The patient has multifocal infiltrating mixed ductal and lobular carcinoma in the left breast with metastasis to the left axillary lymph nodes. The tumor shows angiolymphatic invasion and lobular carcinoma in situ. The nipple has focal invasive carcinoma. Estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor are positive, while HER-2NEU is negative. The surgical margins are negative for tumor involvement.

Final Diagnosis:

- Invasive ductal carcinoma, 2.0 cm, Nottingham Grade 1 (tumor formation score 1/3, nuclear pleomorphism score 2/3, mitotic activity score 1/3)
- Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), nuclear grade 2, cribriform type, constituting approximately 5% of the tumor volume and admixed with the invasive component
- Lymphovascular space invasion not identified
- Margins free, closest anterior/superior within 0.6 cm
- Additional findings include ductal epithelial hyperplasia, fibrocystic changes, sclerosing adenosis, columnar cell change, fibroadenomatoid nodules, and biopsy site changes
- Lymph node involvement: One of two lymph nodes involved, extracapsular extension identified (0.1 cm x 0.07 cm)
- One sentinel lymph node involved, extracapsular extension not identified
- One additional lymph node negative for metastatic carcinoma
- Radial scar, fibrocystic changes, sclerosing adenosis, ductal epithelial hyperplasia, columnar cell change with associated calcifications, and fat necrosis identified in the new lateral margin excision
- Estrogen and progesterone receptors positive, HER2/NEU negative or 1+.
- Pathologic staging: pT1c, pN1, pMx

The margins were clear with a distance of 0.2 cm from the nearest margin. In addition, there was a component of ductal carcinoma in situ with intermediate nuclear grade and central necrosis. Estrogen and progesterone receptors were positive, HER2 was negative, and there were no lymph node metastases identified in the sentinel nodes. The pathologic stage was pT1c NO(i-) MK. Fibrocystic changes and changes from prior biopsy were also noted.

The HER2/neu staining is negative. Additional testing and examination were performed to reach this diagnosis.

The tumor has four foci with a maximum diameter of 2 cm, 3 cm, 0.2 cm, and 2.5 cm. There is also a high-grade intraductal carcinoma with comedo necroses in the tumor periphery. The tumor is surrounded by mastopathy, scleradenosis with microcalcifications, cystic mastopathy, and cylindrical epithelial metaplasia. The overlying skin and nipple are tumor-free, and there is no pagetoid pattern of spread. The outer resection margins are tumor-free. The tumor is classified as M-8500/3, grade 3, and classified as pT2 (m), pN1a (2/25), pMX, stage IIB. The resection is considered complete (RO).

The pathological report shows that a simple mastectomy was performed on the patient's left breast. The report confirms the presence of infiltrating pleomorphic lobular carcinoma, a type of breast cancer. The tumor is graded as Nottingham grade II, indicating moderately differentiated cancer cells. The tumor forms a large mass in the central region of the breast with a separate smaller nodule adjacent to it. Lobular carcinoma in situ is also present within and outside the invasive component. No angiolymphatic invasion is observed. The surrounding non-neoplastic breast tissue shows fibrocystic changes and benign calcifications. The tumor does not involve the nipple, skin, or chest wall. Further testing for Her-2/Neu is ordered on the tissue.

The pathological report shows a biopsy of the left breast, which revealed infiltrating ductal carcinoma measuring 2.2 cm. The tumor is moderately differentiated and histologic grade 3. The tumor also exhibits loss of expression of the binding protein PIAS2. This type of tumor is commonly associated with somatic hypermethylation of the promote region of the MLH gene. There is a possibility of an inherited predisposition to the formation of muRipe serrated neoplasms. The report suggests that individuals with this type of tumor are at an increased risk of metachronous cancer of the right colon.

The report mentions that about 10% of MLH deficient tumors are caused by inherited gene defects in the MLH gene (Lynch syndrome). BRAF mutation analysis was conducted and no mutations were detected. The report also mentions that BRAF mutations in colorectal cancer render the tumor resistant to anti-EGFR therapy. The report concludes by indicating the tumor has invaded nearby tissue and lymphovascular invasion is present. No lymph node status is mentioned in the report.

The pathology report describes a resection of the right colon. The specimen is a 15 cm segment of the proximal right colon with attached distal ileum. There is a tumor mass located in the cecal pouch, 1 cm distal to the ileocecal valve. The tumor is described as a moderately-differentiated adenocarcinoma with mucinous differentiation. It has invaded through the muscularis propria into the pericolonic fat (pT3). The margins of resection (proximal, distal, and radial) are negative for tumor. No vascular invasion is observed. A total of 24 lymph nodes are negative for metastatic carcinoma. Distant metastasis cannot be determined.

This pathology report is for a 50-year-old female with a clinical history of right colon cancer. The specimen received is a right hemicolectomy, including the right colonic segment, terminal ileal segment, appendix, and pericolic lymph nodes. The diagnosis is mucinous adenocarcinoma, signet ring cell type, extending into subserosal tissue. The tumor size is 7.0 x 7.0 x 5.0 cm. The surgical margins are negative for carcinoma, with the invasive carcinoma being within 0.05 cm of the circumferential margin. There is no evidence of metastasis in the pericolic lymph nodes. The gross configuration of the tumor is exophytic, ulcerating. The histologic grade is moderately to poorly differentiated. There is no identified pre-existing polyp. No vascular invasion or perineural invasion is identified. The tumor border configuration is pushing. An additional pathologic finding is a hyperplastic polyp. Thirteen lymph nodes were examined and none were involved. The pathologic staging is pT3N0M0. Immunostains for cytokeratins are negative. The pathologic stage is provisional and does not incorporate the patient's clinical status or prior pathology.

The pathology report describes a surgical resection of the right colon due to a suspected adenocarcinoma. Two masses were identified, one in the cecum and one in the ascending colon. The cecal mass measured 6.4 cm and was high-grade, while the ascending colon mass measured 7.8 cm and was low-grade. Both masses showed invasion through the muscularis propria. Lymphovascular invasion was present. Two tubular adenomas were also found. The margins of resection were clear of carcinoma. The report confirms a diagnosis of colonic adenocarcinoma and provides the pathological staging as pT3N1b for both masses.

This pathology report describes the findings from the samples of the terminal ileum, right colon, and gallbladder. 

In the right colon and terminal ileum resection, the main finding is a moderately differentiated infiltrating colonic adenocarcinoma measuring 3.1 cm. It has extended into the subserosal fat. Seventeen benign lymph nodes were found out of 17 examined. Multiple tubular adenomas were also present. The surgical margins of the small bowel and appendix were not involved. 

In the gallbladder excision, chronic cholelithiasis (the presence of gallstones) was found.

The colorectal cancer template provides additional details about the tumor, including its site (ascending colon), configuration (exophytic), size (8.1 x 2.5 x 0.6 cm), histological type (adenocarcinoma), histological grade (well differentiated), and extent of invasion (focal subserosal adipose tissue). The surgical margins were uninvolved, and no angiolymphatic or perineural invasion was observed. Multiple tubular adenomas were also noted. The extent of resection was complete, and there were no lymph node involvement or implants. The pathological stage was pT2.NO MX.

The gross description of the specimens provides information about their appearance and measurements. The terminal ileum and right colon segment measures approximately 24 cm in length, with a mass present in the ascending colon measuring 3.1 x 2.5 cm. Additional polyps were found in the ascending colon. The gallbladder measures 7.5 x 4.0 x 1.2 cm and appears grossly unremarkable except for the presence of gallstones.

Overall, the pathology report indicates the presence of a moderately differentiated colonic adenocarcinoma with involvement of the subserosal fat. There are also multiple tubular adenomas and chronic cholelithiasis in the gallbladder. The lymph nodes examined were benign and there was no involvement of the surgical margins.

The pathology report describes a right colon specimen from a patient diagnosed with cancerous cecum. The gross description of the specimen indicates the presence of a tumor mass within the cecal pouch, measuring 2.8 x 2.5 cm. The tumor extends through the muscularis propria into the subserosal fat. The margins of excision are negative, indicating that the tumor has been completely removed. There is no evidence of vascular invasion. Twenty-three lymph nodes retrieved from the mesentery and mesocolon are negative for tumor involvement. The histologic type is adenocarcinoma, and it is moderately differentiated. The appendix and ileum are unremarkable, and there is evidence of diverticulosis in the colon.

The pathology report indicates that a right hemicolectomy was performed and the margins of the resection were tumor-free. The report also states that there is an ulcerated, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the region of the Bauhin's valve and the cecum, with infiltration of the surrounding adipose tissue. Additionally, there are four regional lymph node metastases present. The tumor is classified as G2 and is classified as pT3, L1, V0, with local regional overgrowth and lymph node involvement (pN2, 4/23).

Summary:
The pathology report describes a large intestine resection surgery in which a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (a type of cancer) of the colorectal type was found. The tumor was 4.5 cm in diameter and showed infiltration of the pericolic fatty tissue, extensive lymphangiosis carcinomatosa (spread of the cancer through lymphatic vessels), and metastasis to thirty-two regional lymph nodes. The resection margins were clear of tumor. The tumor stage was determined to be pT3 (indicating invasion into the intestinal wall), pN2 (indicating metastasis to regional lymph nodes), and pMX (indicating no distant metastasis). The tumor was classified as Grade 3.

This pathology report describes a case of slightly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the cecum. The tumor is graded as G3, meaning it is moderately differentiated. The tumor has erosion and ulceration on its inner surface and is accompanied by chronic recurrent inflammation and abscess formation. The tumor has infiltrated all layers of the cecal wall up to a depth of 0.1 cm below the serosa. There is also tumor infiltration of the base of the appendix and evidence of chronic recurrent appendicitis. The lymph nodes around the tumor show moderately chronic inflammation but no evidence of tumor involvement (0/20 lymph nodes). The tumor is classified as stage pT3, meaning it has spread beyond the original site but has not invaded nearby organs or spread to lymph nodes. There is no evidence of cancer involvement in the blood vessels or any serous carcinoma.

The pathology report describes a specimen from a patient who underwent a hemicolectomy, which is the removal of part of the colon. The report states that the patient's diagnosis prior to surgery was adenocarcinoma of the transverse colon mass. Upon examination of the specimen, a 2.8 x 2.3 cm, tan-brown, fungating mass was found on the colonic mucosa, near the margin of the colon. This mass did not penetrate the muscular layer of the colon. No additional lesions were identified. Lymph nodes were identified within the associated fat, ranging in size from 0.3 to 14 cm.

In addition to the colon specimen, a segment of small bowel was also received. This segment measured 2.3 cm in length and 27 cm in diameter. Lymph nodes were also found within the associated fat of the small bowel.

The report does not mention any known treatment for the patient's condition prior to the surgery. The type of tumor is not specified. The report also states that there were no tumor cells detected in the lymph nodes that were examined.

The pathology report shows that a right hemicolectomy with en bloc resection was performed. The specimen received was a 24 cm segment of proximal right colon with attached 17 cm of distal ileum. The specimen had a smooth to scabrous tan-pink serosa with moderate inflammation present. A fragment of red-brown skeletal muscle was found near the cecal pouch. The proximal and distal margins of the specimen measured 4 cm and 8 cm in circumference, respectively. On opening the specimen, there was a nearly 2.8 cm thickness of tissue, extending into the muscularis to within 0.15 cm of the inked cauterized surgical margin and within 0.6 cm of the inked free radial serosal surface. The mucosa of the ileum and remaining colonic wall appeared normal. Palpable lymph nodes were found in the mesocolon and mesentery. Sections of representative tissue were submitted for further analysis. The histological diagnosis was adenocarcinoma, moderately-differentiated. The tumor had invaded through the muscularis propria into the serosal fat. The margins of resection were negative for tumor invasion. No metastatic carcinoma was found in the 19 examined mesenteric lymph nodes. There was a pericolonic abscess present next to the tumor, causing adhesion of the abdominal wall to the colon, but there was no direct invasion by the tumor at that site. The appendix also had no significant histopathological findings.

The pathology report describes a right colon and terminal ileum resection specimen. The main findings are as follows:

1) There is an infiltrating poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colon with medullary features. The tumor has invaded through the muscularis propria into the subserosa. Its size is 7x5x1.2 cm. The resection margins are clear and there is no tumor seen. All 23 lymph nodes examined are negative for cancer metastasis.

2) Multiple tubular adenomas and hyperplastic polyps are also present in the ascending colon.

The report provides further details regarding the size, grade, invasion depth, and lymph node involvement of the adenocarcinoma. The stage of the cancer is classified as pT3NO MX. The report also mentions the absence of implants and the presence of precursor lesions (tubular adenomas and hyperplastic polyps) in the non-neoplastic areas.

The gross description of the specimen mentions the tumor location, size, and its penetration into the muscularis propria and subserosal fat. Multiple polypoid lesions are seen in the right colon, with the most distal one located more than 10 cm away from the surgical margin. The remaining colonic mucosa and terminal ileum appear grossly normal.

The report concludes with a list of representative sections that have been taken for microscopic examination, including tumor samples, polypoid lesions, uninvolved colonic mucosa, surgical margins, and lymph nodes.

The pathology report describes a recurrence of a sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma. The tumor is 9 mm in its largest dimension and is located in the sigmoid colon. The lymph nodes show reactive changes and there is no evidence of infiltration or metastasis. The tumor is ulcerated and moderately differentiated. The extent of the tumor involves the pericolonic tissues. No information is provided regarding the size of the specimen, the presence of margins, or the presence of neoadjuvant treatment.

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

- Tumor type: Low (specific type not mentioned)
- There is no invasion of surrounding spaces or lymphovascular spaces.
- Tumor does not penetrate into the superficial muscularis propria.
- Margin status: The deep (radial) margin is negative.
- There is no lymph node involvement.
- Other significant finding: The tumor arises within a tubular adenoma with high-grade dysplasia.
- Postoperative diagnosis: Ascending colon mass with high-grade dysplasia.
- Gross description: The specimen consists of a previously resected right colon mass, measuring 0.4 cm in thickness. The gross appearance does not indicate tumor infiltration into the wall, except for a small area. The rest of the colon and appendix appear normal.
- Microscopic examination: Further sections of the lesion were examined, along with representative sections of the ileocecal valve and lymph nodes.

Overall, the report suggests a low-grade tumor with no invasion of surrounding structures or lymph nodes. The tumor arises within a tubular adenoma with high-grade dysplasia. The margins of resection are negative.

The pathology report describes a partial resection of the colon and caecum due to a clinical diagnosis of cancer of the hepatic flexure. The macroscopic examination reveals a thickened ulceration measuring 4 x 3 cm in the mucosa, which covers 100% of the intestine circumference and infiltrates the perintestinal tissue. Microscopically, the tumor is identified as tubular adenocarcinoma with infiltration into the peritumoral adipose tissue. The ends of the intestine are clear of neoplastic lesions. The lymph nodes show reactive changes and there is a histopathological diagnosis of tubular adenocarcinoma (Dukes B) with a stage of pT3 and no lymph node involvement (pNO).

The patient had a resection of their colon due to a tumor. The resection margins were clear, indicating that the tumor was completely removed. The pathology report identified a hyperplastic polyp and several tubular adenomas with mild to moderate dysplasia (pre-cancerous changes). In addition, there was an ulcerated, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma present in the colon. The adenocarcinoma had invaded the surrounding perimuscular adipose tissue and had spread to several nearby lymph nodes. The adenocarcinoma was classified as G2 (moderately differentiated), pT3 (tumor extends into surrounding tissues), L1 (lymphatic involvement), VO (vascular invasion), with a clear surgical margin (local RO), and pN2 (presence of lymph node metastases, 5 out of 25 lymph nodes involved).

The pathology report describes the resected section of the colon (specifically the descending and sigmoid colon) and provides the following findings:

1. Tumor-free oral and aboral resection margins: The margins of the resected colon section are clear from any tumor cells.
2. Ulcerated, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma: A cancerous tumor with moderate differentiation is present, showing ulceration, in the wall of the colon.
3. Infiltration and regional lymph node metastases: The tumor has extended into the lamina muscularis propria layer of the colon wall, and several nearby lymph nodes show evidence of tumor spread (metastasis). 
4. Florid perifocal inflammation: There is a distinct and extensive inflammation around the tumor area.
5. Encroachment on the peritoneum of the abdominal wall: The inflammation is spreading towards the membrane lining the abdominal wall (peritoneum).

This pathology report describes the findings from a right hemicolectomy and peritoneal biopsy. 

In the right colon specimen, a 5.5 x 4.0 x 3.0 cm mass is identified in the cecal area. The tumor is ulcerated, invasive, and moderately to poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma. It extends to the ileocecal valve, involves the full muscle wall thickness, and extends into the peri-colonic fat. There are metastases to 50 out of 59 pericolonic lymph nodes, with perinodal fat extension. A small 0.6 cm tubulovillous adenoma is found 7 cm from the distal margin, and a small 0.4 cm polypoid adenocarcinoma with submucosal extension is found 3 cm from the ileocecal valve. The appendix is not identifiable. 

The peritoneal biopsy is positive for adenocarcinoma.

Overall, the tumor is classified as moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with lymphovascular invasion and metastases to lymph nodes and perinodal fat. The extent of invasion includes the lamina propria, submucosa, muscularis propria, and subserosa. The margins of the resected specimen are uninvolved by invasive carcinoma. Venous/lymphatic invasion is present, while perineural invasion is absent. In addition to the adenocarcinoma, a tubulovillous adenoma is also present. The pathological staging is pT3N2M1. 
There is no clinical history provided.

The pathology report describes the findings from a sigmoid colon resection surgery. The report includes information about the specimens received and their measurements, as well as a gross description of each specimen. It then provides a diagnosis for each specimen, including the presence of a moderately and poorly differentiated invasive adenocarcinoma in the sigmoid colon. The report also mentions the absence of malignancy in the proximal and distal margins.

Additional findings include the presence of a tubular adenoma and metastatic carcinoma in two out of twenty-four lymph nodes with extranodal extension. The report concludes with the pathological staging of the tumor as pT3N1MX.

An addendum is mentioned, which will provide the results of the analysis of mismatch repair protein expression.

Overall, the report indicates the presence of an invasive adenocarcinoma in the sigmoid colon with metastasis to lymph nodes, but further information is needed from the addendum regarding mismatch repair protein expression.

Summary:

- The pathology report is for a right hemicolectomy specimen, which includes the right colon, appendiceal region, and a segment of ileum.
- The colon measures 14.5 cm in length and up to 6 cm in diameter.
- The appendix is dilated and measures 6.5 cm in length and up to 1.2 cm in diameter.
- There is a fungating mass originating from the appendix, measuring 4.3 cm x 3.5 cm and located 11 cm from the colonic margin of resection.
- A portion of the tumor is taken for research purposes.
- The tumor is classified as colon adenocarcinoma, grade 2.
- The cancer has invaded the propria of the colon into the surrounding pericolonic soft tissues.
- There is moderate acute and chronic inflammation present.
- There is no evidence of malignancy in the attached lymph nodes.
- The PINK stage is 13, indicating no positive lymph nodes.
- The distal appendices lumen is obstructed with fibrosis.

This pathology report describes a right colectomy specimen from a patient diagnosed with cecal cancer. The specimen consists of a segment of the proximal right colon with attached distal ileum. The gross examination reveals a tumor mass occupying the cecal pouch and extending up to the ileocecal valve. The tumor is poorly defined, rubbery to friable, and measures 9.0 x 5.5 cm in size. It has invaded through the muscularis propria into the pericolonic fat. The proximal and distal margins are negative for tumor, but there is lymphatic space invasion and metastatic adenocarcinoma present in 11 out of 23 lymph nodes. The report mentions the presence of an adenomatous polyp adjacent to the tumor and an unremarkable appendix. Overall, the diagnosis is invasive poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colon with lymph node metastasis (pT3N2b).

The pathology report is difficult to interpret as it appears to contain typographical errors and is not clear in its organization. However, it mentions the examination of a rectosigmoid colon, measurements taken, and there is a reference to a liver biopsy. There is also a mention of a specimen labeled "DUAEL METS TE sgug" and a section regarding the "moze sect. site ro." Overall, further clarification is needed to fully understand the report.

This pathology report describes a specimen from an extended hemicolectomy, which was performed to remove two invasive adenocarcinomas with infiltration of the pericolic fatty tissue. The patient had previously undergone endoscopic resection for another adenocarcinoma. Multiple tubular adenomas with moderate dysplasia were also present. Two lymph node metastases were found, but the resection margins in the mucosa and omentum were tumor-free. The tumor is classified as adenocarcinoma, grade 2, with a pT3 stage and negative lymph node involvement.

This pathology report describes a case of adenocarcinoma of the cecum. The tumor has invaded the muscularis propria and pericecal soft tissue margin. It has also spread to the omentum and mesenteric margin. The tumor is high-grade and poorly differentiated. It has metastasized to lymph nodes and has invaded blood vessels. The tumor is 6.5 cm in size and there are no additional tumor characteristics found. There are adenomas present as well. The report also provides information on the specimen type, dimensions, and margins. The pathology stage of the tumor is determined to be pT3cld N2 M1.

Summary: The pathology report describes a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. The tumor is highly aggressive and includes areas of anaplastic solid carcinoma. There are ulcerations and necrosis within the tumor, and it has invaded the layers of the colon wall, reaching the subserous fatty connective tissue. The tumor has also spread to nearby lymph nodes, causing chronic lymphadenitis. The tumor stage is determined to be pT3, pN2, MX, LI, RO.

The pathology report describes a resected colon (specifically the sigma region) with tumor-free margins on both ends. The report also notes the presence of two small tubular adenomas and mild dysplasia (synonymous with mild intraepithelial neoplasia). A small leiomyoma of the lamina muscularis mucosa is also found. Additionally, it is noted that there is an ulcerated, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with infiltration into the perimuscular fatty tissue, along with two local lymph node metastases. The tumor is classified as G2 and staged as pT3. Other findings include L1, VO, and RO pNI 2/30.

This pathology report describes a case of advanced mucinous adenocarcinoma of the cecum. The tumor is poorly differentiated and has invaded all layers of the colon and spread to the peritoneum. It has also metastasized to nearby lymph nodes and has caused carcinosis in the peritoneum or omentum. The staging of the tumor is pT4 (invasion of all layers), LI (lymphatic invasion), VO (vascular invasion), pN2 (multiple lymph node metastases), 9/10 (9 out of 10 lymph nodes involved), and pMI (carcinosis in the peritoneum or omentum).

This pathology report describes a partial organ resection of the descending colon. The clinical diagnosis was cancer of the splenic flexure. The macroscopic examination revealed two cauliflower-shaped tumors in the mucosa of the colon, located 4 cm from one excision line and 2.5 cm from the opposite line. The tumors were found to invade the muscular membrane of the colon. Microscopic examination confirmed the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma tubulopapillare (G1), with infiltration into the muscular layer and periintestinal fat tissue. The minimum side margin was 3 cm, and the excision lines were free of neoplastic lesions. Additionally, there was sinus histiocytosis lymphonodorum (No XIl!) present. The histopathological diagnosis is bifocal adenocarcinoma tubulopapillare of the colon (G1, Dukes B, Astler-Coller 82, pT3, pNO). It is advised to contact a doctor with this report.

The pathology report describes two specimens: a liver nodule and a segment of the right colon.

The liver nodule is 0.8 cm in size and shows a proliferation of relatively bland epithelioid cells separated by fibrovascular stroma. The tissue is largely absent on permanent sections but can be seen on the frozen section. Ancillary studies are not possible, but the epithelioid cells may represent histiocytes or a hyperplastic mesothelial proliferation. There is no evidence of carcinoma, and the report favors a benign process. Clinical correlation is recommended.

The right colon specimen is a segment measuring 19.0 cm long. It includes the cecum, appendix, and a cecal mucosa-based mass. The mass is exophytic, tan in color, with a rolled edge, and measures 4.0 cm in diameter and < 1 cm in depth. The tumor invades into subserosal tissue but does not involve the surgical margins. There are no lymphovascular or perineural invasions. The report classifies the tumor as invasive, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with focal mucinous features.

Fifteen lymph nodes were examined and found to be negative for carcinoma. Microsatellite instability testing has been ordered on the colon tumor for further evaluation.

The synoptic report provides additional details about the tumor's histologic grade, extent of invasion, margins, lymphatic invasion, perineural invasion, and other pathologic findings. It confirms a complete resection with negative margins and provides a pathological staging of pT3aN0Mx.

There is no clinical history provided, and the pre-operative diagnosis was colon carcinoma.

An addendum to the report mentions the results of immunohistochemistry stains, which show MLH1, MSH2, and MSH6 being positive, while PMS2 is negative. These results help guide the interpretation of the stains, but further information about their significance is not provided in the summary.

The pathology report indicates that the sample is an invasive adenocarcinoma in the region of the liver, which is consistent with a metastasis from adenocarcinoma of the colon. The colon adenocarcinoma is moderately differentiated (G2) and has invaded all layers of the colon (pT3), with lymph and blood vessel invasion (L1, V1). Four sections of lymph node metastases are present (pN1), but there are no tumor cells found at the resection margins. The specific tumor classification is ICDO-DA-M 8140/3, G2, pT3, L1, V1, pN1, and MX. The report also includes some additional technical information and identification numbers.

The pathology report describes the findings from the examination of several specimens: 
A) Left tube and ovary: This specimen consisted of an attenuated cystic structure containing serous fluid. The inner lining ranged from smooth white-pink to wrinkled tan white-gold. A frozen section was performed and diagnosed as ovarian serous cyst adenofibroma.
B) Uterus, cervix, right tube and ovary: The uterus was symmetrical with smooth tan-pink serosa and a mottled white-pink cervix. The cervical mucosa had an endocervical polyp, and the uterine cavity was lined by flat white-pink endometrium. The right ovary showed a cribriform appearance with identifiable corpora albicantia. There was also a serous fluid-filled fallopian tube present.
C) Right colon: This specimen included a segment of the proximal right colon and distal ileum. An ulcerated lesion was found within the colon, and a portion of the tumor and normal mucosa were submitted for tissue procurement. The ileal and colonic mucosa appeared unremarkable. Lymph nodes measuring up to 0.9 cm in size were recovered from the attached mesocolon and mesentery.
Microscopic examination revealed that the primary tumor was an invasive adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. The tumor minimally invaded the proximal margin.

The pathology report describes a histopathological examination of a partial organ resection of the sigmoid colon. The macroscopic description notes the presence of a cauliflower-shaped tumor in the mucosa of the large intestine, measuring 4.3 x 0.6 cm. The tumor completely surrounds the intestine and infiltrates its wall. The microscopic examination reveals the presence of tubular adenocarcinoma, grade 2, with infiltration of the muscularis layer. The excision lines are clear of tumor infiltration, and there is also evidence of reactive lymph nodes. The final diagnosis is tubular adenocarcinoma of the colon (G1, Dukes A, Astler-Coller B1, pT2, pN0). The report advises contacting the doctor for further discussion.

The pathology report describes a tumor in the right colon that is moderately differentiated and measures 5 cm in diameter. The tumor has invaded the surrounding tissue and extends to the cecum and ascending colon. However, there is no evidence of tumor in the margins of resection, appendix, or greater omentum. Additionally, all 22 lymph nodes examined are tumor-free and show reactive changes. The stage of the tumor is determined to be pT3 pNO (0/22), indicating invasive spread but no lymph node involvement. The tumor is graded as G2, indicating moderate differentiation.

The pathology report describes a histopathological examination of a multiple organ resection, specifically the transverse colon and the distal part of the stomach. The collected sample was expected to be water-received on the expected time of examination. 

The clinical diagnosis is cancer of the transverse colon infiltrating the stomach. The examination revealed a cauliflower-shaped tumor in the intestinal mucosa, measuring 10 x 8 x 4 cm. The tumor completely surrounds the intestine circumference, 19 cm from the proximal and 10 cm from the distal cut line. The examination also showed macroscopic invasion of the tumor through the stomach wall. 

On microscopic examination, the tumor was identified as adenocarcinoma tubulopapillare (G1). It has infiltrated the entire thickness of the colon and a portion of the stomach. The minimum side margin is 0 cm, and there are no neoplastic lesions at the ends of the invasion lines. There is also sinus histiocytosis lymphonodorum, without any identified metastasis (No Vil). 

The histopathological diagnosis is tubulopapillary adenocarcinoma of the colon, classified as G1. The tumor stage is Dukes B and Astler-Coller 63. The report advises calling the doctor with this information.

The pathology report describes the resected section of colon (rectosigmoid) with an ulcerated colon carcinoma. The carcinoma is characterized as a poorly differentiated, partially mucinous adenocarcinoma of the colorectal type. It measures a maximum of 2.5 cm in diameter and extends up to 10 cm from the resection margin. The tumor has invaded all layers of the intestinal wall and neighboring mesocolic fatty tissue. There are numerous lymphatic processes in the region of the tumor margin. The remaining intestinal wall shows no pathological findings. The report also states that there are tumor-free margins of resection. There are 12 local lymph nodes with metastases from the rectal carcinoma, some of which have transgressed the lymph node capsules. The stage of the tumor is pT3, pN2 (12/12) LI VO; G3 RO.

The pathology report describes a histopathological examination of a segment of the large intestine, small intestine, and appendix. The report identifies a tumor measuring 3.3 x 2.7 x 0.8 cm in the mucosa of the large intestine, located 12 cm from the proximal cut end and 7 cm from the distal cut end. The tumor is classified as adenocarcinoma tubulare and shows infiltration into the surrounding pericolonic adipose tissue. The lymph nodes examined showed reactive inflammation. The overall diagnosis is adenocarcinoma tubulare coli, with a grade 2, Dukes 8, Astler-Coller B2 classification. The tumor has invaded the submucosa (pT3) but has not spread to the lymph nodes (pNO).

The pathology report describes a specimen from the right colon that was removed during surgery for colon cancer. The gross description notes the presence of a large tumor that has invaded the muscle layer of the colon and possibly the surrounding fat. No other gross lesions are seen. The microscopic examination confirms the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, with invasion into the subserosal fat (stage pT3). The margins of excision are negative, indicating complete removal of the tumor. One out of twenty-nine examined lymph nodes shows metastatic carcinoma. The appendix and surrounding bowel appear unremarkable.

The pathology report describes a tumor found in the ascending colon. The tumor is classified as adenocarcinoma and is moderately differentiated. There is no evidence of mucinous or signet ring features. Histologic heterogeneity, host response, and Crohn's like reaction are also not observed. It is unclear if there is a plasma cell rich stroma, growth pattern, presence of inflammatory bowel disease, angiolymphatic invasion, mutator phenotype, or garland necrosis. The exact number of slides and TIL cells per high power field are not provided in the report. The pathologist's comment is redacted.

This pathology report describes a specimen from a segment of colon that measures 13.0 cm in length by 6-8 cm in width. The specimen is opened to reveal a pink fungating tumor located 4.0 cm from the anal margin and 4.2 cm from the proximal margin. The tumor measures 4.4 cm in length and 3-7 cm in width. The remaining sections of the specimen show the presence of 16 polyps ranging in size from 0.5-7 cm. Lymph nodes are examined and a total of 17 possible nodes are submitted for further analysis. Another section of tissue, measuring 2x2 cm, is received in formalin and shows signs of bleeding. The report concludes with a summary of the sections submitted for analysis.

The pathology report shows that the patient was initially diagnosed with colon cancer and the post-operative diagnosis remains the same. The procedure performed was a sigmoid colon resection. The final diagnosis includes the presence of adenocarcinoma in the bladder wall, sigmoid colon, and omentum. The adenocarcinoma in the sigmoid colon measures 2.5 cm and involves the colonic wall transmurally with angiolymphatic and perineural invasion. The surgical margins are clear, but the presence of cauterized carcinoma at the specimen edges is noted. Biopsy of the pelvic sidewall also reveals adenocarcinoma extending to the cauterized specimen edges. Immunohistochemical stains show positive expression of cytokeratin 7 and cytokeratin 19, while CDX-2, TTF-1, and PSA are negative. The DNA mismatch repair proteins MLH-1, PMS-2, MSH-2, and MSH-6 show preserved nuclear expression. The report suggests that this may not be a typical primary colorectal adenocarcinoma and offers possibilities of a primary site in the pancreaticobiliary system or primary peritoneal adenocarcinoma with extension into the colonic wall. One lymph node tested negative for carcinoma.

Summary:

This pathology report describes an invasive, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colon, with permeation of all wall layers. The tumor is classified as G2 and is classified as pT3, indicating invasion into the surrounding tissues. Lymphatic vessel invasion is present (L1) but no lymph nodes were found to be involved. The resection margins are clear, indicating complete removal of the tumor. The specific ICD-O-DA classification is M 8140/3.

The pathology report describes a right-sided hemicolectomy preparation with a cecal carcinoma, a type of cancer in the colon, measuring 5 cm in size at its largest point. The tumor is histologically characterized as a poorly differentiated colorectal adenocarcinoma. The tumor has invaded the subserosa and nearby fatty tissue. The oral and aboral resection margins and greater omentum are free of tumor. The appendix shows evidence of postinflammatory fibrosis. Two out of 16 mesocolic and mesenteric lymph nodes have metastases from the cecal carcinoma, while the other lymph nodes show uncharacteristic reactive lesions. The tumor stage is determined to be pT3 pN1 (2/16), with a grade of G3.

The pathology report describes a segmental resection of the sigmoid colon due to left colon cancer. The gross description mentions a narrowing area where an appendix epiploica is adherent to the colon, and a fungating mucosal tumor measuring 6 cm in length and 1.2 cm in depth. Sections of the specimen are taken for research, and there is a possible pericolonic abscess adjacent to the tumor. 

The microscopic description confirms the presence of colonic adenocarcinoma, classified as grade 2 out of 3. The carcinoma has penetrated into the pericolonic fat, but the margins of resection are negative for malignancy. There is no evidence of vascular invasion, and there is marked acute and chronic inflammation, including an area resembling a diverticulum with pericolonic abscess. No malignancy is found in any of the 30 sampled lymph nodes. 

The diagnosis is moderately differentiated colonic adenocarcinoma in the sigmoid colon. The carcinoma has invaded the pericolonic soft tissue, but there is no evidence of malignancy at the proximal margin of the sigmoid colon.

The pathology report describes a resected section of the sigmoid colon with an ulcerated colon carcinoma. The carcinoma is moderately differentiated and measures up to 3 cm in diameter. The tumor has invaded all layers of the intestinal wall and extends up to 11 cm to the oral resection margin. There are also pseudodiverticula with chronic scarring peridiverticulitis in the intestinal wall. The seminal vesicle attached to the preparation is tumor-free. Overall, the tumor stage is classified as pT3, G2, RO.

This is a pathology report for a specimen from the right colon, indicating the presence of adenocarcinoma. The tumor is moderately differentiated and located in the colon. There is no evidence of tumor invasion into surrounding tissues or lymphovascular invasion. The surgical margins are negative for tumor. There is no evidence of polyps or dysplasia. Lymph nodes were examined and no metastasis was found. The tumor is staged as T2N0 (tumor invades muscularis propria, no regional lymph node metastasis). The report also mentions the examination of a portion of omentum, which appears normal. The report concludes with a summary of sections submitted for further analysis.

This pathology report describes a right hemicolectomy specimen that was taken from a patient with colon cancer. The report indicates that the tumor is a moderately to poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, measuring 6 x 3 cm, located in the cecum. The tumor has invaded the wall of the bowel and has spread to the adjacent liver tissue. The surgical resection margins of the bowel and liver tissue appear to be free of tumor. However, metastatic carcinoma is present in one out of thirty-seven pericolonic lymph nodes. The report also includes details about the extent of invasion, histologic type and grade, as well as other relevant findings. The pathology stage is pT4a, N1, Mx. Further testing is pending for EGFR expression.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the colon. The carcinoma has penetrated all layers of the colon (pT3) and has invaded lymph vessels. Lymph node metastases have also been observed (pN2). No residual tumor was found in certain preparations, indicating that the resection margins were clear. The tumor is classified as ICDO-DA-M 8140/3 and has a grade of G2. Preliminary information is still being compiled.

This pathology report describes the examination of two specimens: A - rectum, sigmoid colon, and anus, and B - colon. In specimen A, a polypoid mass with serpentine borders measuring 2.3 cm is found in the lower portion of the rectum, along with additional polyps in the mid portion of the specimen and diverticula in the proximal region. Sections of the mass, normal appearing mucosa, and lymph nodes are submitted for analysis. In specimen B, a firm indurated polypoid lesion with serpentine borders measuring 5.8 x 5.2 cm is found in the cecum, along with polyps throughout the colon and diverticula in the distal portion. Sections of the mass, normal mucosa, and lymph nodes are submitted for analysis. 

The diagnosis for specimen A is invasive, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the rectum, sigmoid colon, and anus, with lymph node metastasis. The surgical resection margins are negative for tumor. Multiple hyperplastic polyps and a diverticulum are also present. 

The diagnosis for specimen B is invasive, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the right colon and terminal ileum, with lymph node metastasis. The surgical resection margins are negative for tumor. The appendix and ileum show no specific pathologic changes.

Immunohistochemistry for mismatched repair proteins and MSI testing have been ordered for both tumors.

The pathology report indicates the following findings regarding the first tumor in the sigmoid distal portion of the patient:

- Histology: Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with focal mucinous and signet ring features
- Histologic heterogeneity: Present
- Host response: Lymphoid aggregates with Crohn's-like reaction and plasma cell rich stroma
- Growth pattern: Expansile
- Inflammatory bowel disease: Unknown
- Angiolympathic invasion: Unknown
- Mutator phenotype: Unknown
- Necrosis: Focal presence
- Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL): Present
- Pathologist comment: Additional information about CD-0 classification and AGNOR staining is provided, but the content is cut off.

The pathology report describes the examination of a specimen labeled as "right colectomy." The specimen consists of the terminal ileum, cecum, ascending colon, and appendix. The specimen was received fresh and shows normal appearances. Upon opening the specimen, a lesion is identified that is centrally necrotic with a heaped-up border. The lesion spares the ileocecal valve and appendix. The tumor appears to extend into the muscularis propria and possibly beyond it into the pericolonic adipose tissue. The depth of invasion is approximately 25 mm. Lymph nodes in the attached adipose tissue are also submitted for evaluation. Various sections of the specimen, including the resection margins, appendix, ileocecal valve, colon, and serosa, are submitted for further analysis.

Summary: The pathology report describes a specimen of the lower anterior colon, specifically the sigmoid colon, and the appendix. The pre-operative diagnosis was sigmoid colon cancer, but the post-operative diagnosis was rectal cancer involving the apical nodes and possibly the lateral mesentery. The specimen consists of a 22 cm long portion of the colon with a tumor measuring 4.8 x 3.5 x 1 cm near the distal margin. Invasion of the muscularis propria and surrounding fat is noted, as well as multiple lymph nodes. There is also an indurated focus near the proximal margin, possibly containing tumor. A small polyp is also identified, without invasion. Microscopic examination confirms a moderately to poorly differentiated colonic adenocarcinoma with invasion into the mesenteric fat. Positive metastatic lymph nodes and a soft tissue metastasis in the mesentery are also noted. The report provides details on histologic type, grade, margins, lymph node involvement, and presence of distant metastasis, as well as the incidental finding of an adenomatous polyp.

This pathology report describes a case of invasive adenocarcinoma in the descending colon. The patient had a history of polyps and was under surveillance. The tumor is located 36 cm from the proximal margin and 4.3 cm from the distal margin, measuring 3.5 cm in length and 2.2 cm in width. It invades the muscularis propria to a depth of 0.5 cm. There is no regional lymph node metastasis identified in the 12 lymph nodes examined. The surgical margins are clear. Non-neoplastic bowel tissue is also present in the specimen.

In summary, the pathology report indicates a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma in the descending/sigmoid colon. The tumor is of histopathological differentiation grade G3 and has ulceration on the inner surface. There is chronic recurrent inflammation and focal mucus formation around the tumor. The tumor has infiltrated the layers of the colon up to the subserous fatty connective tissue. There are twelve local lymph node metastases present, along with carcinomatous lymphangitis and carcinosis of the blood vessels. The resection margins are tumor-free, and diverticulosis is observed in the sigmoid colon. The tumor spread is classified as pN2, MX, LI, V1.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the sigmoid colon. The tumor has not spread to the resection margins or the central vascular ligature. However, there is a lymph node metastasis present. The tumor is classified as ICDO-DA M, 8140/3, G2, pT3, pN1 (1/19), RO.

The pathology report describes the findings from the surgical removal of tissue samples from three areas: apical lymph nodes, sigmoid and upper rectum, and the appendix. 

In the apical lymph nodes, a small tissue fragment is identified and found to be negative for metastatic disease.

In the sigmoid and upper rectum, a segment of colon containing an ulcerated, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma is identified. The tumor has invaded into pericolonic fat, but no discrete invasion into the fat is seen. The tumor is located 3.5 cm from the distal margin. The tumor is classified as a moderately differentiated infiltrating adenocarcinoma (pT3). Various margins, including the proximal margin, distal margin, and circumferential margin, are negative for tumor. Vascular invasion is not detected. A total of 48 lymph nodes are found in this area, and one of them contains metastatic disease, indicating the presence of regional lymph node involvement (pN1a). No tumors are found outside of the lymph nodes.

In the appendix, no significant pathology is observed.
