The pathology report indicates that the sample is from a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon. The tumor is classified as grade G2 and has erosions on the inner surface. There is also chronic inflammation around the tumor and infiltration into the layers of the sigmoid colon. The lymph nodes and resection margins are free from tumor involvement. The tumor is staged as pT2, pNO, MX, RO.

Summary of the pathology report:

The specimen received for examination is a segment of sigmoid colon measuring 17.0 cm in length and 3.0 cm in diameter. A vegetative lesion with elevated borders measuring 5.0 x 4.5 cm is present in the mucosa, located 1.8 cm from the nearest surgical margin. The lesion has penetrated the full thickness of the wall and inflates the adjacent fat tissue. Two fragments of unlabeled colonic mucosa are also present. One is circular, measuring 2.3 cm in diameter and 0.7 cm in length, while the other is irregular, measuring 1.5 x 0.9 x 0.4 cm. Several lymph nodes have been dissected from the adjacent fat tissue.

Microscopic examination reveals a moderately differentiated, invasive, tubular adenocarcinoma of the sigmoid colon. The tumor penetrates the full thickness of the colonic wall and extends to the percolic fat. Perineural invasion is present. The surgical margins are free of neoplastic involvement. One circular fragment of colonic wall shows no signs of neoplastic involvement, while the irregular fragment consists of adenocarcinoma. Thirteen lymph nodes were examined, and four of them were involved. According to the TNM staging system, the stage is pT3 pN2. The pathology report is signed by the pathologists.

The pathology report describes a specimen labeled "sigmoid colon, partial colectomy" that measures 17 cm in length. The diagnosis is adenocarcinoma, low grade, moderately differentiated, with a tumor size of 4.9 cm in the greatest dimension. The tumor is polypoid in appearance and has infiltrated through the muscularis propria. The margins of resection are negative for tumor involvement. Lymphovascular invasion, extramural venous invasion, and perineural invasion are not observed. A peritumoral lymphoid response is present. There is no residual adenoma. Two out of 13 lymph nodes examined are positive for tumor. The classification of the tumor according to the 6th edition is T3 N1 MX.

Additional specimens submitted include an additional proximal margin, a distal donut, and a proximal donut, all of which are negative for tumor. No clinical data or diagnosis history is provided. The gross examination of the main specimen reveals a tan/pink fungating polypoid mass within the sigmoid colon, invading into the surrounding mesentery and fat. A white/tan soft nodule is also observed. Twelve lymph nodes are identified, with the largest measuring 0.7 cm in dimension.

The additional proximal margin specimen consists of a segment of colon without any identified lesions. Two lymph nodes are present and negative for tumor. The distal donut and proximal donut specimens also do not show any grossly identified lesions.

Overall, the report confirms the presence of adenocarcinoma with invasion into the muscularis propria and lymph node involvement. The margins of resection are clear, and no residual adenoma is observed.

The pathology report indicates that a right-sided hemicolectomy was performed, removing a portion of the colon on the right side. The resected tissue margins were free of tumor cells. However, an ulcerated, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the cecum was present, and it had invaded all layers of the colon wall, including penetrating the peritoneum (the lining of the abdominal cavity). Multiple nearby lymph nodes were found to have cancer spread, and there was also evidence of cancer cells in the peritoneal cavity. The cancer is classified as moderately differentiated (G2) and has a stage of pT4 (invasion through the colon wall), pN2 (multiple lymph node metastases), and pM1 (peritoneal seeding).

The pathology report describes a resected colon sample that shows the presence of a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, which is a type of colorectal cancer. The tumor measures a maximum of 3 cm in diameter and has infiltrated the nearby fatty tissue and penetrated the serosa layer. There are also four lymph node metastases. However, the margins of the resected colon are free of tumor cells. Additionally, there are two tubular adenomas with moderate dysplasia (also known as low-grade intraepithelial neoplasia) present. The tumor stage is described as pT pN2 (4/15) pMI, suggesting locally advanced disease with lymph node involvement. Clinically, there may be liver metastasis, however, this requires further confirmation. The tumor is graded as G2 and described as LO (lymphovascular invasion) and VO (venous invasion), while the resection of the tumor is described as locally RO (radically out).

The pathology report shows that the patient had a resection of the sigmoid colon and rectum due to invasive adenocarcinoma. The tumor measured 5.5 cm and invaded through the muscularis propria into pericolonic adipose tissue. There was no definite perineural invasion seen. The surgical resection margins were negative for tumor. However, multiple regional lymph nodes were positive for metastatic adenocarcinoma (3 out of 14). The pathological stage of the cancer is pT3, N1, M. The tumor is low-grade, well to moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Angiolymphatic invasion is present, but perineural invasion is absent. There were no additional pathologic findings identified.

The pathology report describes a sample from the sigmoid colon with a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma (a type of cancer) that is grade G2. The tumor shows ulceration and necrosis and there is chronic inflammation around the tumor. There is also lymphangitis (inflammation of the lymph vessels) caused by the spread of cancer cells. The tumor has infiltrated the layers of the sigmoid wall and has reached the fatty connective tissue beneath it. There is mild inflammation in the lymph nodes. The surgical margins and anastomosis ring are tumor-free. The patient also has sigmoid diverticulosis (the presence of small bulging pouches in the colon). Based on the sections examined, the tumor is classified as stage pT3, pNO, MX, L1, RO.

The pathology report includes information about the patient's medical history, social history, family medical history, diagnostic studies, surgical treatment, and specimen information. It also contains a pathological description, including the size and extension of the primary tumor, lymph node involvement, distant metastasis, and histological pattern.

Based on the pathology report, the diagnosis is invasive poorly differentiated colonic adenocarcinoma with focal mucinous differentiation. The tumor has extended through the wall of the colon into the wall of the attached small bowel segment. The tumor also extends across the ileocecal valve into the terminal ileum. The margins of resection (proximal, distal, and radial) are free of tumor. There is no evidence of carcinoma in the 15 mesenteric lymph nodes examined. The right fallopian tube and ovary are adhesed to the colon but not involved by tumor.

The pathology report states that there is a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colorectal type in the right hemicolectomy specimen. The tumor is centrally ulcerated and measures up to 3 cm in length with infiltration of the pericolic fat tissue. There are no regional lymph node metastases. The resection margins and omental fat tissue are tumor-free. Additionally, there is moderate chronic fibrosing cholecystitis with chronic fibrosing pericholecystitis and cholecystolithiasis. The tumor stage is pT3 pNO (0/23) pMX, with a grade of G2.

The pathology report describes the findings from a section of the left colon that was removed during a surgical procedure. The report states that there is a 3.7 x 2.5 x 0.7 cm tumor in the colon, which has invaded through the muscularis propria and is connected to the serosal puckering. The tumor is close but not directly involved with the serosal surface. There is also evidence of invasion into the fat near the tumor. Lymph nodes were identified and several sections were submitted for analysis. The report indicates that there is adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, present in the colon. The tumor has invaded through the muscularis propria into the subserosal fat. The proximal and distal margins are negative, but the radial margin is less than 1 mm from the carcinoma. There is probable vascular invasion and there are three out of 27 lymph nodes that show metastatic carcinoma. Additionally, there are four tumor nodules present in the pericolonic area within the serosal fat.

The pathology report describes the resected colon sample as having two moderately differentiated, invasive adenocarcinomas of the colorectal type. The tumors have a maximum diameter of 5 cm and have infiltrated the pericolic fatty tissue. There are also two local lymph node metastases. The colon resection margins and mesenteric resection margin are free of tumor. The tumor stage is classified as pT3 with two local lymph nodes involved (pN1), and the grade is G2. The tumors have lymphovascular invasion (LO) and perineural invasion (VO), but the surgical resection margin is clear of tumor (RO).

The pathology report states that a right hemicolectomy specimen was examined. The resection margins around the tumor were clear, indicating a tumor-free removal. Two adenomas (benign tumors) were found in the colonic mucosal membrane, both showing mild dysplasia (abnormal growth of cells). In addition, an ulcerated, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma (a type of cancer that arises in glandular cells) was identified in the ascending colon. The cancer had invaded the perimuscular fatty tissue but did not spread to nearby lymph nodes (pT3 pNO 0/36 L1 VO RO). The grade of the cancer was G2, indicating moderate differentiation.

This pathology report describes the examination of a total organ resection of the colon and cecum due to a clinical diagnosis of cancer of the hepatic flexure. The macroscopic description includes the presence of an ulcerous tumor in the mucosa, which surrounds 100% of the intestine circumference. The microscopic description reveals the presence of adenocarcinoma in the colon, with infiltration into the muscularis propria and mesenteric adipose tissue. There are also metastases in the lymph nodes. The final histopathologic diagnosis is tubulopapillar and partially mucinous adenocarcinoma of the colon, with cancer metastases in lymph nodes. The tumor is classified as Grade 3, Dukes C, Astler-Coller C2, pT3, pN2. The report advises contacting the doctor with this information.

This pathology report describes a specimen from a hemicolectomy, with no specified size mentioned. The tumor is located in the colon, measuring 6.5 x 4.5 x 4.0 mm. The tumor is characterized as adenocarcinoma and is well-differentiated. It infiltrates the muscularis propria, but there is no information provided about lymph nodes or margins. There is no evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment, and no additional pathologic findings are identified. Overall, there are no specific comments provided about the findings.

The pathology report indicates that a partial organ resection was performed on the transverse colon. The macroscopic description includes the presence of a cauliflower-shaped tumor measuring 3 x 3.5 cm in the intestinal mucosa. The tumor completely surrounds the circumference of the colon, located 3 cm from one cut line and 3 cm from the opposite one. There is also a polyp measuring 0.5 cm diameter found near the tumor. 

Microscopically, the tumor is identified as an adenocarcinoma of tubular and partially mucinous type (G3). It has infiltrated the muscularis propria and the pericolonic adipose tissue. There are no neoplastic lesions present in the excision lines. Outside of the tumor, an adenoma with dysplasia of lower grade is observed. The omentum does not show any metastases, but there are metastatic carcinomas present in one lymph node (No I/XI). 

The final diagnosis is tubular and partially mucinous adenocarcinoma of the colon (G3, Duke C, Astler-Coller C2, p73, pN1a). The report advises contacting a doctor with this information.

The pathology report describes a segment of the large intestine that was resected due to a tumor. The tumor is described as an ulcerous adenocarcinoma with mucinous features, measuring 3.3 x 5.2 x 0.8 cm. It is located in the ascending colon, right half of the large intestine, and extends to the distal segment. The tumor is also accompanied by polyps. Microscopically, it is classified as tubular and mucinous adenocarcinoma. The report mentions infiltration of the pericolonic adipose tissue and the absence of neoplastic lesions in the resected intestine ends. Additionally, there are metastatic carcinoma cells found in the lymph nodes. The final diagnosis is adenocarcinoma with tubular and mucinous features, accompanied by lymph node metastases. The staging is given as G3, Dukes C, Astler-Collier C2, pT3, pN4.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a histopathological examination of a resected section of the sigmoid colon. The clinical diagnosis was a tumor in the sigmoid colon. The macroscopic description details the size and location of the tumor within the intestine. 

The microscopic description reveals that the tumor is classified as an adenocarcinoma tubulopapillare (Gl). Additionally, there is infiltration of the pericolonic adipose tissue by the carcinoma. The incision lines were free of neoplastic lesions. There is also reactive lymphonodulitis present. 

The final histopathological diagnosis is adenocarcinoma tubulopapillare coli (tubulopapillar adenocarcinoma of the colon), categorized as Dukes B, Astler-Coller B2, pT3, pNO. The report advises the patient to contact their doctor with this information.

This pathology report describes a total colectomy specimen that was taken from a patient with sigmoid colon cancer. The tumor is diagnosed as moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, and its size is 3 cm in length. There is evidence of lymphovascular invasion and invasion into the muscularis propria layer of the colon. Three tubular adenomas, as well as non-neoplastic bowel tissue, were also identified. Lymph nodes were examined, and metastasis was found in 2-3 regional lymph nodes. The tumor is staged as T3, N2 (according to the AJCC 7th edition). The report includes a special study request and indicates that the diagnosis is based on a histological examination. The report concludes with a summary of sections taken from the specimen.

This pathology report describes a partial colectomy of the right colon and distal ileum. The main finding is invasive colonic adenocarcinoma. The margins of the resected specimen are negative for malignancy, except for the circumferential margin which is involved by invasive carcinoma. There is evidence of tumor perforation, lymphovascular invasion, and a lymphocytic response in and around the tumor. The tumor arises from a tubular adenoma and shows focal squamous differentiation. No distant metastasis is identified. The report also includes information about special procedures performed, but no clinical history or pre/post-operative diagnosis is provided.

The pathology report indicates the presence of an invasive, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the colon (G2). The tumor has penetrated all layers of the colon wall (pT3) and has also spread into lymphatic vessels (L1). The resection margins are free from cancer in the mucosa region, and the central ligature, adipose connective tissue, and vessels are all normal. In addition, two lymph nodes have been found to have metastases from the carcinoma described above. There are also tubulovillous adenomas present, with one showing a transition to carcinoma (G2) and infiltration of the muscularis (pT2). The report also states that two out of the 14 lymph nodes examined have metastases, but the resection margins and ligature portions are free from cancer. The tumor is classified as ICDO-DA-M 8140/3, G2, pT3, L1, pN1, Mx.

The pathology report describes a poorly differentiated colon carcinoma that measures 11.8 cm in size. It has features of signet ring cells and produces focal mucin. The tumor has infiltrated through the muscularis propria and involves the visceral peritoneum. Lymphovascular invasion is present, indicating spread through the lymphatic and blood vessels. The appendix shows fibrous obliteration and peri-appendiceal adhesions. One out of thirty-two lymph nodes examined is positive for metastatic carcinoma. The surgical procedure performed was a right colectomy. The specimen received consists of a partial colectomy with the terminal ileum, colon, and appendix. The tumor is located at the ileocecal valve and extends into the pericolonic fat. Multiple lymph nodes were identified and submitted for further analysis.

The pathology report describes a resected specimen from the colon, sigmoid, and rectum. The main finding is an infiltrating well-differentiated adenocarcinoma that originated from a tubulovillous adenoma measuring 4 cm in size. The tumor extends through the muscularis propria into the surrounding pericolonic adipose tissue. There is a 3 cm distance to the closest mucosal margin, 0.6 cm to the closest serosal (antimesenteric) surface, and a 3.5 cm distance to the mesenteric radial margin. Smooth muscle proliferation is seen in areas consistent with partial myomectomy. Other non-neoplastic findings include diverticular disease with ruptured diverticulitis, soft tissue inflammation, and fibrosis, as well as an incidental hyperplastic polyp measuring 0.1 cm. Surgical margins and regional lymph nodes are negative for tumor. The pathologic stage is pT3 NO MX.

The pathology report describes a patient who underwent a total colectomy after being diagnosed with ischemic bowel. The final diagnosis after surgery was invasive well-differentiated adenocarcinoma arising in a tubulovillous adenoma, invading into the muscularis propria. There was no angiolymphatic or perineural invasion, and the surgical margins of resection were free of tumor. Twenty-five pericolic lymph nodes were examined and found to be free of tumor. The pathological stage of the cancer was determined to be T2, N0, Mx, Duke's stage A, and Astler-Coller stage B2. There were also small tubular adenomas present. The report also mentions the presence of an incidental carcinoid tumor in the vermiform appendix, which was mostly confined to the submucosa. The report concludes with the synoptic summary of primary colon and rectal tumors, in which the tumor was located in the cecum and measured 0.6 cm in size. It was classified as adenocarcinoma, not otherwise specified, and was well-differentiated. No lymphovascular invasion or involvement of surgical margins was observed. Regional lymph nodes were examined, with no evidence of metastasis. The report does not mention any involvement of adjacent organs or structures. The patient's TNM stage was T2, N0, M0, and the tumor grade was not specified.

The pathology report describes a tumor located in the ascending colon. The tumor is histologically classified as adenocarcinoma, with poor differentiation. There is no mucinous or signet ring feature observed in the tumor. There is no histologic heterogeneity noted, and no host response or presence of plasma cell rich stroma. The tumor shows invasive growth with no evidence of Crohn's-like reaction or angiolymphatic invasion. The presence of a mutator phenotype is unknown. The report does not provide information on the number of slides or the presence of Garland necrosis. The pathologist notes that the deep edge of the tumor was not evaluated.

The pathology report describes a resection of a sigmoid colon and upper rectum. The tumor type is described as sigmoid adenocarcinoma. The grade of the tumor is not mentioned. The tumor measures 2 cm in length and 1.5 cm in width. Tumor budding and increased tumor invading lymphocytes are noted. There is no invasion of subserosal adipose tissue or mesenteric fat. Lymphovascular invasion and large venous invasion are not specified. The surgical margins are not mentioned. There is no dysplasia identified in the polype/mucosa that is away from the carcinoma.

A total of 17 lymph nodes were examined, and metastasis was found in one regional lymph node. Tumor deposits in pericolorectal soft tissue were not identified.

A separate excision of the distal ring of the rectum and proximal ring of the colon were also performed, but no pathological diagnosis was made for either of these specimens.

Overall, the specimen shows invasion of the muscularis propria into pericolorectal tissues and metastasis in one regional lymph node.

The pathology report describes a histopathological examination conducted on a resected sigmoid colon. The clinical diagnosis is cancer of the sigmoid colon, specifically invasive adenocarcinoma of the colon. The macroscopic description states that there is a tumor in the mucosa measuring 8x15 cm, which surrounds 55% of the intestine circumference and invades through the surrounding tissue. The microscopic description confirms the presence of tubular adenocarcinoma (G2) infiltrating the muscularis propria and pericolonic adipose tissue. The incision lines are free of neoplastic lesions. Lymph node involvement is not specified in this report. Further immunohistochemical tests were performed to confirm the diagnosis. The final diagnosis includes additional details such as Dukes stage 8, Aster-Colle B2, pT3, pNO.

The patient underwent a laparoscopic colectomy that was converted to an open right colectomy. The final diagnosis is a well-differentiated colon adenocarcinoma that has invaded the sub-mucosa. The carcinoma arose from a tubulovillous adenoma with serrated features. There are also several non-invasive adenomas present. The resection margins are free of carcinoma and adenoma. No angiolymphatic invasion is observed. Sixteen lymph nodes examined show no involvement. The pathologic stage of the cancer is T1 with no metastasis. The appendix also contains a tubular carcinoid tumor measuring 3mm. Immunohistochemical stains confirm the diagnosis of tubular carcinoid. The specimen was also tested for microsatellite instability, which was not detected. The expression of hMLH1, hMSH2, and hMSH8 was preserved in the neoplastic tissue.

This pathology report describes an invasive adenocarcinoma of the colon in the sigmoid colon. The tumor is classified as G2 and is staged at T3, meaning it has infiltrated the parietal layer and has vascular infiltration. The resection margins are free from tumor involvement, however, there are lymph node metastases present (6 out of 12 nodes).

The pathology report describes a specimen of right colon tissue that was removed during surgery. The specimen includes a tumor mass near the ileocecal valve, which measures 5 x 4.4 cm in size and extends into the muscularis layer. The surrounding mucosa and margins are uninvolved. Multiple lymph nodes were also found in the attached mesocolon and mesentery, two of which show evidence of metastasis. The diagnosis is adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, with invasion through the muscularis propria. The surgical margins are uninvolved, but there are metastatic adenocarcinoma cells in five out of thirty lymph nodes.

This pathology report describes a examination of a specimen from a patient's sigmoid colon. The macroscopic description reveals the presence of a cauliflower-shaped, partially ulcerous tumor measuring 7.5 x 5.5 x 3 cm. The tumor surrounds the entire circumference of the intestine and infiltrates the intestine wall and surrounding tissues. The microscopic description confirms the presence of adenocarcinoma tubulopapillare (G2). There is also evidence of inflammatory invasion and involvement of lymph nodes. The histopathological diagnosis is tubulopapillar adenocarcinoma of the colon with metastases in the lymph nodes. The cancer is categorized as stage p2, Dukes C, Astler-Coller C2, pT4a, pNl. The report suggests sharing the findings with the patient's doctor for further management and treatment.

The pathology report indicates that a tumor sample was taken for analysis. The histology of the tumor is adenocarcinoma, and there is no evidence of other histological features such as mucinous or signet ring. There is no histologic heterogeneity, and the tumor shows a growth pattern that is either expansive or invasive. There is no evidence of inflammatory bowel disease or angiolymphatic invasion. The mutator phenotype is unknown. There is no presence of grand necrosis. The pathologist's comment is not provided.

The pathology report describes a right hemicolectomy specimen of the right colon, cecum, and terminal ileum. The main finding is an exophytic circumferential ulcerated invasive moderate to poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma of the cecum and proximal ascending colon. The tumor has invaded the full thickness of the muscle wall and extended to the subserosal fat. There are also metastases present in six out of 36 pericolonic lymph nodes. The size of the tumor is 8 x 4 x 1 cm. Additionally, a tubulovillous adenoma measuring 1.2 x 1.1 cm is present. The proximal, distal, and radial margins of resection are negative for tumor. The report includes a colonic cancer template with details regarding tumor site, configuration, size, histologic type, grade, invasion extent, margins, lymphatic invasion, and perineural invasion. The pathologic stage is determined to be pT3.N2MX. An addendum mentions negative immunoreactivity for EGFR.

The pathology report describes the findings from a left hemicolectomy. The main diagnosis is a moderately differentiated, invasive adenocarcinoma that has spread to the pericolic fatty tissue. Additionally, there is a tubulovillous adenoma with severe dysplasia. The tumor is classified as G2, pT3 NO (0/27) LO VO RO.

Based on the pathology report, the clinical diagnosis and history include tenderness in the lower right abdomen, a mass at the hepatic flexure of the colon, and a mass in segment 7 of the liver. The colonoscopy revealed a tumor in the colon, and a biopsy showed increased lymphocytic infiltration in the lamina propria.

The specimens submitted for examination include lymph nodes excised from the base of the superior mesenteric artery and middle colic lymph node, as well as a right hemi-colectomy.

The pathology findings include metastatic moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in two lymph nodes near the superior mesenteric artery, and one benign lymph node near the middle colic region. The tumor in the colon is moderately differentiated, measuring 8 cm in length, 6 cm in width, and 1.8 cm in thickness. Extensive tumor budding is observed.

Further findings include subserosal adipose tissue and/or mesenteric fat invasion, lymphovascular invasion, perineural invasion, and evidence of tumor deposits in pericolorectal soft tissue. The pathology report describes a resected section of the colon (specifically, the sigmoid colon) that contains an ulcerated colon carcinoma. The patient's pathology report indicates that a colon tumor was found in the ascending colon, located 2 cm from the ileocecal valve. The tumor is an adenocarcinoma of colorectal type, measuring up to 4 cm in diameter. It is ulcerated and moderately differentiated, with infiltration into the surrounding adipose tissue. However, there is no evidence of tumor spread into nearby lymph nodes or other organs. The resected material also shows clear margins, indicating that the tumor has been completely removed. The tumor stage is determined to be pT3, meaning it has penetrated through the wall of the colon, and there is no evidence of lymph node involvement (pNO 0/39) or distant metastasis (pMX). The tumor is moderately differentiated (G2) and does not show lymphovascular invasion (LO) or perineural invasion (VO). Overall, the surgical resection appears successful in removing the tumor.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a mass in the omentum that was surgically removed. The mass was determined to be metastatic adenocarcinoma, consistent with a primary tumor in the colon. Additionally, a right hemicolectomy was performed, and it was found that there was invasive moderately differentiated colorectal adenocarcinoma in the terminal ileum, appendix, and right colon. The tumor was located in the right colon and had invaded the muscularis propria into the subserosa and nearby soft tissue. There was no lymphovascular or perineural invasion observed. The margins of the resected tissue were negative, and the distance of the carcinoma from the closest margin was less than 1.0 mm from the serosal surface and 8.5 cm from the proximal mucosal margin. One out of 26 regional lymph nodes examined showed evidence of metastasis. Additional findings included follicular lymphoid hyperplasia in the appendix and a satellite nodule of the tumor. The pathologic stage of the tumor was determined to be pT3 pN1a. No evidence of metastatic disease was found in the liver, which showed minimal steatosis and portal triaditis. A hernia sac was also removed, which was determined to be benign. Overall, the patient had a mass in the omentum that was consistent with metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma, and further examination revealed invasive moderately differentiated colorectal adenocarcinoma in the terminal ileum, appendix, and right colon.

This pathology report indicates the presence of an adenocarcinoma of the colon, specifically of the mucinous adenocarcinoma type (G3). The cancer has penetrated all layers of the colon and has infiltrated the blood vessels (pT3, L1, V1). The resection margins are free from cancer cells in both the mucosal and ligature regions. The report also mentions the presence of chronic recurrent appendicitis with fecal impaction. The tumor is classified as ICDO-DA-M G3 with no lymph node involvement (pNO, 0/14).

The pathology report describes the findings from a resected specimen of the left colon. The specimen consists of a 28 cm segment of colon with an ulcerated mass measuring 10.7 x 8.5 x 6 cm, which has infiltrated through the muscularis propria into the subserosa. The mass shows perineural invasion and extensive intramural suppurative necrosis. There is also a pedunculated polyp measuring 4.5 x 3.7 x 3 cm with superficial invasion and several smaller polyps. The margins are negative for carcinoma. One out of eighty-two lymph nodes shows metastatic adenocarcinoma. The overall diagnosis is as follows:

1. Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the left colon infiltrating through the muscularis propria into the subserosa with perineural invasion.
2. Extensive intramural suppurative necrosis.
3. Tubulovillous adenoma with focal high-grade dysplasia.
4. Hyperplastic polyps (multiple).
5. Negative margins.
6. Metastatic adenocarcinoma in one out of eighty-two lymph nodes (1/82).

This pathology report describes a resected specimen from the splenic flexure of the colon, which was diagnosed as adenocarcinoma. The tumor is moderate to poorly differentiated and has invaded through the muscularis propria. The surgical margins are uninvolved, however, there is a close circumferential (radial) margin. Vascular invasion is present. Metastatic carcinoma is found in 7 of 13 pericolonic lymph nodes. Distant metastasis could not be evaluated by this specimen. Additional findings are not noted.

The pathology report describes the findings from a colonoscopy and subsequent surgical procedure for a patient with colon cancer. The report states that there were two separate tumors found, one in the hepatic flexure of the colon and one in the sigmoid colon. Specimens submitted for analysis include a total abdominal colectomy, a proximal anastomotic ring, and a distal anastomotic ring.

The analysis of the total abdominal colectomy specimen reveals an adenocarcinoma with mucinous features, moderately differentiated. The tumor is located in the hepatic flexure, measuring 4 cm in length and 2.5 cm in width, with a maximal thickness of 0.4 cm. Other details such as tumor budding, lymph node invasion, and margins are not identified.

The report mentions that additional immunohistochemical stains for mismatch repair proteins will be reported separately. The proximal and distal margins of the resected colon and the appendix show no pathological findings. A total of 42 lymph nodes were examined, with no regional lymph node metastasis detected.

The gross description of the specimens includes measurements and descriptions of the various parts of the colon and appendix. The tumor in the ascending colon is described as a mass measuring 4 cm in length and 5.5 cm in width. Diverticula are noted in the remaining mucosa, and two tattoo sites are present. The attached adipose tissue is thoroughly examined, and all identified lymph nodes are submitted for analysis.

The pathology report concludes by summarizing the sections submitted for analysis from each specimen, including shaved margins, representative sections, and lymph nodes.

The pathology report describes the presence of an invasive, mucinous adenocarcinoma of the colon. The tumor is classified as grade 3 (G3) and has penetrated all layers of the colon (pT3). There is evidence of vascular infiltration (L1, V1) and free margins of resection in the mucosa region. The deep resection margin contains mature connective tissue. No lymph node involvement is noted. In addition to the adenocarcinoma, there are tubulovillous adenomas with severe dysplasia (high-risk intraepithelial neoplasia). Lastly, there is omental tissue with reactive lesions.

The pathology report reveals a metastasis of a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma in the liver region of the patient. The primary tumor is an invasive adenocarcinoma of the colon that is moderately differentiated with infiltration of all layers of the colon wall and vascular infiltration. The tumor does not involve the resection margins or lymph nodes. Two liver metastases were also detected, located very close together. The tumor is classified as G2 and further details of the tumor formula are provided.

The pathology report describes a right hemicolectomy preparation for a colon and cecal carcinoma. The carcinoma is moderately differentiated, measuring cm in diameter. The tumor has invaded all layers of the intestinal wall up to the surrounding mesocolic fatty tissue. There is also a tubular adenoma with moderate epithelial dysplasia in the ascending colon. The appendix shows chronic appendicitis with periappendicitis, likely due to the tumor affecting the appendix ostium. The cecum and oral section of the ascending colon have a significant amount of macrophage-rich inflammation related to perityphlitis. The stage of the tumor is determined to be pT3, pNO, (0/40) LO vO; G2 RO.

This pathology report is for a female patient with colorectal carcinoma who underwent a right hemicolectomy. The tumor was moderately differentiated and measured 3 cm in length and 3.4 cm in width. The tumor exhibited increased tumor budding and infiltration of lymphocytes. The deepest invasion of the tumor was into the subserosal adipose tissue and/or mesenteric fat. Gross tumor perforation was not identified. The surgical margins were not involved, and there was no dysplasia identified in the surrounding polyps/mucosa. Lymph nodes were examined, and tumor deposits in pericolorectal soft tissue were not identified. The tumor staging according to the AJCC 7th edition was pT3 (tumor invades through the muscularis propria into pericolorectal tissues) and N2a (metastasis in 4-6 regional lymph nodes). Gross examination of the specimen revealed a papillary tumor located distal to the cecum. The tumor invaded into the muscularis and had no significant gross abnormalities. Representative sections of the specimen were submitted for further analysis.

The pathology report states that the colon resection material shows a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colorectal type, measuring a maximum of 2.5 cm. The tumor has infiltrated the pericolic fatty tissue, but two colon resection margins are tumor-free. The report also mentions regional lymph node metastasis. The cancer is categorized as G2 (moderately differentiated), L1 (lymphovascular invasion present), VO (venous invasion present), and clinically R2 (residual tumor present in surgical resection).

The pathology report indicates that a right hemicolectomy was performed on the patient. The resection margins were tumor-free, and the tumor in the ascending colon was found to be an ulcerated, poorly differentiated mucinous adenocarcinoma. It had infiltrated the fatty tissue surrounding the colon but did not show any evidence of local lymph node metastasis. The tumor is graded as G3 (poorly differentiated) and classified as pT3, indicating invasion beyond the submucosa. The report also mentions that there were no regional lymph node metastases found (pNO 0/17).

The pathology report describes a right colon specimen that was removed during surgery for cecal cancer. The specimen consists of a 25 cm segment of the right colon, with attached distal ileum and associated tissues. The report notes the presence of a tumor measuring 5.0 x 4.2 cm, located 3.5 cm distal to the ileocecal valve. Two additional smaller polypoid lesions are also present. The tumor is moderately differentiated invasive adenocarcinoma, invading into the muscularis propria but not into the pericolonic fat or serosal surface. The margins of the tumor are negative for tumor involvement. No vascular invasion or distant metastasis is identified. Other findings include the presence of a tubular adenoma and a serrated adenoma. 26 lymph nodes are negative for metastatic tumor.

This pathology report describes a specimen from an extended right hemicolectomy, which was performed for the diagnosis of hepatic flexure cancer. The gross description reveals the characteristics of the tumor, including its size, location, and invasion depth. The tumor is described as a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma that invades through the muscularis propria into the subserosa. The margins of excision are negative, indicating that no tumor cells are present at the edges of the specimen. There is no identified vascular invasion, and 34 out of 94 lymph nodes examined are negative for tumor involvement. Overall, the report indicates the presence of moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with subserosal invasion, but no involvement of lymph nodes or surrounding tissues.

The pathology report is for a clinical case involving the collection of cancerous tissue. The patient provided informed consent, and their medical history and current symptoms were recorded. Various tests and diagnostic studies were performed, including blood tests and imaging scans. The clinical diagnosis is cancer, and the location and staging of the tumor were noted. Surgical treatment was recommended, and information about the procedure and the extent of the tumor was provided. The pathology report also includes microscopic findings, such as histological pattern and cell distribution. The final pathological staging of the tumor is noted.

The pathology report describes a specimen obtained from en bloc resection of various organs and tissues, including the terminal ileum, right colon, transverse colon, omentum, mid jejunum, greater curvature of the stomach, and abdominal wall. The report reveals the presence of invasive poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, which has invaded the pericolonic fat and muscularis propria of the stomach. The tumor measures 4.5 cm x 4.5 cm and shows focal squamous differentiation. Lymph nodes (25 in total) are negative for tumor involvement, and the margins are negative as well. Focal chronic gastritis is seen in the gastric mucosa. There is also evidence of acute serositis. The report also includes information on the gastric suture line, which shows no evidence of tumor. The overall pathological stage is pT4 NO Mx.

The pathology report describes findings from a specimen labelled "Right hemicolectomy" with a clinical diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. The report includes details about the tumor, lymph nodes, and the surrounding tissues.

The gross description of the specimen indicates that it consists of a segment of the terminal ileum, cecum with attached appendix, and ascending colon. The tumor is described as a 3.7 cm lesion located in the large bowel, invading through the muscularis and serosa. The depth of invasion is reported as 0.3 cm grossly. Multiple minute polypoid lesions are noted on the terminal ileum mucosa.

The lymph nodes were examined, and a total of 19 nodes were identified. However, no tumor deposits were found in pericolorectal soft tissues. The tumor staging according to the AJCC 7th Edition is reported as "PTS" (tumor invades through the muscularis propria into pericolorectal tissues), and there is no regional lymph node metastasis.

The report also mentions the presence of subserosal adipose tissue and/or mesenteric fat, lymphovascular invasion, large venous invasion, surgical margins, polyp/mucosa dysplasia away from the carcinoma, and non-neoplastic bowel. Representative sections of the specimen have been submitted for permanent sections and for TPS.

Additionally, the report includes a summary of sections from the small bowel specimen, indicating that it appears grossly unremarkable. Representative sections have been submitted.

Overall, the report provides information about the tumor characteristics, lymph node involvement, and the absence of tumor deposits in surrounding tissues.

This pathology report describes a surgical resection of the transverse colon for a patient with a pre-operative diagnosis of transverse colon cancer. The report states that a 50 cm segment of colon was received, with a tumor located 15 cm from the distal margin. The tumor is described as poorly differentiated mucinous signet ring cell carcinoma. The tumor has invaded through the wall of the colon into the omentum, and vascular invasion is present. Thirteen of the forty-one mesenteric lymph nodes contain metastatic adenocarcinoma. The margins of resection (proximal, distal, and radial) are negative. The report also mentions the presence of an adenomatous polyp in the appendix. Overall, the diagnosis is invasive poorly differentiated mucinous signet ring cell adenocarcinoma of the transverse colon, with metastasis to lymph nodes.

The pathology report for the patient with colon cancer and liver metastasis is as follows:

- Liver biopsy: Metastatic mucinous adenocarcinoma consistent with the patient's colon primary cancer.
- Right hemicolectomy: Invasive poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma with areas of mucinous differentiation. The carcinoma has invaded through the muscularis propria and into serosal adipose tissue. There is metastatic adenocarcinoma in one of ten lymph nodes with focal extracapsular extension.
- Open cholecystectomy: No significant pathologic findings.
- Excision of right kidney mass: Multiple renal cortical cysts with associated hemorrhage and organizing hematoma. No evidence of malignancy.
- HER-2/neu FISH studies: The ratio of HER-2/neu to the centromere of chromosome 17 is 1.70, indicating low-level HER-2/neu amplification in the targeted region.
- Synoptic report of the primary colon and rectal tumors: The tumor is a 6.5 cm adenocarcinoma arising in the ascending colon. It is poorly differentiated and infiltrating through the muscularis propria into the serosa.
- TNM Stage: T4 N1 M1, Dukes' Stage C2.

Overall, the patient has colon cancer with liver metastasis and involvement of the lymph nodes. The cancer is poorly differentiated with areas of mucinous differentiation. The liver biopsy confirms the metastasis, and the kidney mass is non-malignant. The HER-2/neu amplification indicates a potential target for treatment. The stage of the cancer is advanced, indicating a need for further management and treatment.

The pathology report describes a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma in the right colon flexure. The tumor is grade G3 and exhibits ulceration and erosions on its inner surface. There is chronic recurrent inflammation surrounding the tumor, along with an acute inflammatory flare. There is also evidence of carcinomatous lymphangitis and tumor infiltration in the layers of the colon, extending into the subserous fatty connective tissue. No tumor is found in the 20 lymph nodes examined. There is moderate chronic lymphadenitis present, as well as a diverticulum within the tumor. Tumor-free margins are identified in all other resection areas, including the perivascular fatty tissue and omental fatty tissue. Based on the available sections, the tumor stage is determined to be pT3, pNO, MX, L1, RO. The tumor is classified as an adenocarcinoma according to the ICDO-DA-M 8140/3 classification.

Summary:

The pathology report indicates the following diagnoses:

1. A polypoid neoplasm of the colonic mucosa with the structure of a tubular adenoma showing high-grade dysplasia or intramucosal adenocarcinoma in situ.
2. Small portions of tubular adenomas of the colonic mucosa with slight dysplasia.
3. Another tubular adenoma of the colonic mucosa with high-grade dysplasia and transition to intramucosal adenocarcinoma in situ.

There is no evidence of a transition to a deeper colon carcinoma.

The specimen from the right hemicolectomy shows an ulcerated colon carcinoma measuring 4 cm in diameter, arising from a tubulovillous adenoma with severe epithelial dysplasia. The invasive tumor has spread to the muscularis propria.

The appendix shows a mucocele with obstructive characteristics, along with persistent or florid chronic appendicitis and perityphlitis.

The margins of resection and the greater omentum are tumor-free.

The lymph nodes (24 examined) are tumor-free with uncharacteristic reactive changes.

The tumor stage is determined to be pT2, pNO (no lymph node involvement), LO (lymphovascular invasion is absent), VO (venous invasion is absent), and G2 (moderate differentiation). Complete tumor resection is recommended if not already done.

The pathology report describes the findings of surgical specimens that were submitted for analysis. The first specimen is a colon tumor, which is moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. The tumor size is 6.8 cm and shows no evidence of lymph node involvement or invasion into surrounding tissues. The second specimen is a liver biopsy fragment, and the third and fourth specimens are fallopian tubes and ovaries, which are benign. The report also provides details on the size and characteristics of the specimens.

This pathology report describes the findings of a tubulovillous adenoma in the colon mucosa with mild dysplasia of the cylindrical epithelium. Additionally, a right hemicolectomy specimen showed a slightly differentiated mucinous adenocarcinoma with a histopathological differentiation grade G3. The tumor showed significant extracellular mucus accumulation, chronic recurrent inflammation, acute inflammatory activity, fine focal necrosis, erosion of the inner surface of the tumor, and infiltration of the colon wall layers up to the pericolic fatty connective tissue. There was also evidence of carcinomatous lymphangitis. However, the lymph nodes in the resected area were tumor-free (0/36). Moderate chronic lymphadenitis and chronic appendicitis were also present. All other sections of the resection were tumor-free. The tumor stage was determined to be pT3, pN0 (0/36), MX, L1, RO according to the examination of the section preparations. The tumor is classified as ICDO-DA M8480/3.

This pathology report describes a case of colorectal adenocarcinoma arising from a tubulovillous adenoma with high grade dysplasia in the right colon. The tumor is moderately differentiated and located in the cecal pouch. It is not invading through the muscularis propria or showing lymphovascular or perineural invasion. The margins are negative for malignancy, with the tumor being 5.2 cm from the proximal margin. There are no regional lymph node metastases. There is also a separate tubulovillous adenoma with high grade dysplasia, as well as acute serositis in the appendix. The pathological stage is pT2 pNO.

The pathology report describes several findings:

1. Chronically fibrosing cholecystitis: Inflammation and scarring of the gallbladder.
2. Reactive hyperplasia of a local lymph node: Enlargement of a lymph node in response to an infection or inflammation.
3. Tumor-free fatty tissue: No evidence of tumor in the surrounding fatty tissue.
4. Resected colon with a centrally ulcerated, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma: A tumor in the colon that is moderately differentiated and has caused an ulcer.
5. Tumor located 1.5 cm from the aboral resection margin: The tumor is close to the surgical margin where the colon was removed.
6. Wide infiltration of pericolic fatty tissue: The tumor has spread into the fatty tissue around the colon.
7. Four local lymph node metastases: The tumor has spread to four nearby lymph nodes.
8. Tumor-free colon resection margins: The edges of the removed colon specimen are clear of tumor cells.
9. Tumor-free mesocolic resection margin: The margin of the mesocolon, the connective tissue that supports the colon, is clear of tumor cells.
10. Diverticulosis coli: Presence of diverticula, small pouches that form in the colon wall, in the colon.
11. Stage of tumor: The tumor is classified as pT3 (tumor invades through the muscularis propria), pN2 (tumor has spread to multiple nearby lymph nodes), and pMX (distant metastasis cannot be assessed). The tumor is moderately differentiated (G2) and shows lymphovascular invasion (LI) and tumor deposits in pericolorectal/perirectal tissues (VO). The surgical resection margin is clear of tumor (local R0).
12. Aino coreedsrar nies 8140/3: Not specified in the summary.
13. Sites aigmeid coe (aad cece) C187: Not specified in the summary.
14. Vasa: Not specified in the summary.
15. a396- 223486304870 dacted: Not specified in the summary.
16. Lea: Not specified in the summary.

Overall, the report indicates the presence of a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the colon that has spread to nearby lymph nodes. The surgical resection margins are clear, but there is infiltration into surrounding fatty tissue. The specific stage and other details of the tumor are provided.

The pathology report describes a case of colon cancer. Block A shows an invasive adenocarcinoma of the colon with aggressive infiltration into the surrounding fatty connective tissue and blood vessels. Block B shows an additional polyp, which is a tubular adenoma with severe dysplasia that has transitioned into a confined adenocarcinoma and has infiltrated the submucosa. The tumor is classified as G3 for the invasive adenocarcinoma and G2 for the polypoid lesion. The resection margins are free from cancer cells, including the margins at the ileum and colon, as well as the circumferential margin. Additionally, the lymph nodes sampled are free from cancer cells.

The pathology report describes a right hemicolectomy surgery that was done to prepare for a cecal carcinoma (cancer in the cecum, which is a part of the large intestine) diagnosis. The tumor is a moderately differentiated colorectal adenocarcinoma (a type of cancer that originates in the glandular cells of the colon or rectum), which is almost completely covering the cecum and measuring 5.5cm in diameter. The tumor has invaded all layers of the intestinal walls up to the fatty tissue and subserosa (outermost layer of the intestine). However, the margins of the resected area (areas where the tumor was cut out) and the greater omentum (a fatty tissue that hangs down from the stomach) are free of tumor cells. Lymph nodes in the mesocolic and mesenteric regions (near the colon and small intestine) are also free of tumor cells, but some of these lymph nodes show reactive lesions (abnormal but non-cancerous changes). The final tumor staging is pT3 (tumor has invaded through the outermost layer of the colon), pNO (no cancer cells found in the lymph nodes), LO (no cancer cells found at the margins of the resected area), V1 (blood or lymphatic vessel invasion is present).

The pathology report states that a segment of the sigmoid colon was surgically removed. The colon contained an invasive moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma that extended to the subserosa, with a tumor size of 3.5x3.2x0.6 cm. There was no evidence of angiolympatic/perineural invasion. Eighteen lymph nodes were examined and found to be negative for tumor. The tumor originated from a tubular adenoma. In addition to the tumor, the uninvolved colon showed a hyperplastic polyp and a diverticulum. Two additional specimens, a proximal donut and a distal donut, were excised from the colon and showed no signs of tumor. The overall stage of the colorectal cancer is T3 NO Mx.

This pathology report describes two separate samples from the patient named Jeb. 

1. Sample 10: The diagnosis is a colon resectate (removal of part of the colon) that includes a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma (cancerous tumor derived from glandular tissue) of the colorectal type with a maximum size of 3 cm. The tumor has infiltrated the surrounding pericolic fatty tissue and has spread to seven regional lymph nodes, including one in the mesenteric resection margin (the tissue removed during surgery). The resection margins of the small and large intestines are free of tumor.

2. Sample 10: This is another colon resectate that includes a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colorectal type. This tumor formed at the base of a tubular adenoma (precancerous growth) with high-grade dysplasia (abnormal cell growth). The tumor has infiltrated the submucosa layer of the cecum (part of the large intestine). However, there are no tumor cells found in the regional lymph nodes or in the resection margins of the small and large intestines, the mesenteric resection margin, the appendix, or the omental fat tissue.

The tumor stage for the first sample is pT3 pN2 (7 out of 25 lymph nodes affected) pMX (metastasis cannot be determined); G2 (moderate differentiation), LI (lymphatic infiltration) VO (vascular infiltration), locally RO (residual tumor is not observed). The tumor stage for the second sample is pT1 (tumor confined to the innermost layer of the colon) pNO (no lymph node involvement) pMX (metastasis cannot be determined); G2 (moderate differentiation), LO (no lymphatic infiltration), VO (vascular infiltration), RO (residual tumor is not observed).

Summary: The pathology report describes a case of bifocal cancer of the large intestine involving the sigmoid colon and rectum. The specimen consisted of the sigmoid colon with two tumors. The first tumor was cauliflower-shaped, measuring 5 x 3 x 2.5 cm. It completely surrounded the intestine, narrowing its lumen, and penetrated the intestinal wall and fat tissue. The second tumor measured 2.5 x 3 x 1 cm and was located 5 cm away from the first tumor. It also penetrated the intestinal wall. Both tumors were diagnosed as tubulopapillary adenocarcinoma with some mucinous features. The tumors infiltrated the muscularis propria layer and pericolonic adipose tissue. The minimum side margin for the first tumor was 1.1 cm, while for the second tumor it was 2.5 cm. The report also mentions lymph node involvement and provides information on the stage and grade of the cancer.

This is a revised pathology report of a surgical procedure including a uterine implant biopsy and a right hemicolectomy for a patient with a clinical diagnosis of colon cancer. 

The uterine implant biopsy shows a nodule of benign smooth muscle consistent with leiomyoma. 

The right hemicolectomy specimen reveals an adenocarcinoma with a poorly differentiated histologic grade. The tumor has invaded through the muscularis propria into the pericolic adipose tissue. Lymphatic and venous invasion as well as perineural space invasion are present. The proximal and distal margins are free of tumor, but the circumferential (radial) margin is involved with tumor. 

A total of 15 lymph nodes were examined, and metastasis was found in an unspecified number of nodes. The pathologic TNM stage is at least pY3, cannot exclude pT4, pN2, pMx. 

Additional findings include fibrous obliteration of the appendix and no pathologic abnormalities in the attached portion of small bowel. 

A frozen section was performed during the intraoperative consultation of the uterine implant biopsy, which revealed benign fibromuscular tissue with no carcinoma seen. 

The gross appearance of the tumor in the right colon is described as an indurated depression with a rolled border. Cross sectioning revealed rubbery firm white solid tissue with focal yellow necrosis in the pericecal adipose tissue/subserosa. The tumor showed infiltrative growth and extended to the radial margin. The dimensions of the tumor are 6.5 x 3.0 x 3.0 cm with a circumferential growth of 40%. The tumor invades through the muscularis propria into the subserosa/pericecal adipose tissue and is close to or potentially perforating the visceral peritoneum. There is no luminal obstruction, and the distance of the tumor from the margins is noted. 

Multiple foci of yellow/white tumor nodules are found within the subserosa below the primary tumor mass, possibly representing lymph node involvement or desmoplastic response to subserosal tumor deposits. 

Several tissue blocks were submitted for further investigation, including margins and tumor samples. 

Overall, the pathology report suggests a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma in the right colon with local invasion and potential lymph node involvement. The exact stage of the cancer is pending further clinical review and additional information.

The pathology report states that the specimen removed from the patient's colon is diagnosed as a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the colorectal type located in the cecum. The tumor is approximately 5.5 cm in size and has invaded the surrounding fatty tissue. There are no signs of regional lymph node metastases and the margins of the resected intestines and mesentery are free from tumor cells. In addition, two submucosal lipomas are found in the ascending colon. The tumor stage is classified as pT3, pNO (0/27), pMX with a tumor grade of G2 and involvement of lymphovascular invasion, venous invasion, and perineural invasion.

This pathology report describes a tumor located in the proximal part of the cecum. The tumor sample was procured on an unknown date. The histology of the tumor is adenocarcinoma, and it is poorly differentiated. The presence of mucinous and signet ring features is unknown, but there may be focal signet ring cells. There is no histologic heterogeneity, Crohn's like reaction, or plasma cell-rich stroma present. The growth pattern of the tumor is unknown, as is the presence of inflammatory bowel disease, angiolymphatic invasion, and mutator phenotype. Two slides were examined, and garland necrosis was not present. The number of TIL (tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte) cells per high power field is unknown. The pathologist did not provide any additional comments.

The pathology report describes a partial resection of the sigmoid colon, which was done to treat sigmoid colon cancer. The gross description of the specimen includes details about the appearance of the colon, such as its length, color, and the presence of fat. The report mentions the presence of a tumor measuring 2.7 x 2.2 x 0.4 cm, located 7.5 cm from one end of the specimen. The tumor is described as minimally invading the muscularis propria and not invading the fat. Multiple diverticula are also noted in the mucosa. Lymph nodes are identified in the fat surrounding the specimen. Representative sections of the specimen, including margins, tumor, diverticula, and lymph nodes, are submitted for microscopic examination.

The microscopic examination reveals that the tumor is an adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated. It is noted to invade through the muscularis propria. Sixteen lymph nodes examined are negative for tumor involvement. The report concludes with the diagnosis of sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, invading into but through the muscularis propria, with negative lymph nodes.

This pathology report is for a patient with multiple organ resection, including a segment of the large intestine, small intestine, and appendix. The report indicates the presence of an ulcerous tumor in the mucosa measuring 4.7 x 4 x 2 cm. The tumor is located 7.0 cm from the proximal cut end, 12.0 cm from the distal cut end, and 0 cm from the Baughin valve. The minimum side margin is 5.0 cm.

The diagnosis is adenocarcinoma tubuloapapilar (Gi) with infiltration into the muscularis propria and pericolonic fatty tissue. The minimum side margin is 5.0 cm. There is no evidence of neoplastic lesions in nearby lymph nodes, but reactive lymph nodes are present. The final histopathological diagnosis is adenocarcinoma tubulopapilare coll (Gt; Dukes 8, Astler-Collr 82; pT3; pNO). The report advises contacting the doctor with this information.

The pathology report describes a tumor found in the cecum, specifically the proximal part. The tumor is identified as adenocarcinoma and is moderately differentiated. There is no mucinous or signet ring feature. Heterogeneity in histology and a host response in the form of lymphoid aggregates are not observed. There is no Crohn's-like reaction, plasma cell-rich stroma, or angiolymphatic invasion. The growth pattern of the tumor is described as expansile and possibly invasive. Inflammatory bowel disease and mutator phenotype are unknown. Garland necrosis is not present. The pathologist comments that the mucosa is mostly adenocarcinoma.

The pathology report indicates that the specimen received is a paraffin block of tissue. The report does not provide specific information about the specimen or the disease. The report includes microscopic descriptions of the histological pattern and cellular features, including differentiation and nuclear appearance. It also mentions the absence of certain markers and provides comments, but no final diagnosis is given.

This pathology report describes a surgical excision of a specimen from the right colon. The report states that there is an intact vermiform appendix present. In the cecum, there is a polypoid mass measuring 1.8 x 2.6 x 0.8 cm identified as an adenocarcinoma with low-grade, moderately differentiated histologic type. The tumor has penetrated into the muscularis propria but does not extend to the inked serosal surface. The margins of the excised tissue are uninvolved by invasive carcinoma. No metastases are identified in the examined lymph nodes. The tumor is classified as pT2, pN0, pIx according to the pathologic staging.

The pathology report indicates that the specimen taken from the sigmoid colon shows a low-grade, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. The tumor is located in the sigmoid colon and has a polypoid and fungating ulcerative appearance with an infiltrating border. The tumor has invaded into the muscularis propria but has not spread beyond the serosa. There is no lymphovascular invasion or extramural venous invasion identified, and perineural invasion is also not identified. There is a peritumoral lymphoid response. There are no residual adenomas present. The regional lymph nodes (13 total) are negative for tumor invasion. The AICC classification is pT2 NO MX. Associated diseases include hyperplastic polyps and diverticulosis. The proximal and distal resection margins are negative for tumor. The gross description of the specimen indicates the size and location of the tumor and the presence of polyps. The proximal and distal donut sections of the specimen show no gross lesions.
