The pathology report describes the analysis of a lung nodule and lymph nodes. The lung nodule is identified as adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, located at the medial aspect of the right upper lobe. The tumor is unifocal, confined to lung parenchyma, and does not show lymphovascular invasion. The report also shows that the peribronchial lymph nodes are negative for malignancy, and the lymph nodes are benign. Finally, there is emphysematous change found and calcified granulomata, and there is no evidence of fungal or acid-fast organisms.
The pathology report is not complete and only contains basic patient information and order details. No results or findings are provided.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy of lung tissue that revealed a poorly differentiated bronchiolo-alveolar adenocarcinoma. The extent of the tumor, nodules, lymph nodes, lymphatic invasion, venous invasion, margins, and evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment were not specified. There were no additional pathologic findings, and no comments were made.

The pathology report shows results of various samples collected during surgery for left upper lobe lung cancer. Several lymph nodes were excised and found to be negative for carcinoma. A poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma was identified in the left upper lobe nodule, and samples were taken for genomic study. The report includes frozen section diagnoses, microscopic examination findings, and the final diagnosis for each sample.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy on the right upper lobe of a female patient, revealing adenocarcinoma with separate tumor nodules in the same lobe. The cancer has not invaded the pleura, and no lymphatic or vascular invasion is identified. The chest wall margin is also uninvolved. The lymph nodes sampled are negative for malignancy, and there is additionally evidence of centrilobular emphysema. Ancillary studies revealed a strong staining for TTF-1 and no staining for p83, supporting an adenocarcinoma diagnosis. Subsequent EGFR mutation analysis yielded a wild-type result. Several nodules resembling lymph nodes were also submitted, but they are benign. The final diagnosis is Stage IIB adenocarcinoma.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, compatible with lung origin, that is 1.5 cm in maximum dimension and has invaded the visceral pleura. The patient underwent lobectomy and regional lymph node dissection, and nine lymph nodes were found to be negative for metastasis. The margin status was negative, and the tumor was staged as IB. Additionally, an incidental spindle cell carcinoid tumor measuring 0.5 cm in greatest dimension was identified.

The pathology report includes the results of a surgery to remove lymph nodes and a lung lobe due to cancer. The lymph nodes were negative for metastatic carcinoma, except for one peribronchial lymph node. The lung tumor was identified as adenocarcinoma, mixed subtype, with solid and micropapillary patterns. It measured 6.3 x 6.3 x 5.0 cm and showed perineural invasion and visceral pleural invasion. The resection margins were negative for carcinoma. The report includes the tumor size, lymph nodes involvement, TNM descriptors, and other relevant information about the tumor and margins. The patient had a previous skin biopsy of a seborrheic keratosis that was benign.

The report describes two tissue samples collected from resected men and muff tumors. The men tumor was diagnosed as T2, N2, and M0, meaning it involves both upper and middle right lobes, with no distant metastasis. The muff tumor was also diagnosed as T2, N/A (not available), and M0, and there are no additional comments on histology. URLs for the slides were not provided.

The pathology report indicates that multiple lymph nodes were negative for malignancy. A mass was found in the left lung with a biopsy revealing moderate to poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma. Two lesions were present, measuring 6x5x4 cm and 3x2.5x1.5 cm respectively. The bronchial and vascular margins of resection were free of tumor, but one lymph node was partially involved. It is not clear from the histology if this represents two separate primary tumors or an antepulmonary metastasis from the main lung tumor.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent surgery to remove a tumor from their left upper lung lobe. The tumor was identified as adenocarcinoma and was moderately differentiated. The tumor measured 5.5 cm and had invaded the venous, arterial, and lymphatic systems. The tumor also had visceral pleural invasion and invaded the perineural area. The surgical margins were positive for pleural, bronchial, and vascular invasion. Of the 14 lymph nodes biopsied from various stations, 10 were positive for metastatic malignancy. The pathology stage was pT2b pN2 pM N/A. Further clinical review is pending. One of the lymph nodes from Station 5 had frozen metastatic non-small cell carcinoma. Other lymph nodes were negative, and no tumor was seen in the R4 lymph node. The report also includes details about the size and location of the tumor and the gross appearance of the specimen.

The pathology report describes a surgically removed 1.7 cm invasive poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma on the right upper lobe of the lung with visceral pleural invasion, without angiolymphatic invasion. No cancer was found in any of the sampled lymph nodes. The surgical resection margins were free of tumor. Emphysema, parenchymal scar, and smoker's bronchiolitis were reported as underlying diseases. The final pathological stage was T2NOMx. Additional ancillary studies such as histochemical stains and immunohistochemical stains were conducted, but no further information was provided about the results.

The patient had a right upper lobe lobectomy for adenocarcinoma with a size of 2.5 cm, negative for vascular and lymphatic invasion, and negative margins. The lymph nodes (#4, #7, #11, and 10R) were negative for neoplasm. The right lower lobe wedge excision had two nodules, which were also negative for neoplasm. Multiple lymph nodes submitted with various sizes were aggregating and all were negative for neoplasm. The final diagnosis was T1b N0 M0 (Stage IA).

The pathology report describes a case of lung cancer in a patient who underwent a right lower lobe wedge resection. The tumor was identified as predominantly solid type adenocarcinoma, poorly differentiated, with a size of 3.5x 3.3 x 3.2 cm. There was no visceral pleural invasion or definite vascular invasion identified, but metastatic carcinoma was found in one out of two lymph nodes. The report also mentions atypical adenomatous hyperplasia and acute bronchopneumonia in the lung tissue. The tumors found in parts A and C are histologically different, possibly representing separate primary tumors. Further details about tumor margins, treatment effect, and TNM descriptors are also mentioned in the report.

The pathology report includes information on two samples of tissue collected from the left upper lobe (LUL). Both samples were collected three years prior to the report. The first sample was collected as a tumor and prepared as formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue, while the second sample was collected as a buffy coat and also prepared as FFPE tissue. The histology diagnosis for both samples is T2,NOS (meaning a tumor with a size of 3.5 cm) and there is no evidence of nodal involvement (N0) or distant metastasis (M0). The comments section indicates that both samples have the same T stage and differentiation grade. VALCSG stage is not specified. Slide URLs are also provided.

The pathology report describes the specimens received from a patient with right lung cancer. Eight lymph nodes and a bronchial margin were submitted for microscopic evaluation. The report describes the size and appearance of each specimen and notes the absence of tumor seen in some of the lymph nodes and the bronchial margin. The final diagnosis indicates no evidence of tumor in some of the lymph nodes examined.

The pathology report describes a 2.7 x 1.0 cm poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma in the right lower lobe of the lung that invades the visceral pleura surface, without evidence of angiolymphatic invasion or venous invasion. Multiple subpleural nodules are described as small foci of metaplastic epithelial proliferations. No lymph node metastases were found and the bronchial margin is negative for carcinoma. Immunohistochemical stains support the interpretation of a primary lung adenocarcinoma. The final diagnosis is pT2 (PL2),NO,MX bronchiolo-alveolar adenocarcinoma. No evidence of neoadjuvant treatment or other significant pathologic findings were identified.

The pathology report describes the examination of several specimens, including lymph nodes and lung tissue. The diagnosis reveals a metastatic non-small cell carcinoma in the mediastinal lymph nodes and invasive adenocarcinoma in the right lower lobe of the lung. The lymphovascular space status is negative for invasion, and the pleural surface is negative for carcinoma. The TNM classification is pT1a pN2, with multiple peribronchial lymph nodes affected. A complete lobectomy was performed, and the bronchial margin is negative for carcinoma.

The pathology report describes the results of tests on several samples, including lymph nodes and lung tissue. One lymph node was found to have metastatic adenocarcinoma, with the primary tumor being 2.3cm in size and poorly differentiated. There was invasion into regional lymph nodes but no distant metastasis, and margins were uninvolved. Molecular analysis was also ordered, with EGFR mutation analysis coming back positive for a mutation that has been reported to correlate with responsiveness to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapies in non-small-cell lung cancer. ALK FISH analysis was negative, showing no evidence of rearrangement of the ALK gene.

The report describes a lymph node excision from station 4 and station 7, both of which were negative for tumor. However, a lobectomy was also performed on the left upper lobe of the lung, which revealed a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma measuring 5 cm with features of papillary adenocarcinoma of the lung and a peripheral bronchioloalveolar component. The tumor did not invade the pleura, but there was evidence of focal vascular invasion. One lymph node was found to have metastatic carcinoma.

The pathology report describes a large adenocarcinoma of the right upper lobe of the lung with a predominantly mucinous bronchiolo-alveolar component and a smaller acinar and solid part. The tumor is classified as pT2 pNO RO, stage IB. There is no evidence of cancer in the visceral pleura or the lymph nodes and margins are clear of tumor.

The patient has a large mixed adenocarcinoma in the left lower lobe of the lung with a partially bronchioloalveolar pattern of spread and localization in specific areas. There is also a small, non-mucinous bronchioloalveolar carcinoma in a peripheral area. The TNM classification based on this shows it is a pT2(2) pNO pMX RO stage IB 34,3 with two specific types of cancer cells present.

The report describes a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with focal mucinous, bronchioloalveolar, and papillary features that measures 3.4 cm in the left lower lobe of the lung. The carcinoma does not invade the pleura and there is no identified lymphovascular invasion. The resection margins are free of tumor. Seven lymph nodes were removed and examined, but showed no evidence of malignancy. Additionally, one small hyalinized granuloma was found. The non-neoplastic lung tissue shows no pathologic abnormalities. The histopathologic type, histological grade, tumor size, and invasion of lymphatic, venous, and arterial structures are documented.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy specimen taken from the right-upper lung of the patient. The tumor is identified as a papillary adenocarcinoma that is well differentiated. The report states that the extent of the tumor and any other nodules present are not specified, but there is no lymphatic or venous invasion. The lymph nodes examined show no evidence of metastasis. The report does not provide information regarding margins or neo-adjuvant treatment. Other pathologic findings are also not specified. TTF1 and CD15 are both reported as positive.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy specimen from the right upper lobe of a lung, indicating the presence of invasive adenocarcinoma with mucinous features measuring 2.6 cm. The bronchial, vascular, parenchymal, and visceral pleural margins are free of tumor, indicating negative margins. However, one out of five peribronchial lymph nodes showed metastatic adenocarcinoma. The specimen was positive for CK7 and TTF-1 and negative for CK20 and COX-2, which supports a lung primary. The histological grade was 1, and the TN stage was pT1bN1. The report also examines other tissues from the surgery and found no evidence of malignancy.

The pathology report describes a surgical resection of a right lower lobe superior segment adenocarcinoma in a patient with no identified KRAS or EGFR mutations. Fluorescence insta hybridization studies indicate ne EGFR amplification in the targeted region. The report also notes the presence of a typical carcinoid and numerous carcinoid tumorlets and diffuse neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia throughout the lung. Lymph nodes biopsied were found to contain anthracotic pigment, but were otherwise benign. Pathologic stage is T2NOMr. Emphysematous change is noted in the lung parenchyma.

The pathology report describes the results of a lobectomy for lung cancer. The report includes multiple specimens of lymph nodes and lung tissue, most of which are found to be reactive lymph nodes with one lymph node involved in the cancer. The primary tumor is diagnosed as adenocarcinoma with a size of 3.7 cm. There is no invasion of visceral pleura and all margins are uninvolved by invasive carcinoma with a distance of 3mm from the closest margin. Lymphatic invasion is present, and the final pathological stage is determined to be pT2a with pNL. Additional findings include emphysematous changes in lung tissue.

The pathology report is missing and a form is being filled out to provide some basic information. The patient's tumor type is LVAD, and the specimen was originally sent to the BCR. The date the specimen was received was 2/10/2010. The ICD-0-3 Histology and Site Codes are not provided.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a right lung mass that is a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma measuring 15 cm in greatest dimension. The surgical margins are uninvolved, but arterial, venous, and lymphatic invasions are all suspicious. There is also no evidence of distant metastasis in the examined specimens, but metastasis is present in three out of five level 4 lymph nodes. The report also includes results for other examined lymph nodes, including levels 7, 9, 11, and 12, which all show no evidence of metastasis.

The pathology report describes specimens taken from a patient with a lung nodule, including a wedge resection, lymph node biopsies, and a complete lobectomy. The report reveals a diagnosis of adenocarcinoma with mixed subtypes present in the right lower lobe, with measurements and details provided. The lymph node biopsies and lobectomy confirm the absence of residual tumor and report negative results for carcinoma. The report also mentions addendums for molecular studies and includes a macroscopic description of the specimen received.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of a well-differentiated adenocarcinoma with clear cell features in the left lower lobe tumor. There is overexpression of the EGFR protein and an increased copy number of chromosome 7, indicating aneuploidy. The report also includes information on lymph node involvement and surgical procedures performed. The diagnostic evaluation was conducted by the named pathologist.

The report describes the analysis of a surgical specimen obtained from a lobectomy performed on the right upper lobe of the lung. The main diagnosis is adenocarcinoma with acinar and bronchioloalveolar components. The report also describes the absence of neoplasms in lymph nodes at levels 10 and 11. There was no vascular or lymphatic invasion, and the bronchial margin was negative. The tumor was classified as Stage IA (oT tb NO) according to the AJCC classification. The tumor was sent for EGFR mutational analysis, and the results were negative. In summary, the report identifies an early-stage adenocarcinoma that appears to have been completely removed during the surgery.

The pathology report describes a lung lobe tumor that is 3.5 x 3 cm in size and diagnosed as adenocarcinoma with a solid growth pattern. Seven examined hilar lymph nodes showed reactive changes but no metastasis was detected. The margins are not involved, and there is no mention of neo-adjuvant treatment or any other findings.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a left upper lobe wedge resection and completion lobectomy for a lung mass. The diagnosis is adenocarcinoma with a micropapillary predominant pattern and additional components of acinar, lepidic, and giant cell. The tumor is 3.5 cm in size and there is no tumor involvement in the margins of resection. Three lymph nodes biopsied from stations 9 and 11 are benign. The tumor is classified as pT2aN0 (stage IA). The specimen also shows emphysema. Additional molecular and biomarker studies are pending.

The patient underwent a right middle lobe lobectomy for a pulmonary mass, which was diagnosed as invasive adenocarcinoma on pathology. The tumor measured 4.5 cm in size and invaded but did not extend through the pleural elastica. Of the five lymph nodes biopsied, one was positive for metastatic carcinoma. The tumor was poorly differentiated and surrounded by lung or visceral pleura without bronchoscopic evidence of invasion more proximal than the lobar bronchus, making it pT2a. One lymph node was involved, making it PN1, while there was no distant metastasis. The surgical margins of all tissues were uninvolved by invasive carcinoma. The gross description indicated an elongated to irregular grey firm tumor measuring 4.5x4x3.4 cm. Other findings included areas of emphysema and congestion and obstructive pneumonitis.

The pathology report describes multiple biopsies and tissue samples from a patient with a diagnosis of right lung cancer. Tissue samples were collected from various sites including biopsies at different depths (42 cm, 40 cm, and 34 cm), portions of the right 6th rib, lymph nodes at different levels (9, 11, 8, 10, and 7) and the right lower lobe of the lung. Frozen section evaluation of the bronchial margin found no tumor. The report does not provide a final diagnosis or detailed analysis of the samples, but describes the gross appearance of the tissues and which sections were submitted for further testing.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had lung cancer, and multiple specimens were taken for analysis. The portion of the 6th rib showed no tumor. Seven lymph nodes in level 9 showed no evidence of cancer, but two of fifteen lymph nodes in level 5 were found to have metastatic carcinoma. The diaphragmatic adhesion was determined to be a fibrous adhesion. Three of six lymph nodes in 11L showed metastatic carcinoma, and no tumors were seen in five lymph nodes in 12L. Two lymph nodes tested in level 7 had no tumor, while two of three lymph nodes in another area tested positive. The left lung pneumonectomy showed a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, with angiolymphatic invasion but no invasion of the visceral pleura. Of the twelve peribronchial lymph nodes tested, four were found to have metastatic carcinoma. A new bronchial margin excision showed no tumor, and three lymph nodes in level 6 also showed no tumor. Overall, the report confirms the presence of lung cancer with metastasis to some lymph nodes, but the surgical margins were found to be free of cancer. Additionally, the patient had emphysema.

The pathology report describes a biopsy of a lesion in the right upper lobe of the lung, which was diagnosed as poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma. The tumor was found to grossly extend to within 2 cm of the surgical resection margin and was 0.2 cm deep to the pleural surface. The surgical margin was negative for carcinoma, and there was no evidence of space invasion. Two lymph node biopsies were benign. The final diagnosis is pT1a pNO lung adenocarcinoma. Immunophenotypic analysis supported the interpretation of adenocarcinoma.

The report describes a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma present in the left upper lobe of the lung, which has been surgically removed along with 11 lymph nodes. The margins of resection are negative, but the tumor has invaded the lymphatic vessels. No large vessel invasion or distant metastases have been detected. Several tissue fragments have been sampled for further examination.

The pathology report describes a tumor in the left upper lobe of the lung, measuring 8.0 x 7.0 x 4.0 cm, which has been diagnosed as adenocarcinoma, papillary with infiltration of the pleura visceralis. The tumor is classified as pT2, pNO (0/37), pMx, G2 after examination by a pathologist.

The pathology report describes a surgical specimen of lung tissue that was removed from a patient with a lung mass. The report identifies the presence of adenocarcinoma, a type of cancer, which was moderately differentiated and unifocal. The tumor did not invade the visceral pleura, which is the lining of the lung, or the lymphovascular space. The surgical margin distances from the tumor were recorded. The lymph nodes in levels 7, 8, and 10 were found to be benign. Additionally, there was evidence of organizing pneumonia. The overall stage was assigned as pT1aNo.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy specimen taken from the lung of a patient with adenocarcinoma. The tumor size was 6 x 6 x 6 cm and was found to be moderately differentiated. There was no evidence of lymphatic or venous invasion. One out of one lymph node examined was positive for metastasis. The report did not specify other tumor nodules, tumor extent, margins, or evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment. No additional pathologic findings were noted.

The pathology report indicates that a lobectomy was performed on the right lower lobe of a patient with a preoperative diagnosis of lung cancer. The tumor was found to be invasive adenocarcinoma with bronchioloalveolar features, measuring 2.5 cm in its greatest dimension and located 5 cm from the bronchial resection margin. The tumor is graded as I-II and categorized as pT2, invading the visceral pleura. No regional lymph node metastasis was found in 3 peribronchial lymph nodes, 1 station 8 paraesophageal lymph node, and 1 station 11 interlobar lymph node. Distant metastasis cannot be assessed. The margins are uninvolved by invasive carcinoma, and no direct extension was identified. Venous and arterial invasion were absent, and no lymphatic invasion was found. The report also notes a central scar associated with the tumor and one lymph node showing sinus histiocytosis with anthracosis.

The pathology report describes a case of lung cancer, with a poorly differentiated adenosquamous carcinoma present in the left upper lobe of the lung. The tumor is unifocal, confined to the lung parenchyma and measures 3.7 x 3.5 x 3.3 cm. The report notes that there is no evidence of invasion to the visceral pleura or lymphovascular space, but there is noted tumor extension to within 1 mm of the pleural surface. Peribronchial and other lymph nodes have been excised and are negative for metastatic carcinoma. The report also notes the presence of emphysematous changes.

This pathology report provides information on the diagnosis and stage of lung cancer. The ethnicity and clinical diagnosis are not specified, but the tumor was located in the lung. The tissue sample was analyzed and classified as a tumor, with no observed normal tissue. The histological description and grade of the tumor are not mentioned, but the TNM stage is noted. No information is given on the treatment plan. The report also includes some demographic details of the patient, including age and gender.

The patient underwent a right thoracotomy and right lobectomy due to lung cancer. The specimen received consisted of the right upper lobe and lymph nodes. The tumor measured 7.7 cm and was identified as adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, invading the visceral pleura. The bronchial margins were negative for tumor, but lymphovascular invasion was positive for tumor. Multiple lymph nodes were negative for tumor. Overall, the specimen was intact and the tumor appeared to be unifocal. The histology grade of the tumor was moderately differentiated.

The pathology report describes the examination of nodules found in the right upper lobe of a lung, which were removed and analyzed for cancerous cells. The two nodules were found to be invasive moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, and appear to be connected in a "dumbbell" shape. A lymph node biopsy shows no evidence of metastatic disease. A small amount of tumor growth was found on the outer surface of the visceral pleura. The report includes additional information on the histology and margins of the nodules.

The pathology report shows a diagnosis of adenocarcinoma in a lymph node with a tumor size of 8.8% 4.3x3.8 cm. There is evidence of invasion in the lymphovascular space and presence of a possible tumor mass. The surgical margins are stapled and there is a possibility of a 6 Tom parabronchial lymph node. Representative sections of the specimen have been submitted for examination. Further information is needed regarding the patient's clinical history.

The pathology report describes a surgical procedure where multiple samples were taken from the lung and lymph nodes of a patient. One of the samples showed a 1.2cm adenocarcinoma in the right upper lobe of the lung, consisting of acinar and lepidic components. The tumor was completely removed in a subsequent lobectomy surgery, and no cancer was found in the lymph nodes. The report also noted the presence of emphysema. Further molecular studies were ordered and are reported in four addenda.

The patient was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma in the right lung upper lobe. The tumor was moderately differentiated and measured 2.5 x 2.3 x 1.6 cm, located at the posterior apex and subpleural. The malignancy did not extend through the visceral pleura, and no lymphovascular space invasion was identified. The lymph nodes from various levels were negative for malignancy or showed reactive hyperplasia and noncaseating granulomata. One small lymph node from level 9 and several fragments from level 10 showed dystrophically calcified granulomas. The patient's TN stage was pT1b NO.

The pathology report shows a diagnosis of adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated, in a resected right upper lobe of the lung with uninvolved margins. There is no evidence of metastasis in nine lymph nodes from the resection, two lymph nodes from 2R, and three lymph nodes from station 7, while station 9 has one negative node. The report also notes the presence of granulomatous inflammation in station 7. A possible secondary lesion measuring 0.8 x 0.7 x 0.4 cm is present along the pleural aspect of the lung, which is submitted for tissue procurement. There are some biopsy site changes present in blocks A7 and A8. Overall, the post-op diagnosis remains the same as the pre-op diagnosis of Lung cancer.

The pathology report describes the results of a surgical procedure that involved biopsies and lymph node removal of a patient with a right upper lobe mass. The report states that the pleural biopsy showed no tumor, while the right upper lobe biopsy revealed a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma measuring 2.5cm that extended into the pleura. The report also notes that the bronchial, vascular, and stapled surgical margins were free of tumor. Lymph node biopsies showed anthracosis, and the final diagnosis was pT2N0Mx. The report also includes gross descriptions of the specimens received during the procedure.

The pathology report performed mutational analysis on the EGFR and KRAS genes and ALK locus rearrangement by FISH to detect tumor-associated genetic changes that impact prognosis and treatment options in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The report found no mutations in the EGFR or KRAS genes and no rearrangement involving the ALK gene, suggesting a negative result for NSCLC. However, an incidental result showed a gain of the ALK region in a small proportion of the tested cells, which suggests that further analysis is required to determine the clinical significance of this finding. The report highlights the importance of considering other clinical and laboratory data in combination with the results to determine a diagnosis and treatment plan for NSCLC.

The pathology report for CGA-49-4505 indicates that the patient had a lobectomy on their right lower lobe due to infiltrating adenocarcinoma, with the carcinoma measuring 5.5 cm and extending through the visceral pleura. One of the six lymph nodes tested showed metastatic carcinoma. The bronchial and vascular margins were negative for tumors. The report also indicates that the patient had a cavitary fibrotic cyst in their right upper lobe, which was colonized by branching hypal fungal forms morphologically consistent with Aspergillus. A wedge resection of the right upper lobe showed infiltrating well-differentiated adenocarcinoma measuring 1.5 cm.

The report describes a lung tissue sample measuring 14.5 x 11.0 x 6.0 cm, with a tumor measuring 4.8 x 3.5 x 3.0 cm. The tumor has a mixed subtype of adenocarcinoma, exhibiting partially papillary, acinar and solid patterns. The tumor has not infiltrated the pleura visceralis. The cancer is staged as pT2, pN1 (with 2 out of 54 lymph nodes affected), and Mx. The cancer is classified as Grade 3, with an unclear note related to "feb-o-3." There is also a mention of an "adinecarcchonrr" and "mixed Silty po" with no context. The report concludes with a possible specimen identification code and a mention of the pathologist who examined the tissue sample.

The pathology report describes a surgical resection of a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the right upper lobe of the lung. No evidence of malignancy is found in 4 out of 4 lymph nodes (R4) and 2 lymph nodes in level X and level VII. The tumor size is 3.7 cm with no vascular invasion. The report also mentions emphysema in the non-tumor lung. Immunohistochemical staining confirms the adenocarcinoma. The clinic information suggests lung cancer. No abnormalities are found in the bronchial resection margin, pulmonary margin of resection, or pleura. The report includes gross descriptions of the specimens taken, including lymph nodes.

The pathology report describes the case of an 8-year-old female with a lung nodule. The frozen section diagnosis revealed adenocarcinoma. The report lists 13 containers with different labelled lymph nodes and lung specimens. A lobectomy specimen was received consistent with the left lower lobe revealing no other mass lesion. The report also includes a block summary. Overall, the report suggests the presence of cancerous tumours in the lymph nodes and lungs.

The pathology report indicates the presence of an adenocarcinoma in a partial pneumonectomy sample taken from the upper lobe of the lung. There is also evidence of extensive lymphatic invasion and metastatic carcinoma in one lymph node and the aortic arch lymph node. The tumor in the lymph nodes is poorly differentiated and has extended into perinodal soft tissue.

This pathology report describes a moderately differentiated bronchiolo-alveolar adenocarcinoma located in a lung tissue specimen from a patient who underwent a pneumonectomy. The report does not specify the extent of the tumor, whether there were other tumor nodules, or the status of lymph nodes and venous invasion. Margins and evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment were also not specified. The report also mentions a lateral excision in the lower portion.

The pathology report describes biopsies and excisions from various areas including lymph nodes, lung, and rib. The lymph nodes were found to be benign & anthracotic with no evidence of carcinoma. A resected portion of the right upper lobe of the lung showed a 1.5 cm adenocarcinoma, predominantly bronchioloalveolar, with a focus of invasive adenocarcinoma. There was no evidence of carcinoma in the bronchovascular margin, and pleural fibrosis was noted. Additionally, three foci of carcinoid tumorlets were identified. The rib showed no diagnostic abnormality. Molecular studies were performed, including testing for the KRAS mutation, and the tumor was found to be positive for the p.G12C mutation. The report includes a pTNM staging with no evidence of distant metastasis and a note about special stains negative for fungi and acid-fast organisms. A comment suggests correlation with microbiology. The report also includes a macroscopic description of the submitted specimens.

The pathology report describes a lung biopsy from a female patient with a history of breast cancer and a positive smoking history. The biopsy revealed an adenocarcinoma without pleural invasion. The frozen section diagnosis was confirmed by further examination, which showed a gland-forming carcinoma without mucinous differentiation. The lineage was determined to be lung primary through immunohistochemistry testing, which showed immunoreactivity for TTF-1 and HER2 but no reactivity for GCDFP or ER. The tumor was moderately differentiated and 2.5 cm in diameter. Surgical margins were not involved. Further testing was recommended to exclude metastasis.

The pathology report shows that there was a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma present in the right upper lobe of the lung. There was evidence of cancer in one lymph node at level 11, while the lymph node at level 10 did not show any evidence of malignancy. The tumor had not invaded any nearby veins, arteries or pleural tissue. The surgical margins were clear of cancerous cells, and there was no evidence of distant metastasis. The overall international stage was 1a.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, poorly differentiated, with venous and lymphatic invasions. Metastatic carcinoma was found in one of the thirteen lymph nodes. Four lymph nodes in station R-4, three lymph nodes in station 7, one lymph node in lower R-4, and one lymph node in station R-11 were negative for the tumor. The report also notes the absence of tumor in a pleural plaque excision. Some tests were performed using reagents not approved by the FDA. The clinical history of the patient is that of lung cancer.

The pathology report describes a white-gray nodule that was found to be an adenocarcinoma with moderate to poorly differentiated features. The tumor is 3.0 cm in size and does not involve the bronchial or visceral pleural. There is no evidence of venous/arterial invasion or lymph node involvement. Other findings include enphysema and intraalveolar hemorrhage. Two fibrotic pleural-based nodules were also noted. A lobectomy was performed on the right upper lobe and a wedge resection on the right lower lobe. No definitive lymph nodes were identified in the soft tissue biopsy.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy of the right lower lobe of the lung for an adenocarcinoma found in a patient with lung cancer. The tumor size is 3mm, with moderate to poorly differentiated histologic grade, and it is surrounded by lung without evidence of invasion more proximal than the lobar bronchus. No lymphovascular invasion is present, and lymph nodes are negative for malignancy. The pathology stage is pT2b pN0. The report suggests that immunohistochemical stains for cytokeratin-7, cytokeratin-S/8, TTF-1, and p63 were performed to evaluate for a mixed subtype, and molecular studies may be indicated. Representative sections are submitted for examination.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy of the right upper lobe of the lung due to adenocarcinoma, which was found to have acinar and lepidic components and extracellular mucin. The tumor was 3.5 cm in size and surrounded by lung or visceral pleura without involvement of the bronchus or vascular margins. Seven lymph nodes in the area were negative for carcinoma. Biopsies of lymph nodes from stations 2, 4, 7, and 11 were also negative for carcinoma. Molecular studies were conducted and will be reported in addenda to the report. The report notes the patient's history of breast cancer.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has a mixed adenocarcinoma with a predominant papillary and small acinar component, slight mucin formation, and is located in segments 7 to 9 of the right lower lobe of the lung. The tumor has extended to 4 of the middle lobe, but the resection margin of the bronchus and vessels, as well as all removed lymph nodes, are tumor-free. The tumor is classified as pT2 pNO pMX RO, and its subtype is M8255/3.

The pathology report describes an excision of a tumor in the lung measuring 6 x 6 x 6 cm. Histologically, it is an adenocarcinoma that is poorly differentiated and has spread to the visceral pleura. There is no indication of lymphatic or venous invasion, and the status of margins and neo-adjuvant treatment is not specified. Ck7, CD15, and TTF-1 are positive, while CK10 and P63 are negative. One out of six lymph nodes is positive for metastasis.

The pathology report indicates that the patient's EGFR gene does not have any known mutations or changes that could result in amino acid changes. However, the report found a KRAS mutation in the patient's DNA that is abnormal. FISH analysis did not show any rearrangement of the ALK gene, but there was a gain of the ALK region, and the significance of this finding is unknown. The report also provides information on the significance of mutations in EGFR, KRAS, and ALK genes in non-small cell lung cancer, and how they can inform prognosis and treatment decisions. No neoplasia is found in the lymph nodes examined. The omentum and surgical margins are also free of neoplasia. The esophageal margin is uninvolved. No neoplasia is found in the lymph nodes along the celiac trunk. A single lymph node along the anterior hepatic artery is uninvolved. Cholelithiasis is noted in the gallbladder. Additional lymph nodes from the greater curvature were not observed and are pending examination.

The pathology report indicates the presence of moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the stomach, specifically in the omentum. The cancer is of mixed type, according to the Lauren classification. The tumor is ulcerative and infiltrative, measuring 8.0 cm in size and extending to the serosa. Lymphatic and perineural infiltration are present. The tumor has a spiculated growing pattern and there is moderate inflammation surrounding it. The surgical margins are clear of neoplasia. The adjacent mucosa shows signs of active chronic pangastritis with incomplete intestinal metaplasia. Additionally, there are metastatic carcinoma cells found in the lymph nodes, with involvement in 10 out of 12 lymph nodes dissected from the lesser curvature and 11 out of 14 lymph nodes dissected from the greater curvature. Capsular infiltration is present, but omentum is not involved by the cancer. The report also mentions the presence of metastatic carcinoma in three out of seven lymph nodes dissected from the celiac trunk lymph node.

This pathology report describes a case of gastric adenocarcinoma in the stomach, specifically in the cardia region. The tumor measures 6.0 cm in diameter and shows signs of ulceration. The histological pattern is tubular, specifically the intestinal type according to Lauren's classification.

The tumor has infiltrated the layers of the stomach, including the mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria, and perivisceral fat. There is also extension to the esophageal mucosa. Neural infiltration, lymphatic vascular invasion, and blood vascular invasion are not detected. The surgical margins are clear of cancer cells.

Lymph nodes in the greater curvature, L1B chain lymph nodes, 8A chain lymph nodes, 12A chain lymph nodes, and 111 lymph nodes are all uninvolved by cancer cells (0/15, 0/4, 0/2, 0/2, and 0/2 respectively). The esophageal margin is also free from neoplastic involvement.

The pathology report is for a subtotal gastrectomy specimen from the stomach. The tumor in the antrum of the stomach is ulcerated and is diagnosed as a poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma. The tumor measures 5 x 4 x 2.5 cm and has invaded the adjacent structures (lesser and greater omentums). Out of the 8 lymph nodes examined, 3 are positive for metastasis (3/8 intraabdominal). The report does not specify the presence of lymphatic, venous, or perineural invasion. The margins are uninvolved and there is no evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment. No additional pathologic findings are mentioned and there are no comments.

This pathology report describes a case of stomach (body) cancer. The report indicates that a subtotal gastrectomy (removal of part of the stomach) was performed, along with D2 lymphadenectomy (removal of lymph nodes). 

The tumor is described as moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the intestinal type, measuring 3.3 cm in length. It has infiltrated the wall of the stomach and reached the perigastric adipose tissue. There is evidence of angiolymphatic invasion and perineural invasion. Moderate peritumoral desmoplasia (tissue reaction to the tumor) is observed, along with discrete peritumoral lymphocitary (presence of lymphocytes around the tumor). The surgical margins are clear of tumor cells.

Additionally, the non-neoplastic gastric segment (part of the stomach not affected by the tumor) shows chronic gastritis with intestinal metaplasia (abnormal changes in the stomach lining), while the epiploon segment (a fatty layer of tissue covering the stomach and intestines) exhibits congested mature adipose tissue.

A total of 18 lymph nodes were examined, with 12 in the perigastric adipose tissue on the small curvature and 6 on the greater gastric curvature. None of the lymph nodes showed evidence of involvement by the tumor.

The pathology report indicates the following:

1. Biopsy of the esophagus revealed a small focus of atypical glands with high-grade dysplasia. Squamous mucosa with chronic inflammation was also present.

2. Biopsy of the esophageal tumor revealed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma associated with squamous mucosa.

Gross description:
- Soft tissue fragments measuring 0.5 x 0.4 x 0.3 cm in aggregate, submitted for analysis.
- Multiple pink-gray soft tissue fragments measuring 0.8 x 0.4 x 0.4 cm in aggregate, also submitted for analysis.

Clinical history: Esophageal cancer.

The TCGA Pathologic Diagnosis Discrepancy Form indicates that there was a discrepancy between the initial pathology report and the TCGA Case Quality Control Form. The form does not provide further details on the discrepancy or the reason for it. The reviewing pathologist or biorepository director is not mentioned in the report.

This pathology report describes a case of gastric adenocarcinoma, specifically the signet ring type. The tumor is located in the antrum of the stomach and is poorly differentiated. It is ulcerated and necrotic, with invasion into the muscle layer and involvement of lymphocytes in the stroma. The tumor measures 5x3 1.5 cm and has spread to the serosa. Lymph node metastasis is present in all 11 lymph nodes examined. Further information regarding lymphatic, venous, and perineural invasion, margin status, and evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment is not provided in the report. There are no additional pathologic findings mentioned.

The pathology report is for a patient with a clinical diagnosis of stomach cancer. The specimen submitted for analysis is a distal gastrectomy, which is the surgical removal of the lower part of the stomach. The report provides measurements of various parts of the stomach and describes the tumor location as the middle third of the stomach on the posterior wall.

The report states that there is no gross serosal invasion, meaning that the tumor has not spread to the outer layer of the stomach. Representative sections of the tumor and surrounding tissues were examined, as well as sections of the antral and body mucosa of the stomach. Lymph nodes from various locations were also examined.

The tumor type is diagnosed as adenocarcinoma, which is a type of cancer that arises from glandular tissue. The report indicates that the tumor is moderately differentiated and has invaded into the submucosa of the upper third of the stomach. There is no evidence of tumor in the margins of the resected stomach.

The report provides additional information about the growth pattern, lymphoid reaction, lymphovascular invasion, venous invasion, perineural invasion, and lymph node metastasis. Special stains were performed, including Cresyl Violet stain for detecting H. pylori infection, but the results are not reported.

The final diagnosis is given as distal gastrectomy for adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated (early cancer). The lymph nodes examined show no evidence of tumor involvement.

This pathology report describes a specimen obtained from a subtotal gastrectomy, indicating surgery to remove a portion of the stomach. The tumor site is the stomach, and the tumor size is 5x5x1 cm. No specific features are mentioned about the tumor. The histologic type is adenocarcinoma, and it is moderately differentiated. The tumor extent is subserosa. The pathology report indicates that no lymph nodes showed evidence of metastasis. No information is provided about lymphatic invasion, venous invasion, perineural invasion, margins, or evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment. No additional pathologic findings are specified. Overall, the report suggests the presence of an adenocarcinoma in the stomach, with regional lymph nodes showing no evidence of metastasis.

The pathology report describes the findings from the examination of a total organ resection of the stomach. The diagnosis is tubular and partially mucocellular invasive adenocarcinoma of the stomach, which is a type of stomach cancer. The cancer has infiltrated the whole thickness of the stomach wall, peritoneum, and fat tissue of the omentum. There are also metastases (cancer spread) in the lymph nodes, including lymph nodes 15, 1, 4, 6, and 9. The report recommends contacting a doctor with this information.

This pathology report describes a gastrectomy specimen from a patient with adenocarcinoma of the stomach. The tumor is poorly differentiated and measures 5x4x1.5 cm. Metastasis is observed in 7 out of 15 lymph nodes examined. There is involvement of the greater omentum. There is no evidence of lymphatic or venous invasion, perineural invasion, or neo-adjuvant treatment. The margins are uninvolved. No additional pathologic findings or comments are provided.

The pathology report indicates the following findings:

- The examined material includes the stomach and omentum.
- There is wall thickening in the orifice region of the stomach, measuring 4.8 x 6.2 x 1.4 cm.
- Microscopically, there is a diagnosis of mixed type mucinous adenocarcinoma of the stomach, with a grade 3 (G3) differentiation. There is invasion of the blood vessels.
- Metastases are identified in lymph nodes (1 out of 16).
- The final histopathological diagnosis is mucinous adenocarcinoma of the stomach with metastases in lymph nodes and vascular invasion.

The pathology report indicates that the specimen obtained from the gastrectomy and secondary esophageal resection includes a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma (gastric carcinoma) located in the prepyloric antrum. The tumor has spread to all layers of the wall and has penetrated the peritoneum. There are five regional lymph node metastases and peritoneal carcinosis. The specific staging for this tumor is pT4a, L1, VO, RO, pN2 (5 out of 52 lymph nodes involved), and pM1 (metastasis).

Additionally, the report mentions the presence of a poorly differentiated, partially mucinous Barrett's adenocarcinoma located in the area of the esophagogastric junction. This tumor is staged as pT3, LO, VO, RO, pNO (no lymph node involvement) 0 out of 52.

The pathology report describes the diagnosis of a moderately differentiated gastric adenocarcinoma in the distal stomach. The tumor has invaded the subserosal soft tissues but does not involve the visceral peritoneum. Lymphovascular invasion and perineural invasion are present. The surgical resection margins are negative, indicating that no tumor is present at the edges of the resected tissue. No tumor is seen in the lymph nodes examined. Other findings include chronic active gastritis, intestinal metaplasia, and intact surgical anastomosis. The report suggests a pathologic staging of pT3 pNO, although a comprehensive review of all available information is recommended for final staging. Additional specimens, including omentum and lymph nodes, show no evidence of tumor.

This pathology report describes two samples collected from the stomach. The first sample is labeled as "Murry FF" and the second sample is labeled as "Wv0ur FF". The samples were collected during a resection procedure and the primary diagnosis for both samples is adenocarcinoma. The size of the tumors is 6 cm for both samples. The histology shows invasion of the full thickness of the muscularis propria into the adventitia for both samples. The grade and differentiation of the tumors are not specified.

This pathology report describes a specimen from a left partial nephrectomy, which was performed on a patient diagnosed with a left renal mass. The diagnosis from the pathology report is renal cell carcinoma, papillary type, with a Fuhrman grade of 2. The tumor size is 4 x 3.8 x 3 cm, and it is limited to the kidney, although the surgical margin is focally positive (0.1 cm). The report also mentions the absence of invasion of vascular/lymphatic tissues and perinephric tissue invasion. The report indicates that the tumor is unifocal and provides additional information about the WHO classification, histologic grade, and presence of glomerular disease. The pathological staging is pT1aNXMX, and no lymph nodes were sampled. The gross description of the specimen mentions the size and characteristics of the mass, including a ruptured area and involvement of surrounding adipose tissue.

The pathology report shows that the patient had multiple renal cell carcinomas of the papillary type in their left kidney. The report also mentions the presence of scar tissue, benign kidney parenchyma, and cystic lesions with irregular lining. No tumors were seen in the surrounding soft tissue or in the skin biopsy.

Summary: The pathology report shows that a left nephrectomy was performed on a patient with a preoperative diagnosis of left renal cancer. The gross examination of the specimen revealed a tumor measuring 5 x 5 x 4.9 cm, located at the superior pole of the kidney. The tumor was described as friable, tan-brown, and necrotic, with no involvement of the renal sinus, pelvis/calyces, renal vein, or adrenal glands. The tumor did not invade the perinephric fat, but it did bulge the renal capsule. Margins were negative for tumor involvement. Microscopic examination confirmed the diagnosis of papillary renal cell carcinoma (type 2) with a Fuhrman grade of 2. The tumor was confined to the kidney and did not show sarcomatoid features. Pathologic staging indicated a primary tumor size of 7 cm or less within the kidney, and the regional lymph nodes were unable to be assessed. Non-neoplastic findings included nephrosclerosis and chronic inflammation. The report also mentions that an intradepartmental consultation was obtained.

The pathology report is for a patient who underwent a partial nephrectomy for a right renal tumor. The diagnosis is renal cell carcinoma of the papillary type, with a Fuhrman Nuclear Grade of 2. The tumor measures 4.5 cm in greatest diameter and does not show local invasion or renal vein invasion. The surgical margins are free of tumor. Non-neoplastic kidney tissue shows moderate arterionephrosclerosis. No adenoma glands or lymph nodes are identified. The tumor is staged as T1, which means it is less than 7.0 cm in greatest dimension and limited to the kidney. The gross description of the specimen reveals a golden yellow encapsulated tumor measuring 4.5 x 3.5 x 3.5 cm, with no involvement of adjacent tissues. A representative section of the margin is submitted for frozen section diagnosis, and a portion of the tumor is submitted for further examination.

The pathology report states that the specimen in question is a 3.8 cm maximum dimension, moderately differentiated Papillary renal cell carcinoma. It also mentions the presence of glomerulosclerosis, interstitial nephritis, and massive arteriosclerosis. The resection margins are tumor-free. The PTNM classification of the tumor is Stage pT1a, pNX, pMX. The grade of the carcinoma is Gil.

This pathology report describes the findings from the examination of a left kidney and adrenal gland specimen. The main diagnosis is papillary renal cell carcinoma (type 2), with a Fuhrman's nuclear grade of 3. The tumor measures 6.5 cm in maximum dimension and is confined to the kidney. Multiple renal coral adenomas and simple cysts are also present in the kidney. Adrenal cortical hyperplasia is noted in the adrenal gland. Additionally, there is one metastatic focus of papillary renal cell carcinoma in one of three hilar lymph nodes. The gross description includes details about the size and appearance of the tumor and other structures. The report also includes section codes for the submitted tissue samples. The clinical history provided is "left renal mass."

This pathology report describes the findings from a partial nephrectomy procedure on a patient with bilateral multifocal papillary renal tumors. The report includes the following diagnoses:

1. Adipose tissue over right renal mass: No tumor seen.
2. Kidney, right, upper pole, cyst wall: Renal parenchyma with fibrosis.
3. Kidney, right, mass/cyst: Renal cal carcinoma, papillary type. The renal parenchyma also has cysts and fibrosis.

The specimens submitted for analysis include adipose tissue over the right renal mass, cyst wall fragments from the right upper pole renal cyst, and a disrupted cystic structure from the right renal mass. The report states that no tumor was seen in the adipose tissue and that the cyst wall is comprised of renal parenchyma with fibrosis. The disrupted cystic structure is consistent with renal cal carcinoma, papillary type and also contains cysts and fibrosis. Approximately 50% of the tissue from the right renal mass/cyst was procured for further analysis.

Overall, the report suggests the presence of renal cal carcinoma, papillary type, along with associated fibrosis and cysts in the right kidney.

The pathology report describes a surgical pathology of a left renal mass. The report states that a small irregular fragment of soft tissue was submitted for intraoperative consultation and no malignancy was seen. The main specimen received was a partial nephrectomy specimen, with a tan-brown, scabrous renal resection margin. The capsular margin was smooth with minimal attached fat. The specimen was inked for identification and a well-circumscribed mass was found, measuring 1.8 cm in size and extending to the capsular surface. The remaining cut surface of the specimen appeared normal and no other lesions were identified.

The microscopic examination revealed a papillary renal cell carcinoma, type 1, grade 1. The tumor was limited to the kidney and had not invaded the margins or lymphatic vessels. The tumor was small in size and unifocal. No sarcomatoid features or tumor necrosis were identified. The final pathologic staging was pT1a, indicating a limited extent of tumor.

The report also mentions the presence of chronic pyelonephritis in the non-neoplastic kidney.

Additional sections pending to determine capsule invasiveness, which will be reported in an addendum. A supplementary report was added, mentioning the identification of a steaplellary adenoma and no capsular invasion.

Overall, the report describes a small, low-grade papillary renal cell carcinoma that was limited to the kidney and had not spread to other tissues.

The pathology report describes the findings of a left renal mass that was incidentally discovered on a CT scan. The specimens submitted for analysis include a partial nephrectomy of the left kidney, a completion nephrectomy of the left kidney, and an excision of perinephric fat. 

The diagnosis of the left kidney mass from the partial nephrectomy is renal cell carcinoma of the unclassified type, with features of oncocyfic, tubular, and papillary patterns. The size of the tumor is 3.8 cm. There is no local invasion identified and no renal vein invasion identified. The surgical margins are free of tumor. The non-neoplastic kidney and adrenal gland are unremarkable, and no lymph nodes are identified.

The diagnosis from the completion nephrectomy is that no residual carcinoma is identified. The renal parenchyma is unremarkable, but there is a 0.2 cm ancient metullary bone mentioned.

The perinephric fat excision is found to be benign fibroadipose tissue.

Immunohistochemical stains show that the tumor cells are strongly positive for E-cadherin and CD117, positive for Ca.9 and racemase, and negative for CK.

The gross description of the specimens includes the size and appearance of the tissue samples. Representative sections are submitted for further analysis.

The frozen section diagnosis during the intraoperative consultation confirms the presence of left renal oncocytic renal cell carcinoma.

Overall, the report provides information about the type of tumor, its characteristics, size, invasion, surgical margins, and other findings from the analysis of the kidney mass and related samples.

The pathology report describes a surgical resection of a portion of the kidney. The diagnosis is renal cell carcinoma, papillary variant, type 1, measuring 3.0 cm in size. The margins are negative and no lymph nodes are identified. The tumor is staged as pT1a, with no regional lymph node involvement or distant metastasis. There is no lymphovascular invasion or perineural invasion identified. Immunohistochemical staining supports the diagnosis. There is a discussion about the margin status and uncertainty regarding the involvement of the parenchymal edge of the specimen. Overall, the report confirms the presence of renal cell carcinoma with certain histological features and provides staging information.

The pathology report shows that the patient underwent a right partial nephrectomy. The final diagnosis reveals an oncocytic variant of papillary renal cell carcinoma, with a Fuhrman nuclear grade of 2. The tumor is confined to the kidney and the resection margin is free of tumor. The deep margin of the renal parenchyma does not show any tumor presence. The pathological stage is determined to be pT1a, NX, MX. Immunohistochemical staining was performed, showing positive results for cytokeratin 7 and E-Cadherin, and weak and focal positivity for vimentin. The tumor cells are negative for CD10, RCC, and C117. Other key pathological findings include the tumor type, nuclear grade, tumor size, and pattern of growth. There is no evidence of renal capsule invasion, perinephric adipose tissue invasion, renal vein invasion, lymphovascular invasion, perineural invasion, adrenal gland involvement, or lymph node involvement. The report also states that there was no clinical history provided, and the preoperative diagnosis was a right renal mass. Intraoperative consultation confirmed an oncocytic lesion in the right partial nephrectomy. The gross description provides details about the size and appearance of the tumor mass and the normal surrounding tissue. Overall, the report suggests that the tumor was removed successfully, with negative margins, and provides important information for staging and further treatment decisions.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a right renal mass, which was surgically excised. The diagnosis of the mass is renal cell carcinoma, specifically papillary Type I. The report also mentions the presence of incipient lesions. Immunohistochemical staining for CK7 was negative. The report includes information about the procedure and specimens submitted. The gross description describes the characteristics of the mass and mentions the procurement of tumor tissue for further analysis. Representative sections were submitted for permanent processing.

The pathology report indicates that the sample is a tumour from the left kidney of the patient. The diagnosis is papillary renal carcinoma, with a tumour size of 4 cm. The histology reveals papillary renal carcinoma with a Fuhrman nuclear grade of 3/4. The pathological examination indicates T1a stage, with no lymph node involvement (Nx) and no distant metastasis (M0).

The pathology report describes a case of metastatic renal cell carcinoma (RCC) involvement of the kidney, adrenal gland, and hilar lymph nodes. The tumor is high grade with tubulopapillary features and is classified as renal cell carcinoma. Local invasion into the renal hile fat and angiolymphatic invasion into the renal vein are noted. Surgical margins are free of tumor. The adrenal gland is involved by metastatic carcinoma, and there are metastatic deposits in the lymph nodes. There are also mentions of immunohistochemical stains and ISH tests that were performed. The report also mentions differential diagnoses, including distal nephron tumor, collecting duct carcinoma, type 2 papillary carcinoma, and hereditary leiomyomatosis. Overall, the report provides detailed information about the extent and characteristics of the tumor in the patient.

The pathology report describes findings from a right hemicolectomy specimen and a radical nephrectomy specimen.

In the right colon specimen, five polypoid lesions were identified. The largest polyp (2.2x1.5x0.7 cm) is located 13.0 cm from the distal margin and is superficial. There is a second polyp (1.4x0.8x0.3 cm) located 5.0 cm from the leocecal valve and 12.0 cm proximal to the largest polyp. The third polyp (0.4 cm) is located 4.0 cm from the distal margin and 8.0 cm distal to the largest polyp. Additionally, there are two small polypoid lesions in the cecum, one measuring (0.6 cm) and the other measuring (0.3 cm). No invasive tumor is identified, and the surrounding colonic mucosa is unremarkable.

The radical nephrectomy specimen shows a well-circumscribed firm tumor (4.5x4.0x3.5 cm) in the lower pole of the kidney. The tumor is gray-tan with a small area of hemorrhage. It is confined to the kidney and does not invade into perinephric adipose tissue or extend to Gerota's fascia. The adjacent kidney parenchyma is unremarkable, and lymph nodes are not identified.

Immunohistochemical stains support a diagnosis of type 2 papillary renal cell carcinoma based on the morphologic features and staining patterns.

Overall, the pathology report describes multiple tubular adenomas and sessile serrated adenomas in the right colon, as well as a papillary renal cell carcinoma in the right kidney.

The pathology report indicates that a left renal mass was biopsied and found to be benign on frozen section. The patient then underwent a partial nephrectomy. The tumor was identified as papillary renal cell carcinoma, solid type, with Fuhrman grade 2/4 nuclear grade. There was no lymphovascular space invasion or sorcomatoid features. The tumor contained foamy histiocytes and rare focal papillary architecture at the periphery. The clinical history was renal and ureteral disease, and the postoperative diagnosis was not specified. The specimens received were labeled as the deep margin of the left renal mass and the deep renal mass. The specimens were examined and submitted for further analysis. An intra-operative consultation confirmed the findings.

The pathology report describes the findings from a surgical procedure involving the removal and examination of various tissues from a patient. The specific findings are as follows:

1. A soft tissue mass located near the right paracaval region was resected. No tumor was seen in the lymph node associated with this mass.
2. A lymph node in the right hilar region was resected. Nerve and ganglia were observed in this lymph node.
3. The deep margin of a right renal mass was resected. No tumor was seen in the renal parenchyma.
4. A partial nephrectomy was performed on the right kidney, removing a mass with characteristics consistent with Papillary renal cell carcinoma, Type 1. Extensive necrosis, hemorrhage, and involvement of nerves were observed.

The report indicates that the tumor is limited to the kidney and does not show sarcomatoid features. The tumor is more than 4 cm but not more than 7 cm in size. No regional lymph node metastasis or distant metastasis was identified. There was insufficient non-neoplastic tissue available for analysis.

The clinical information provided states that the patient had a right renal mass with gross hematuria and that specimens were taken for further analysis. The specimens submitted for examination include the right paracaval mass, right hilar lymph node, deep margin of the right renal mass, and the right kidney mass.

An intraoperative consultation was conducted, and the frozen sections of the submitted specimens were examined. The frozen section diagnosis confirmed that no tumor was seen in the lymph node associated with the right paracaval mass, and nerve and ganglia were present in the right hilar lymph node.

The gross description of the specimens includes the size and color of the tissue fragments and their submission for permanent processing.

The pathology report describes the findings of a biopsy or excision of a tissue sample. The report states that the sample is negative for carcinoma or cancer. It also mentions the presence of benign verrucous squamous papilloma. The report includes details about the appearance and characteristics of the sample, as well as the analysis conducted by the attending pathologist. Additional findings include mentions of a margin and surrounding tissue. The report concludes with a summary of the specimen and its representativeness.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a partial nephrectomy for a renal tumor. The report states that the tumor is a papillary renal cell carcinoma, type 1, with a Fuhrman nuclear grade of 3 and predominant nuclear grade 2. The tumor measures 2.2 x 1.9 x 0.8 cm and is limited to the kidney. There is no evidence of vascular invasion. The TNM pathologic stage is pT1a. The report also mentions benign fibroadipose tissue with chronic inflammation in the capsule overlying the tumor and benign renal parenchyma with patchy chronic interstitial inflammation in the deep margin. Immunohistochemistry shows diffuse and strong positivity for CK7 and racemase (P5048), consistent with a papillary renal cell carcinoma. Overall, the report indicates the presence of a papillary renal cell carcinoma with certain characteristics and no involvement of lymph nodes or adrenal gland.

This pathology report describes the findings from various specimens collected from a patient with a clinical diagnosis of left renal mass with thrombus. The specimens submitted include samples from the caval wall, kidney and adrenal gland, vena cava, lymph nodes, and hernia sac. 

The diagnosis for each specimen is as follows:

1. SP: Caval wall, biopsy: Portion of vein with attached cluster of atypical cells mixed with fibrous tissue in the lumen, favor reactive.

2. SP: Kidney and adrenal gland, loft, radical nephrectomy: Renal cell carcinoma, unclassified, with papillary features and high nuclear grade. The tumor has invaded the renal cortex, extending into Gerota's fascia, renal pelvis, and renal fat. There is also invasion of the renal vein and extensive vascular invasion.

3. SP: Vena cava, additional, biopsy: Portion of vein with detached atypical cells mixed with fibrous tissue in the lumen, favor reactive. No definite tumor seen.

4. SP: Lymph nodes, left perihilar, resection: There are metastatic nodes that show extracapsular extension. The largest metastatic deposit measures 2.5cm.

5. SP: Lymph nodes, paracaval, resection: There are metastatic nodes that show extracapsular extension. The largest metastatic deposit measures 3.6cm.

6. SP: Lymph nodes, aortocaval, resection: No involvement of lymph nodes detected.

7. SP: Hernia sac, abdomen, resection: Benign mesothelium lined fibrovascular and adipose tissue consistent with hernia sac.

The report also includes comments regarding immunohistochemistry testing and interpretation, as well as information about the testing and laboratory certification.

In summary, the patient has been diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma, unclassified type, with metastasis to lymph nodes and invasion of the renal vein. The tumor has also involved the periadrenal soft tissue and abuts the capsule of the adrenal gland.

The pathology report describes the findings of a renal mass that was surgically removed. The report includes the following information:

- A frozen section biopsy of the base of the left renal tumor showed no tumor present.
- The specimen of the left renal peritumor fat showed fibroadipose tissue and no tumor.
- The specimen of the left renal tumor, which underwent a partial nephrectomy, revealed the presence of two types of renal cell carcinoma: papillary renal cell carcinoma and chromophobe renal cell carcinoma.
- The tumor had a greatest dimension of 1.8 cm for chromophobe renal cell carcinoma and 1.6 cm for papillary renal cell carcinoma.
- The tumor was multifocal and limited to the kidney.
- There was tumor necrosis present.
- The histologic grade was G2 for papillary renal cell carcinoma, while chromophobe renal cell carcinoma did not have an applicable grade.
- The tumor was limited to the kidney and did not invade the margins (closest margin was 1 mm from the capsular margin for papillary renal cell carcinoma and 1 mm from the renal parenchymal margin for chromophobe renal cell carcinoma).
- Lymph-vascular invasion was not identified.
- The stage of chromophobe renal cell carcinoma was pT1,pNX,pMX, and the stage of papillary renal cell carcinoma was pT1,pNX,pMX.
- Immunohistochemistry tests were performed and supported the diagnosis of chromophobe RCC being positive for CK7 and negative for CD15, vimentin, and 504s; papillary RCC was positive for 504s.

Overall, the pathology report confirms the presence of both papillary and chromophobe renal cell carcinomas in the left renal tumor.

Summary:

A. Soft tissue - benign adipose tissue with no neoplastic process identified.
B. Kidney (posterior margin) - no tumor identified.
C. Kidney (right, partial nephrectomy) - renal cell carcinoma, papillary subtype with a tumor size of 4.0 cm. The tumor is confined to the kidney without lymphovascular invasion or sarcomatoid features. The surgical margins are negative for tumor. No lymph nodes were submitted for evaluation.

The renal neoplasm shows a predominantly papillary architecture with some areas of clear cell change. The overall appearance is consistent with papillary renal cell carcinoma.

Additional specimens include peritumor fat, posterior margin #1, and the right renal tumor (partly fragmented partial nephrectomy specimen).

Intra-operative consultation confirmed no tumor on frozen section for posterior margin #1.

The pathology report describes a radical nephrectomy specimen, which includes the left kidney, proximal ureter, perinephric soft tissue, and adrenal gland. The main finding is a 2.7 cm papillary renal cell carcinoma (RCC) located in the lower portion of the upper pole of the kidney. The tumor does not penetrate the renal capsule and there is no involvement of the adrenal gland. The remaining kidney shows scattered foci of interstitial chronic inflammation and mild arteriolosclerosis. The immunoperoxidase stains confirm the renal origin of the tumor. The report also includes information about the macroscopic and microscopic extent of the tumor, histologic type (papillary), histologic grade (Purhman nuclear grade 2), and absence of venous and adrenal involvement.

The pathology report confirms the presence of renal cell carcinoma - Papilary type 2, with no lymph nodes identified in the sample. The tumor has a nuclear grade of Wut and measures 38 cm in diameter. It involves the renal fat but does not invade the renal vein. The surgical margins are free of tumor, and there is no involvement of the adrenal gland or lymph nodes. The staging indicates that the tumor invades the perinephric tissues but not beyond Gerola's fascia. Additionally, a previous excision site is noted on the kidney. The report includes descriptions of additional specimens received for frozen section consultation, including a fragment of fibroadipose tissue with fat necrosis and multiple surgical staples. Overall, the report suggests that the patient had previous nephrectomy and now has a recurrent renal cell carcinoma in the lymph nodes and perinephric tissues.

The pathology report indicates that there were two tumors found in the right kidney. 

Tumor #1 is described as a white soft tissue fragment with a tan homogeneous cut surface. It is diagnosed as renal cell carcinoma with features of papillary RCC type 1 with solid and clear cell areas. 

Tumor #2 is described as a soft tissue fragment with a white/tan, variegated cut surface. Attached normal parenchyma is seen. It is diagnosed as multiple foci of renal cell carcinoma with features of papillary RCC type 1 with solid areas. 

A portion of both tumors were sent for electron microscopy, and the remainder was sent for further processing. The case will be discussed with a specialist, and a supplemental report may be provided if necessary.

The pathology report describes a left renal mass that was surgically removed. Two specimens were received for analysis: para-aortic lymph nodes and the left kidney with the adrenal gland.

The para-aortic lymph nodes were described as multiple soft yellow-tan fragments. The lymph nodes were sectioned, revealing soft to firm lymph nodes measuring up to 2.2 cm in size. These lymph nodes were entirely submitted for examination and showed no evidence of tumor.

The left kidney specimen included the kidney, surrounding perinephric fat, and the attached ureter. The kidney weighed 1,080 grams and measured 22 x 18 x 9.5 cm. The ureter appeared normal with a tan-pink smooth mucosal lining. The kidney was bisected, revealing a 7.5 cm ill-defined midpole mass located near the superior pole capsule. The mass also involved 90% of the renal pelvis. Representative sections of the mass and surrounding tissues were submitted for examination.

The final diagnosis for the para-aortic lymph nodes was no tumor seen. In the left kidney, a papillary renal cell carcinoma (type 2) measuring 7.5 cm was identified. No definitive extrarenal extension was observed, and the vascular and ureteral margins were free of tumor. The pathological staging was determined as pT2N0Mx.
