Other findings in the report include cataractous lenses, atrophic changes in the ciliary muscles, and degenerative changes in the retinal tissue overlying the tumor.

The pathology report describes a left eye enucleation surgery for an 18mm uveal melanoma, composed mainly of pigmented epithelioid cells with severe cyto/nuclear atypia. The tumor has infiltrated all of the thickness of the sclera but has no extra-scleral extension. There is one intra-scleral endovascular tumor embolism present. The optic nerve, ciliary body, and anterior chamber are free of tumor. Samples have been frozen for genetic studies and the entire piece has been fixed and included.

The pathology report is describing a choroidal melanoma with mixed epithelioid and fusiform cells and low mitotic index. The tumor measures 13 mm and has infiltrated the choroid and sclera up to two thirds of its thickness. There is also a neoplastic embolus in the orbital fat. However, the optic nerve, ciliary processes, and meningeal sheaths are free of the tumor. There was a discrepancy between the pathology report and the TCGA case quality control form, but the reason for the discrepancy is not clearly stated. The form was signed by the reviewing pathologist and the principal investigator.

The report describes a pathology examination of a right eye with a tumor involving the ciliary body and the choroid. The diagnosis is "Sik Cseshap a) Qeavirn g Lgl." The report notes minimal scleral invasion and no extracurricular extension. Vortex veins and optic nerve are negative for the tumor. Mitoses are low, and a PAS stain was performed. The report includes a detailed gross description of the eye and the tumor. No clinical history is given.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a malignant melanoma, predominantly spindle cell type in their right eye, which was removed through enucleation. The tumor was found to involve the choroid with focal invasion into the sclera but was uninvolved in the optic nerve, extra-scleral tissues, ciliary body, and lens. Margins were clear, and there was no evidence of primary tumor or extrascleral extension. Mitotic figures were frequent, but necrosis was absent. The report complies with the guidelines of the College of American Pathologists Protocols and the AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 7th edition, 2010, for the reporting of cancer specimens.

The pathology report describes a case of choroidal melanoma in the right eye of a patient. The tumor is made up of fusiform cells, some containing melanin pigment. It measures 14 mm and has a low mitotic index. The tumor is located close to the ciliary processes and infiltrates the superficial internal layers of the sclera, but the optic nerve, optic foramen, and meningeal sheaths are free of the tumor. Samples have been taken for cryo preservation, cytogenetic studies, and preclinical investigation.

The pathology report describes a right eye enucleation that reveals a solitary dome-shaped, pigmented choroidal mass consistent with spindle cell-type choroidal melanoma. The tumour measures 12mm in diameter and 10.5mm in height and has no extension through the sclera, optic nerve, or vortex veins. The report also notes that there are prominent vessels arising from the optic disc with closed loops present in the planes of sections, and lymphocytic infiltrate within the tumour is minimal. The MLPA analysis reveals lows of chromosome 1p, monosomy 3, normal chromosome 6, and gains in chromosome 8, placing the patient in the high-risk group.

The pathology report describes a choroidal melanoma with a mixture of spindle and epithelioid cells, pigmentation, and moderate mitoses. The tumour occupies a local area with no obvious infiltration. The lateral margins are free of tumour. A molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from the tumour cells will be performed using multiplex-ligation dependent probe amplification (MLPA), looking at chromosomes 1, 3, 6, and 8. A supplementary report indicated a loss of chromosome 1, a gain in chromosome 6p, and a gain in chromosome 8. The report notes that these molecular data require correlation with clinical and morphological data for metastatic risk assessment.

The report describes the enucleation of the right eye of a patient with a uveal melanoma. The tumor measures 13 mm and is mainly composed of fusiform cells with moderate nuclear atypias and cytoplasm loaded with melanin. The mitotic index is low. The lesion invades the ciliary body but the sclera is free, and there is no extrascleral extension. The optic nerve and meningeal sheath are also free of tumor. The diagnosis is a uveal melanoma composed of 97% fusiform cells and <3% epithelioid cells, with a tumor size of 13 mm and extension to the ciliary body.

The pathology report describes an enucleation/evisceration of a right eye from a patient with neovascular glaucoma and a large choroidal malignant tumor causing total retinal detachment and pain. The final pathologic diagnosis states that the eye contained a choroidal melanoma, iris neovascularization with partial angle closure, retinal detachment, and cataract. The report includes a synoptic report for the uveal melanoma, which indicates that the tumor was 16mm in the gross size and 13mm from the slide, with a solid growth pattern, poorly formed vascular mimicry patterns present, and invasion of Bruch's membrane, among other features. The histopathologic type was identified as epithelioid cell melanoma with a pG of p63. The tumor margins did not contain melanoma, and extrascleral extension was negative. The report includes additional findings and comments, including the use of PAS staining to evaluate for vascular mimicry patterns and negative cytokeratin AE1/3 result ruling out carcinoma/metastasis and strongly positive HMB-45 and melanA consistent with melanoma.

The pathology report describes a case of uveal melanoma, a pigmented tumor located in the eye. The tumor is mainly composed of epithelioid cells, with severe cell atypia and moderate mitotic activity. It measures 15x15 mm and has focal infiltration of the inner third of the sclera but does not extend beyond it. The ciliary body, optic nerve, and optic nerve cut end are free of tumor. Tissue specimens have been taken for genetic studies and cryopreservation before fixation.

The pathology report is for tissue taken from the left orbit of an individual with a history of uveal melanoma. The morphology of the tumor is consistent with recurrent melanoma with spindled B morphology. The pathologic stage is NA (recurrence). Biomarker testing was performed on local tumor block A4. The report does not provide any information on treatment or further management.

The pathology report indicates the enucleation of the right eye due to the presence of an uveal melanoma composed of mainly fusiform cells. The tumor measures 20 mm in size and partially invades the ciliary body without infiltration of the iris. Furthermore, it infiltrates the sclera and presents an extrascleral nodule of 6 mm. The optic nerve in its entire course, cut end, and meningeal sheaths are free of tumor. The report recommends further cryopreservation and genetic studies on the tumor specimen.

The pathology report describes the enucleation of the right eye due to a uveal melanoma, which is mainly composed of fusiform cells and few epithelioid cells with low mitotic activity. The tumor is located at a distance from the optic nerve, with a focal infiltration of the inner third of the sclera without extra-scleral extension. The ciliary body, optic nerve, and meningeal sheaths are free of the tumor. The diagnosis on the initial pathology report shows a discrepancy with the case quality control form, as the frozen sample used for TCGA reflects a section of the tumor where the epithelioid part is predominant. There is no mention of treatment or further recommendations in the report.

The report describes a case of uveal melanoma in the left eye with a tumor size of 12x7 mm composed of fusiform and epithelioid cells. There is low mitotic index, no necrosis, and no extrascleral extension. Tumor invasion is limited to the ciliary body and the sclera, optic nerve, meningeal sheath, and cut end of the optic nerve are free of tumor. A discrepancy form was completed due to a difference in the percentage of spindle cells and epithelioid cells between the initial pathology report and the TCGA Case Quality Control Form. The reviewing pathologist or biorepository director confirmed the information provided was accurate and had been quality controlled. The attending pathologist or department chairman was informed of the discrepancy in diagnoses.

The pathology report describes an enucleation (surgical removal) of the right eye due to a uveal melanoma. The tumor is composed mainly of epithelioid cells with severe atypias. The pigmented load is mild and the mitotic activity is low. The tumor has an extension on the inner part of the sclera but does not extend outside the sclera. The optic nerve and anterior chamber are free of tumor. The size of the tumor is 17 mm.

The pathology report describes a case of choroidal melanoma of mixed cell type in a patient with a nevus. The tumor size was 15mm by 4.7mm, with minimal mitotic activity and no tumor necrosis. There is a breach in Bruch's membrane and minimal tumor extension into the sclera. Molecular genetic analysis showed loss of chromosome 1p, monosomy 3, partial losses of chromosome 6, and gains in chromosome 8q, which require correlation with the clinical and morphological data for metastatic risk assessment. The report also notes no tumor cells seen at the resection margins, and no significant abnormality in the cornea, iris, or anterior chamber angles.

The pathology report describes a case of a left choroidal melanoma causing a visual field defect in a patient. The report notes a large, amelanotic ciliochoroidal melanoma of mixed cell type with minimal lymphocytic infiltrate and no tumor necrosis. Focal tumor extension into the sclera is noted, but there is no ring pattern of spread or involvement of anterior chamber angle noted. Molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from the tumor cells is recommended, and a supplementary report will be provided in due course. The report also notes the displacement of the lens, degeneration of the retina adjacent to the tumor, and a breach in Bruch's membrane in the sections examined.

The pathology report describes a local resection specimen of a choroidal melanoma in the right eye with attached normal choroid and sclera. The tumour is partially pigmented and consists mostly of spindle cells, with small foci of epithelioid cells. The melanoma cells are positive for Melank, HSP-27, and partially positive for CD10. The number of mitoses is moderately high, and the microvasculature of the melanoma is prominent. There is tumour extension into the sclera and close to the scleral resection margin at the base of the tumour, but the lateral resection margins are free of tumour. Molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from the tumour cells will be performed, and a supplementary report will follow. The molecular data require correlation with the clinical and morphological data for metastatic risk assessment.

The pathology report describes an enucleation specimen from a patient's left eye, which was found to have a choroidal melanoma with fusiform cells. The tumor measures 13mm at the basis with 7mm thickness and is implanted at the posterior pole without involvement of the sclera or extrascleral extension. The ciliary processes, optic foramen, and optic nerve are all free from the tumor. The specimen has been prepared for cryo preservation and xenografts.

The pathology report describes the enucleation specimen of the right eye measuring 25 mm in diameter with a segment of optic nerve of 7 mm of length. A pigmented tumor measuring 20 mm is present in the posterior chamber. The specimen has been included entirely after fixation in 11 blocks. Microscopy results show the presence of a mixed-type (epithelioid and fusiform) choroidal melanoma with low mitotic activity. The tumor has infiltrated the internal third of the sclera but has not extended beyond it. The optic foramen, optic nerve and its cut end are free of tumor. Samples have been taken for cytogenetic studies. The report notes a discrepancy between the pathology report and the provided case quality control form for TCGA, specifically regarding the distribution of epithelioid and spindle cells in the tumor. Potential reasons for the discrepancy are discussed, including the sectioning of frozen samples and differences in interpretation.

The pathology report describes a left eye enucleation due to uveal melanoma composed mainly of epithelioid cells with severe nuclear atypia and low mitotic index. The tumor measures 17mm and infiltrates the internal half part of the sclera without extrascleral extension. However, the optic nerve on its entire course, cut end, and meningeal sheets are free of tumor. No intra-vascular tumor embolisms were found. Samples were frozen for genetic studies and the piece has been fixed and included entirely.

The pathology report describes a left choroidal melanoma, which is a type of eye cancer. The tumor is large and partially pigmented with a mixed cell type, with the epithelioid component amounting to approximately 25%. The tumor has infiltrated into the sclera and vortex vein but has not extended through the optic nerve. There is moderate lymphocytic infiltration within the tumor, with no tumor necrosis observed. The report also notes oedema of basal epithelial cells, focal pigmented iris epithelium adherent to the anterior surface of the lens, and extensive retinal detachment. Molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from the tumor cells will be performed in a supplementary report.

The pathology report describes a left choroidal melanoma with probable focal underlying extrascleral extension. The tumor consists predominantly of spindle cells, expresses Melan-A and HSP 27 (score 2), has approximately 7 mitotic figures in 40 high power fields, and has focally present closed loops. The lymphocytic infiltrate within the tumor is minimal, and scattered macrophages are present. The tumor appears breached in the sections examined but has no extension through optic nerve or vortex veins. The completeness of excision may not be guaranteed as the tumor infiltrates through the sclera, emerging on the scleral surface and loosely attached episcleral tissue. There is no necrosis. The diagnosis is left choroidal melanoma of predominantly spindle cell type with extrascleral infiltration.

The pathology report describes a choroidal melanoma in the patient's eye, measuring 19 by 18 mm in size. The tumor mainly consists of epithelioid cells (97%) and has invaded the sclera with an extrascleral extension. The report notes the presence of tumor embolus and cells around the nerve ending but no tumor extension to the iris or ciliary body. There is an associated retinal detachment, but the optic nerve, meningeal sheaths, and the cut end of the optic nerve are free from tumor invasion. Sample tissue has been cryopreserved.

The pathology report describes a diagnosis of choroidal melanoma in the right eye, with spindle type 8. The tumor is 11 mm at the base and shows superficial scleral invasion. Vortex vein invasion is not identified, and the optic nerve is uninvolved. The tumor shows mitotic activity at two per 10 high power fields. Further details on the tumor's appearance and gross description are also provided, along with clinical history and SNOMED codes. A comment notes that the tumor is amelanotic and shows focal complex vortex veins by PAS. The report's accuracy and performance have not been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration.

The pathology report describes a case of a 16.24 x 10.81 x 14.79mm choroidal melanoma in the right eye of a patient who presented with blurred vision, visual field defect, and pain for six months. The tumor consists predominantly of spindle cells with approximately 4 mitoses per 40 high power fields and focally present closed loops. The lymphocytic infiltrate within the tumor is minimal, and tumor necrosis is not observed. The report also notes that the tumor has not extended to the optic nerve or vortex veins. The supplementary report confirms that the tumor cells express Melan-A and HSP 27 (score 2). Molecular genetic analysis using MLPA reveals borderline losses of chromosome 3 and gains in chromosome 6p, but the chromosome 1p and 8 are normal. The report concludes that the pathology is consistent with a spindle cell choroidal melanoma.

The pathology report describes a choroidal melanoma in the left eye of a patient, including the dimensions and location of the tumor. Histopathological analysis shows a mixture of cells, both epithelioid and spindle, with invasion of the inferomedial vortex vein. There is also evidence of perivascular and intravascular infiltration of the sclera in the same area. The report includes information about the tumor's lack of pigmentation, presence of retinal invasion at the apex, and high number of mitoses. The optic nerve is tumor-free, and the remaining vortex veins are clear. Molecular genetic analysis using multiplex-ligation dependent probe amplification (MLPA) will be performed and a supplementary report will be provided when complete.

The pathology report describes a diagnosis of choroidal melanoma in the right globe of the eye, with a mixed spindled and epithelioid cell type. The tumor is centered on the choroid and measures 18 x 15 mm with a 1 cm height. Testing for biomarkers was done on a tumor block from the primary tumor. The report also includes information on the stage of the tumor, which is pT3 with no regional lymph node involvement or distant metastases. No clinical history is provided.

The report describes the findings of a pathology analysis of a left globe enucleation. A solitary pigmented choroidal mass that is likely melanoma is observed on intraocular analysis. Microscopy confirms a ciliochoroidal melanoma of predominantly spindle cell type, with closed loops and minimal lymphocytic infiltrate. The report notes that there is no tumor extension through the sclera, optic nerve, or vortex veins examined and imaging techniques will assess Melan-A and HSP 27 expression and molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from the tumor cells will be performed. After further examination, the genetic analysis report states a loss in chromosome 3.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a malignant melanoma in the choroid region of their right eye, which was removed through enucleation. The tumor was a spindle cell melanoma of pG1 grade and showed moderate pigmentation, while there was no evidence of vascular invasion or Bruch's membrane invasion. FISH analysis showed gains in chromosome 3 and of CMEC. The report concludes that there was no melanoma at the margins and no evidence of scleral involvement. Retinal detachment was positive, and drusen were present.

The pathology report describes a diagnosis of choroidal melanoma, predominantly spindled type, with nearly full thickness invasion of the sclera and no evidence of extraocular extension or vortex vein invasion. The tumor is positive for pan-melanoma markers and negative for synaptophrysin, consistent with the diagnosis of melanoma. The gross description states that the tumor is loosely attached to the sclera and covered by a loosely adherent retina. The clinical history indicates that this is a right eye case and the SNOMED codes used are T-AAQ0O and M-87203.

The pathology report describes the enucleation of a right eye with the presence of a choroidal melanoma measuring 16mm by 12mm, made up mostly of medium or large epithelioid cells with irregular nuclei and a few mitotic figures. The tumor is partially cystic and protrudes into the vitreous cavity, infiltrating less than one third of the thickness of the sclera and staying distant from the ciliary body, iris, anterior chamber, and the optic nerve on its entire course. Cryopreservation and cytogenetic studies have been performed on the samples. The diagnosis is choroidal melanoma with no extrascleral extension.

The pathology report describes a case of malignant ciliochoroidal melanoma of the left eye, with mixed cell type and intrascleral involvement. The tumor size was 11.5 mm in basal diameter and 8.1 mm in height, with no melanoma at margins. Additional findings included a high mitotic rate, presence of extravascular matrix pattern, mild pigmentation, and infiltration of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. The patient had undergone enucleation, and the specimen was submitted in various sections for evaluation. There were no reported distant metastases, and regional lymph nodes could not be assessed. A cataract was also noted. DNA extraction was pending as an additional procedure. The clinical diagnosis was choroidal melanoma.

The pathology report describes a melanoma with fusiform cells that measures 18 by 12 mm in the left eye that required enucleation. The tumor infiltrates the internal layers of the sclera but has no extraocular infiltration. It also infiltrates the posterior part of the ciliary body but stays outside the iris, the irido corneal angle, and the anterior chamber. The intraocular emergence of the optic nerve is free on its entire course, including the prelaminar part, optic foramen, post-laminar part, meningeal sheaths, and posterior cut end. Cryopreservation samples have been taken for future use.

The pathology report describes a case of uveal melanoma in the left eye that has been enucleated. The tumor is composed of large sheets of epithelioid cells with abundant cytoplasm and a large nucleus with prominent nucleolus. There are 5 mitotic features per 10 high power fields. The tumor size is 17 mm and there is focal extension to the ciliary body but without extrascleral extension. There is also tumor infiltration of the 1/3 inner part of the sclera. The optic nerve and meningeal sheaths are free of tumor.

The pathology report describes an enucleation of the left eye due to the presence of a uveal melanoma composed of epithelioid cells measuring 16 mm in size. The tumor has infiltrated the ciliary body and sclera and has formed a 3 mm focal extra-scleral tumor nodule. Mitotic activity is moderate with 4 mitoses per 10 HPF and about 60% of cells are pigmented with melanin. However, the optic nerve on its entire course and meningeal sheaths are free of the tumor.

This is a pathology report for a specimen of the right eye's enucleation, which reveals a choroidal melanoma that is 14 mm in diameter and of spindled type. The tumor shows superficial scleral invasion, but no optic nerve invasion or extraocular extension. The report mentions mitotic activity, and a review of the internal ocular structures has been recommended. The vortex vein is negative for the tumor. The report is based on microscopic examination and is not formally approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

The pathology report describes a surgical pathology report for a patient with melanoma in the left eye. The final diagnosis is malignant melanoma with ciliary body involvement but no extrascleral extension. The report also includes a synoptic report which provides details about the tumor and its severity, including the involvement of different parts of the eye. Additionally, the report notes that there is no evidence of vascular invasion or hemorrhage. The report includes information about the mitotic rate and Ki-67 marker, as well as the tumor size category and primary tumor stage. The report concludes with a brief description of the specimen received for examination.

The pathology report describes a specimen labeled "Right Globe" consisting of a mostly amelanotic mass arising from the ciliary body and choroid. The mass extends posterior to the equator, with no gross evidence of extrascleral extension. The tumor measures 15 mm in diameter and is 8 mm thick. Histological examination reveals a cillochoroidal malignant melanoma, mixed cell type with invasion of peripheral anterior chamber and trabecular meshwork. There is also a partial retinal detachment and a cataract. There is no evidence of extrascleral extension in the available sections. The report does not mention any evidence of metastasis.

This is a pathology report for a patient who underwent enucleation of their right eye due to an endo-ocular tumor. The tumor was found to be a uveal melanoma composed of a mix of epithelioid (50%) and fusiform cells (50%). The tumor measured 15 mm in diameter and invaded partially into the ciliary body but did not invade the sclera or extend beyond. The optic nerve, including the cut end and meningeal sheaths, were free of the tumor. The diagnosis from the pathology report was inconsistent with the information provided on the Case Quality Control Form completed for the submitted case. The discrepancy was due to a section of the tumor where the epithelioid part was predominant.

The pathology report describes a pigmented choroidal melanoma of mixed cell type in a right intact globe, which was enucleated. The tumour measures 2mm in height and 7mm in size and demonstrates both epithelioid and spindle cells, with a dominance of the latter cell type. The melanoma cells are immunoreactive for MelanA, CD117, and HSP-27, with an approximate number of 7 mitoses per 40 high power fields. There is a large accompanying exudative retinal detachment with haemorrhage, and the retina overlaying the tumour is atrophic with degenerative changes. The molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from the tumour cells will be performed to assess the status of chromosomes 2, 3, 6, and 8, and a supplementary report will follow. The supplementary report indicates that the status of chromosome 3 in the tumour cells is normal.

The pathology report describes a choroidal melanoma in the right eye that was enucleated. The tumor measures 15 by 12 mm and is located at the periphery of the eyeball, close to the intraocular emergence of the optic nerve. The tumor superficially infiltrates the sclera but does not extend beyond it, and is distant from the ciliary body, iris, and anterior chamber. Samples have been preserved for cryopreservation. The diagnosis is choroidal melanoma with fusiform cells.

The pathology report indicates that a left eye enucleation was performed due to the presence of an uveal melanoma comprised of predominantly epithelioid cells (80%), with a low mitotic index and an average tumor size of 19 mm. The tumor invaded the periphery of the iris and ciliary body but did not involve the sclera or extrascleral tissues. The optic nerve and meningeal sheets were free of tumor on their entire course and cut end. The conclusion confirms the diagnosis of uveal melanoma of the left eye, with no discrepancies between the initial pathology report and TCGA case quality control form.

The pathology report describes an intact left eye with a pigmented tumor confirmed as a choroidal melanoma of mixed cell type, measuring 6mm in size and 9mm in height, with focal early scleral invasion but no tumor extension through optic nerve or vortex. The report also notes abnormalities in the ciliary body and retina and plans to assess immunohistochemistry for MelanA and HSP 27 and perform molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from the tumor cells. The supplementary report showed MLPA analysis demonstrating normal chromosome 1, essentially normal chromosome 3 with borderline losses, gains in chromosome 6, and normal chromosome 8. These results require correlation with the clinical and morphological data for metastatic risk.

The pathology report describes a case of left choroidal melanoma of mixed cell type with focal scleral infiltration. The tumor is partially pigmented and has a size of 17mm x 7mm. The number of mitosis is small with approximately 2/40 high power fields. The microvasculature of the tumor is prominent, and there are no closed loops in the planes of sections. The lymphocytic infiltrate within the tumor is minimal, and tumor necrosis is not seen. The tumor does not extend through optic nerve or vortex veins but focally infiltrates adjacent sclera along a vascular channel. The cornea shows no significant abnormality, the iris shows no significant abnormality, but the ciliary body appears atrophic with nylinisation of ciliary processes. Focal serous retinal detachment is seen away from the tumor.

The pathology report describes a left eye enucleation due to the presence of a 12mm choroidal melanoma. The tumor is composed mostly of non-pigmented, fusiform cells organized in criss-crossing bundles, with some atypical ovoid nuclei showing few mitotic figures. The tumor infiltrates the whole thickness of the sclera with extrascleral extension, but is distant from the emergence of the optic nerve and ciliary processes. There are tumor cells around the extra-scleral vessels without visible neoplastic embolus in the lymphatic channels. The mitotic index is low and the optic nerve and meningeal sheaths are free. The specimen has been preserved for genomic profiling.

The pathology report describes the enucleation of the right eye and identifies a Uveal melanoma composed of fusiform cells (70%) and epithelioid cells (30%) with low mitotic index and mild pigmentation load. The tumor infilterates the 1/3 inner part of the sclera without extrascleral extension. The cut end of the optic nerve and other parts free of tumor are mentioned. The report also includes a discrepancy form, indicating a difference in diagnosis percentages between the initial pathology report (70% spindle cells) and the TCGA Case Quality Control Form (1-30% spindle cells). The reason for the discrepancy is attributed to the different sections of the frozen sample used for analysis. The report is signed by the reviewing pathologist or biorepository director and the principal investigator.

The pathology report describes a case of melanoma of the choroid in the left eye, originating at the ciliary processes. The size of the tumor is determined to be 12 mm and the tumor infiltrates the thickness of the choroid but does not infiltrate the sclera. The optic nerve on its entire course, including the cut end, is free of tumor. The report mentions that the tumor is nearly only made with fusiform cells organized in short little bundles, separated by conjunctival vascular septum. Moderate nuclear atypia, ovoid nuclei with a small nucleolus, and a few mitotic figures are also observed. Some of the cells are pigmented, and there is no visible endolymphatic embolus. Various samples have been preserved for cryopreservation and cytogenetic studies.

The pathology report describes the left eye enucleation of a person with uveal melanoma, a malignant tumor in the choroid region of the eye. The tumor is 13 mm wide and invades the majority of the sclera in a perivascular pattern, but no extraocular tumor is identified. The ciliary body is uninvolved, and the optic nerve and vortex veins are free of tumor. The clinical history confirms the diagnosis of uveal melanoma. No further information is provided.

The pathology report describes the results of a resection of a choroidal melanoma in the patient's right eye. The tumor is of the epithelioid cell type and arises from the ciliary muscle and body, bilobed, and extends posteriorly into the adjacent choroid. The tumor shows a small area of necrosis, and there is no evidence of scleral invasion or extraocular growth. The examined vortex veins are free of the tumor. The molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from tumor cells was performed to look for any abnormalities, and the results demonstrate monosomy 3 and gains in chromosome 8. The report suggests that further investigations and genetic testing are needed to determine the patient's prognosis.

The pathology report describes a choroidal melanoma of mixed cell type in the left eye, with a tumor size of 16.8mm diameter. The tumor is predominantly composed of epithelioid cells with mild lymphocytic infiltration and a low mitotic frequency of 2/40 high power fields. The tumor does not show necrosis, closed loops, or invasive spread to the optic nerve or vortex veins. The iris and cornea show no significant abnormality, while the retina overlying the tumor is slightly atrophic with peripheral cystoid degeneration. HSP 27 positivity is noted, and clear margins are achieved. The prognosis is reported as prognostic 97012.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a choroidal melanoma with a spindle type, measuring 12 base x 8 mm height, in the right globe. Scleral invasion is present in a perivascular pattern and mitoses are identified at 3 per 10 high power fields. Extraocular extension is not identified, and vortex veins and optic nerve are negative for the tumor. The gross description states that the intact right globe has an unremarkable sclera and clear anterior chamber, with a shadow present 10 mm from the limbus and 6 mm from the optic nerve. The report suggests no aspiration testing was performed on the right eye. The clinical history points to a presumed uveal melanoma.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a choroidal melanoma, a type of eye cancer, in the right eye. The tumor is mostly made up of fusiform cells, containing melanin pigment. The mitotic index is comparatively low with only five mitosis out of ten high magnification fields. The tumor is found to be infiltrating the internal third of the sclera and the intraocular emergence of the optic nerve, but the optic foramen, post-laminar section, cut end, meningeal sheaths, iris, ciliary body, and anterior chamber are free of tumor. The size of the lesion is reported as 1mm.

The pathology report describes a left globe enucleation (removal of the eye) due to a pigmented choroidal mass suspicious for ciliary body involvement. The tumor was found to be a choroidal melanoma with a mix of epithelioid and spindle cells and a dominant epithelioid cell type. The melanoma cells were heavily pigmented, moderately mitotic, and had a prominent microvasculature. The report also mentions molecular genetic analysis of the tumor DNA using MLPA. The final diagnosis was choroidal melanoma of epithelioid cell type.

The pathology report describes the results of an enucleation of the right eye, which revealed a pigmented tumor that measured 18x15mm. Microscopic analysis indicated the tumor was an uveal melanoma, made up predominantly of fusiform cells (60%) with some large cells showing strong cytonuclear atypia. Melanin was also present in some tumor cells. The mitotic activity was low, and there was no necrosis or scleral extension. The optic nerve was free of tumor on its entire course. The conclusion is a diagnosis of uveal melanoma of the right eye, with fusiform cells predominant (60%) and epithelioid cells (40%).

The pathology report describes a case of uveal melanoma in the right eye. The tumor is 10mm in size and composed of fusiform cells with ovoid nucleus. There are sparse mitotic features but no necrosis or microcalcifications. The tumor invades the inner part of the sclera but does not extend beyond it. The anterior chamber and the optic nerve are free of tumor. Enucleation of the eye has been done.

The pathology report indicates that the patient has a choroidal melanoma in the right eye, with mixed epithelioid and spindled features and 18 mm base. The tumor has extraocular extension, invades sclera, and extends to subconjunctival surface; however, optic nerve and vortex veins are negative for tumor. The specimen for the right eye was sent out for further diagnostic testing. Biomarker testing was done on the primary tumor. The clinical history of the patient includes right eye uveal melanoma.

The pathology report describes a case of choroidal melanoma in the right eye, which was enucleated. The tumor is predominantly composed of spindle cells and shows Melan-A and HSP 27 expression. Mitotic frequency is low, and lymphocytic infiltration and tumor necrosis are not observed. The tumor size and thickness are 22 mm and 10 mm, respectively. The examination of the tumor's DNA reveals normal chromosomes 1p, 6 and 8, and disomy 3, indicating a low risk for metastatic development. Oedema is observed in the basal cell layers of the cornea, while the anterior chamber shows normal characteristics. Ciliary body atrophy and subcapsular degenerative changes in the lens are noted, while the retina overlying the tumor appears lightly atrophic.

The pathology report describes a case of choroidal melanoma with fusiform cells that infiltrated the internal third of the sclera and contained melanin pigment. The mitotic index was low with only 1 mitosis out of 10 high 400 magnification fields. The tumor was 15mm in size and distant from the internal emergence of the optic nerve, the optic foramen, the pre and post laminar section, the cut end, and the meningeal sheaths. The iris, ciliary body, and anterior chamber were free of tumor. Samples were taken for cryopreservation.

The patient had a suspected choroidal melanoma in the left eye, measuring 16mm LBD x 12mm in height. The tumor was pigmented and consisted of a mixture of cells, both epithelioid and spindle cells. The melanoma cells were immunoreactive for MelanA and HSP-27 (score 2), and had a high mitotic frequency of approximately 12/40 high power fields. The lymphocytic infiltrate within the tumor was minimal, and macrophages were scattered throughout the tumor in moderate density. There was no evidence of scleral invasion or extraocular growth. The diagnosis was a choroid melanoma of mixed cell type with large diameter and thickness. Molecular genetic examination using MLPA looking at chromosomes 1, 3, 6 and 8 was planned. A supplementary report was provided later, stating that the DNA concentration was high and of good quality, and the MLPA reaction was run at least twice on differing occasions, resulting in similar results.

The pathology report describes a case of enucleation surgery for a melanoma tumor in the posterior pole of the patient's right eye. The tumor is composed of fusiform cells with ovale nucleus and exhibits mitosis with no necrosis or microcalcification. The tumor's size is 16mm with infiltration of the ciliary body and internal third of the sclera. The iris, anterior chamber, optic nerve, and meningeal sheaths are free of the tumor. Samples were taken for cryopreservation and cytogenetic studies.

The patient had a malignant melanoma in their left eye which was predominantly spindle cell type mixed with other cells. A biopsy of the vortex vein in the eye showed no presence of malignant melanoma. Cytogenetic testing showed an abnormal clone of cells with a translocation between chromosomes 3 and 6, which is rare in uveal melanomas and its significance is unknown. The tumor was mostly located in the inferior aspect of the posterior chamber and was a brown-black, partially fragmented mass measuring 1.5 cm in diameter and 1.4 cm in height. The ciliary body was not affected, and there was no scleral or extrascleral extension. The optic nerve was not observed on the sections taken. The report was issued by a surgical pathology laboratory.

The pathology report describes an uveal melanoma measuring 18mm in diameter composed of epithelioid and fusiform cells, with severe cell atypias and low mitotic activity. The tumor infiltrates the ciliary body and inner part of the sclera, on a thickness of about 1mm, without extra-scleral extension. The optic nerve and meningeal sheaths are free of tumor. There is a discrepancy between the initial pathology report and the TCGA Case Quality Control Form regarding the percentages of spindle and epithelioid cells, likely due to differences in the analyzed sections. The report also includes a form for resolution of the discrepancy.

The pathology report describes an enucleated eye with a non-pigmented choroidal melanoma, with an area of necrosis and total retinal detachment. The melanoma consists predominantly of spindle cells with numerous balloon cells and the number of mitoses is approximately 4/40 high power fields. The microvasculature of the melanoma is prominent with occasional "vascular lakes" observed. The lymphocytic infiltrate within the tumor is minimal and macrophages are scattered throughout the tumor in a mild density. MLPA will be performed on chromosomes 2, 3, 6, and 8 for molecular genetic examination of the DNA extracted from the tumor cells, and a supplementary report will follow with the results.

The report describes a choroidal melanoma of spindle cell type in the right eye of a patient. The tumor is pigmented and partially consists of spindle cells. The melanoma cells are immunoreactive for MelanA, CD117 and HSP-27. The report also includes information on the size and location of the tumor, as well as the absence of scleral invasion or extraocular growth. The optic nerve is tumor-free. Additionally, a genetic analysis using the MLPA technique reveals alterations in chromosomes 3, 6, and 8.

The pathology report describes a case involving a patient with floaters, visual field defects, and flashes of light in the right eye. The diagnosis of choroidal melanoma is confirmed, with the tumor measuring 11.34mm in diameter and 7.6m in thickness. The tumor is predominantly composed of spindle cells with a low mitotic activity and no evidence of tumor necrosis. The report recommends an immunohistochemistry examination to assess the expression of Melan-A and HSP27 by tumor cells, as well as a molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from the tumor cells to be performed using MLPA. The supplementary report reveals borderline losses on chromosome 1, 7 borderline losses in chromosome 3, gains of chromosome 6p, and gains of chromosome 8q. These molecular data require correlation with the clinical and morphological data for metastatic risk assessment.

The pathology report shows that there is a malignant melanoma in the right eye that has invaded the ciliary body and extended into the anterior chamber. There is also scleral invasion with possible involvement of the canal of Schlemm and extraocular extension present. The report further states that the tumor has mixed spindle and epithelioid cell types with a 19 mm base and a 12 mm height. Mitotic rate is 2 per 10 hpf. The primary tumor is classified as pT3a, and there is no evidence of regional lymph node involvement or distant metastases. The report suggests that further testing will be done on the biopsy sample for additional diagnostic information. The patient's clinical history indicates uveal melanoma. Further sections of the iris and sclera will be taken for evaluation, and biomarker testing will also be conducted.

The pathology report describes a diagnosis of choroidal melanoma in the right globe of the eye, predominantly of the epithelioid type and with a base of 20mm. There is evidence of focal choroidal invasion, and the tumor surrounds the optic nerve but has not extended extraocularly. The report notes erosion of Bruch’s membrane and the presence of miloses. The globes are intact, with clear anterior and vitreous portions. The report includes SNOMED codes T-AA000 and M-87203.

The report describes a pathology analysis of a tumor present in the right eye that is a ciliochoroidal melanoma of mixed cell type. The tumor is non-pigmented and has exudative retinal detachment. The tumor cells express Melan-A and HSP 27. The number of mitosis is high, and there is a minimal lymphocytic infiltrate within the tumor. The molecular analysis of the tumor DNA using multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) technique revealed normal chromosome 1, monosomy 3, normal chromosome 8, and gains of chromosome 6q. The report suggests that the molecular data require correlation with the clinical and morphological data for metastatic risk assessment. No tumor cells are seen at the resection margins.

The pathology report describes a left eye enucleation due to a choroidal melanoma with mostly fusiform cells and localized nests of epithelioid cells. The lesion measures 9mm in size and is localized at the posterior pole, infiltrating the internal third of the sclera without extension into the meningeal sheaths or extrascleral tissue. Samples have been taken for cryopreservation and cytogenetic studies. The report also includes a discrepancy form between the initial pathology report and the TCGA (The Cancer Genome Atlas) diagnosis for the case, which indicates a variation in the percentages of spindle and epithelioid cells mentioned in the reports.

The report describes an enucleated left eye with an endo-ocular tumor measuring 18mm x 10mm which has been diagnosed as uveal melanoma of mixed type with a main component of fusiform cells and a focal component of epithelioid cells. The tumor has infiltrated the inner third of the sclera without extra-scleral extension, but the ciliary body, iris, anterior chamber, lamina cribrosa, optic nerve on its entire course, and meningeal sheaths are free of tumor. There is some discrepancy between the initial pathology report and the TCGA Case Quality Control Form, specifically regarding the percentages of spindle and epithelioid cells present in the tumor.

The pathology report describes an intact right eye with a choroidal melanoma in the posterior segment. The tumor is partially pigmented, consists of a mixture of epithelioid and spindle cells, and is approximately 15mm in size with a large accompanying exudative retinal detachment. There is some retinal invasion and mild atrophic changes in the ciliary processes. Mitoses number approximately 5/40 high power fields, with a prominent microvasculature and minimal lymphocytic infiltration. There is also a large extraocular growth of the tumor. The optic nerve is tumor-free. Molecular genetic examination will be performed to look at chromosomes.

The pathology report describes a case of left eye enucleation with the diagnosis of ciliochoroidal melanoma of mixed cell type. The tumor is shown to consist primarily of spindle cells with a minor component of epithelioid cells, with a size of 14 x 19.73 x 6.55 mm. Mitosis is reported to be approximately 4/40 high power fields, and there is no lymphocytic infiltration or tumor necrosis. Bruch's membrane appears breached in one section, but there is no tumor extension beyond the enucleation margin. Assessment of KSP27 expression and molecular genetic examination of DNA extracted from the tumor cells will be performed in a supplementary report. A MLPA was performed and the results indicate a normal chromosome 1p and disomy in chromosomes 3, 6, and 8.

The pathology report describes a case of malignant choroidal melanoma, predominantly epithelioid cell type, in the right eye. The tumor involved the choroid and did not extend into the optic nerve. The tumor was solid and measured 7.8 mm in basal diameter and 12.2 mm in height. The mitotic rate was 3 per 40 high power fields, and there was invasion of Bruch's membrane. Pigmentation was mild, and there were few macrophages and tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. The report notes the absence of melanoma at the margins and the involvement of the sclera but not the ciliary body or regional lymph nodes. There was also retinal detachment and cataract.

The pathology report describes a uveal melanoma in the right eye, composed of epithelioid and fusiform cells. The tumor measures 20mm in main line and partially invades the ciliary body, as well as the inner half part of the sclera. The iris and anterior chamber are free of tumor, and the optic nerve and meningeal sheaths are free of tumor as well. The report also includes a Pathologic Diagnosis Discrepancy Form, suggesting a discrepancy between the initial pathology report and the diagnosis provided on the Case Quality Control Form. The reason for the discrepancy is explained as the section of the frozen sample used for sending to TCGA corresponding to a section of the tumor where the epithelioid part is dominant.

The pathology report describes a choroidal melanoma with mixed epithelioid and spindled types measuring 13 mm in base. Vortex vein invasion is present and the tumor extends extraocularly in the vortex vein region. The tumor is mitotically active with 1 mitosis per 10 high power fields. The optic nerve and the choroid are negative for tumor. The specimen is an intact globe with an intact optic nerve and unremarkable sclera. The vitreous is clear and the tumor has a brown color. The diagnosis was made based on histological examination of the tissue samples. The clinical history indicates that this was a case of melanoma.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a high-grade adrenal cortical carcinoma in the patient's right adrenal gland. The tumor is localized within the gland without extension to surrounding tissue. Additionally, a biopsy of the left lobe of the liver revealed benign hepatic parenchyma with steatosis and no evidence of carcinoma. The report does not provide further information on the patient's condition or prognosis.

The pathology report describes findings from various tissue samples obtained during a surgical procedure on a patient diagnosed with adrenocortical carcinoma. The report lists lymph nodes, fibroadipose tissue, gall bladder, kidney, and liver as some of the specimens examined. The lymph nodes and fibroadipose tissue did not show any pathological diagnosis, while the gall bladder showed no pathological diagnosis but was removed during a cholecystectomy. The kidney exhibited some arteriosclerosis, and the liver exhibited mildly active steatohepatitis but no fibrosis. The primary diagnosis was angioinvasive adrenal cortical carcinoma which invaded into the vena cava but did not show evidence of direct invasion into the kidney, gall bladder, or liver, and no evidence of distant metastases into these organs. The report documents the size and weight of the tumor, as well as margin involvement and regional lymph node examination results. The pathologic staging is based on AJCC/UICC TNM, 7th Edition. The report also notes that if there is a clinical indication or suspicion of an abnormality requiring additional studies, the signing pathologist should be contacted within one month of the report being issued.

The pathology report describes a left adrenal gland biopsy taken for Conn's syndrome and genetic studies. The specimen showed a primarily trabecular adrenal tumor with a mitotic rate of less than 6 per 50 hpf and cytological atypia. The tumor is consistent with an adrenal cortical neoplasm of indeterminate malignant potential, with no definite vascular invasion. The report recommends long-term clinical follow-up. Electron microscopy showed features of aldosterone-secreting tumors but cannot predict the behavior of the adrenal cortical tumor, so reliance should be placed on the usual macroscopic and histological criteria.

The specimen is an en block resection of the kidney, adrenal gland, renal vein, and surrounding fat. The tumor is a high-grade adrenal cortical carcinoma with features of malignancy, including coagulative necrosis, dystrophic calcification, venous and sinusoidal invasion, and a tumor thrombus in the renal vein. The mitotic rate is high, and atypical mitoses are present. The tumor abuts the renal vein margin and extends into the surrounding perinephritic fat but does not invade the kidney parenchyma. The adjacent non-neoplastic adrenal gland and kidney show no histological abnormalities. The Ki-67 proliferative index is 5%. IGF-2 staining is diffuse and strongly positive, and glucocorticoid receptor staining is positive. No lymph nodes are found.

The pathology report describes a product of en-bloc resection of the left kidney, spleen, and left adrenal mass with a fibrous-capsulated mass weighing 810 g and measuring 18 x 14 x7 cm. The mass shows areas of fibrosis and necrosis, along with two cystic areas. The left kidney and spleen appear macroscopically normal. Lymph node resection shows a gray nodular structure resembling an accessory spleen. The product of right adrenal mass resection reveals adrenocortical carcinoma with a Weiss score of 8 and features such as nuclear grade, mitotic count, capsular and venous invasion, and extra-capsular extension. Immunohistochemical markers show positivity for Melan A, Inhibin, 35BHI1, ABI/ ARS, CD10, $-100 protein, and Vimentin, while Chromogranin and Synaptophisin are negative.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a right adrenalectomy and was diagnosed with adrenal cortical carcinoma. The tumor weighed 254g and measured 12 x 6 x 6.5cm. The Weiss score was 7, indicating a high likelihood of malignancy. No lymph node metastasis was detected.

The pathology report describes a sample of an adrenal gland tumor with a diameter of 12mm. The tumor is confirmed as an adrenal cortical carcinoma with areas of invasion into the extra-adrenal fat and positive Calretinin immunohistochemistry. The tumor has a high proliferative index (up to 30% in areas) and its Weiss score is high due to high nuclear grade, atypical mitoses, predominantly eosinophil cell type, and areas of microscopic invasion into the extra-adrenal fat. The report also notes that the bulk of the tumor is separated from the soft tissue resection margin by an intact capsule, while carcinoma extends to involve the soft tissue margins in a few areas. The adrenal area away from the tumor is normal.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of adrenocortical carcinoma in a patient who underwent left adrenal gland resection. The tumor is described as faintly nodular, soft, and well-circumscribed with areas of necrosis. Additional research immunostains show a proliferation rate consistent with a low-grade adrenocortical carcinoma. The report also notes that the laboratory performing the test is certified under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 and qualified to perform high complexity testing. Additional reports are pending with further sections and immunohistochemistry.

The pathology report describes the examination of three specimens: a left upper quadrant mass, segment 3 liver, and peri-peritoneal fat behind the tumor. The left upper quadrant mass is a tumorous mass near the spleen, pancreas, and kidney, measuring 100mm by 80mm by 50mm. The tumorous mass is identified as adrenal cortical carcinoma with white-yellow sections containing areas of hemorrhage and central necrosis. The segment 3 liver also contains a nodular white firm tumor measuring 20mm by 20mm. It is identified as adrenal cortical carcinoma. The peri-peritoneal fat behind the tumor does not contain any tumor deposits. Immunohistochemistry reveals positive staining for Melan-A and inhibin and negative staining for calretinin, EMA, CAMS.2, and AE1/AES. The diagnosis is adrenal cortical carcinoma in both the left upper quadrant mass and segment 3 liver, while the peri-peritoneal fat behind the tumor is negative for malignancy.

The pathology report indicates a diagnosis of adrenocortical carcinoma in the patient's left adrenal gland. The tumor measures 6.5 cm and weighs 105 grams. The capsule is invaded focally. The lymph node status is negative, and the tumor is stage 2M. The surgical procedure was a left open adrenalectomy.

The report describes a surgical excision of the right adrenal gland and kidney due to a history of an adrenal mass and Cushing's syndrome. The excised tissues weighed 255 grams and measured 9.3 x 8.2 x 6.7 cm. The adrenal gland was found to have a 9.8 cm high-grade adrenal cortical carcinoma that was adherent to, but not directly invading, the kidney and liver. Margins were negative, and the kidney did not show any lesions. The report rules out the previous diagnosis and confirms the presence of adrenal carcinoma.

The pathology report confirms the presence of a large adrenocortical carcinoma in the right adrenal gland measuring 7.2 cm with partial invasion of the renal artery. There were no lymph nodes involved and the margins were negative. The kidney was also removed but found to be unremarkable. The central portion of the tumor was notable for a cystic area lined with granular tissue and the cut surface was tan and hemorrhagic with focal areas of necrosis. The report concludes with a diagnosis of adrenocortical carcinoma and the signing pathologist's affirmation of personal examination and interpretation of all slides from the case.

The pathology report describes the results of a surgical consultation for a male patient named Koa. The report includes descriptions of three specimens submitted for analysis: an accessory spleen, a splenectomy specimen, and a left adrenalectomy, nephrectomy, splenectomy, and distal pancreatectomy specimen. The report notes that the first two specimens did not show any pathological diagnosis, while the third specimen revealed an invasive adrenal cortical carcinoma measuring 12 cm and weighing 448 grams. The tumor displayed clear and compact cells with marked nuclear pleomorphism, numerous mitoses, and extensive geographic necrosis, with ful thickness invasion of the capsule and peritumoral fat. Two lymph nodes were identified but showed no signs of involvement. The report also noted no significant pathologic alterations in the kidney or pancreas.

The pathology report identifies a case of adrenocortical carcinoma found in the left adrenal gland. The tumor is fully encapsulated and weighs 447 grams, with evidence of necrosis and high mitotic activity. The tumor has a close but negative surgical margin and focal extra-adrenal extension. Lymph nodes are negative for carcinoma. Additional tissue samples, including a lymph node packer and left suprarenal soft tissue, are negative for carcinoma. Immunohistochemistry supports the diagnosis of adrenocortical carcinoma.

The pathology report describes a 9.0 cm adrenal mass that is an adrenocortical neoplasm of uncertain malignant potential. The tumor is primarily confined to the adrenal gland and the surgical margins of resection did not show the presence of tumor. The tumor has some characteristics that suggest malignancy, such as the presence of mitotic figures and an elevated KI-67 index, but it does not invade into the periadrenal soft tissue, and no necrosis is present. The modified Weiss criteria score the tumor with a score of 4, which supports the diagnosis of uncertain malignant potential. A gross description of the tumor is also provided, showing areas of hemorrhage and possible necrosis. The report notes that there is a discrepancy between the initial pathology report and the Case Quality Control Form completed for the case, but it does not provide details about the discrepancy.

The pathology report describes a tumor removed during a right adrenalectomy. The tumor weighed 208g and had a size of 9.3 x 8.7 x 5.5cm. The diagnosis was adrenal cortical carcinoma with a Weiss score of 6. The report also noted chronic cholecystitis and cholelithiasis.

The pathology report analyzed slides from a study comparing CGH on benign and malignant adrenal cortical tumors. The pathologist confirmed the diagnosis of adrenal cortical carcinoma in a tumor that weighed 085 grams and measured 9 cm, with 25% involvement in the adrenal gland, and vascular invasion. The report also identified metastasis in tissues from the IVC, diaphragm, and transverse colon.

The pathology report describes an adrenal cortical carcinoma, which was surgically removed through a right adrenalectomy. The tumor weighed 760g and measured 13.5 x 9.5 x 6cm. The Weiss score was around 7, indicating a high likelihood of malignancy. The tumor did not extend into the liver or kidney and there was no evidence of any lymph node involvement.

The pathology report describes a case of high-grade adrenal cortical carcinoma affecting the left adrenal gland and left kidney. The tumor has invaded the renal vein and replaced six lymph nodes in the hilum, but has not spread to the ureter or other parts of the kidney. Mitotic count is high, with extensive necrosis and invasion of surrounding tissues. Immunohistochemistry testing was performed, and the results do not suggest Lynch syndrome. Overall, the report indicates a serious malignancy with significant metastatic involvement.

The report describes a low grade adrenal cortical carcinoma, measuring 40mm, which was incidentally found during a right adrenalectomy for a complex lesion. The carcinoma is confined to the adrenal gland and has not invaded the surrounding tissues. It fulfills 3 of the Weiss criteria for malignancy. The mitotic rate is low and there is no necrosis or vascular invasion. The diagnosis is supported by immunohistochemistry, with diffusely strongly positive staining for IGF2 and positive staining for Calretinin and MelanA.

The pathology report describes the diagnosis of adrenal cortical carcinoma, which is a tumor composed of variably pleomorphic cells arranged in diffuse sheets, nests, and cords. The tumor cells have enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei, and there are scattered cells with markedly atypical nuclei. There are occasional mitoses and variable amounts of eosinophilic granular cytoplasm. The tumor demonstrates four of the nine Weiss criteria, comprising high nuclear grade, loss of clear cells, diffuse architecture, and sinusoidal invasion. The report also includes additional information on the Weiss score and details of the histologic features of the tumor.

The pathology report describes a resected right adrenal mass weighing 316g with a multinodular appearance and areas of hemorrhage. The diagnosis is adrenocortical carcinoma with a largest diameter of 11 cm, nuclear grade 3, diffuse architectural pattern, and mitotic count of 6 in 50 LPF. There is no evidence of capsular or venous invasion, but sinusoidal invasion is present. The Weiss score is 6, and there is no evidence of neoplastic infiltration in the periadrenal fatty tissue.

The report describes the pathological findings from a patient who underwent a resection of the spleen, omentum, perirenal lymph node, retroperitoneal fat, left adrenal gland, and left kidney due to previous oligonucleosis. The spleen and omentum show no significant abnormalities, while the perirenal lymph node and retroperitoneal fat are negative for neoplasia. However, the left adrenal gland and the attached mass show adrenocortical carcinoma with vascular invasion, while the left kidney is unremarkable and free of tumor. No residual adrenal tissue is identified, and a portion is sent for tissue procurement.

The pathology report describes a case of adrenocortical carcinoma in the left adrenal gland with low-grade malignancy and capsular invasion. No vascular invasion was identified. Further testing was pending to identify potential vascular invasion. The tumor was 4.5 x 5 x 5.5 cm, protruding from the midsection of the adrenal gland, and appeared homogeneous and arising in the cortex of the gland. Surrounding cortex and medulla did not appear to be altered. The report includes sections and representative images of the tumor, as well as the adjacent adrenal gland.

The initial report showed a positive surgical margin for an adrenocortical carcinoma with vascular invasion and extraadrenal extension. However, an addendum report shows that the previously reported positive surgical margin was not true, and the tumor was completely excised. The revised diagnosis is still adrenocortical carcinoma with vascular invasion and extraadrenal extension. The report includes details of the surgical specimen and margins, as well as additional sections examined. A frozen section report showed negative results for carcinoma.

The pathology report confirms the diagnosis of adrenal cortical carcinoma in a case of a left adrenal mass, clinically suspected to be associated with Cushing's syndrome. The report describes a tumour with multiple nodules and a disrupted fibrous capsule. The tumour cells show significant nuclear pleomorphism, frequent mitoses, occasional atypical mitoses, and necrosis. Additionally, immunohistochemistry results indicate positive expression for synaptophysin and melan-A, while they are negative for AEL/AE3. These findings are consistent with the diagnosis of adrenocortical carcinoma. The case was reviewed in an endocrine clinicopathological meeting, and another doctor has concurred with the diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a non-functional left adrenal tumor that weighs 504g and measures 110 x 140 x 85 mm in size. The tumor appears to be at least partially encapsulated with multi-nodular growth and a variable cut surface. The report also indicates there is no macroscopic evidence of invasion and a small amount of uninvolved adrenal is identified. Microscopically, the tumor is identified as a left adrenal cortical carcinoma by Weiss criteria. The tumor is composed of polygonal cells and has areas of myxoid degeneration with fibrous septa. The nuclei are enlarged and pleomorphic with coarse chromatin and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemistry shows positive staining for inhibin, calretinin and Melan A. The report concludes that the morphological features and immunohistochemical profile is in keeping with an adrenal cortical carcinoma. The tumor has a Weiss score of 8 and stage II (pT2, NX, MX) according to AJCC Staging, 7th Edition.

The report describes a tumor removed from the right adrenal gland and kidney of a female patient. The tumor is identified as an adrenocortical carcinoma with a diameter of 12 cm, presenting diffuse architecture, clear cells in less than 25% of the neoplasm, areas of necrosis, 3 mitoses per 50 high power fields, atypical mitosis, and capsular and venous invasion. The tumor is partially encapsulated and infiltrates surrounding fatty tissue. No signs of invasion are seen in the right kidney. The report includes a macroscopic description of the tumor and its attached tissue.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a high-grade adrenocortical carcinoma with capsular and vascular invasion, including invasion of the vena cava. The surgical margins are negative, but there is metastatic carcinoma in one of two lymph nodes. There is also an incidental finding of a pheochromocytoma and interstitial cell tumor. The report includes information about the frozen section and surgical specimens, as well as immunohistochemistry results. The diagnosis has been revised to reflect the findings.

The pathology report describes a low-grade adrenal cortical carcinoma with clear margins. The specimen consists of a previously weighing tumor measuring 65 x 20 and there is no evidence of vascular or sinusoidal invasion. The immunohistochemical profile is consistent with the diagnosis of adrenal cortical carcinoma with a proliferation index of 8% and diffusely positive GF2 and strongly positive glucocorticoid receptor. The reporting pathologist confirmed the diagnosis of adrenal cortical carcinoma.

The pathology report describes that a right adrenalectomy was performed and the tumor weighed 168g and measured 8.3 x 7 x 4.5cm. The diagnosis of adrenal cortical carcinoma was made with a Weiss score of 6 and there was no lymph node metastasis.

The pathology report indicates that a right adrenalectomy was performed. A tumor weighing 198g and measuring 8.5 x7.5 x 6m was found in the adrenal gland. The tumor had oxyphilic cells and a Weiss score of 5, which is consistent with carcinoma. Based on Bisceglia et al's paper, the tumor was classified as having malignancy potential. No lymph node metastases were found, but a 1.4 hyperplastic nodule was found on segment V of the liver. The gallbladder had undergone cholecystectomy and showed no changes in histology.

The pathology report describes the findings from a left adrenal gland and spleen resection, a retroperitoneal lymph node dissection, and diaphragm resection. Low grade adrenocortical carcinoma with extensive necrosis was found in the left adrenal gland, along with no capsular or vascular invasion, negative surgical margins, and negative lymph nodes. An adrenocortical adenoma was also incidentally found. The retroperitoneal lymph nodes and ganglia were histologically unremarkable and negative for carcinoma. The diaphragm was negative for carcinoma and the fibromuscular tissue was unremarkable. Overall, the report suggests that the patient's low grade adrenocortical carcinoma had not spread beyond the left adrenal gland and immediate surrounding areas.

The pathology report describes an adrenal mass that has been previously incised. The mass is identified as a high grade adrenal cortical carcinoma with areas of haemorrhage and necrosis. The tumour has variable architecture with diffuse sheets, areas of glandular and papillary formation, and regions where the cells are more insular. The tumour has thick fibrous capsule and local excision appears complete. The report concludes that the tumour shows prominent vascular space permeation and the patient has an atrophic adrenal cortex. Further testing is recommended using T-93000 M-80103.

The pathology report describes a tumor in the right adrenal gland that was removed surgically (right adrenalectomy). The tumor weighed 244g and measured 8.2 x 7.5 x 6.5cm. The diagnosis is adrenal cortical carcinoma with oncocytic features, which is a type of cancer that originates from the cortex or outer region of the adrenal gland. The Weiss score, which is a tool used to assess the aggressiveness of adrenal cortical carcinomas, was 5 indicating a high likelihood of spread to other parts of the body.

The pathology report describes a specimen from a right adrenal gland of a male patient with a history of fevers, weight loss, and a CT showing a possible malignant adrenal mass. The specimen is largely replaced by a neoplastic infiltrate consisting of highly pleomorphic cells with numerous atypical mitotic figures, infiltrative borders, and necrosis and hemorrhage. Immunohistochemical stains show occasional scattered positive cells. Electron microscopy suggests a primary adrenal cortical carcinoma, but the standard of preservation is not sufficient for a firm diagnosis. No evidence of metastatic tumor is seen. The report recommends further evaluation and treatment.

The report describes a left adrenal tumor identified as adrenocortical carcinoma, measuring 8.0 cm in greatest dimension. The tumor shows diffuse growth with areas of necrosis, Fuhrman nuclear grade 3, and clear cells comprising less than 25% of tumor cells. There are 7 mitotic figures in 60 high-power fields. The tumor was completely resected, and no tumor cells were present in the margin of resection. An immunostain for Ki-67 showed 6.8% of cells were positive.

The pathology report describes the case of a patient who underwent a right adrenalectomy and right nephrectomy. The gross description noted an adrenal tumor weighing 172g, diagnosed as adrenal cortical carcinoma with a Weiss score of 7 and no lymph node metastasis. A 0.7cm nodule in the right kidney was also found, with granulomatous cells and gigantic cells raising the possibility of tuberculosis. The report also mentions chronic inflammatory changes due to a prior cholecystectomy.

The pathology report describes the findings of a surgery to remove an adrenal mass and left kidney. The adrenal mass was found to be a 19cm adrenocortical carcinoma with features such as diffuse architectural pattern, clear cells in <25% of the neoplasm, areas of necrosis, mitotic count of 28 in 10 H.P.E., atypical mitosis, capsular invasion, and venous invasion. The Weiss score was 8. There was no evidence of neoplastic infiltration in the renal parenchyma. The surgical margins were stained with green indian ink.

The pathology report is for an adrenal mass of unknown behavior. The specimen is an encapsulated tumour with a homogenous tan appearance, areas of cystic change, necrosis and yellow patchy areas. Microscopic examination shows an adrenocortical oncocytic carcinama, which appears to be confined to the adrenal gland. No unequivocal vascular space invasion or true coagulative tumor necrosis is identified, and there is no significant mitotic activity. The tumor directly underties the capsule of the adrenal gland, which is what separates the tumour from the inked surface. The tumour has an adrenocortical origin and is considered at least of "uncertain malignant potential" or "borderline." The tumour cannot be considered benign given its size and bizarre cellular atypia.

The pathology report describes multiple specimens received from a patient. The first specimen is an adrenal gland with an angioinvasive low-grade adrenal cortical carcinoma measuring 11.5 x 8.2 x 5.8 cm, weighing 156 g. The tumor has a very low mitotic activity but shows the presence of angioinvasion, atypical mitosis, increased p53 expression, paucity of clear cells and diffuse architecture, consistent with an angioinvasive low-grade adrenal cortical carcinoma. No pathological diagnosis is made for the gallbladder and fibroadipose tissue specimens. The liver segment 5 specimen shows focal nodular hyperplasia and no evidence of metastatic disease. The gross description of the adrenal gland shows a distorted tan-yellow adrenal gland measuring 10.0 x 7.0 x 5.2 cm, with a solid and partially cystic mass adjacent to it, measuring 10.0 x 6.7 x 5.2 cm with a tan-white fibrous capsule over its surface. Representative tissue is submitted for electron microscopy. The margins are uninvolved by the tumor, and no lymph nodes involvement is identified.  The pathology report provides additional synoptic data on the size and weight of the tumor gland and indicates that pathologic staging is based on AJCC/UICC TNM, 7th Edition.

The report describes a pathology examination of a patient with carcinoma of the adrenal gland with oxyphilic features. The patient underwent left adrenalectomy and left nephrectomy, and the tumor was found to measure 14x13cm, with a Weiss score of 8. There was a thrombus in the renal vein, but no lymph node metastasis was detected. Peritoneal fluid also did not contain any malignant cells. The weight of both the adrenal gland and kidney was 1060g.

The pathology report describes a case of adrenocortical carcinoma in a female patient who underwent a right nephrectomy and right adrenal mass resection. The tumor had a largest diameter of 20 cm and a Fuhrman nuclear grade of 3. There was a diffuse architectural pattern with clear cells present in less than 25% of the neoplasm. There were no areas of necrosis, atypical mitosis, capsular invasion, venous invasion or sinusoidal invasion detected. Weiss score was 3. The renal parenchyma did not show evidence of neoplastic infiltration. A liver biopsy revealed a hyperplastic regenerative nodule, and immunohistochemical markers showed positivity for Melan A, Inhibin, and 35BH11, while being negative for cytokeratin 20, cytokeratin 7, Sinaptofisin, Hep-Par |, Chromogranin, CEA, and Calretinin.

The report describes a specimen labeled as "resection adrenal gland mass left" that measures 7.0 x 6.0 x 6.0 cm and weighing 70.2 g, and a piece of fibroadipose tissue that measures 5.5 x 2.2 x 1.7 cm.
