The right carinal pneumonectomy specimen contained a 6cm x 4.5cm x 4cm moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the right main bronchus. The margins of the bronchus are free of tumors, but there is evidence of bronchiopneumonia, extensive necrosis, and intrabronchial hemorrhage. Multiple peribronchial lymph nodes were also identified and will be examined microscopically. One anthracotic lymph node (level 7) and one red-tan lymph node (level 9) were also removed and submitted for examination.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a 7.8 cm squamous cell carcinoma in the left upper lobe of the lung, which has extended into the left lower lobe and is associated with four tumor nodules of similar morphology. There is no evidence of visceral pleural invasion. All sampled lymph nodes are benign. The report suggests that the pathologic staging of the tumor is challenging as there was a previous positive result for non-small cell carcinoma in the right upper lobe, and it is uncertain whether the tumors represent two independent primaries or a metastasis. Clinical correlation is recommended to determine the appropriate stage of the tumor.

The pathology report describes a left pulmonectomy specimen taken from a patient with squamous cell carcinoma of the lung. The tumor is moderately differentiated and measures 3x3x3 cm. The report does not provide details on the tumor extent, lymphatic or venous invasion, margins, or evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment. No other tumor nodules or additional pathologic findings are mentioned. The report also indicates that the tumor was located in the left-upper area of the lung.

The clinical case report includes the patient’s medical and social history, diagnostic studies, and treatment information. The report also contains a pathology form that includes the specimen information, pathological description, and microscopic description. The primary tumor was found to be 2 gm in size with no extension, and there were some malignant cells found in the examined lymph nodes. Further information about the exact diagnosis is not provided in the summary.

The report describes a lobectomy specimen from the lung of a patient with squamous cell carcinoma, although the histologic grade and tumor extent are not specified. Two regional lymph nodes were examined and 0/2 were positive for metastasis. There is no evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment and no other significant pathologic findings were observed.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy specimen taken from a lung tumor measuring 8 x 8 x 8 cm. The tumor is identified as squamous cell carcinoma and is poorly differentiated. There is evidence of metastasis in 8 out of 10 lymph nodes in the thoracic region. There is no information provided about lymphatic or venous invasion or margin status. No information is given about additional pathologic findings or neo-adjuvant treatment.

The pathology report describes a tumor sample collected from the right lower lobe. The diagnosis shows squamous cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified (NOS), with a tumor size of 6.2 cm. The pathological staging indicates T2, N0, M0, and VALCSG stage. The sample type is buffy. No further information is available about the age of the patient or the days to the procedure and diagnosis.

The pathology report describes specimens submitted for biopsy from various parts of the body, including the lung, soft tissue, and lymph nodes. The biopsy results indicate a squamous cell carcinoma in the upper lobe of the lung and involvement of several lymph nodes, including one with follicular lymphoma. The tumors are positive for specific markers like CD20, BCt-2, and CD10. The report also mentions benign lymph nodes and metastasis to some lymph nodes. Overall, the report provides detailed information about the presence and status of various tumors in the patient.

The pathology report describes a case of poorly differentiated, large-cell, nonkeratinizing squamous cell carcinoma of the right upper lobe of the lung. The tumor is 2.8 cm in size and has invaded nearby subsegmental branches and alveolar septa. Lymph nodes were also examined, but they only show reactive lesions and anthracotic pigment deposits. The tumor has not spread to other areas and the excised lymph nodes and margins are tumor-free. The TNM classification is pT1N0M0, stage IA. The report also notes the presence of marked focal centroacinar pulmonary emphysema.

The pathology report describes a specimen of lung tissue obtained via lobectomy. The tumor present in the tissue is a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with a size of 3.5 x 3.5 x 3.5 mm. There is no information available regarding the extent of the tumor or any other nodules present. Out of the two lymph nodes examined, both are negative for metastasis. The report does not provide any details about lymphatic or venous invasion, nor is there any information available regarding the margins of the tissue.

The pathology report describes multiple lymph nodes and a right upper lobe specimen from an unknown patient with a pre-operative diagnosis of a right upper lobe mass. The intraoperative diagnosis shows that lymph nodes in levels 4R, 7, and 4L are negative for carcinoma. However, the right upper lobe specimen shows a moderately differentiated non-keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma measuring 5.1 x 4.2 cm, with no involvement of bronchial margins or visceral pleural. The report also indicates negative lymph node involvement in Ipsilateral Hilar and/or Peribronchial, Ipsilateral Mediastinal and/or Subcarinal, and Contralateral Mediastinal/Hilar, Scalene or Supraclavicular levels. The histologic grade of the tumor is G2, and there is subpleural fibrosis and ossification found. The final pathological staging is pT2 NO MX.

The pathology report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma of the lung with poor differentiation. The tumor has a size of 3x2.5x2.5 cm and is localized without evidence of lymphatic or venous invasion. Nine bronchopulmonal and five hilar lymph nodes were examined, none of which showed signs of metastases. The surgical margin and vessels are free of tumor elements. There is no evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment, and no additional pathologic findings are reported.

The pathology report describes a surgical resection of a tumor in the right upper lobe of the lung diagnosed as moderately differentiated squamous carcinoma without involvement of nearby structures or pleura. In situ carcinoma was present, but invasion was not identified in venous, arterial, lymphatic, or perineural structures. The surgical margins were not involved, and no metastatic carcinoma was found in the lymph nodes. The lymph nodes were removed from different stations and submitted separately for analysis. Frozen sections were requested to check for the presence of cancer but were negative. The tumor size was 5 cm, and it surrounded distal bronchial structures. The report recommends a comprehensive review of all available information to determine the final staging of the disease.

The report is based on a tumor sample of a squamous cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified (NOS) in the right lower lobe. The tumor size is 55 cm and the pathological grade/differentiation is unknown. The pathology report also mentions that the patient underwent a resect procedure. However, other details such as the patient's age and the year of the sample collection are not mentioned for this sample. Additionally, the report includes a second sample of a Buffy, but no information is given regarding its diagnosis, age and sample collection details.

The pathology report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma in the right upper lobe of the lung with a tumor size of 10/12/8 cm. The tumor infiltrated the visceral pleura and showed necrosis and central ulceration. The microscopic examination reveals a G2 tumor type with a tendency to keratinization, solid islands of large and pleomorphic cells, atypical mitoses, and hotbeds of necrosis. There was no metastasis in the hilar lymph node, and fragments of pleura and rib showed no tumoral infiltration. The report does not provide information about lymphatic and venous invasion, margins, and neo-adjuvant treatment.

The pathology report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma in the right upper lobe of the lung, with possible pleural invasion. One lymph node adjacent to the tumor is involved, but others appear to be reactive only. No blood vessel, lymphatic, or perineural invasion is observed. The report also notes the presence of bronchiectasis and endogenous lipid pneumonia in the lung. One lymph node contains a small silicotic nodule, and another appears to contain a deposit of squamous cell carcinoma within a fibrous capsule. There is no evidence of malignancy in the other lymph nodes examined.

The pathology report describes a bronchopulmonary neoplasm of the papillary squamous cell carcinoma type without keratinization. It is moderately differentiated and has monomorphous cellularity, nuclear atypias, and isolated atypical mitoses with hotbeds of necrosis and abundant fibrous-inflammatory stroma. The tumor is present in the main bronchus and is obstructing the airway. There is evidence of lymphatic invasion and no metastases in lymph nodes. No information is provided about margins or additional pathologic findings. No neo-adjuvant treatment has been given.

The pathology report describes a tumor sample (TCGA-63-As fag) that was diagnosed as Squamous Cell Carcinoma NOS. The tumor was found in the right upper lobe and was resected. The size of the tumor was 5cm and it was found to be differentiated as well as T2. The pathological N was NO and M was MX. The histology comments mention that the sample was a Buffy sample and 30% of the sample showed squamous cell carcinoma. No information is available about the year and age at sample collection or the days to procedure date and diagnosis.

The pathology report shows that the patient had a 4.5 cm infiltrating poorly differentiated non-small cell carcinoma in the left upper lobe of the lung. The tumor had squamous and glandular features and involved a large airway, but did not involve the pleura. Seven lymph nodes were removed and all were negative for tumor. The pathologic stage was T2NOMX. Multiple lymph nodes were also removed from levels V, VI, and VIII, and all were negative for tumor.

ased squamous cell carcinoma of the right lung with extensive local and nodal spread including involvement of hilar, paratracheal, pulmonary ligament and subcarinal lymph nodes. Tumor spread across the pleural fissure questionably into the upper lobe. There is also evidence of occupational exposure to asbestos. The report includes detailed macroscopy findings and a large number of sections for examination. Histological and cytological findings are not included in the summary.

The pathology report shows a 2 cm pinky-gray tumor in a section of lung tissue measuring 18x16 cm that was removed via lobectomy. It is diagnosed as a well-differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma with a micro abscess in the S3. There is no evidence of venous invasion, and margins are absent. No lymphatic invasion is specified, but 0/8 lymph nodes tested positive for metastasis in the bronchopulmonary area. There is no evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment specified.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the right lower lobe of the lung, with pleural invasion and a satellite metastasis. Two of thirteen lymph nodes examined were positive for metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor had invaded the visceral pleura and demonstrated an angiolympathic invasion. The FGFR1 FISH studies performed on the squamous cell carcinoma were positive for amplification. The final diagnosis is T3 N1 stage carcinoma. There is also evidence of severe emphysematous change with respiratory bronchiolitis and smoker's-associated interstitial fibrosis. In addition, there were other findings in the pathology report, including no evidence of malignancy in several lymph node biopsies and the presence of small carcinoid tumorlets and focal bronchiolar dysplasia in the right upper lobe. There was patchy post-obstructive pneumonia and atypical adenomatous hyperplasia as well. The report provides further details about the size, grading, and location of the tumor, as well as other relevant clinical findings.

The report describes a lung nodule that was investigated using a procedure called bronchoscopy with biopsy. The pathology report confirms the presence of a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma measuring 2.0 cm in the right lower lobe of the lung with angiolymphatic invasion identified. Lymph nodes were biopsied, with no evidence of cancer found. The final diagnosis indicates the stage of the cancer as T1, NO, MX. The report also includes a description of the received specimens and their frozen sections for diagnostic purposes.

The pathology report indicates that there is a carcinoma, specifically a basaloid squamous cell carcinoma, present in the lung of the patient. The tumor size is 15 millimeters and there is no invasion of the visceral pleura or chest wall. The lymph node status is negative and the final diagnosis is pT1pNo.

The pathology report describes a surgical procedure involving a left thoracotomy to remove parts of the lung and lymph nodes. The final diagnosis shows that all lymph nodes were negative for malignancy, except for one that showed lymph-vascular invasion. The right lung showed a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma that invaded the visceral pleura and had lymph node involvement in the peribronchial station. The report also notes additional findings such as respiratory bronchiolitis, emphysematous changes, bronchiole dilation, and a hyalinized and calcified granuloma. Intraoperative consultation confirmed that there was no tumor identified at the bronchial margin.

The pathology report describes the findings after a lobectomy and lymph node biopsies in a patient with suspected carcinoma. Lymph nodes showed no evidence of carcinoma. However, the left lower lobe lung resection revealed a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with a dimension of 4.0 cm. The tumor showed venous invasion, and one lymph node out of nine was positive for metastatic adenocarcinoma. The report suggests the involvement of lymph node station 12L and a second primary squamous cell carcinoma. There were also post-obstructive changes in the lung.

The pathology report describes a specimen labeled "right lower lobe," which is a treoctomy with a 48mm poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor is subpleural and proximal to central bronchi, with visceral pleural invasion present. No lymph node metastases are identified, and there is no blood vessel, lymphatic, or perineural invasion. The bronchial margin is clear, and there are no significant changes in non-neoplastic lung tissue. Special stains confirm the invasion into but not through the visceral pleura. The staging is T2NO.

The report is a Missing Pathology Report Form for a tumor sample. The tumor type is LVSu and the specimen was originally sent to Bice. The date of specimen arrival at the BCR was 4/19/208. The histology code for the sample is 8010/3 and the site code is C34.4. No diagnosis is available for the patient.

The report describes the pathological findings of a surgical excision of lymph nodes and a left upper lobe lobectomy. The lymph nodes examined did not show any evidence of tumors. The left upper lobe lobectomy tissue showed a poorly differentiated basaloid squamous cell carcinoma with a tumor size of 3.3 cm x 2.5 cm. Additional dimensions, lymph node involvement, and non-neoplastic lung findings are also provided. Further immunohistochemistry and special staining were conducted, with results showing CD56 positive spotty and SYNAPTOPHYSIN negative. The final pathological staging is pr2, NO MX. No clinical history was provided.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy specimen of a lung lobe with a tumoral structure obstructing the bronchus, spreading to the periphery without invading the pleura. The microscopic examination reveals it to be a bronchopulmonary neoplasm of epidermoid carcinoma type, forming solid globes with keratinization and a fibrous-inflammatory stromal reaction. The interlobar and hilar lymph nodes show neoplastic infiltrates of the carcinoma, with two out of six lymph nodes tested positive for metastasis. The diagnosis is moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the lung. No information is provided regarding tumor extent, lymphatic or venous invasion, margins, or neo-adjuvant treatment.

The pathology report shows that the patient had invasive squamous cell carcinoma in the bronchus intermedius lymph nodes and the right lung, with metastasis to peribronchial lymph nodes. There was also evidence of centrilobular emphysema and a previous surgical procedure, likely a middle lobectomy, with a giant cell reaction to suture material. The first rib showed no significant pathology. However, lymph nodes in 10R, 11R, 12R, 4R, and periphrenic lymph node #7 were negative for neoplasia. The tumor was located in the right hilum and measured 3 cm in its greatest dimension. The pathologic stage was p stage IA (T1b N1 Mo). The clinical diagnosis was lung cancer.

The pathology report indicates the absence of malignancy in lymph nodes, the 5th rib, and inferior pulmonary ligament, as well as negative resection margins in the bronchus. However, the report shows the presence of a 3.0 cm invasive moderately-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the peripheral left lower lobe of the lung, with no pleural invasion. The malignancy has been removed completely through surgical resection.

The pathology report describes specimens from various sites including lymph nodes and lung tissue. The frozen section diagnosis for the lung tissue showed no tumor, but moderate squamous dysplasia was present. Further examination of the lung tissue revealed a centrally-located, partially necrotic mass extending into the main stem bronchus. Additional bronchial margins were also examined. Multiple lymph nodes were identified and representative tissue was submitted for analysis. No definitive diagnosis is provided in the summary.

The report describes the results of an excision of a left lower lobe lung tumor that was found to be invasive stage 3 squamous cell carcinoma. Four intrapulmonary peribronchial lymph nodes were negative for tumor, with one having a hyalinized granuloma. The remaining lung parenchyma showed organizing pneumonia. Multiple lymph nodes in the superior and inferior mediastina, aortic N1, were negative for tumor.

The report describes the following specimens: a right lower lobe wedge resection, a lymph node from station 9, a lymph node from station 7, and two lymph nodes from station 4. The resected lung specimen shows a poorly differentiated 1.6 cm squamous cell carcinoma without lymphovascular invasion. The staple line margin is free of tumor. The lymph nodes are negative for carcinoma. There is an additional finding of emphysema. The report also mentions that immunohistochemical stains confirm the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma. No other nodules were identified in the lung specimen. Special procedures were done to determine the presence of mucin. The report notes that the tests were developed and their performance characteristics were determined by the Department of Pathology and have not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

The pathology report describes the analysis of five specimens from a patient with lung cancer. The first specimen, labeled "right upper lobe," shows a 35mm, well-circumscribed squamous cell carcinoma with central necrosis near the endobronchial resection margin. The carcinoma has involved the peribronchial resection margin, predominantly through spread along perineural spaces, but does not involve the pleura. The remaining lung parenchyma shows changes of emphysema. Four lymph node specimens labeled 7 Node, 11 R Node, 4 R Node, and Hilar Node show only reactive changes and no evidence of metastatic carcinoma.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent excision of lymph nodes at levels X, IV-R, VIII, IX, and II, as well as excision of soft tissue and a lung lobectomy due to a lung mass. The level X and VIII lymph nodes showed no evidence of malignancy, while the level IV-R lymph node showed metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. The level VII lymph node showed fragments of a benign lymph node and necrotic tissue. The soft tissue excision showed crystalline material with a foreign body response. The lung lobectomy revealed moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with a peribronchial lymph node and extensive pleural crystalline deposition with a foreign body reaction. The lung tumor measured 3.4 cm in greatest dimension and was classified as pT2, N2. The lung bronchial margin was negative for malignancy on frozen section diagnosis. Overall, the report suggests the presence of metastatic cancer in the lymph nodes and lung.

The pathology report describes the findings from the excision of left upper lobe lung tissue, multiple lymph nodes in the inferior mediastinal, aortic and left interlobar regions. The lung tissue shows a Grade 3 squamous cell carcinoma mass that is not directly invading the pleura. The lobectomy of the left upper lobe shows benign lung parenchyma with no residual tumor and negative bronchial margin. Multiple lymph nodes are negative for tumor, except for the excised tissue from the aortopulmonary lymph node which shows fibrovascular tissue with no lymphoid tissue.

The pathology report describes a biopsy procedure for a patient with squamous cell cancer. The specimen includes a resected right lower lobe of the lung and lymph nodes. The report describes multiple tumor masses, including one that encases and potentially obstructs the bronchus and involves adjacent peribronchial lymph nodes. Another tumor mass is located at the apex of the superior segment. Frozen section examination confirms a negative bronchial resection margin but identifies a nonsmall cell carcinoma of high grade with necrosis and extensive invasion of vascular channels, likely lymphatics. The report also includes detailed information on the gross appearance and microscopic findings for the various specimens collected during the biopsy.

The report describes a left pneumonectomy specimen received for frozen section evaluation. The lung was covered by a red-purple pleura with a 9.5 cm firm mass lying beneath the parietal pleura. The cut surfaces were tan to gray-tan, variegated, firm, and nodular with focal anthracotic stain. The margins were irregular. The non-neoplastic lung tissue showed pneumonia with abscess. Several hilar lymph nodes were palpable, and a representative section of each was submitted. The final diagnosis is squamous cell (epidermoid) carcinoma, keratinizing type, poorly differentiated, with a maximum dimension of 9.5 cm. There is no lymphatic, venous, or arterial invasion, invasion into or through the pleura by tumor, and only moderate tumor necrosis. The surgical margins are uninvolved by tumor. The total number of nodes examined is five, and the total number of positive nodes is zero.

The pathology report documents the examination of various specimens from a surgery that removed a right lower lobe lung mass. The report confirms a diagnosis of poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, measuring 7x4cm, with positive peribronchial lymph nodes and negative lymph nodes in other areas examined. The report also includes details on the examination of lymph node specimens from levels 7, 8, 9, and 10R, which all came back negative for carcinoma except for two out of 17 peribronchial lymph nodes. No visceral pleural involvement or satellite tumors were detected.

The pathology report describes a lung cancer diagnosis based on the frozen section analysis of a lymph node (level 5) which showed non-small cell carcinoma. The gross description of the left upper lobe specimen showed a white-tan-gray firm focus grossly consistent with tumor, measured 3.5 x 2.5 x 2.5 cm, and was contiguous with the umbilication on the pleura. The report also mentions two black-red irregular soft tissue segments from level 7, which were entirely submitted in one cassette.

The report describes various tissue specimens received from different levels and lobes of the lungs of an individual. One section, labeled "right upper lobe," measures 5cm and shows a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. The margins of resection are uninvolved, and the tumor has not invaded large vessels or lymphatic vessels. Four lymph nodes are negative for metastases, and there is no evidence of metastatic disease in other specimens.

The diagnosis is moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma located in the right lower lobe of the lung, with a tumor size of 3.3 cm. The lymph nodes in the region (25 total) were all negative for the presence of cancer cells. The tumor has not invaded the lymphovascular or perineural systems, and the surgical margins were negative. The tumor is staged as pT2a, and the overall pathologic stage is IB. No distant metastasis was observed. The report also details the various specimens obtained during surgery and evaluated for cancer.

The pathology report describes tissue samples taken from a lung mass identified prior to surgery. The report describes the gross appearance of the tissue samples, which include lymph nodes and lung tissue. The final diagnosis includes reactive sinus histiocytosis and anthracosilicosis in the lymph nodes with no metastatic carcinoma identified. The right lung tissue showed characteristics of squamous cell carcinoma with extensive necrosis and degeneration. The carcinoma extended into but not through the pleura, and there was no evidence of lymphovascular space invasion. The surgical margins appear to be clear.

The pathology report describes a tumor sample from the left lower lobe of the lung that was classified as Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified (NOS) with a size of 35 cm. The sample was obtained through resection. No lymph node involvement was detected, and the cancer has not spread to other areas of the body. No further information or comments were provided in the report.

The patient underwent a wedge resection of the left lower lobe due to weight loss, productive cough, and a cream-colored mass measuring 32 mm in diameter located about 10 mm from the wedge resection margin. The mass was identified as a well-differentiated to moderately-differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma with central necrosis, pulmonary arterial invasion, and probable lymphatic permeation, with a pathological stage of T2NX. The adjacent lung tissue showed usual interstitial pneumonitis with honeycombing, fibrosis, and interstitial lymphocytic infiltration. Resection margins were clear, and no lymph nodes were involved. A copy of the report was sent to the cancer department.

The report describes a case of squamous cell carcinoma in the left lung, involving both the superior lobe (basal segment) and the inferior lobe (apical segment). The tumor size is 1.60x6.0x5.5 cm, with involvement of the visceral pleura but no chest wall invasion. The diagnosis is poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, with no lymph node involvement (NO, 0/35) and a staging of NM1 pT3 pNO (0/35) G3 RO.

The pathology report describes the findings from the excision of rib, lymph nodes, and lobectomy of the right lower and middle lobes of the lung. The excised rib and lymph nodes were negative for malignancy. The right lower lobe excision revealed an invasive, moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with lymphovascular invasion and pleural invasion. There was no malignancy in bronchovascular margins or soft tissue margins of the diaphragm. The right middle lobe excision was negative for malignancy. Ancillary studies will be performed on one of the blocks for further analysis. The T stage was pT1N0, N stage was N0, and M stage was not applicable. Additional studies such as histochemical stains, immunohistochemical stains, FISH studies, and molecular structures will be performed.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, basaloid type, grade 3, measuring 2.5 cm in the right upper lobe, with lymphovascular invasion. There was metastatic poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with extracapsular extension in the level 12R lymph node. A residual invasive poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, basaloid type, grade 3, measuring 1.3 cm was found after a right upper lobe lobectomy. There were fragments of benign lymph nodes found in the 2R, 4R, and level 8 lymph nodes. The tumor did not invade the bronchial, vascular, or visceral/parietal pleura, and the lymph node status was positive for metastatic tumor in level 12R and negative in other lymph nodes. The final diagnosis was pT2AN1PLO stage squamous cell carcinoma.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a right upper lobe wedge resection, a Level 10 lymph node resection, a right upper lobe lobectomy, R4 lymph nodes resection, and subcarinal lymph nodes resection due to a right lung mass. The report indicates that the mass was a 2.1cm moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, with uninvolved margins. There was no evidence of metastasis found in any of the examined lymph nodes, and there were no other findings. The report also includes detailed descriptions of the specimens received and examined in the laboratory.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a lobectomy for a 3.5 cm moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the right lower lobe of the lung. The tumor was confined to the lung and there was no pleural involvement or lymphatic/vascular invasion by tumor. Lymph nodes were negative for metastasis. The pathologic staging was determined to be pT2aN0M0, stage IB. The report also includes details on a benign bone lesion and a negative lymph node biopsy. Ancillary testing was not possible due to insufficient tissue. The report notes the patient's history of heart transplant and previous attempts to diagnose the lung mass.

The pathology report indicates that there is a moderately differentiated keratinising squamous cell carcinoma in the left lung, which has extended into the extra-pleural soft tissue surrounding the lung and metastasized to peribronchial and number 7 lymph nodes. There is no evidence of malignancy in the hilar lymph node or lymph node designated as number 5. However, residual microscopic tumor cannot be excluded in the mediastinum based on histologic grounds. Further sections of pericardium, mediastinal soft tissue, and pleura have been submitted for histology.

The pathology report describes a specimen from a lung surgery, including multiple lymph nodes and a rib section. The lung specimen shows a large tumor mass in the right middle lobe that obstructs the airways and extends towards the pleura, with areas of necrosis and yellow discoloration. The tumor has invaded the bronchus and penetrated the mucosa. There is metastasis to para-arterial and parabronchial lymph nodes. The FSA anthracotic nodes and rib section are negative for tumor. The tumor is identified as a halfway differentiated squamous cell carcinoma.

The pathology report describes a 15x13x14 cm lung tumor that is grey-whitish in color and located near the bronchus. Microscopic examination shows it to be a keratinizing squamous carcinoma of the lung, with a well-differentiated G1 grade. Two subcarinal lymph nodes show anthracosis, and there is no evidence of venous invasion. The tumor extent is localized, and there are no specific mentions of additional tumor nodules, lymphatic invasion, or neo-adjuvant treatment.

The pathology report shows that the patient has two squamous cell carcinoma tumors in the left lung inferior lobe, with the larger tumor measuring 4mm in diameter and the smaller measuring 2.5mm in diameter. There is visceral pleural invasion present, but no invasion of the chest wall. The histological diagnosis is moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with focal keratinization. There are no positive lymph nodes (NO) out of 31 nodes examined. The tumor stage is pT4 pNO (0/31) and the tumor grade is G2.

The pathology report describes multiple tissue samples taken from various lymph nodes and a rib, as well as a left upper lobe lung resection, with one lymph node from each level submitted for analysis. The report indicates that none of the lymph nodes tested positive for tumor cells and the bronchial margin is negative for tumor. However, a large tumor mass with central areas of necrosis was found in the left upper lobe, with multiple sections submitted for analysis. The report does not provide a definitive diagnosis or further information on the nature of the tumor.

The pathology report describes a case of moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the left upper lobe of the lung. The tumor measured 25mm and showed extensive vascular and focal lymphatic invasion. There was no evidence of pleural invasion or peribronchial lymph node involvement. The bronchial resection margin showed focal squamous metaplasia and mild dysplasia. Adjacent lung tissue showed peritumoral scarring and obstructive changes, as well as apical bullous emphysema with fibrosis and pleural adhesion. The pathological stage was T1 NO.

The pathology report describes the analysis of lymph nodes and lung tissue from a patient. The lymph nodes examined were negative for malignancy. The lung tissue contained an invasive moderately-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma that was completely resected, with no invasion into the visceral pleura. The bronchial margin of resection and lobar lymph nodes were negative for malignancy. A focal area of nonspecific pleuropulmonary fibrosis and pulmonary emphysema were also observed. Multiple sections of the lung tissue were examined, with representative sections submitted for analysis.

The pathology report describes the results of a pneumonectomy on the left lung due to moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. There was no sign of neoplasm on the pleural surface. The tumor measured 4.5 cm and the bronchial margins of the surgical resection were free. Two out of six hilar lymph nodes were found to be positive for metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. Lymph node dissection revealed one negative lymph node in the 4L lower paratracheal nodes, three negative lymph nodes in the 7 subcarinal lymph node, seven negative lymph nodes in the 8 paraesophageal below carina lymph nodes, and two negative lymph nodes in the 9 pulmonary ligament lymph nodes. The case corresponds to a pathological AJCC stage of T2a,N1. Frozen section examination revealed no tumor in the bronchial and vascular margins. The gross examination revealed a 45 x 3.2 cm white firm mass in the upper lobe of the lung surrounded by lung parenchyma. Seven possible lymph nodes were identified at the hilum of the lobe ranging from 0.4 to 1.8 cm in greatest dimension. The lymph nodes were examined and those found to be negative were submitted in toto for analysis.

The pathology report describes a surgery removing a part of the right lower lobe lung and several lymph nodes. The lung section shows a grade 3 invasive squamous cell carcinoma with necrotic tissue forming a mass near the bronchial resection margin, and the visceral pleura is involved in a localized area. The lymph nodes removed from the superior and inferior mediastinal areas and interlobar regions are negative for cancer.

The pathology report indicates that a lobectomy was performed on a patient with a 4.5cm non-small cell carcinoma with squamous features located in the right upper lobe of the lung. All 13 lymph nodes were negative for tumor. The tumor was poorly differentiated (G3) and pT2 (greater than 3cm in size). Margins were uninvolved by invasive carcinoma and there was no venous/arterial invasion. Lymphatic invasion was indeterminate. Additionally, specimens from multiple lymph nodes and fibroadipose tissue were negative for tumor. No clinical history was provided.

The report is for a sample (buffy coat) collected from a patient who underwent a procedure for a squamous tumor. The tumor is a grade 3 (moderately differentiated) squamous cell carcinoma, with a size of 3.7cm. The cancer has invaded into the deeper layer of tissue (T3) and there is no evidence of lymph node involvement (N0). The staging is Mo, indicating no distant metastases. No further information about the patient or treatment is provided.

The pathology report describes a moderately differentiated, slightly keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma in the left upper lobe of the lung with central to peripheral bronchopulmonary involvement and main location in S2. The tumor has spread to the central section of B3 and peripheral spread is observed, including the formation of nodules in various lymph nodes. Moderate centrocinar pulmonary emphysema, pigmented macrophages, and subpleural cicatricial zone are also noted. The report states that the resection margin of bronchus and vessels, the visceral pleura, and all excised and identified lymph nodes are tumor-free. Asbestos exposure is also mentioned, but further investigation is required to determine the extent of exposure. The TNM classification of the tumor is pT2 pN0PMX V1 RO stage B.

This is a pathology report of a patient who had surgery for a right lung mass. The report describes specimens of various lymph nodes, pleural nodules, lung tissue, and additional margins taken during the surgery. The FSA, FSB, and FSC samples tested negative for carcinoma, but the FSE sample tested positive. The report includes gross descriptions of the specimens and submits sections for further study. The final diagnosis is not mentioned in the summary.

The pathology report shows that the patient had surgically removed lymph nodes, and all of them were negative for metastatic carcinoma. The report also reveals that the right lung was removed due to moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, with multiple nodules present, and the margins of resection are negative for cancer. There was evidence of squamous dysplasia, squamous metaplasia, and post-obstructive pneumonia in the lung tissue. The tumor is staged as pT3 due to the separate tumor nodule present in the same lobe, away from the main central tumor. Multiple representative sections of the mass and lymph nodes were submitted for further analysis. The pathology report does not provide a final diagnosis.

The pathology report describes three specimens received, including a right lower lobe (RLL) lobectomy specimen. The RLL lobectomy specimen shows a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma that measures 55 mm in maximal dimension and extends out towards the pleura. Lymphatic permeation is identified but no blood vessel or perineural invasion is present. There is no pleural invasion identified and the bronchial margin is clear, but there is a soft tissue extension partly related to a lymph node that extends close to or at the hilar resection margin. Several peribronchial lymph node metastases are seen. The final diagnosis is T3N0M0 squamous cell carcinoma of the RLL.

The pathology report includes information about two tissue samples collected from the right upper lobe with a difference of 11 days. Both samples were diagnosed as T2, NOS with no metastases. The histology report does not mention any comments or slide URL for further reference. The age of the patient at the time of sample collection was not disclosed in the report.

The report describes surgical procedures and results of a pathology examination in a male patient with a diagnosis of lung cancer. The pathology report identifies a poorly differentiated non-squamous non-small cell lung carcinoma in the right upper lobe, as well as metastasis to a lymph node and chest wall plaque. Other samples obtained from the patient showed only benign tissues and chronic inflammation. Various tests were performed on samples obtained, including immunoperoxidase stains. The report includes frozen section diagnoses and comments.

The report provides information on a lobectomy specimen taken from the lungs, but does not include details on the size or extent of any tumor present, or on lymph nodes and margins. There is no evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment and no additional pathological findings noted. There are no comments included.

The pathology report describes the examination of a lung and lymph nodes from a patient diagnosed with bronchial carcinoma, specifically large-cell carcinoma. The right lung measured 14x12cm at the base and up to 26cm high, with a tumor in the lower lobe that extended to the visceral pleura. The report also notes involvement of nearby lymph nodes and infiltration into surrounding tissue. Microscopy revealed solid structures of large atypical epithelia with prominent nucleoli, mitoses, and areas of necrosis. The lung parenchyma and bronchi were also affected.

The pathology report describes a left lower lobe lung tumor measuring 10 x 7.5 cm with suspected mediastinal lymph node metastasis. Multiple lymph nodes were found to be lesioned. The tumor had arcuate contours and involved adjacent sections of S 6 and 9, with central tumor extension within 1.3 cm of the bronchus resection plane. Microscopic evaluation confirmed lymph node involvement by a large-cell solid carcinoma, possibly with squamous cell differentiation, with extensive infiltration by atypical epithelia arranged in partly branched solid structures. There were also areas of necrosis and dense granulocytic infiltrates. Other lymph nodes showed intact underlying structure and inconspicuous cell content. Further testing was done with multiple stains, including Blastica-van Gieson, PAS, and diastase-PAS.

The pathology report form is missing, and the TCGA Missing Pathology Report Form should be completed instead. The report asks for information related to the tumor type, the BCR (Biospecimen Core Resource) specimen origin and shipment date, histology code, and site code. No specific information regarding the diagnosis or findings of the specimen is provided in this report.

The pathology report describes the examination of various tissues and nodes from a patient with a clinical diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma of the right upper lobe of the lung. A large tumor measuring up to 8.5 cm with unclear demarcation and an irregular cavity is present. The tumor has invaded surrounding tissues, including the pleura and nearby nodes. The report also notes the presence of hard areas and discoloration in the lower lobe of the lung. Lesioned nodes are found in several locations, including the right middle and upper lobes, parietal pleura, and hilum. Overall, the findings support a diagnosis of malignancy.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a lobectomy in the left upper lobe of the lung which revealed a Grade 4 squamous cell carcinoma tumor measuring 2.0 x 2.0 x 1.8 cm. Ten intrapulmonary peribronchial lymph nodes and the visceral pleura were negative for tumor. Additionally, there was Grade 4 non-small cell carcinoma with squamous features in the soft tissue of the left hilar region that was excised. There was also an excised lymph node in the left lower lobe that was negative for neoplasm, but had non-necrotizing granulomatous inflammation. Multiple lymph nodes in the superior mediastinal, aortic, inferior mediastinal, and left lower lobe bronchus were negative for tumor. The findings of special stains for microorganisms will be reported separately.

The pathology report describes the results of surgical removal of lymph nodes (Levels 7 and 11), a lobectomy of the right upper lobe of the lung, and the histologic classification of the removed cancerous tissue. The lung tumor is identified as an invasive, moderately differentiated keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, with in situ carcinoma present but without identified invasion into surrounding blood vessels or nerves. The tumor is also found to have spread to one peribronchial lymph node but there is no identified extracapsular extension. The report recommends further review of available information for a comprehensive staging of the tumor.

The report indicates that the patient's tissue sample was diagnosed with Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified (NOS). The sample was collected from the right lower lobe and was identified as T2b pathological staging, with no pathological N and clinical M status. The report does not include any comments about the histology of the sample, and the patient's age and the year of sample collection are not specified. The sample was obtained through a resect procedure, and a separate BUFFY sample was also collected.

The pathology report describes a case of a  year old male who underwent a Limited left thoracotomy with upper lobectomy due to the presence of a left lung mass. The tumor was identified as Squamous cell carcinoma with a poor differentiation grade and a size of 1.8cm. The surgical margin was free of the tumor, and no direct extension of the tumor or lymphatic or venous invasion were identified. Six lymph nodes were examined, and none were involved. The case was classified as pT1a, pN0, and pMx. No significant inflammation or fibrosis was observed in the lung tissue, and the lymph nodes were benign with anthracotic pigment.

The pathology report describes a surgical excision of a superior segment of the right lower lobe of the lung and a lateral basilar segment wedge resection. The diagnosis is invasive poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, which was unifocal and measured 4.9 x 4.8 x 3.5 cm. The tumor did not invade any margins, and lymph nodes were negative for neoplasm. The final pathological stage is T2a NO MX. The report also notes that additional testing (Movat stains) will be pending to assess for visceral pleural invasion.

The pathology report describes the examination of a tissue sample from a suspected right bronchial carcinoma. The report indicates the presence of a large, poorly differentiated or undifferentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the right upper lobe of the lung, with a tumor classification of pI2 NI VI RO and a stage of IIB. There are also findings of tumor necroses and inflammation, chronic pleuritis, and emphysematous stromal remodeling with the formation of subpleural cysts. Additionally, lymph nodes show deposits of anthracotic pigment and reactive macrophages with small foci of epithelioid cell reaction. The carcinoma appears to have invaded the visceral pleura.

The pathology report describes a case of moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the right middle lobe of the lung, measuring 4.5cm and involving the pleura. The tumor has invaded the visceral pleura and the hilar area of the right middle lobe. The bronchial margin is negative for tumor but there is tumor present in deep pulmonary parenchyma supporting the vascular resection margins. Multiple lymph nodes are positive for metastatic squamous cell carcinoma with extranodal tumor. There is lymphatic invasion present in the sample adjacent to the venous resection margins. No distant metastasis is identified. The lymph node fragments are negative for malignancy. A section of tissue labeled "RA" is an aggregate of pink white black irregular soft triable tissue fragments. An elastic stain was evaluated on blocks B2 and 93.

The pathology report includes findings from multiple tissue samples taken from the patient with lung cancer including excised portions of lymph nodes (levels V, XI, XII, VI, VII), a portion of the sixth rib, and a left lingula resection. The sixth rib portion showed no tumor and normal bone marrow. Two out of seven level V lymph nodes, seven out of nine XIL lymph nodes, and three out of four XIIL lymph nodes were found to have metastatic carcinoma. The left lingula resection revealed a 4.2 cm poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with lymphovascular invasion identified, and no involvement of the visceral pleura. Additionally, emphysema was noted. One of eight level VI lymph nodes showed metastatic carcinoma, while no tumors were found in the eleven level VII lymph nodes.

The pathology report describes a case of moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the right upper lobe of the lung, measuring around 55mm and invading the chest wall and intercostal muscle. However, the soft tissue resection margins are free of cancer, and there is no evidence of lymph node metastasis. The report also notes patchy squamous metaplasia and mild dysplasia in the bronchial resection margin and patchy organizing pneumonia in the adjacent lung parenchyma. The decalcified section of rib shows no evidence of periosteal or bony invasion by carcinoma. The pathological stage is classified as TS NO.

The pathology report describes the findings from the surgical resection of a left lower lobe lung tumor. The tumor is identified as a 4.5 cm poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with no invasion of surrounding large vessels. One lymph node out of the four examined shows no evidence of metastasis. The lymph nodes at level 9 and 11 also show no evidence of metastasis. The surgical margins are uninvolved. No distant metastasis is evident in this specimen.

The pathology report describes a tumor sample from the left lower lobe diagnosed as Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Not Otherwise Specified (NOS) with a tumor size of 2 cm. The tumor grade/differentiation is low (W1) and lymph nodes are negative (N0). There is also a comment about the presence of focal obstructive pneumonitis. Additionally, there is another sample mentioned (BUFFY) but there is no information provided about its diagnosis or findings.

The pathology report describes the results of a surgical biopsy of several lymph nodes and a lobectomy of the right lower lobe of the lung. The lymph nodes were found to have no malignancy and showed follicular lymphoid hyperplasia. However, the lung tissue showed moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with necrosis, which invaded the visceral pleura. Resection margins were negative for malignancy, and all peribronchial lymph nodes were negative for malignancy as well. Mild centroacinar emphysema and focal non-specific pneumonitis were also noted in the remaining lung tissue. The tumor was 7.7 cm in size and G2: moderately differentiated. The pathologic staging was pT2, pN0, and pMX (cannot be assessed). There were no regional lymph node metastases, and there was slight centrilobular emphysema. The representative sections were submitted for issue banking.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent left thoracotomy for removal of left upper lobe cancer. The report includes the results of examination of lymph nodes and other tissues. The lymph nodes from levels 2, 5, 6, and 7 were negative for metastatic carcinoma. The left pleural clot showed no evidence of carcinoma. However, the left upper lobe showed poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma that invaded into adjacent ribs and intercostal soft tissue, and perineural invasion was identified. All surgical margins were negative for carcinoma. The tumor was unifocal, with a greatest dimension of 7 cm, and was classified as pT3. No lymph node metastasis was detected (pN0). The report notes that additional stains are pending.

The pathology report describes the examination of a resected right upper lobe of the lung with a poorly differentiated and non-keratinizing, maturing squamous cell carcinoma measuring a maximum of 65 mm. The main tumor mass is in the apical section of the lung with infiltration of the visceral pleura and the parietal pleura with subpleural adipose tissue. Multifocally, angioinvasion is noted in the center of the tumor with vascular tumor thrombi. The bronchial resection margin and peribronchial lymph nodes are tumor free, with the latter exhibiting anthracosis. All further lymph nodes are also tumor-free with varying degrees of distinct anthracosis. The final diagnosis is stage 1B squamous cell carcinoma of the lung.

The report describes a left pneumonectomy (removal of one lung) and lymph node biopsies. The main specimen from the lung shows a non-small cell carcinoma with areas of necrosis, containing scattered foci suggestive of squamous differentiation but no evidence of keratinisation. Mitoses are frequent and abnormal. Vascular invasion is identified and there is invasion into, but not through, the mediastinal pleura. Metastatic carcinoma is present in peribronchial lymph nodes. The bronchial resection margin is clear of dysplasia and invasive malignancy, although a small amount of largely necrotic tumor appears to be free in the lumen. A fragment of hilar lymph node and No. 8 lymph node are also examined.

The pathology report indicates that there is a single lesion in the right lung superior lobe, which is a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with peripheral squamous cell carcinoma in situ. The tumor size is 4.55 cm, and it has invaded the visceral pleura and chest wall. The lymph node status is 2 N1 (2/26) for intrapulmonary lymph nodes, and the TNM classification is T2b N41 (2/26) G3 RO.

The pathology report describes a diagnosis of lung cancer. The report details the examination of various specimens, including a wedge of lung and surrounding tissue, lymph nodes, and soft tissue and bone fragments from the chest wall. The tumor is identified as a sacrococcygeal mass that invades the chest wall and pleura and is located 1 cm from the bronchial margin. The lymph nodes show evidence of metastasis. The final pathological stage is pT3 p0. The report notes that the exact operative procedure is available in the surgeon's operative report.

The pathology report describes multiple biopsies and specimens from lymph nodes, a rib, and lung, indicating the presence of poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the left lower lobe of the lung. The tumor measured 8.5 cm in maximum dimension and showed invasion of the pleura, lymphatic invasion, and moderate tumor necrosis. One of the examined lymph nodes showed metastatic carcinoma, but there was no evidence of tumor invasion through the venous or arterial walls. Additionally, non-neoplastic lung tissue showed acute bronchopneumonia. The report concludes that the tumor is stage N1 with one positive hilar lymph node out of a total of nine nodes examined. No clinical history or diagnosis is provided.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy specimen from a lung tumor that is 5 x 5 x 5.0mm in size and is identified as a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. There is no specified information on the tumor extent, other tumor nodules, lymphatic or venous invasion, or margins. However, 0 out of 4 lymph nodes were found to be positive for metastasis and no evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment was identified. No additional pathologic findings were reported. The tumor was located in the right-lower part of the lung.

The pathology report indicates that the patient had a partial nephrectomy of the left kidney and was diagnosed with a grade 1 papillary-type renal cell carcinoma, which forms a mass of 1.9 x 1.7 x 1.7 cm. The tumor is confined to the kidney, and there is no evidence of coagulative tumor necrosis or sarcomatoid differentiation. The surgical margins are negative for tumor by 0.2 cm. The report was revised from the original diagnosis, which indicated a clear cell type of renal cell carcinoma.

This is a partial pathology report that provides sample collection details, histology, and staging information for two samples labeled as BUFFY and J TUMOUR. The samples were collected on different dates and the site of collection was in the left upper lobe (LUL) for both samples. The histology and tumor stage information is incomplete, with only the size, differentiation, and lymph node involvement provided for one of the samples. No additional clinical comments or explanations were given.

The report describes the examination of various tissue samples from a patient with clinical diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma in the left upper lobe, possibly caused by exposure to asbestos. The report details the macroscopic and microscopic findings of the tissue samples, which include the primary tumor, adjacent pleura, and lymph nodes at various stations. The report also mentions the use of various staining methods for analysis.

The pathology report indicates that there was a 6.0 cm moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the right lower lung lobe. The carcinoma had angiolymphatic and visceral pleural invasion, but did not involve the surrounding lymph nodes. The pathological stage of the cancer was T2 NO MX. There was no evidence of malignancy in the lymph nodes that were biopsied. In addition, there was reactive change in several lymph nodes and benign fragments of fibroadipose tissue and nerve were found in other areas. There was also evidence of submucosal acute and chronic inflammation in the bronchial mucosa. Elastic tissue stains show pleural invasion. The squamous cell carcinoma had a unique subpleural pattern of growth with lymphatic infiltration. Overall, the report suggests a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the right lower lung lobe without lymph node involvement.

The pathology report describes the examination of multiple lymph nodes and lung tissue from a patient with LLL NSCLC. Lymph nodes from levels 7, 9, and 10 were all biopsied and found to be negative for metastatic carcinoma. The left lung contained a subpleural central mass that invaded both upper and lower lobes and was found to partially replace an enlarged lymph node and another lymph node further away. The report diagnoses the lymph nodes examined in levels 7, 9, and 10 as "reactive, anthracotic lymph nodes, negative for metastatic carcinoma" and the lymph nodes in levels 5 and 6, and level 9 as "negative for metastatic carcinoma." No further information is given regarding possible malignancy in the lung tissue.

The report describes the examination of three specimens - a right upper lobe of the lung, lymph node number 10, and a fragment of the fourth rib on the right. The lung specimen showed a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with invasion through the pleura and into the chest wall but no evidence of lymphatic, vascular or perineural invasion. The lymph node showed sinus histiocytosis with no evidence of metastatic carcinoma, and the rib fragment showed normal intercostal muscle and adipose tissue with no evidence of invasive or metastatic carcinoma. No final report was issued yet as sections of the ribs were still being examined.

The pathology report describes a 2.5 cm squamous cell carcinoma tumor in the lung lobe with surgical margins free of tumor. Twelve lymph nodes were examined and showed antracosis and sinus histiocytosis, with no evidence of metastasis. The tumor was moderately differentiated and had a tendency towards keratinization. No lymphatic or venous invasion was found. The report also indicates no evidence of additional tumors or previous treatment.

The pathology report pertains to a tumor specimen taken from location and anatomical site of TCGA-37-4141. The specimen is frozen and there is a normal blood sample as well. The report does not provide information about the tumor stage or treatment details. The grade and histological description of the tumor are also not mentioned. There is a reference to a chemo and hormone therapy detail, but it is unclear if it pertains to this patient or not.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a right thoracotomy and pneumonectomy for lung cancer. The tumor was a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, 9.3 cm in size, that invaded the pleura and ribs. No tumor was found in any of the 12 examined lymph nodes. However, the tumor was found in the bone marrow of the ribs. The report also indicates the histologic type and grade of the tumor, as well as information regarding margins and direct extension of the tumor. Additionally, pre-operative diagnoses and gross descriptions of the specimens received are provided. A clinical history is not given.

The pathology report describes a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma in the right lung nodule, which is invasive of the pleura. There is no evidence of carcinoma in the intrapulmonary lymph node or margin of resection. The tumor has a predominantly acinar pattern with small papillary and peripheral bronchioloalveolar components. The rib segment is negative for carcinoma. TTF1 stain is positive, and no lymphovascular invasion is seen. The report also includes details of the specimens received, sections taken, special procedures performed, and intra-operative consultation. The immunohistochemical stains used in the report are not cleared or approved by the US Food and Drug Administration.

The report summarizes the pathology results of several lymph nodes and lung tissue from a patient with left lung cancer. The lymph nodes in various locations were biopsied and found negative for metastasis. The left upper lobe of the lung contained a tumor measuring 4.0x3.5x3.0cm, which was removed from the bronchial margin and pleural surface. Frozen sections were taken for examination, and representative sections were submitted in ten cassettes for testing. No information is provided on whether the tumor was malignant or not.

The pathology report describes a case of poorly differentiated, large-cell, focally keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma located in the right lower lobe of the lung (TNM stage IB). The report also notes the presence of fibrosing interstitial pneumonia and reactive lesions in lymph nodes, as well as invasion of blood vessels by the carcinoma. No asbestos bodies are found in the prepared section planes, but further investigation is needed to determine the extent of asbestos exposure. All excised lymph nodes, resection planes, and visceral pleura are tumor-free.

The pathology report describes a patient with a left lung mass who underwent a VATS lobectomy. The report identifies the presence of two primary tumors, an adenocarcinoma and a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma, as well as involvement of lymph nodes in the left lung and mediastinum. There is no invasion of the visceral pleura, but lymphovascular invasion is present. One of the lymph nodes biopsied is positive for adenocarcinoma. The report also notes the presence of emphysema. The TNM staging indicates a pT2a tumor, with no regional lymph node metastasis. The report specifies the margins involved and treatment effect is deemed not applicable.

The biopsy was benign, and a lymph node showed no tumor. Several lymph nodes were negative for cancer. A lung lobe specimen with attached bronchus and blood vessels showed a definitive mass with bronchial mucosa appearing normal and lymph nodes measuring 0.3 to 0.9 cm. Testing for acid-fast bacilli and fungi was negative. No additional samples were examined during the intraoperative consultation.

The report includes information on multiple specimens received for analysis, including lymph nodes and a portion of the lung (left upper lobe) measuring 17 x 10 x 2.5 cm with a tumor identified. The report also provides details on the size and location of the tumor (subpleural with irregular borders) and notes that it does not appear to involve the bronchus. Lymph nodes are identified and submitted for examination. Representative sections are taken for analysis. No specific diagnosis is provided in this report.

The pathology report describes the analysis of several specimens obtained from a patient who underwent right middle and lower lobectomy, partial resection of right upper lobe and lymph node sampling. The report confirms the presence of a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma measuring 52mm in diameter in the apical segment of the right lower lobe. Invasion of parietal pleura and extensive vascular invasion are also noted. The tumor has focal perineural invasion and there is evidence of metastatic carcinoma in one of the lymph nodes. The final pathological stage is reported as T3 NL.

The pathology report describes a left pneumonectomy specimen that includes a lung with multiple lymph nodes. The lung has a poorly circumscribed, moderately differentiated keratinising squamous cell carcinoma that completely obstructs a segmental bronchus but is clear of the pleura and bronchial resection margin. The tumor directly invades several hilar lymph nodes but shows no evidence of lymphatic or vascular invasion. The lung distal to the tumor has secondary obstructive changes. Tissue from the lower lobe shows no definite pathological features. The lymph nodes show reactive changes but no evidence of metastatic carcinoma. The final diagnosis is squamous cell carcinoma, pathological stage T2 NI with no evidence of malignancy in the lymph nodes. No clinical details were provided.

The pathology report describes a lung nodule in the right lower lobe that was diagnosed as large cell carcinoma consistent with squamous cell carcinoma. The tumor measured 2.3 cm in diameter and was poorly differentiated, with no involvement in the visceral pleura. No carcinoma was identified in the margins of resection, and the lymph nodes were negative for metastasis. Other findings included fibrous pleural plaque, emphysematous changes, and inflammation in the lung and pleura. The final stage was pT1bNO, and a mucin stain and several immunohistochemical stains were performed.

The report describes a right upper lobectomy for carcinoma of the lung, with exposure to asbestos. The primary tumour is poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with extensive central necrosis and cavitation. It is associated with bronchial structures, but no definite bronchial origin is identified. The tumour is at least 20mm clear of the hilar resection margin and there is no evidence of pleural invasion. However, vascular invasion and metastatic carcinoma in one peribronchial lymph node are present. A mucous gland adenoma is seen at the bronchial resection margin. The report concludes with a pathological stage of T2 N1. The other specimens submitted (hilar lymph node, partial bronchus right side, and mediastinal lymph node) show no evidence of metastatic carcinoma.

The pathology report indicates the presence of a poorly differentiated basaloid squamous cell carcinoma in the lung. The tumor size measures approximately 1.35 cm. There is invasion of the visceral pleura, but no chest wall invasion. The node status is positive with N4 (2 out of 28 nodes affected). The grade of the tumor is G3 and the ICD-0-3 code is 308. The lung location is in the lower lobe.

The pathology report describes findings of a right upper lobe bronchial carcinoma, with adhesions to the chest wall, nodular tumor, and extension to adjacent lymph nodes. There is also evidence of blackish pigmentation in various lymph nodes, which may suggest metastasis. The report does not provide specific information regarding asbestosis. Additionally, a lipoma was also present in the examined material. Overall, further treatment and management would depend on the extent and staging of the cancer.

The report describes a tumor in the lower lobe of the left lung measuring 9.0 x 7.0 x 6.5 cm. The diagnosis is squamous cell carcinoma with infiltration of the pleura visceralis. It is staged as pT2, pN1 (3/57), pMx with a grade of G3. The report is signed by a pathologist with the initials Cp-o3 from CACC Roma and SGuamncns. The tissue sample came from the left lung lower lobe.

The pathology report describes a lobectomy of the right upper lobe of a lung due to invasive squamous cell carcinoma. One of four peribronchial/hilar lymph nodes is positive for carcinoma by direct extension. Three lymph nodes from station #4 and two from station #7 were negative for carcinoma. An excised lymph node from station #10 and four lymph nodes from station #11 were also negative for carcinoma. The tumor was poorly differentiated with a size of 3.7 cm and lymphovascular invasion. No other major findings were reported. One additional pathologic finding was a hyalinized nodule. The report includes detailed measurements and margin involvements.

The pathology report describes a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma measuring 4.5 cm in the right lower lobe of the lung. The tumor extends subpleurally but does not invade through the visceral pleura. Three lymph nodes were negative for tumor. The pathologic stage is T2N0Mx. The report notes that although the tumor is likely a primary lung carcinoma, the possibility of a lung metastasis cannot be completely ruled out. Two excised lymph nodes were also negative for tumor.

The report describes a lobectomy specimen of the right lower lobe with some lymph nodes recovered from the hilar region. A centrally cavitary, rubbery tan-white tumor mass is identified, approaching the pleura and hilum. The bronchial stump is calcified, and the mucosa is trimmed for frozen section. No additional mass lesion or abnormality is identified in the specimen, which is divided into multiple blocks for tissue procurement and further investigation. Lymph nodes and other soft tissues in the vicinity are also examined. A frozen section diagnosis reveals a PSA tumor.

The pathology report describes the results of the examination of various tissue samples from a patient who underwent surgery for a right lung mass. The report confirms that the mass was invasive squamous cell carcinoma, moderately differentiated, with a size of 4.5 cm. The tumor had spread to three out of fifteen peribronchial lymph nodes tested, and was also associated with squamous cell carcinoma in situ involving the adjacent bronchus. The report states that there was no malignancy in the lymph nodes tested in the right and left proximal and distal paratracheal regions and subcarinal level 7. Additionally, no abnormalities or malignancies were identified in the bone sample from the rib portion sent for testing.

The pathology report indicates that the patient underwent a biopsy of the Pleura and excision of multiple lymph nodes. No tumor was identified in any of the lymph nodes or in the pleura biopsy except for a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the right lower lobe of the lung. The report includes a frozen section diagnosis of fibrosis with no tumor seen in the pleura biopsy, and a non-small cell carcinoma favoring squamous in the excision of the right lower lobe of the lung. No lymphovascular invasion was identified and there were no tumor involvement in the shaved margins. There was also a benign chondroid hamartoma incidentally identified in the right lower lobe of the lung. Overall, the report suggests that there is no evidence of metastasis of the lung cancer to the excised lymph nodes.

The pathology report describes a biopsy of a soft tissue mass on the chest wall, which was consistent with a lipoma and did not show any evidence of malignancy. The report also notes the presence of a lung tumor, specifically squamous cell carcinoma, and the examination of multiple lymph nodes which did not reveal any evidence of cancer. One peribronchial lymph node did show signs of metastatic prostate carcinoma. The report indicates that due to the size of the chest wall lipoma, there is a risk of local recurrence, and also mentions the presence of hyalinized granulomas in the non-neoplastic parenchyma. Frozen section diagnosis was squamous cell carcinoma.

The report appears to be a missing pathology report form with incomplete information. It requests the tumor type, date of shipment, histology code, and site code for a case. However, the specific details are missing or redacted. Therefore, it is difficult to provide a summary of the actual pathology report as it is not available in the document provided.

The pathology report describes a pulmonary tumor that was surgically removed via pulmonectomy. The tumor was 3 x 2.5 x 2.5 cm in size and identified as squamous cell carcinoma, poorly differentiated. The tumor extent and the presence of other nodules were not specified. There were no lymphatic or venous invasions noted, and the margins were not specified. About three lymph nodes were examined, and none of them tested positive for metastasis. The report did not describe any other pathologic findings, or whether there had been any neo-adjuvant treatment. Overall, the report indicates that the patient had a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in their lung that had not yet metastasized to surrounding lymph nodes.

The pathology report describes the results of a biopsy of a patient with squamous cell carcinoma in their left lower lobe. The specimen received for frozen section was found to be representative of the tumor, which measured 3.5 cm and had a yellow-tan-gray variegated appearance with necrosis. The resection margin was free of tumor and the pleura was 0.1 cm from the tumor. Other specimens received included a wedge of lung with a stapled margin and an AP window node measuring 1.6 cm in greatest dimension. The frozen section diagnosis confirmed squamous cell carcinoma, which was also confirmed by permanent section. The stage of the cancer was determined to be IB. The report was reviewed by Dr. Jin who concurred with the diagnosis.

The pathology report describes a resected specimen of a poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma in the right upper lobe of the lung, with no evidence of malignancy in lymph nodes except for one in the rib. The tumor shows a high grade with a mitotic index of 12 mitoses per 10 high power fields and pierces through the pleura into skeletal muscle. Vascular invasion is absent, and there is emphysema in the non-tumor lung. The report also includes results of antibody tests for TTEL, p63, and CRS/6<1, with positive results for p63 and CRS/6<1. Eight specimens are received, including the lung, lymph nodes, rib, and soft tissues, for further analysis.

The pathology report describes a case of lung squamous cell carcinoma, with a tumor size of 4.0x3.5x3.0cm. There is evidence of visceral pleural invasion and chest wall invasion. The tumor is poorly differentiated and keratinizing. The node status is NO (0/34) and the tumor is classified as pT2a pNo (0/34) G3 RO.

The pathology report describes the presence of moderately to poorly differentiated invasive squamous cell carcinoma in the right lower lobe of the lung. The tumor does not invade the visceral pleura but extends subpleurally. Benign hilar lymph node is seen. Excised lymph nodes in stations 7, R-11, R-10, and R-4 are negative for cancerous cells. The pathologic stage is T2NOMX. The surgical pathology report also describes the characteristics and sections of the right lower lobe resection and lymph nodes excised for examination.

The pathology report is describing a tumor in the lung that is 5.5/4.5/4.5 cm in diameter and invading a parietal fragment with 2 rib fragments. The tumor is formed of solid beaches of relatively monomorphous cells with hotbeds of necrosis and abundant fibrous-inflammatory stroma. It is a squamous cell carcinoma of moderate differentiation with lymphatic invasion and no venous invasion. There is no evidence of metastases in lymph nodes. Margins and neo-adjuvant treatment are not specified. Overall, the report describes a localized lung cancer with features of invasion and lymphatic involvement, but without evidence of distant spread.

The pathology report describes a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma measuring 7.0x4.5x4.0 cm in the inferior lobe of the right lung. The tumor has not invaded visceral pleura and chest wall. There is no regional lymph node metastasis. The TM 2 pT2pNO(0/20) G2 Ro staging of the tumor indicates that it has a low risk of progression.

The pathology report indicates that there is metastasis present in all four lymph nodes in the intrathoracical region. However, there is no information provided regarding lymphatic or venous invasion, margins, and evidence of neo-adjuvant treatment. There are also no additional pathologic findings mentioned. The excision date and location are not clear.

The pathology report describes two specimens received, one labeled "right middle lobe" which shows a moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with extensive central necrosis.
